Chlorophyll Sweeper.description:
• Venusaur, due to its ability in Chlorophyll and excellent coverage, is a strong offensive threat in the metagame. These traits are complemented by Venusaur's access to Sleep Powder, which lets it put threats it and its partners struggle with like Garchomp and Aerodactyl to sleep.

  • Earth Power versus Grass-type Coverage: Earth Power deals with Steel-types like Archaludon and Kingambit that resist its STAB moves. This coverage pairs well with its best partner in Mega Charizard Y, as Earth Power also deals with Rock- and Fire-types that Mega Charizard Y struggles to deal with, such as Glimmora and Blaziken. However, if the rest of the team is able to handle these threats, Grass-type coverage may be used instead.

  • Sleep Powder versus Grass-type coverage: Sleep Powder has shaky accuracy but makes Venusaur especially terrifying. This is because Venusaur's boosted Speed under the sun lets it shut down checks like Mega Staraptor and Incineroar. If Venusaur is using Life Orb, a third move in Solar Beam or Leaf Storm is preferred to take advantage of the damage boost.

  • Solar Beam versus Leaf Storm: Solar Beam gives Venusaur a more spammable STAB move. When boosted by Helping Hand, Solar Beam OHKOes Garchomp and Mega Aerodactyl. On the other hand, Leaf Storm OHKOes threats like Milotic regardless of the weather at the cost of dropping Venusaur's Special Attack.

  • Abilities: Chlorophyll boosts Venusaur's Speed under the sun, letting it outspeed Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon, Sneasler, and Mega Aerodactyl and put these threats to sleep or heavily damage them.

  • Items: Focus Sash makes Sleep Powder's inaccuracy easier to handle, as it lets Venusaur at least have another chance to put a foe to sleep in case it misses. Focus Sash can also be crucial to let Venusaur deal some damage or inflict sleep in case the opponent sets up Tailwind. Alternatively, Life Orb boosts Venusaur's damage, letting it take out most Pelipper with Leaf Storm and non-bulky Mega Floette with Sludge Bomb.

Other Options

  • Protect versus a Third Attacking Move: Protect may be dropped in favor of a third attacking move to maximize Venusaur's offensive capabilities, as Venusaur will generally go first under the sun and put an opposing threat to sleep or finish it off before it can attack. Furthermore, Venusaur has decent bulk, surviving hits from Kingambit, Archaludon, Garchomp, and can have extra insurance if it's using a Focus Sash. However, dropping Protect leaves it vulnerable to Fake Out disruption.

  • Energy Ball: Energy Ball is not dependent on the weather and does not drop Venusaur's Special Attack while still doing enough damage to remove Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert. However, this leaves Venusaur unable to OHKO bulky Basculegion-M.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: While Venusaur can invalidate most of its offensive checks with Sleep Powder, it can find itself in an extremely bad situation if Sleep Powder misses. Venusaur also fails to OHKO most threats like Mega Staraptor, Mega Metagross, and Hydreigon even with the Life Orb boost and will get OHKOed back.

  • Bulkier Steel- and Grass-types like Gholdengo and Mega Venusaur give problems to Venusaur, as they shrug off its attacks. If Venusaur is lacking Earth Power, Gholdengo can even use it as setup fodder and OHKO it with +2 Make it Rain.

  • Weather setters like Alolan Ninetales, Mega Tyranitar, and Pelipper can swap in and shut down Venusaur's ability, allowing their teammates to outspeed and remove it.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is Venusaur's best partner, as it sets sun to activate Chlorophyll and deals with Steel- and Grass-types that Venusaur struggles with, such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Mega Venusaur.

  • Tailwind setters such as Aerodactyl and Whimsicott provide an extra Speed boost to match opposing teams' Tailwind. Aerodactyl also deals with opposing Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox, while Whimsicott provides more disruption in Encore and can also use Fake Tears to allow Venusaur to pick up surprise OHKOs.

  • Incineroar helps Venusaur put a foe to sleep more safely by using Fake Out, and it also deals with Mega Metagross and Gholdengo.

  • An alternative sun setter in Torkoal may be considered, as it frees up the Mega Evolution slot and allows the rest of the team to utilize other modes of play, such as Trick Room. Torkoal also provides Helping Hand support, which allows Venusaur to OHKO Archaludon, Mega Metagross, and Garchomp.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Mega Venusaur is a solid option thanks to its bulk, good coverage, and excellent matchup against Basculegion-M, Sylveon, Rotom-Wash, and Mega Floette. It also has a decent matchup against many common threats, such as Sneasler, Kingambit, and Incineroar.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power provides coverage against Steel- and Poison-types that Mega Venusaur would otherwise be unable to damage. Examples include Kingambit, Sneasler, Archaludon, and Mega Gengar, all of which Mega Venusaur can 2HKO. It also notably 3HKOes Incineroar, which Mega Venusaur can beat thanks to Thick Fat.

  • Mega Evolving Venusaur: When in the sun, Venusaur can outspeed the entire unboosted metagame. This means it may not always be optimal to Mega Evolve Venusaur when facing foes like Mega Charizard Y, as remaining in its base forme allows it to use an extremely fast Sleep Powder or clean up a weakened foe before it can attack. Alternatively, Mega Evolution provides Mega Venusaur with Thick Fat, which turns Mega Dragonite's Flamethrower from a 2HKO into a 4HKO, Mega Froslass's Blizzard from a 2HKO into a 3HKO, and Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball in the sun from a guaranteed OHKO into a 2HKO.

Other Options

  • Leech Seed: Leech Seed lets Mega Venusaur deal residual damage and increase its longevity. It helps Mega Venusaur win in the long term against bulky foes like Corviknight, which it otherwise can't damage well. Leech Seed will usually replace Earth Power or Giga Drain due to the importance of Sludge Bomb and Protect. Without Earth Power, Mega Venusaur lacks meaningful damage against Steel- and Poison-types like Kingambit and Sneasler. Without Giga Drain, Mega Venusaur becomes far less threatening to Water-types like Basculegion-M.

  • Sleep Powder: Sleep Powder can end a game if it hits, and Venusaur can use it multiple times in a single game thanks to its amazing bulk. However, Sleep Powder also comes at the cost of a precious move slot, meaning it will most likely replace Earth Power or Giga Drain. It can also make Venusaur a more inconsistent Pokemon to bring due to its poor accuracy.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 7 Def / 18 SpA / 9 Spe with Modest: This spread allows Venusaur to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M in the sun. The HP and Defense investment allows Venusaur to survive +2 Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. The remaining SPs are invested in Special Attack to maximize damage, allowing Mega Venusaur to still 2HKO specially defensive Archaludon sets.

  • 32 HP / 19 Def / 12 SpD / 3 Spe with Bold: 3 Speed SPs allow Venusaur to outspeed Mega Delphox in the sun. The remaining SPs are invested in bulk, allowing Venusaur to comfortably survive Psychic from Modest Mega Delphox, Brave Bird from Talonflame, and even a 200-Base Power Last Respects from Adamant Choice Scarf Adaptability Basculegion-M.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Although Mega Venusaur is protected from its usual weaknesses through Thick Fat, it is still weak to Flying- and Psychic-type attacks. This includes Pelipper, Mega Aerodactyl, Talonflame, Farigiraf, and Mega Delphox. Mega Delphox and Talonflame are particularly big problems, as they resist Giga Drain, are immune to Earth Power, and threaten it back with Psychic and Brave Bird, respectively. Mega Dragonite can also tank any attack from Mega Venusaur and 3HKO it with Dragon Pulse. It can also set up Tailwind right in front of Mega Venusaur. Corviknight completely walls Mega Venusaur; it can easily set up in front of Mega Venusaur and KO it with Brave Bird.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Rain teams appreciate Mega Venusaur's ability to switch into Grass-, Fighting-, and Electric-type attacks such as Sneasler's Close Combat and Rotom-Wash's Thunderbolt for partners like Archaludon, Pelipper, and Basculegion-M. It can also use Earth Power against Kingambit for Basculegion-M. In return, Archaludon can use Electro Shot to deal with Flying-types like Corviknight and Talonflame, while Basculegion-M can take out Mega Delphox. Pelipper can also switch in and massively reduce Mega Charizard Y's damage to Mega Venusaur with Drizzle. Kingambit and Incineroar are decent switch-ins to Psychic-type moves. They help check Farigiraf, which can easily tank Mega Venusaur's attacks and 2HKO it, while Mega Venusaur can switch into Fighting-type moves for them. Sableye is also a good switch-in to Psychic-type moves, as it can set up screens to make Mega Venusaur even harder to remove. In return, Mega Venusaur can handle the Fairy-types that threaten Sableye.

  • How to Overcome Mega Venusaur's Weaknesses: Pelipper, Archaludon, and Basculegion-M are great partners to bring against weather teams, as Pelipper hampers Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball and shuts down Mega Froslass's Aurora Veil, while Archaludon and Basculegion-M threaten them with Electro Shot and Last Respects. Partners like Sableye are better against setup spam and hyper offense teams; Sableye can use Encore to lock Mega Blastoise into Shell Smash while providing priority screens. Knowing when to use Protect is also very important for positioning, as it gives the team an extra turn to bring in Basculegion-M to threaten Psychic- and Fire-types, Pelipper against Mega Charizard Y, or Sableye to set up screens and shield Mega Venusaur from a strong attack.

Special Tank.description:
• Mega Venusaur's respectable defensive stats, great typing, and access to the fantastic Thick Fat ability often make it a Mega Evolution of choice for bulky teams. It notably walls the most popular Primarina, Mega Lopunny, and Meowscarada sets; can stomach hits from powerful special attackers like Mega Gengar, Mega Charizard Y, and Archaludon; and provides utility with its immunity to Toxic against the likes of Umbreon, Toxapex, and Bellibolt.

  • Sludge Bomb: Sludge Bomb's decent chance to poison foes can punish defensive switch-ins and cripple bulky Pokemon that Mega Venusaur otherwise struggles to damage, like Umbreon, by chipping away at their health, especially when combined with the damage from Leech Seed.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power provides complementary coverage against the Poison- and Steel-types that Mega Venusaur's STAB attacks cannot hit well. For example, Earth Power will always 2HKO Archaludon.

  • Leech Seed: Leech Seed's healing can allow Mega Venusaur and potentially its teammates to remain healthy throughout the game; for example, a Timid Leech Seeded Mega Charizard Y has a very slim chance to 2HKO Mega Venusaur with Flamethrower in sun, giving it the opportunity to alternate between attacking and using Synthesis. Additionally, defensive Pokemon don't appreciate Leech Seed's chip damage, and it provides great insurance against Yawn cycling from Hippowdon and Umbreon by healing off some of the entry hazard damage taken by Mega Venusaur's teammates if it's forced to switch out to avoid falling asleep.

  • Giga Drain: At the cost of some of Leech Seed's more general utility, Giga Drain makes Mega Venusaur a bit more threatening to Ground-types like Hippowdon and Garchomp and Water-types like Mega Gyarados and Mega Blastoise. Though it does considerable damage to Basculegion-M, keep in mind that a 150-Base Power Last Respects 2HKOes Mega Venusaur even after Giga Drain's healing, meaning that this matchup is unfavorable for it unless Basculegion-M has already lost some HP.

  • Chlorophyll: While both of Venusaur's possible base abilities are very situational, Chlorophyll allows it to always outspeed and potentially revenge kill Mega Charizard Y in sun and is therefore generally preferred over Overgrow even on sets using Giga Drain.

  • Beware of Corviknight: Corviknight, as well as other slow and bulky pivots like Galarian Slowking to a lesser extent, is particularly annoying for Mega Venusaur because it can shrug off any attacks the Grass / Poison type throws at it and denies Leech Seed healing with U-turn. Mega Venusaur greatly appreciates teammates that can set hazards, such as Garchomp and Archaludon, to dissuade the opponent from repeatedly switching Corviknight in and out.

Other Options

  • Toxic: Though it's less useful against offensive teams than Leech Seed, stall teams can be devastated by a well-timed Toxic. If you elect to use Toxic, Sludge Wave may be preferable to Sludge Bomb to lessen the chance of Mega Venusaur inadvertently inflicting the weaker poison effect.

Other SP Spread

32 HP / 21 Def / 13 SpD with Bold: Mega Venusaur can run a physically defensive set, giving it a better matchup against Mega Lucario, Aegislash, and Swords Dance Garchomp at the cost of not being able to easily switch in on special attackers. With this spread, it avoids the 2HKO from Jolly Mega Lucario's Meteor Mash, and it has enough Special Defense to always survive Timid Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Overheat from full HP and avoid getting 2HKOed by Timid Mega Gengar's Sludge Wave.

Sun Sweeper.description:
• Mega Charizard Y is a ruthless sweeper dealing immense damage with its Fire-type attacks. It threatens OHKOs and 2HKOs on the majority of the metagame such as Mega Floette, Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Mega Metagross. Mega Charizard Y opts to run bulk rather than maximizing its offense and Speed to help it survive longer in contrast to Regulation M-A.

  • Three Attacks Sweeper: Mega Charizard Y dominates simply using three attacks: Heat Wave, Weather Ball, and Solar Beam. Heat Wave provides powerful spread Fire-type damage. Weather Ball deals insane Fire-type damage while sun is active or provides handy coverage depending on the weather, and it is unaffected by Wide Guard. Solar Beam is necessary to threaten Water-types like Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert.

  • Drought: The sun set by Drought increases the damage of Mega Charizard Y's Fire-type attacks, guaranteeing that Heat Wave will OHKO Kingambit and Sinistcha. It also allows Solar Beam to be used in a single turn, enables Venusaur's Chlorophyll, and reduces the damage of Wave Crash from Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert.

  • Mega Evolving Charizard: Mega Charizard Y should not Mega Evolve right away unless there are no foes that can override the sun. It is best to wait until the opponent has sent out or Mega Evolved their weather setter like Pelipper and Mega Froslass before Mega Evolving Mega Charizard Y to ensure sun is not overridden.

Other Options

  • Helping Hand: Helping Hand can be run over Solar Beam when Mega Charizard Y is paired with Venusaur. Helping Hand-boosted Solar Beam from Life Orb Venusaur OHKOs Garchomp and Mega Aerodactyl, dealing significantly more damage than Mega Charizard Y's own Solar Beam.

  • Ancient Power: Ancient Power is a niche move used instead of Solar Beam primarily as a surprise attack to OHKO opposing Mega Charizard Y and to let it threaten Ceruledge and Hisuian Arcanine. An omni boost from Ancient Power is also extremely beneficial for Mega Charizard Y, letting it survive Rock Slide and giving it a chance to OHKO Mega Floette with Weather Ball.

SP Spreads

  • 16 HP / 25 Def / 12 SpA / 13 Spe with Modest: The given spread lets Mega Charizard Y survive Rock Slide from non-Life Orb Garchomp and gives it a good chance to survive Mystic Water-boosted Wave Crash from Adaptability Jolly Basculegion-M in the sun. 13 Speed SPs let Mega Charizard Y outspeed maximum Speed Modest Venusaur without active Chlorophyll, and the remaining SPs are invested into Special Attack to maximize Mega Charizard Y's damage output.

  • 30 HP / 31 Def / 1 SpA / 4 Spe with Modest: This bulkier SP spread provides Mega Charizard Y with a high chance to survive Rock Slide from Life Orb-boosted Jolly Garchomp and Aerodactyl and grants a favorable chance to survive Wave Crash from Life Orb-boosted Adaptability Basculegion-M in the sun. The Speed investment ensures Mega Charizard Y outruns Adamant Mega Swampert and Mega Tyranitar in the sun, and the remaining SPs are put into Special Attack.

  • 16 HP / 17 Def / 10 SpA / 23 Spe with Timid: This faster SP spread allows Mega Charizard Y to outspeed Excadrill in the sun as well as Glimmora and Hisuian Arcanine. The defensive investment allows Mega Charizard Y to survive Rock Slide from -1 Lycanroc-D, and the leftover SPs maximize Mega Charizard Y's Special Attack.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Charizard Y's biggest adversaries are Rock-types such as Mega Tyranitar, Mega Aerodactyl, Lycanroc-D, and Glimmora. They all easily threaten OHKOs with Rock Slide, Accelerock, and Power Gem respectively while Mega Charizard Y struggles to KO them.

  • Mega Raichu Y outspeeds Mega Charizard Y and easily threatens an OHKO with Zap Cannon.

  • Rain teams are difficult for Mega Charizard Y to defeat. Rain significantly reduces the damage of Heat Wave and Solar Beam, and it enables Mega Swampert's Swift Swim, allowing it to outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Wave Crash. Pelipper, Archaludon, and Sinistcha are also difficult for Mega Charizard Y to remove while rain is active. Pelipper and Archaludon threaten to OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Weather Ball and Electro Shot, respectively. Sinistcha can also set up Trick Room, allowing Pelipper and Archaludon to attack first, and it can provide them with redirection as well as healing thanks to Hospitality.

  • Although Mega Charizard Y can survive their attacks, Garchomp and Basculegion-M are still threats to it. Mega Charizard Y is naturally outrun by Garchomp and is unable to KO it with Solar Beam before Garchomp attacks twice with Rock Slide. Basculegion-M can outspeed Mega Charizard Y with Tailwind support from Whimsicott, giving Basculegion-M an opportunity to KO Mega Charizard Y before it can attack.

  • While it is an uncommon pick, Ceruledge walls all of Mega Charizard Y's attacks, so it can easily take advantage of this to set up with Bulk Up and proceed to snowball.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp and Basculegion-M are Mega Charizard Y's best partners, easily threatening Rock-types and Ceruledge as well as opposing Garchomp and Basculegion-M. Garchomp in particular can remove Mega Raichu Y. They are also great at pressuring opposing Mega Charizard Y.

  • While Mega Floette cannot be used in the same battle as Mega Charizard Y, it synergizes well as an alternative Mega Evolution when Mega Charizard Y has an unfavorable matchup. Mega Floette is great at removing Garchomp and deals devastating damage to Pokemon commonly found on rain teams like Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Archaludon. In return, Mega Charizard Y can easily threaten Mega Metagross, Gholdengo, Mega Gengar, and Mega Mawile, all of which Mega Floette is threatened by.

  • Incineroar is great at providing damage mitigation with Intimidate, ensuring that Mega Charizard Y survives Rock Slide from the Rock-types and Garchomp. It also provides Fake Out support to let Mega Charizard Y dish out damage safely.

  • Venusaur threatens Mega Aerodactyl and Garchomp, which Mega Charizard Y struggles to damage, as well as common Water-types like Basculegion-M, Mega Blastoise, and Mega Swampert. Sleep Powder can also disrupt foes, letting Mega Charizard Y stick around for longer.

Bulky Sweeper.description:
• Mega Charizard Y is very popular in the M-A metagame and has incredible sweeping potential due to its monstrous Special Attack stat and ability to set up sun. It can punish common Steel- and Grass-type foes such as Kingambit, Aegislash, and Sinistcha with its sun-boosted Fire-type attacks.

  • Sun-Affected Moves: Mega Charizard Y's sun helps it secure OHKOs against foes such as Kingambit, Aegislash, and Sinistcha with Heat Wave. Weather Ball takes advantage of sun by becoming another Fire-type STAB move that deals immense damage against specially defensive foes such as Mega Floette, Farigiraf, and Mega Gardevoir. Weather Ball also adapts to opposing weather, punishing foes like Maushold with a 2HKO in rain. The move can also get around Wide Guard from the likes of Aegislash and Aerodactyl. Solar Beam helps Mega Charizard Y threaten Water-type foes such as Milotic and Basculegion-M, OHKOing non-bulky Basculegion-M sets and 2HKOing Milotic and Garchomp.

  • Weather Wars: Mega Charizard Y can't always set up sun safely, as foes such as Alolan Ninetales, Mega Froslass, Pelipper, and Mega Tyranitar can change the weather upon switching in. Positioning is very important for Mega Charizard Y so that it can make full use of sun and not worry about it being overridden. Aside from switching Mega Charizard Y out, waiting to Mega Evolve is an optimal choice to prevent losing the weather war.

Abilities

Drought: Drought sets up sun, supporting partners by activating abilities like Venusaur's Chlorophyll and supporting Mega Charizard Y itself by increasing the damage of its Fire-type attacks and weakening Water-type attacks from threats like Milotic. Drought often forces opposing weather teams to remove Mega Charizard Y before executing their plans so they can maintain their weather. Drought can thwart opposing weather like rain by hindering the offensive capabilities of Swift Swim Basculegion-M and Pelipper. Mega Froslass struggles to set up Aurora Veil or rely on Blizzard in the face of Mega Charizard Y's Drought.

SP Spreads

  • 14 HP / 28 Def / 11 SpA / 13 Spe with Modest: The bulk on this spread allows Mega Charizard Y to survive Rock Slide from the likes of Excadrill and Garchomp, as well as Wave Crash from Basculegion-M as long as sun is active. The Special Attack SPs help it OHKO Basculegion-M with Solar Beam and give it a chance to OHKO Aegislash in Shield forme as well as Mega Froslass with Heat Wave. The Speed investment allows Mega Charizard Y to outspeed Adamant Swift Swim Basculegion-M while supported by Tailwind.

  • 24 HP / 14 Def / 11 SpA / 17 Spe with Modest: This spread offers more Speed than the previous spread while still giving Mega Charizard Y a good chance to survive Rock Slide from Excadrill and Garchomp, though it is not guaranteed. The HP investment allows it to avoid a 2HKO from Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball and almost always avoid a 2HKO from Rotom-Wash's Hydro Pump while in sun. The Speed helps it move before Archaludon and non-maximum Speed Rotom formes.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: This spread maximizes Mega Charizard Y's Speed and Special Attack. The Speed investment helps Mega Charizard Y outspeed maximum Speed Glimmora as well as maximum Speed Rotom formes while guaranteeing at least a Speed tie with Mega Kangaskhan. The Special Attack investment allows Weather Ball to 2HKO Mega Floette in sun.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: While all Pokemon that change the weather away from sun prove to be a problem for Mega Charizard Y, it struggles most against Mega Tyranitar's sand and Pelipper's rain. Mega Tyranitar's sand enables Sand Rush Excadrill to move before Mega Charizard Y and threaten it with Rock Slide, while Mega Charizard Y struggles to deal any significant damage to Mega Tyranitar in sand and can be OHKOed by its Rock Slide in return. Pelipper's rain enables Swift Swim Basculegion-M, which threatens Mega Charizard Y with its Water-type moves. Rain can also grant Pelipper a Water-type Weather Ball, which is enough to OHKO Mega Charizard Y. Choice Scarf Garchomp and Aerodactyl can threaten Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide, with Aerodactyl being able to OHKO it. Glimmora can easily threaten Mega Charizard Y with Power Gem and is a great pick in mirror matchups against opposing Mega Charizard Y. Opposing Glimmora and bulky Garchomp have an easier time threatening Mega Charizard Y under Tailwind.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Whimsicott can support Mega Charizard Y with Tailwind, helping it outspeed threats such as Choice Scarf Garchomp, and use Encore to put a foe into an unfavorable position, such as Sneasler after it uses Fake Out. Other Fairy-type partners like Mega Floette and Sylveon can threaten Dragon-type foes that resist Mega Charizard Y's Fire-type moves, such as Mega Dragonite and Garchomp, with Whimsicott and Sylveon not taking up a Mega slot. Aerodactyl has access to Tailwind and Wide Guard to prevent Rock Slide spam, as well Unnerve, which can help it deal with Sitrus Berry Basculegion-M and Garchomp sets. Garchomp can help against opposing Garchomp with Dragon Claw and opposing Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide. It can also use Earthquake next to Mega Charizard Y to threaten Rock-type foes such as Mega Tyranitar, Hisuian Arcanine, and both Mega and base Glimmora. Basculegion-M is a strong sweeper that can handle opposing Fire-types such as Mega Delphox with Wave Crash or Aqua Jet, while Last Respects can be used as a general sweeping option due to its immense damage output. Kingambit helps in the Trick Room matchup due to its low Speed and can also threaten Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch and Farigiraf with Kowtow Cleave. Sneasler pairs well with Mega Charizard Y, as it provides Fake Out support and can threaten Rock-type foes such as Mega Tyranitar and Lycanroc-D with Close Combat. Incineroar also provides Fake Out and Intimidate support against foes such as Basculegion-M and Garchomp, and it can threaten Basculegion-M with Throat Chop or Darkest Lariat.

  • How to Overcome Mega Charizard Y's Weaknesses: Leading with Mega Charizard Y can be risky against opposing weather teams, as it could easily lose weather control. Keeping it in the back can help position around opposing weather set by Pelipper and Mega Tyranitar. Eliminating opposing weather setters can put Mega Charizard Y in an advantageous position, as it no longer has to worry about sun being removed. Waiting to Mega Evolve until opposing weather has already been set up can also grant it a favorable position. It does, however, struggle to damage Dragon-type foes such as Dragonite, Garchomp, and Archaludon in rain. Having a Fairy- or Dragon-type partner such as Sylveon, Mega Floette, or Garchomp can help against the aforementioned foes. Mega Floette is great at covering matchups that Mega Charizard Y struggles against, such as Mega Tyranitar and Dragonite teams. Basculegion-M can help against Rock-type threats like Mega Tyranitar, Hisuian Arcanine, and Aerodactyl with its Water-type moves. Opposing Tailwind can cause foes such as Mega Tyranitar and Glimmora to outspeed Mega Charizard Y. Whimsicott can counter opposing Tailwind with a Tailwind of its own or by using Taunt on the opposing Tailwind user. Dual screens from foes like Sableye can also cause Mega Charizard Y and its partners to lose momentum. Stalling out screen turns with Protect or switching is an option to get around them. Protect and switching around are ways to avoid Fake Out cycling aimed at Mega Charizard Y.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Drought Offense.description:
• Drought turns Mega Charizard Y into one of the most ferocious wallbreakers in the game, as well as effective support against Water-types such as Primarina and Rotom-Wash!

  • Flamethrower versus Weather Ball: Flamethrower is Mega Charizard Y's most reliable Fire-type STAB move. Weather Ball offers a bit more power and gives Mega Charizard Y some extra coverage when the weather is changed, but this isn't always beneficial depending on the team you're facing.

  • Solar Beam: The blistering sun removes Solar Beam's biggest drawback, making it great coverage against common Water-types like Primarina and Rotom-Wash. Just be weary of weather changers like Hippowdon, Tyranitar, and Pelipper, which not only weaken Solar Beam's power but change it back to being a two-turn move!

  • Overheat: Overheat gets boosted to the heavens with the sunlight, with even Fire-resistant foes like Rotom-Wash and Garchomp taking over half their health from it! Just beware that the hit-and-run tactics Overheat encourages are heavily impacted by your opponent's team placing down Stealth Rock.

  • Flame Charge: Flame Charge transforms Mega Charizard Y into an effective late-game cleaner, with the bonus of destroying Focus Sash and Disguise.

  • Air Slash: Air Slash is a good secondary STAB move regardless of the current weather, especially against Mega Venusaur, whose Thick Fat can make it tricky to break through without risking an Overheat.

  • Timid versus Modest: Charizard is common enough where Speed ties can make or break games, but Modest does enhance Mega Charizard Y's wallbreaking power, with Overheat now having a small shot of OHKOing specially defensive Hippowdon.

  • Blaze versus Solar Power: Solar Power actually gives Charizard more power than its Mega Evolution, which can come in handy against opposing Mega Charizard Y teams. However, the damage it takes in the sun is unwelcome when Stealth Rock is in play, making Blaze the safer ability.

  • Sand Stream Partners: Since Mega Charizard Y relies on the warmth of the sun, resetting it with another weather ensures it keeps on roasting foes! Hippowdown is the star teammate here, having excellent defensive synergy with Mega Charizard Y and supporting it with Stealth Rock. Tyranitar doesn't work quite as well defensively, but it's still a worthy teammate as well thanks to its less predictable array of movesets.

  • Dealing with Stealth Rock: Mega Charizard Y should always run an odd HP stat to avoid getting 2HKOed by its archnemesis, Stealth Rock. Removing Stealth Rock is rather tricky in the current format, but if needed, Glimmora is the best Pokemon for that job with Mortal Spin, with the bonus of having Stealth Rock to further support Mega Charizard Y.

Other Options

  • Roost: While not a defensive Pokemon, Mega Charizard Y forces out enough Pokemon to justify using Roost. This can be especially helpful when Stealth Rock is up, giving Mega Charizard Y another chance to switch in.

  • Focus Blast: While not a reliable attack, Focus Blast deals massive damage to Tyranitar, which is otherwise one of Mega Charizard Y's strongest checks.

  • Dragon Pulse: Dragon Pulse is Mega Charizard Y's strongest attack against Dragon-types like Garchomp and Mega Dragonite, though note that Garchomp still takes massive damage from Fire-type attacks as long as the sun is shining.

  • Ancient Power: Ancient Power is a surprising attack to prevail in mirror matches against other Mega Charizard Y.

Dragon Dance.description:
• After a single Dragon Dance, Mega Charizard X can outspeed common metagame threats such as Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox and key Choice Scarf users such as Adamant Garchomp and Basculegion-M.

  • Roost vs. Coverage: Flare Blitz forces Mega Charizard X to take a lot of damage while attacking; Roost will allow Mega Charizard X to have more longevity and potentially allow for the option to set up more. Thunder Punch can be substituted in this slot if you are worried about Primarina, as at +1, it will OHKO maximum HP Primarina guaranteed. Earthquake is another coverage move to give Mega Charizard X the option to take on Tyranitar and Glimmora while at +1.

  • Adamant vs. Jolly: A Jolly nature gives +1 Mega Charizard X the Speed advantage versus foes like Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Adamant Garchomp as well as faster Mega Evolutions like Mega Gengar and Mega Greninja. Adamant cannot hit the same important Speed points, so can be used instead to bulk out Mega Charizard X to give it better opportunities to set up.

  • Possible Partner Pokemon: Mega Charizard X really does not enjoy facing down Glimmora, so having a reliable switch-in to its STAB options would go a long way. Hippowdon is a very strong option, as Hippowdon resists Glimmora's STAB moves and will provide Mega Charizard X with entry hazard support, allowing it to sweep more reliably. Other hazard setters like Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott can assist Mega Charizard X in getting OHKOs after a single boost.

Other Options

  • Outrage: Outrage can be used over Dragon Claw as a more oppressive option, but its move lock will limit Mega Charizard X's options in certain situations.

  • Scale Shot: Scale Shot is an interesting option over Dragon Claw that provides a better matchup against Garchomp, boosting Mega Charizard X's Speed further and getting around Focus Sash users. It, however, does not receive a boost from Tough Claws and can either miss or only hit twice, failing to get KOs.

  • Fire Punch: Fire Punch can be used over Flare Blitz if you want to maximize Mega Charizard X's longevity, but the drop in power will be significant.

SP Spreads

  • 12 HP / 29 Atk / 3 Def / 1 SpD / 21 Spe with Jolly: This spread is more optimized than just a basic 32/32/2 spread. The Speed investment allows Mega Charizard X to outspeed Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp after a Dragon Dance. The bulk investment will allow Mega Charizard X to survive Jolly Basculegion-M's 150-Base Power Last Respects guaranteed and Timid Mega Floette's Moonblast almost all of the time. An odd HP number will let Mega Charizard X switch in on Stealth Rock four times without fainting.

  • 16 HP / 30 Atk / 9 Def / 11 Spe with Adamant: This spread focuses more on Mega Charizard X's bulk than Speed while maximizing its damage output. After a Dragon Dance boost, Mega Charizard X will be able to OHKO maximum HP Mega Kangaskhan with Flare Blitz and OHKO maximum HP Archaludon sometimes, or guaranteed after a single layer of Spikes, with Flare Blitz. The HP and Defense investment lets Mega Charizard X tank a 150-Base Power Last Respects from Adamant Basculegion-M. 11 Speed SPs will allow Mega Charizard X to outspeed Mega Starmie and Adamant Choice Scarf Basculegion-M after a single Dragon Dance.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant or Jolly: If you're feeling uninspired, Mega Charizard X can run a basic offensive spread. An Adamant nature will allow for maximum power, but be aware that Mega Charizard X will miss important Speed benchmarks such as outrunning Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp. Jolly will provide Mega Charizard X with the Speed security, but it's worth knowing that beyond outspeeding Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp, there are not any significant Speed benchmarks unless your team is weak to Timid Choice Scarf Hydreigon.

Double Dance.description:
• Swords Dance will turn Mega Charizard X into a nuke with very few switch-ins. With access to Flame Charge and Scale Shot, Swords Dance Mega Charizard X can effectively run a set that will be difficult to stop.

  • Scale Shot vs. Flame Charge: Flame Charge is 100% accurate but significantly weaker, and it will lock Mega Charizard X out of coverage options if you run it alongside Flare Blitz. Scale Shot has the potential to be as powerful as Flare Blitz, but it can miss or only hit two or three times. It also does not get the Tough Claws boost, though after a single Swords Dance, a two-hit Scale Shot can knock uninvested Garchomp out.

  • Rounding Out the Set: Mega Charizard X doesn't need a lot of coverage when it has a +2 Attack boost. Roost will allow Mega Charizard X to use Flare Blitz multiple times and, in the right circumstances, set up further boosts. Dragon Claw can act as a more reliable STAB option for situations where Mega Charizard X doesn't want to risk using Scale Shot. Thunder Punch provides the coverage it needs to break through Primarina.

Other Options

  • Outrage: Outrage can be used as the third attack over a coverage move or Dragon Claw. It can provide Mega Charizard X the same massive damage output of Flare Blitz against Fire-resistant foes at the cost of being locked into the move.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake can be used as a strong neutral coverage option. It does not receive a boost from Tough Claws, but it can easily deal with Pokemon Mega Charizard X would otherwise not enjoy facing such as Tyranitar.

SP Spreads

  • 12 HP / 29 Atk / 3 Def / 1 SpD / 21 Spe with Jolly: The Speed allows Mega Charizard X to outspeed Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp after a Flame Charge or Scale Shot boost. The defensive investment will allow Mega Charizard X to survive 150-Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion-M and a Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette while having enough HP to allow Mega Charizard X to switch in on Stealth Rock four times.

  • 32 HP / 12 Atk / 3 Def / 1 SpD / 18 Spe with Adamant: Going Adamant will give Mega Charizard X a lot more bulk to play around with. This spread's bulk investment will allow Mega Charizard X to always survive Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake and Timid Glimmora's Power Gem. After a Speed boost from Scale Shot or Flame Charge, 18 Speed SPs will let Mega Charizard X outspeed Mega Lopunny. The Attack investment will let +2 Mega Charizard X knock out uninvested Garchomp with a two-hit Scale Shot.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant or Jolly: A simple offensive spread with either an Adamant or a Jolly nature can work, though it will lose out on important defensive calcs stated above. The leftover 2 SPs can be placed anywhere, but it should be noted that 2 or 0 HP SPs will leave Mega Charizard X with an odd HP number, letting it switch in on Stealth Rock four times.

Tank.description:
• By maximizing its physical bulk, Mega Charizard X can become a surprising answer to common Pokemon that would normally be expected to beat it one-on-one, such as Garchomp and Mega Starmie.

  • Dragon-type Move: Mega Charizard X can run a variety of viable Dragon-type moves on this set that all serve different functions. Dragon Tail will allow Mega Charizard X to act as a phazer and block foes' attempts to set up. Breaking Swipe will cripple almost all physical attackers, making them unable to break through Mega Charizard X. Dragon Claw is a good, reliable option if you are looking for consistent damage.

  • Flame Charge: Flame Charge will allow Mega Charizard X to more reliably take on common physical attackers such as Mega Starmie and Garchomp by allowing it to burn them with Will-O-Wisp before they can attack.

  • Possible Partner Pokemon: Tank Mega Charizard X will benefit from partners that can remove entry hazards or deter setup of them. Pokemon such as Meowscarada and Greninja will scare away common setters such as Garchomp and Hippowdon. Your own Garchomp or Hippowdon can scare away Glimmora while also providing Mega Charizard X with hazard support to complement burn damage and chip away at foes by phazing with Dragon Tail. Corviknight can Defog hazards away and protect Mega Charizard X.

Other Options

  • Flare Blitz: If you don't feel that the Speed security of Flame Charge is necessary for your team, Mega Charizard X can use other Fire-type STAB options. Flare Blitz will offer the highest damage but comes at the cost of Mega Charizard X's longevity.

  • Fire Punch: Fire Punch can be used over Flame Charge as a form of more reliable damage; it's not as powerful as Flare Blitz but does not have any major drawback.

SP Spreads

  • 30 HP / 29 Def / 7 Spe with Impish: This spread maximizes Mega Charizard X's physical bulk while running enough Speed to outspeed Mega Starmie and Sneasler after a single Flame Charge, letting it burn them with Will-O-Wisp before they can attack. The physical bulk investment lets it take on key threats such as Mega Starmie, Mega Kangaskhan, Garchomp, and Basculegion-M by being able to take a big hit, burn them, and then recover off the damage with Roost. The HP investment leaves Mega Charizard X with an odd HP number to maximize the number of times it can switch in with Stealth Rock up.

  • 26 HP / 29 Def / 11 Spe with Impish: Compared to the first one, this spread sacrifices a little bit of survivability in favor of outspeeding Adamant Basculegion-M. The HP stat remains an odd number to maximize the number of times Mega Charizard X can switch into Stealth Rock.

Setup Sweeper.description:
• Mega Blastoise uses Shell Smash and Water Spout to become a strong spread damage dealer after a supported setup turn. Mega Blastoise's natural bulk gives it setup opportunities with support from Fake Out, Rage Powder, or Armor Tail. However, it must be positioned carefully because chip damage weakens Water Spout, and Shell Smash's defense drops make it easier to revenge kill.

  • Shell Smash: After a Shell Smash boost, Mega Blastoise can outspeed most of the unboosted metagame, which makes a full-power Water Spout extremely difficult to switch around.

  • Water Spout: At full power, +2 Water Spout threatens OHKOs on offensive Garchomp, Farigiraf, Kingambit, and Sylveon, and it can even OHKO Mega Charizard Y through sun and Mega Tyranitar in sand.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse is a reliable attack to fall back on after Water Spout has been weakened, hitting Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Sinistcha, Mega Gengar, Aegislash, Basculegion-M, and Farigiraf. Notably, it has a high chance to 2HKO Basculegion-M even after Leftovers recovery. Its low flinch chance can also help against slower targets that survive the first hit, though it should not be relied on as Mega Blastoise's main way of breaking through checks.

  • Protect versus Fake Out: Protect is preferred because Mega Blastoise must respect both foes targeting it before and after it sets up, and Protect can also let Mega Blastoise stall Tailwind, weather, or Trick Room turns while its partner attacks. Fake Out is an alternative for teams that want Mega Blastoise to help create the opening turn instead. However, it is harder to justify on teams already using Sneasler or Incineroar, and losing Protect makes Mega Blastoise much easier to overwhelm after it boosts.

Other Options

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam can be used over Shell Smash to hit Dragon- and Grass-types such as Garchomp, Mega Dragonite, and Venusaur more effectively. However, dropping Shell Smash makes Mega Blastoise much less threatening against neutral targets, especially once Water Spout has been weakened.

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere can be used over Protect or Fake Out to give Mega Blastoise coverage for Kingambit, Archaludon, Hydreigon, and Mega Kangaskhan, notably always 2HKOing Archaludon. That said, losing Protect or Fake Out makes it harder for Mega Blastoise to either keep itself safe or help create its own setup turn.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest: This spread maximizes Mega Blastoise's damage and Speed, making it the preferred option for sweeping with Shell Smash. Even before boosting, a full-power Water Spout OHKOes Mega Delphox and Mega Aerodactyl. After a Shell Smash, Mega Blastoise outspeeds fast unboosted threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Delphox, and Sneasler, as well as Choice Scarf users such as Garchomp, Rotom-Wash, and Basculegion-M. At +2, Dark Pulse OHKOes Sinistcha and has a chance to OHKO Farigiraf, while a full-power Water Spout OHKOes specially bulky Corviknight.

  • 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpA with Modest: This bulkier spread keeps maximum Special Attack investment while trading Speed for better chances to set up against super effective hits. It notably lets Mega Blastoise survive Mega Charizard Y's Solar Beam and Rotom-Wash's Thunderbolt. The lack of Speed investment means Mega Blastoise misses out on outspeeding threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Delphox, Choice Scarf Garchomp, and Choice Scarf Jolly Basculegion-M after a Shell Smash. Because of this, Mega Blastoise benefits more from Trick Room support from partners like Farigiraf and Sinistcha, since it can still use Shell Smash to boost its damage without relying as heavily on the Speed boost under Trick Room.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Blastoise is heavily dependent on keeping its HP high, since chip damage, Fake Out, priority moves, and double targeting can quickly weaken Water Spout. Fake Out is especially disruptive after Mega Blastoise has already set up, as it can stop Water Spout for a turn and give the opponent time to chip Mega Blastoise, reposition, or stall out Tailwind. Priority moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch, Aegislash's Shadow Sneak, and Mega Dragonite's Extreme Speed are problematic, as they can deal meaningful damage with Shell Smash's defense drops and weaken Water Spout before Mega Blastoise gets to attack. Wide Guard from Pokemon such as Aerodactyl, Pelipper, and Aegislash blocks Water Spout entirely and forces Mega Blastoise to rely on single-target attacks. Pokemon like Venusaur and Rotom-Wash threaten Mega Blastoise with super effective damage. Mega Venusaur is especially difficult to break, as it comfortably takes Dark Pulse and Ice Beam while threatening Mega Blastoise with Giga Drain. Archaludon can threaten Mega Blastoise with Electro Shot in rain, but it is not always a safe answer after Mega Blastoise has boosted, as a +2 full-power Water Spout in rain can still deal massive damage to it. Dragon-types like Hydreigon and Kommo-o resist both Water Spout and Dark Pulse, with Hydreigon further weakening Mega Blastoise through Snarl. Mega Dragonite can also take a hit thanks to Multiscale and threaten back with Thunderbolt. Sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal weakens Water Spout, making it harder for Mega Blastoise to brute force teams with spread damage.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Sinistcha is one of Mega Blastoise's best partners. Its Rage Powder can redirect attacks, while Hospitality and Life Dew keep Water Spout strong. Farigiraf supports Mega Blastoise with Armor Tail, blocking priority moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Fake Out from Mega Kangaskhan, Sneasler, and Incineroar. Sinistcha and Farigiraf can also set Trick Room, giving an uninvested Mega Blastoise a way to attack faster teams without needing to use Shell Smash. In return, Fake Out variants of Mega Blastoise can help them set Trick Room. Partners like Sneasler and Incineroar provide Fake Out support, helping Mega Blastoise find setup oppurtunities; they also disrupt Wide Guard users such as Aerodactyl and Pelipper for a turn to let Water Spout connect. Additionally, Sneasler threatens Kingambit, Archaludon, and Hydregion with Close Combat, while Incineroar weakens physical attackers with Intimidate and can pivot with Parting Shot. With Rage Powder and Sleep Powder, Vivillon can deny attacks directed at Mega Blastoise, and it can also use Hurricane to pressure Grass-types, which resist Water Spout. Furthermore, Vivillon's Tailwind immediately gives Mega Blastoise speed control without requiring Shell Smash; and its Rain Dance removes sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal while strengthening Water Spout, allowing Mega Blastoise to OHKO uninvested Garchomp and 2HKO Sinistcha. Maushold can support Mega Blastoise with Follow Me as well as Rain Dance and Feint, with Feint being especially useful for breaking Protect and Wide Guard so that Water Spout can connect. Basculegion-M appreciates Mega Blastoise pressuring Pokemon such as Sinistcha, Farigiraf, and Aegislash with Dark Pulse. In return, it can target Mega Gardevoir's and Mega Floette's lower Defense stats while acting as another strong Water-type attacker that pressures Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y.

  • How to Overcome Mega Blastoise's Weaknesses: Mega Blastoise should usually be positioned with a support Pokemon that either helps it preserve its HP or prevents it from being picked off after setting up. Redirection from Sinistcha, Vivillon, or Maushold can protect it from single-target attacks, while Farigiraf prevents priority moves from cutting a sweep short. Against Wide Guard users, Mega Blastoise should use Dark Pulse or Aura Sphere instead of Water Spout; partners such as Sneasler, Kingambit, and Basculegion-M can also pressure these Pokemon so that it doesn't only rely on Feint and Fake Out support. Against sun teams, avoid setting up with Mega Blastoise too early because Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal can weaken Water Spout; instead, use teammates such as Basculegion-M, Sneasler, and Incineroar to pressure them before it attempts to sweep.

Half-Shell Hero (Shell Smash Sweeper).description:
• With an excellent typing and Shell Smash, Mega Blastoise is a potent and adaptable setup sweeper. If checks like Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Primarina are out of the way, Mega Blastoise's momentum can be difficult to stop!

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere is Mega Blastoise's most indispensable coverage option, allowing it to break through defensive mainstays Archaludon and Umbreon.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse puts the pressure on Mega Starmie and Basculegion-M, which can otherwise cut the momentum of a Mega Blastoise sweep short.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam may not benefit from Mega Launcher, but it's needed if you want Mega Blastoise to take on Mega Dragonite. It can also OHKO the ever-present Garchomp, as well as Hippowdon after a Shell Smash.

  • Water Pulse versus Hydro Pump: Water Pulse is the go-to STAB option thanks to Mega Launcher, and it's Mega Blastoise's best attack against threats like Mega Blaziken and Mega Mawile. Hydro Pump is less consistent then Water Pulse with only a small power increase, but the improved chance of OHKOing some Hippowdon without needing Shell Smash can make it worth the risk.

Other Options

  • White Herb: While the loss of Mega Launcher is a serious power drop, running White Herb can help Blastoise maintain its survivability while notably freeing up Mega Evolution for a teammate. Do note that Blastoise should be running Surf over Water Pulse due to the lack of Mega Launcher.

  • Water Spout: When Mega Blastoise is at full health, an unboosted Water Spout is a guaranteed OHKO on any variant of Hippowdon. In most other circumstances though, Blastoise is usually taking damage during Shell Smash setup, meaning that Water Spout will often be a worse option compared to Water Pulse or Hydro Pump.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 19 HP / 18 SpA / 29 Spe with Modest: This spread sacrifices some offensive power to let Mega Blastoise almost always avoid the 2HKO from Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake, which can be particularly important against Focus Sash leads. Enough Speed is maintained to outrun Jolly Choice Scarf Garchomp after a Shell Smash.

  • 11 HP / 29 SpA / 26 Spe with Modest: This spread is tuned towards Jolly Meowscarada, giving Mega Blastoise just enough bulk to always survive Flower Trick and almost always OHKO back with Ice Beam. Enough Speed is retained to outrun Timid Choice Scarf Hydreigon after a Shell Smash.

Turtle Power! (Bulky Attacker).description:
• Mega Blastoise packs high power upfront thanks to Mega Launcher. With a wide variety of coverage options, it can cause immediate havoc for opposing offensive teams!

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere helps Mega Blastoise trade effectively with all variants of Archaludon, in addition to 2HKOing physically defensive Umbreon and OHKOing maximum HP Hisuian Samurott.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse tips the Aegislash matchup into Mega Blastoise's favor and deals massive damage to Gholdengo and Mega Starmie.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam is necessary to deal any significant damage to Dragonite, and it's the best option against Garchomp and Meowscarada as well.

  • Water Pulse versus Hydro Pump: Water Pulse hits key targets like Hippowdon and Mega Blaziken hard and will also 2HKO maximum HP Mega Mawile. Hydro Pump trades the consistency of Water Pulse for a higher chance at OHKOing some Hippowdon.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet further cements Mega Blastoise's trading potential, letting it finish off weakened targets such as Focus Sash Garchomp and Sturdy Archaludon.

Other Options

  • Mirror Coat: Mirror Coat is an option for dealing with Primarina and Rotom-W, though be wary of Calm Mind Primarina.

Fast Attacker.description:
• Mega Raichu Y is a great utility Mega Pokemon that is able to support its teammates with the fastest Fake Out currently available in the game and access to perfectly accurate Zap Cannons that heavily pressure metagame staples such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Aerodactyl, and Basculegion-M, and the guaranteed paralysis acts as speed control for partners with middling Speed against fast threats such as Chlorophyl Venusaur, Mega Delphox, and Sneasler.

  • Lightning Rod: Before Mega Evolving, Raichu can act as a strong option against opposing Raichu and stifle the attempts of opposing Archaludon to steamroll with Electro Shot. Delaying Mega Evolution can let Raichu boost its Special Attack off the attacks of certain opposing Pokemon, letting it set up to get major OHKOs it wouldn't be able to normally such as Chople Berry Kingambit with Focus Blast.

  • Focus Blast: Focus Blast lets Mega Raichu Y beat Pokemon like Archaludon, Hydreigon, and the ever-present Kingambit. It also provides useful neutral coverage into important Pokemon that resist Zap Cannon such as Garchomp.

Other Options

  • Grass Knot: Sacrificing utility for coverage, Grass Knot can be a good option for Mega Raichu Y to be able to OHKO Mega Swampert should it receive speed control. While Grass Knot can flip the matchup against Mega Swampert, it is only really valuable versus Mega Swampert. The Fake Out slot is generally considered the flex slot on Mega Raichu Y, so Grass Knot or any other moves considered would replace it. Losing Fake Out will make Mega Raichu Y more one-dimensional, as it will not be able to actively support its teammates and will no longer have much value before Mega Evolving.

  • Volt Switch: Volt Switch can be used as an option to pivot Mega Raichu Y around and keep it healthy to provide late-game pressure once its checks have been dealt with.

  • Encore: Encore is a greatly oppressive tool that can punish passive play, such as Protect, Fake Out, and setup. This can be used over Focus Blast to lean into the support potential of Mega Raichu Y. Threatening the potential of Fake Out, making opposing Pokemon use Protect, and punishing them immediately after with Encore provides teammates such as Kingambit more opportunity to set up.

SP Spreads

  • 29 HP / 14 Def / 23 Spe with Timid: The HP and Defense means Raichu can take Black Glasses Kowtow Cleave from Adamant Kingambit, Close Combat from Jolly Sneasler, and almost always survive Psychic Fangs from Jolly Mega Metagross. The HP investment and Mega Raichu Y's natural Special Defense stat lets it take a maximum Special Attack Modest Mega Charizard Y Heat Wave in the sun. The Speed investment will allow Mega Raichu Y to outspeed Jolly Sneasler and Timid Mega Froslass.

  • 32 HP / 21 Def / 5 SpD / 8 Spe with Timid: This spread sacrifices some of the Speed of the previous spread in favor of allowing Mega Raichu Y to survive Earthquake from an Intimidated Jolly Life Orb Garchomp. It will also let Mega Raichu Y survive Life Orb Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Jolly Mega Staraptor's Close Combat. The Special Defense investment will guarantee survival from an Earth Power from Modest Life Orb Venusaur. The Speed outspeeds Modest Mega Froslass and Adamant Sneasler.

  • 32 HP / 1 Def / 1 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: This spread is a lot more simplified to take advantage of Mega Raichu Y's impressive base 130 Speed stat, allowing it to Speed tie Aerodactyl and Mega Gengar. Maximum HP investment with 1 Defense SP will guarantee survival from a Sucker Punch from Life Orb Adamant Kingambit, with the last SP going into Special Attack.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Raichu Y struggles greatly into opposing Ground-type Pokemon. Mega Swampert and Garchomp are especially difficult for Mega Raichu Y to maneuver around safely. Each of them are capable of OHKOing Mega Raichu Y with Ground-type moves such as Earthquake and High Horsepower or Stomping Tantrum, respectively. Mamoswine can be difficult for Mega Raichu Y if it is a Choice Scarf or Focus Sash variant or has redirection support. It does not appreciate taking a Focus Blast, but if it can avoid it the hit by being faster, or having redirection, or surviving the hit with Focus Sash, it will be able to OHKO Mega Raichu Y with High Horsepower. Sand Rush Excadrill can cause issues for similar reasons; the boosted Speed and Focus Sash to guarantee survival from a Focus Blast can be difficult to navigate.

  • Grass-type Pokemon, such as Sinistcha and Venusaur, that resist Focus Blast and Zap Cannon are near-impossible to muscle through. Sinistcha can freely set up Trick Room in front of Mega Raichu Y or enable its partner to freely deal with Mega Raichu Y by redirecting hits with Rage Powder. Venusaur, both Mega and non-Mega, is a great challenge for Mega Raichu Y. The Mega Venusaur variants are able to shrug off any hit and threaten it back with Earth Power or recover the damage with Giga Drain, while the non-Mega variants outspeed with a Chlorophyll boost and either potentially KOing Mega Raichu Y with Life Orb Earth Power or taking advantage of Mega Raichu Y's own No Guard for perfectly accurate Sleep Powders. Whimsicott also resists all of Mega Raichu Y's coverage options but with the added pressure from Encore locking any Fake Out attempts. It can also enable its partners such as Basculegion-M to outspeed and KO Mega Raichu Y after setting up Tailwind.

  • Due to Mega Raichu Y's overall lackluster defensive stats, it can be easily kept in check with strong priority moves such as Sucker Punch from Kingambit and Aqua Jet from Basculegion-M; both of these are capable of 2HKOing even bulky variants of Mega Raichu Y, though Basculegion-M requires a boosting item such as Mystic Water or Life Orb to have a chance at a 2HKO.

  • Good Partners: Teammates that hit popular Ground-type Pokemon such as Garchomp and Mega Swampert are a must. Sinistcha is a great Grass-type partner that can beat Mega Swampert while providing passive recovery and redirection support. Basculegion-M loves the support Mega Raichu Y provides and can pin Garchomp and Mega Swampert with exceptionally powerful Wave Crashes and Aqua Jets. Setup Pokemon such as Kingambit enjoy the Fake Out and paralysis support provided by Mega Raichu Y while keeping problem Pokemon like Sinistcha and Basculegion-M in check. Fairy-type Pokemon such as Sylveon and Whimsicott check the most common Ground-type currently, Garchomp. While not as common anymore, Ice-types such as Mamoswine and Alolan Ninetales will be able to keep Garchomp in check, with the latter being able to handle Mega Swampert if it's running Freeze Dry. Ice-type Pokemon can also keep Grass-type Pokemon in check, while Mega Raichu Y covers the Water-type Pokemon that resist their moves.

  • Farigiraf is able to block priority attacks with Armor Tail to keep Mega Raichu Y safe from being picked off at low HP by Kingambit and Basculegion-M and block Fake Out to allow Mega Raichu Y to keep its momentum going. Farigiraf's Helping Hand can boost Mega Raichu Y to secure big OHKOs such as Chople Berry Kingambit with Focus Blast or +1 Special Defense Mega Staraptor with Zap Cannon. Strong Fire-type options such as Hisuian Arcanine and Incineroar can help Mega Raichu Y deal with the Grass-type Pokemon that it would otherwise struggle with such as Sinistcha, Whimsicott, and non-Mega Venusaur.

  • Synergies: Staraptor and Aerodactyl can function without having to Mega Evolve, being immune to Ground and providing the ever-important Tailwind support. Both have a positive matchup into Garchomp, as the former can Intimidate and the latter often runs Ice Fang or Wide Guard. Mega Raichu Y also complements them both in their more challenging matchups, as it can threaten Mega Charizard Y for Staraptor and Mega Blastoise for Aerodactyl. Mega Floette has also seen success alongside Mega Raichu Y, with Raichu being able to support without Mega Evolving with Fake Out and Mega Floette being a solid option into matchups Mega Raichu Y doesn't do well in such as Mega Swampert versions of rain or teams where Garchomp is the focal point.

All-Out Attacker.description:
Mega Raichu Y is one of the best special attackers in the tier thanks to its incredible Special Attack and Speed stats, combination of No Guard and Zap Cannon, and wide selection coverage options. Zap Cannon can 2HKO many common threats like Mega Floette, Clefable, Aegislash, and Rotom-Wash; additionally, Dragapult, which otherwise outspeeds and threatens to either KO or pivot out with U-turn, is unable to switch in due to Zap Cannon's power and guaranteed paralysis. Focus Blast provides Mega Raichu Y a way to tear through Electric-resistant and -immune foes like Archaludon and Excadrill, as well as Kingambit. Grass Knot targets Hippowdon, notably 2HKOing mixed variants, and Mega Swampert, but Alluring Voice can be ran instead, as this allows it to hit Dragapult and Garchomp for super effective damage. Surf 2HKOes specially defensive Gliscor, which otherwise walls Mega Raichu Y's Electric-type attacks. Volt Switch provides its team momentum while escaping bad matchups, such as those against Mega Dragalge, Mega Meganium, and Galarian Slowking. Substitute is another option to ease prediction around Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott trying to revenge kill it with STAB Sucker Punch while making use of the switches Mega Raichu Y forces, allowing it to spread paralysis with Zap Cannon much more easily.

Mega Raichu Y can be found on offense and bulky offense teams that benefit from its paralysis support via Zap Cannon. It also serves as an amazing speed control option for these types of teams, outpacing almost the entire unboosted metagame and pressuring it with its coverage attacks. Pokemon like Excadrill and Garchomp can pressure its checks like Mega Dragalge and Galarian Slowking with Earthquake. In return, Mega Raichu Y can threaten Corviknight and Rotom-Wash for said Ground-types. Mega Raichu Y is extremely frail, which leaves it vulnerable to faster revenge killers like Mega Lopunny and Choice Scarf users like Meowscarada, as well as causing it to struggle to switch in safely. To fix this problem, you can pair it with pivots, such as Corviknight and Galarian Slowking Corviknight's great physical bulk allows it to easily switch in on both Meowscarada and Mega Lopunny, and it can easily remove entry hazards with Defog, which can otherwise wear down Mega Raichu Y. Galarian Slowking can bring Mega Raichu Y in safely with Chilly Reception and absorb Toxic Spikes, which can otherwise wear Mega Raichu Y down. It can also provide Future Sight support to help Mega Raichu Y break through Mega Dragalge, a Pokemon that otherwise shrugs off its attacks, while making pivoting into Mega Raichu Y much more of a chore. Hisuian Samurott, in particular, is a great teammate, setting up Spikes with Ceaseless Edge while threatening faster threats to Mega Raichu Y, like Mega Delphox, with STAB Sucker Punch; a single layer of Spikes guarantees that Mega Raichu Y's Grass Knot OHKOes physically defensive variants of Hippowdon. Dark-type attackers like Kingambit, Hydreigon, and Hisuian Samurott appreciate Volt Switch support and take care of Galarian Slowking, which otherwise switches in on Mega Raichu Y, while Mega Raichu Y deals with Corviknight, Clefable, and Primarina for them.

The Rat (Paralysis Spreader).description:
• Mega Raichu Y is a fast but frail paralysis spreader that uses No Guard to fire off Zap Cannon and Focus Blast with perfect accuracy. Zap Cannon notably OHKOes bulky Primarina and severely dents Gholdengo while paralyzing most foes that survive, such as Mega Floette, often allowing Mega Raichu Y to outspeed and finish them off if they cannot KO it immediately. This makes Raichu difficult to revenge kill without a Ground-type or a faster attacker.

  • Focus Blast: Focus Blast covers Pokemon that resist Zap Cannon, OHKOing offensive Archaludon, Hydreigon, and Kingambit. However, specially defensive Archaludon, Rotom-Wash, and Garchomp can survive Focus Blast, so Mega Raichu Y or its teammates must weaken them first.

  • Grass Knot: Grass Knot prevents Ground-types from completely shutting down Mega Raichu Y; it notably OHKOes offensive Mega Swampert, has a good chance to OHKO physically defensive Hippowdon, and 2HKOes specially defensive Hippowdon.

  • Substitute versus Volt Switch: Substitute takes advantage of the switches Mega Raichu Y forces and works well with Zap Cannon's guaranteed paralysis; behind a Substitute, it can safely use Zap Cannon against faster foes such as Mega Delphox and Choice Scarf Hydreigon. If Hydreigon stays in to break the Substitute, Zap Cannon's paralysis will allow Mega Raichu Y to outspeed and KO it with Focus Blast, while switching risks getting Hydreigon's teammate paralyzed instead. Substitute also blocks priority moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and status moves such as Hippowdon's Yawn. Volt Switch lets Mega Raichu Y maintain momentum against switches it forces, but forgoing Substitute leaves it much more vulnerable to faster attackers and Choice Scarf users.

  • Mega Evolving Raichu: Raichu usually Mega Evolves immediately to gain No Guard and improved offensive stats. However, delaying Mega Evolution lets it absorb Electric-type attacks such as Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch and Archaludon's Electro Shot with Lightning Rod and gain a Special Attack boost, which is retained after Mega Evolving.

Other Options

  • Fake Out: Fake Out lets Mega Raichu Y provide immediate chip damage, notably breaking Focus Sash on common users such as Garchomp and Glimmora. It can also break Multiscale on Dragonite, letting Raichu or its teammates handle Dragonite more easily.

  • Alluring Voice: Alluring Voice gives Mega Raichu Y meaningful coverage against defensive Garchomp, which is immune to Zap Cannon and otherwise is usually 3HKOed by Focus Blast. It 2HKOes most non-Sitrus Berry Garchomp variants and deals considerably more damage than Focus Blast to specially defensive variants.

  • Encore: Encore punishes priority-based attempts to play around Mega Raichu Y, notably locking Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott into Sucker Punch or Aegislash into King's Shield. However, its usefulness is much more situational compared to Substitute, Volt Switch, or Fake Out.

Offensive Support.description:
• Alolan Ninetales utilizes its support movepool in conjunction with its ability to set snow to disrupt the common weather setters of the format like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Tyranitar while boasting strong matchups into metagame staples like Garchomp, Sinistcha, and Whimsicott.

  • Aurora Veil: Aurora Veil allows Alolan Ninetales to, in the snow, survive attacks such as Heat Wave from Modest Mega Charizard Y and Dire Claw from Adamant Sneasler and almost always survive 200 Base Power Last Respects from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M.

  • Encore: Encore allows Alolan Ninetales to punish defensive play from the likes of Kingambit and Mega Aerodactyl, scaring them away from setting up Swords Dance and setting Tailwind, respectively. It also heavily punishes Fake Out from Pokemon such as Incineroar and Sneasler.

Other Options

========

  • Freeze-Dry: Freeze-Dry allows Alolan Ninetales to threaten heavy damage onto Basculegion-M and Pelipper while providing an Ice-type STAB move that isn't thwarted by Wide Guard. This does come at the cost of Encore, however, weakening the utility of Alolan Ninetales.

  • Disable: Disable + Encore is a devastating duo that can easily turn foes against themselves, especially when combined with Mega Gengar, providing them with no escape. In order to run Disable, it must be used over Aurora Veil, though this doesn't particularly matter to the teams that Disable Alolan Ninetales is placed on, as they appreciate its ability to shut down foes for allies like the aforementioned Mega Gengar to set up Perish Song.

Items

========

  • Never-Melt Ice: Never-Melt Ice allows Alolan Ninetales to 2HKO low bulk variants of Sneasler a solid amount of the time and always OHKO Whimsicott with Blizzard.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash increases Alolan Ninetales's survivability, allowing it to survive attacks such as Mega Gengar's Sludge Bomb and retaliate back or use Encore or Disable.

Abilities

========

  • Snow Warning: Snow Warning sets up the snow, allowing Alolan Ninetales to survive Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, increase Blizzard's accuracy, and use Aurora Veil.

Teambuilding

========

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fire-type Pokemon like Incineroar and Mega Charizard Y threaten Alolan Ninetales with huge damage by using Flare Blitz and Heat Wave, respectively. Mega Charizard Y, as well as other weather setters like Mega Tyranitar, can shut off the snow, making Blizzard unreliable and rendering Aurora Veil useless. Mega Tyranitar, similar to Mega Charizard Y, also has the ability to deal big damage to Alolan Ninetales with Rock Slide. Other Rock-type Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl and Lycanroc-D threaten Alolan Ninetales with Rock Slide, with the former being able to outspeed Alolan Ninetales or use Wide Guard to prevent it from dealing damage. Steel-type Pokemon like Kingambit and Archaludon threaten to OHKO Alolan Ninetales with Iron Head and Flash Cannon, respectively, even when the snow and Aurora Veil are set up. Sneasler and Mega Gengar can outspeed Alolan Ninetales and threaten it with Dire Claw and Sludge Bomb. Trick Room from Farigiraf enables strong attackers like Torkoal, turning Alolan Ninetales's high Speed against it and allowing them to outspeed and OHKO Alolan Ninetales with Eruption.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp threatens the Fire-, Rock-, Steel-, and Poison-type Pokemon that all threaten Alolan Ninetales with Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum while targeting down Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide. In return, Alolan Ninetales threatens opposing Garchomp and other Dragon-type Pokemon like Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite while using Encore to prevent setup sweepers like Mega Floette from getting out of hand. Kingambit can scare away opposing Trick Room by being able to take advantage of it itself and threatening Farigiraf and Sinistcha, common Trick Room setters, with Kowtow Cleave. It also scares away Incineroar thanks to Defiant and threatens Mega Tyranitar and opposing Kingambit with Low Kick, opposing Rock-type Pokemon with Iron Head, and Mega Gengar with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch. Alolan Ninetales uses Aurora Veil to give Kingambit an easier time setting up and threatens Garchomp with Blizzard. Mega Gengar appreciates Encore and potentially Disable from Alolan Ninetales to shut down troublesome Pokemon for it like Kingambit and Incineroar, and it traps and KOes Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar and Archaludon in return with Perish Song. Mega Pokemon like Mega Glimmora and Mega Aerodactyl are helpful as well, using their Rock-type STAB moves to KO opposing Fire-type Pokemon.

  • How to Overcome Alolan Ninetales's Weaknesses: Using Pokemon that beat opposing weather setters is mandatory for Alolan Ninetales, as it needs the snow to be up for many of its main qualities. Consider bring Alolan Ninetales into weather matchups as well, as it can override opposing weather. When combined with Mega Gengar, opposing weather setters can stay trapped, leaving snow as the prevailing weather and making foes like Archaludon and Excadrill much less threatening.

Aurora Veil Support.description:
• Alolan Ninetales provides support in Aurora Veil and weather disruption, the former of which enables scary setup threats like Mega Gyarados, Mega Blaziken, and Mega Delphox. You can pair it with teammates like Aegislash and Gholdengo that can defensively switch into Steel-type threats like Mega Metagross and Archaludon.

  • Freeze-Dry: Freeze-Dry allows Alolan Ninetales to threaten Water-types like Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Mega Gyarados, and Primarina.

  • Blizzard versus Moonblast: Blizzard OHKOes Garchomp, heavily damages Hippowdon, and chunks offensive Archaludon sets that may switch into Alolan Ninetales. On the other hand, Moonblast lets Alolan Ninetales deal more damage to Mega Gyarados, Mega Blaziken, and Hisuian Samurott.

  • Encore: Encore disrupts opposing setup Pokemon like Swords Dance Mega Mawile, Calm Mind Mega Floette, and Iron Defense Corviknight, and it annoys defensive responses such as Defog Corviknight and Toxic Bellibolt.

SP Spreads

  • Alolan Ninetales prefers to have an even Defense stat, as it grants Alolan Ninetales one extra point of Defense when under snow.

  • 31 HP / 9 Def / 26 Spe with Bold: This spread allows Alolan Ninetales to generally survive Adamant Mega Metagross's Bullet Punch at full HP under snow, letting it set Aurora Veil for the team. The remaining SPs are invested in Speed, enabling Alolan Ninetales to outspeed Excadrill and Modest Mega Floette.

  • 31 HP / 3 Def / 32 Spe with Timid: Maximum SPs in Speed let Alolan Ninetales set Aurora Veil as early as possible, disrupt setup threats like Swords Dance Mimikyu with Encore, and outspeed and neutralize Garchomp. Near-maximum HP investment in tandem with snow lets it have a good chance to not get 2HKOed by +1 Mega Gyarados's Earthquake and OHKOed by +2 Garchomp's Earthquake, allowing it to set Aurora Veil or outright eliminate those threats. It also allows Alolan Ninetales to survive a Flash Cannon from Archaludon with Aurora Veil up, letting Alolan Ninetales come back later to set up snow or Aurora Veil.

  • 1 HP / 1 Def / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: A fully offensive SP spread lets Alolan Ninetales's Freeze-Dry have a good chance to OHKO Mega Swampert and guarantee an OHKO on offensive variants of Garchomp, and it also lets Moonblast OHKO offensive variants of Hisuian Samurott.

Fast Attacker.description:
• Hisuian Arcanine is capable of threatening many of the top Pokemon in the format such as Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Mega Charizard Y with its super powerful STAB moves in combination with Rock Head; it's so powerful that it is even able to easily 2HKO Pokemon such as Sneasler that resist its Rock-type STAB move.

  • Head Smash: Head Smash, in conjunction with Rock Head, becomes a devastating no-drawback attack capable of almost always OHKOing Mega Froslass through Aurora Veil in the snow; weaker options like Rock Slide don't come close to this power.

  • Extreme Speed: Extreme Speed allows Hisuian Arcanine to pick off low-HP foes like a Sneasler or Whimsicott that has been brought down to Focus Sash by an ally or by Hisuian Arcanine itself.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash allows Hisuian Arcanine to survive attacks such as Earth Power from Venusaur, retaliating with Flare Blitz.

Other Options

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide allows Hisuian Arcanine to deal spread damage and possibly fish for flinches, though it does come at the cost of Extreme Speed, leaving Hisuian Arcanine unable to beat Sneasler.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Water-type Pokemon like Mega Swampert in the rain and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed Hisuian Arcanine and easily survive its attacks or bring it down to Focus Sash with Flip Turn to leave it vulnerable to any attacks, respectively. Milotic with Coil can set up and heal off Hisuian Arcanine's damage with Recover, while Focus Sash Basculegion-M, thanks to its immunity to Extreme Speed, can use two Aqua Jets to dispatch of Hisuian Arcanine.

  • Ground-type Pokemon: Ground-type Pokemon like Garchomp and Excadrill in the sand can outspeed and bring Hisuian Arcanine down to Focus Sash with Earthquake. Garchomp in particular resists both of Hisuian Arcanine's STAB moves and breaks Hisuian Arcanine's Focus Sash with Rough Skin if it attempts to attack Garchomp.

  • Problematic Mega Pokemon: With the combination of Fake Out and Focus Blast, Mega Raichu Y can KO Hisuian Arcanine without allowing it to make a move. Mega Tyranitar can easily tank Hisuian Arcanine's attacks, dealing lots of damage with Rock Slide while enabling its ally Excadrill. Mega Staraptor outspeeds and 2HKOes Hisuian Arcanine with Close Combat, using Roost to recover the big chunks of damage that Hisuian Arcanine could deal to it.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Sylveon is able to target down Garchomp and Mega Staraptor, and it boasts huge burst damage potential in Hyper Beam to help break through bulky Pokemon like Archaludon, appreciating the help it gets into Steel- and Fire-types from Hisuian Arcanine. Hisuian Arcanine also pairs nicely with Kingambit, taking out Mega Charizard Y and other Fire-types with ease while receiving help into Basculegion-M and Mega Tyranitar. A Basculegion-M can also be of help to Hisuian Arcanine, threatening Mega Swampert under the rain, Mega Tyranitar, and Ground-types with Wave Crash while swapping in on Fighting-type attacks like Close Combat from Sneasler and Mega Staraptor for Hisuian Arcanine.

  • Mega Pokemon: Mega Staraptor does well into Mega Tyranitar and opposing Fighting- and Ground-type Pokemon, using Tailwind to allow Hisuian Arcanine to outspeed and OHKO or deal major damage to Pokemon like Mega Floette with Head Smash. Mega Charizard Y and Ceruledge are dealt with by Hisuian Arcanine, while Mega Staraptor deters Intimidate from Incineroar thanks to Contrary, allowing Hisuian Arcanine to deal as much damage as possible. Mega Raichu Y is another good Mega Pokemon to pair with Hisuian Arcanine, threatening the Water-type Pokemon that scare Hisuian Arcanine with Zap Cannon.

Perish Trapper.description:
• Mega Gengar uses its Shadow Tag ability to stop foes from switching, heavily limiting the opponent's options, and its high Speed and Special Attack allow it to threaten foes like Basculegion-M and Sinistcha. Perish Song allows it to take out foes without damaging them directly, and Shadow Tag stops opponents from removing the Perishing counter by switching.

  • Perish Trap Strategy: Mega Gengar can force opponents to adopt an offensive playstyle to claim KOs before the Perishing counter runs out then punish these plays with Disable. The rest of the team can be built around disrupting foes and supporting Mega Gengar as opposed to dealing damage, though sweepers can be put on the team to force the opponent to cover for them and be used against Perish Song's poor matchups. A team can further commit to this strategy with a second Perish Song setter to keep up momentum, given that Mega Gengar will usually switch out on the last turn of Perish Song. This strategy allows you to neglect foes' defenses.

  • Disable vs. Sludge Bomb: Disable allows Mega Gengar to block detrimental moves, such as Kowtow Cleave from Kingambit and Parting Shot from Incineroar, which would otherwise let it switch out. When paired with a teammate using Encore such as Maushold or Whimsicott, it can completely shut down a foe. Sludge Bomb is an alternative that hits Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon, helping teammates like Kommo-o sweep.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 29 Def / 5 Spe with Timid: The defensive investment allows Mega Gengar to survive 100-Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion-M at -1 almost always, Psychic and Psyshock from Mega Delphox with Friend Guard active, and Earthquake from Excadrill. The Speed investment allows it to always outrun Garchomp and Mega Floette.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: Mega Gengar can be played as a fast offensive Pokemon by forgoing Perish Song. It has good coverage with Shadow Ball and Sludge Bomb, and keeping Disable allows for Disable and Encore combinations, which are still useful even without a Perish Song mode.
