Shadow Ball is much more likely to OHKO Basculegion-M and Sinistcha with maximized Special Attack, and Sludge Bomb will deal such heavy damage to Mega Floette and Sylveon that they will faint soon if they are poisoned. The added Speed makes it easier to disrupt faster foes like Sneasler with Disable. A team built around this set should be comprised mostly of offensive Pokemon like Sneasler to cover for Mega Gengar's weakness to Dark-type Pokemon, as opposed to heavy support.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and opposing Mega Gengar are able to switch out despite Shadow Tag and threaten an OHKO on Mega Gengar with boosted Last Respects and Shadow Ball, respectively. Mega Delphox outspeeds it and threatens an OHKO with Psychic. Opposing Dark-types like Kingambit and Incineroar can threaten an OHKO onto Mega Gengar, and Kingambit cannot be weakened by Intimidate. Moves like Parting Shot from Incineroar and Volt Switch from Rotom-W bypass Shadow Tag, thus preventing Perish Song from getting a KO. Garchomp threatens heavy damage that cannot be redirected with Earthquake, and it pairs well with Flying-types like Mega Charizard Y and Aerodactyl, which have spread attacks of their own that can finish Mega Gengar off. Mega Charizard Y in particular can also threaten an OHKO with Weather Ball, making Mega Charizard Y and Garchomp a deadly combination. Taunt from Pokemon like Whimsicott prevents Mega Gengar from getting Perish Song off or stalling turns with Protect.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Incineroar's Intimidate helps Mega Gengar survive moves that would hit it for heavy damage like Earthquake from Garchomp. Fake Out makes it safer to set up Perish Song, and Throat Chop threatens Ghost-types while stopping opposing Incineroar from switching out with Parting Shot. Incineroar can weaken almost any foe with its own Parting Shot, which can be also used after Mega Gengar switches out to bring Mega Gengar back in and preserve the Shadow Tag trap. Maushold has Friend Guard to help with Mega Gengar's mediocre bulk, and it's a fast Encore user to combine with Mega Gengar's Disable, completely shutting down slow foes like Kingambit and Incineroar. Kommo-o's Soundproof makes it immune to Perish Song allowing it to fight alongside Mega Gengar, and it can threaten Dark-types like Kingambit and Incineroar with heavy damage by using Aura Sphere. Mega Gengar can in turn use Disable on the Fairy-types that threaten Kommo-o or threaten them directly with Sludge Bomb. Politoed is useful as a secondary Perish Song setter, and it can rewrite Mega Charizard Y's Drought with Drizzle. Sinistcha's Hospitality and Life Dew are great healing options that help sustain a Perish Song and Kommo-o mode, and it can protect its partners with Rage Powder.

  • How to Overcome Your Weaknesses: Maushold's Follow Me stops Mega Gengar from being Taunted, and it specifically redirects the aforementioned Ghost-type attacks that would OHKO Mega Gengar into an immune target. Fake Out is pivotal for stopping foes like Kingambit for a turn, while Protect and Parting Shot can stall out turns of Perish Song. Protect is important for baiting out foes' attacks like Kowtow Cleave, Volt Switch, and Parting Shot so that they can be Disabled the next turn or locked into a suboptimal move with Encore, so they cannot select a strong attack or pivot move for future turns.

Focus Sash.description:
• Gengar's useful Speed tier, typing, and movepool give it a small niche as a Focus Sash user, disrupting setup sweepers with Destiny Bond. It can also trade with foes that often revenge kill it, such as Choice Scarf Garchomp and Mega Delphox.

  • Icy Wind: Icy Wind allows Gengar to threaten Dragonite and Garchomp while slowing down foes so it can reliably use Destiny Bond against them. However, Gengar should avoid using Icy Wind against Mega Staraptor, as it gains a Speed boost when hit by the move.

  • Destiny Bond: Destiny Bond lets Gengar force a lose-lose situation in a disadvantageous matchup, usually against setup sweepers trying to end games.

  • Focus Blast: Gengar can opt for Focus Blast to hit Kingambit and Tyranitar, two of the few Pokemon in the tier that resist its STAB combination. However, this comes at the price of unreliability.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt provides Gengar with coverage to hit foes such as Mega Gyarados and Pelipper, with the former usually resisting Shadow Ball.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp can neuter physically offensive foes such as non-Choice Scarf Garchomp, Kingambit, and Mega Staraptor, with the former two posing a threat to Gengar.

All-Out Attacker.description:
• Mega Kangashkan is the ultimate wild card and a frequent second option for Mega Evolution, as it is extremely adaptable when it comes to covering a team's weak spots.

  • Double-Edge versus Body Slam: Double-Edge exerts maximum pressure particularly on bulky checks that don't resist it, but the recoil can be problematic against faster, more offensive teams. Body Slam is much weaker but gives better balance between offense and survivability, and its paralysis chance synergizes excellently with Parental Bond.

  • Fake Out: With STAB and Parental Bond, Fake Out is a strong option for reliable priority and chip damage. Beware though, as it is easily predicted and can invite problematic checks in such as Stamina Archaludon and Flame Body Volcarona.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch is a more flexible priority option for Mega Kangashkan and is particularly threatening to Mega Gengar and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M.

  • Fire Punch: Fire Punch can turn the tables on Mega Scizor, which otherwise resists Mega Kangashkan's strongest moves. It also provides the best damage against Corviknight, though it fails to 2HKO physically defensive builds.

  • Ice Punch: Beyond dealing massive damage to Garchomp and Dragonite, Ice Punch getting two chances to freeze with Parental Bond can let Mega Kangashkan eke its way out of some dicey matchups.

  • Scrappy: Scrappy is the preferred ability prior to Mega Evolution, allowing Mega Kangashkan to get some quick free damage on Ghost-types with Fake Out. If it’s not using Fake Out, Inner Focus is a valid alternative but generally still not worth delaying Mega Evolution for.

Other Options

  • Facade: While highly situational, Facade can circumvent the problematic Flame Body Volcarona, turning a potential burn into a big power increase.

The Original Starwalker (All-out Attacke.description:
• Owing to its excellent Speed tier and immediately high damage output thanks to Huge Power, Mega Starmie is a threatening wallbreaker that is less reliant on setup than other physical Water-type attackers like Mega Gyarados and Mega Swampert. It does, however, have to deal with a low base HP and a weakness to common Choice Scarf users like Meowscarada, Hydreigon, and Basculegion-M, which leave it prone to being worn down and revenge killed.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet helps Mega Starmie pick off faster Pokemon, dealing significant damage to the threatening Mega Raichu Y, Mega Gengar, and Mega Blaziken. Having a priority attack also denies Sucker Punch from slower Pokemon like Kingambit, forcing the opponent to make awkward predictions.

  • Ice Spinner: Ice Spinner provides complementary coverage to Liquidation, super effectively hitting Dragon- and Grass-type Pokemon like Mega Dragonite and Mega Meganium. It will notably always OHKO even the most bulky of Garchomp.

  • Flip Turn: Thanks to Mega Starmie's high Speed, Flip Turn is a consistent pivoting option against Pokemon that defensively check it. Flip Turn additionally lets it deal chip damage while scouting for potential problematic coverage attacks like Thunder Punch from Mega Metagross. Against Pokemon that can run both offensive and defensive sets, Flip Turn can be useful to gauge damage while keeping Mega Starmie safe. For example, Liquidation will almost always OHKO offensive Mega Charizard Y in sun but cannot do the same to variants with HP investment, which can then punish Starmie for staying in by OHKOing it in return with Solar Beam.

  • Zen Headbutt: Zen Headbutt offers Mega Starmie a powerful option to neutrally hit Water-types it would otherwise struggle to damage, like Primarina and Rotom-Wash, and gives it a way to break the otherwise problematic Mega Venusaur and Toxapex. Electing to run Zen Headbutt over Ice Spinner will leave Mega Starmie with no good way to hit Hydreigon, however.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature helps Mega Starmie deal with Pokemon like Jolly Mega Metagross, letting it avoid Metagross's powerful attacks and do some chip damage with Flip Turn before Metagross is weak enough to be knocked out with Liquidation. Jolly additionally enables it to outspeed and potentially OHKO Mega Lucario and Mega Staraptor. An Adamant nature maximizes damage output, giving Ice Spinner an almost guaranteed chance to OHKO Hydreigon on the switch in and a decent chance to OHKO Mega Dragonite through Multiscale, and it still allows Mega Starmie to outpace Garchomp.

Other Options

  • Psycho Cut: Psycho Cut's higher accuracy when compared to Zen Headbutt makes it a bit more reliable, and with an Adamant nature, Mega Starmie retains a significant chance to OHKO specially defensive Mega Venusaur and Toxapex. However, Psycho Cut's lower power makes it difficult for even Adamant Mega Starmie to power through bulky Sitrus Berry variants of Rotom-Wash and Primarina.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Sweeper.description:
• With Intimidate, Gyarados is able to set up, Mega Evolve, and sweep even under the pressure of physically offensive threats!

  • Waterfall: Even after a Dragon Dance, Mega Gyarados has just over a 50% chance to OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Waterfall under the sun!

  • Earthquake: An unboosted Earthquake is a reliable option for knocking out Mega Gengar with no HP investment and Mega Mawile. Earthquake also lets Mega Gyarados deal significant damage to Kingambit, Archaludon, and Mega Dragalage. Mega Gyarados is even capable of surviving Kingambit's STAB moves with two Supreme Overlord boosts! And thanks to Mold Breaker, it can also hit Levitate users such as Rotom-Wash, Rotom-Heat, and Mega Delphox.

  • Ice Fang: Ice Fang is extremely effective on Dragonite and Garchomp. It also covers Grass-types such as Mega Venusaur, Mega Meganium, and Meowscarada, which would otherwise be problematic for Mega Gyarados.

  • Crunch: Crunch can be used over Earthquake for landing a OHKO on Mega Gengar variants with maximum HP investment while covering Pokemon like Aegislash, the Basculegion-M, Mega Starmie, and Dragapult. After a Dragon Dance, Mega Gyarados manages to land a surprising OHKO on Shield forme Aegislash as long as it has no Defense investment! Keep in mind Crunch is a contact move, making Mega Gyarados susceptible to the Attack-lowering effect of King's Shield.

  • Power Whip: This is a situational and high-risk, high-reward option for Mega Gyarados to land an OHKO on opposing Mega Gyarados and Mega Swampert, as well as the bulkiest of Primarina and Rotom-Wash after a Dragon Dance.

  • Taunt: At the cost of dropping a coverage move, Taunt prevents defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon and Toxapex from healing themselves and disrupting Gyarados with Yawn and Haze, respectively. It also renders Corviknight incapable of using Iron Defense and Roost.

  • Mega Evolving Gyarados: It is recommended to wait until the right moment to Mega Evolve. This allows Gyarados to come into specific situations to create win conditions for itself. It's also important to note that non-Mega Gyarados and Mega Gyarados share the same Speed stat but have different typing and abilities; therefore, abstaining from Mega Evolving right away can be quite beneficial depending on the situation in question.

  • Before Mega Evolution: For example, Gyarados can switch in on a Choice-locked Earthquake from Garchomp in order to safely set up with Dragon Dance. It can also prevent Corviknight from using Iron Defense with Taunt while resisting Body Press and setting up additional Dragon Dances for a potential sweep. Finally, Gyarados's typing ensures that it won't be OHKOed by Mega Mawile's Play Rough.

  • After Mega Evolution: Mega Gyarados's Dark typing helps it resist Foul Play from Umbreon, Rotom-Wash, Rotom-Heat, and Archaludon, as well as Sucker Pucnh from targets like Mega Mawile and Kingambit. Mold Breaker also ignores various problematic abilities that can ruin its offensive momentum. Examples include Disguise from Mimikyu, Unaware from Skeledirge, and Levitate from Rotom-Wash and Rotom-Heat, with the last two being huge threats to Gyarados.

Abilities

  • Intimidate: This is the preferred option for cycling and safely setting up on physically offensive threats.

  • Moxie: Revenge killing a weakened and slower Pokemon with Moxie is an alternative for gaining an Attack boost before Mega Evolving.

SP Spreads

  • 1 HP / 32 Atk / 1 Def / 32 Spe with Jolly: This simple spread not only minimizes Stealth Rock damage but also lets Gyarados outspeed base 80 Speed Pokemon such as Mamoswine and non-Mega Dragonite. It also outspeeds Jolly or Timid Choice Scarf Basculegion-M after a Dragon Dance, and Swift Swim Mega Swampert after two uses of Dragon Dance.

Focus Sash Offensive Support.description:
• Aerodactyl leverages both its high Speed to set Tailwind and STAB Rock Slide to either check metagame staples such as Mega Charizard Y or simply steal turns with flinches. A fast Rock Slide in particular sets Aerodactyl apart from other Tailwind users such as Whimsicott and Talonflame, as Rock-type coverage pairs well with other spread move attackers' STAB moves, such as Garchomp with its Earthquake and Mega Charizard Y with its Heat Wave, making Aerodactyl a key component in these offensive cores.

  • Dual Wingbeat versus Wide Guard: Dual Wingbeat covers Fighting-types that resist Rock Slide, most notably Sneasler, as Aerodactyl is one of the few Pokemon that can outspeed and OHKO it. Dual Wingbeat hitting multiple times cuts through any potential Focus Sash from Sneasler and Whimsicott.

  • Wide Guard protects both Aerodactyl and its partners from opposing Aerodactyl and Garchomp using Rock Slide, which Mega Charizard Y in particular appreciates. It also offers defensive counterplay against other strong spread move users, such as blocking Water Spout Mega Blastoise, Blizzard Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales, as well as Hyper Voice Sylveon.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt is a viable option over Dual Wingbeat or even over Protect as a surprise option in a best-of-one setting. Suppressing moves like Trick Room, Follow Me, Rage Powder, and Mega Gengar's Perish Song can stop such strategies without relying on Rock Slide flinches.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash ensures Aerodactyl can set Tailwind regardless of its common weaknesses. In particular, it ensures that Tailwind is set against faster threats such as Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash, Rotom-Heat, and Basculegion, as well as Sand Rush Excadrill and priority attackers such as Mega Scizor with Bullet Punch.

Abilities

  • Unnerve: Unnerve is uniquely positioned in Regulation M-A, as many commonly used items are berries. Stopping Sitrus Berry from being used helps deal with problematic defensive Pokemon such as Incineroar and Sinistcha, with targets like the latter notably being stopped from activating Sitrus Berry midway through Dual Wingbeat. Unnerve also assists partner attackers such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler score in scoring OHKOs despite opposing resist berries such as Occa Berry defensive Whimsicott, Chople Berry Kingambit, and Incineroar's choice of Passho Berry, Chople Berry, or Shuca Berry.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Aerodactyl has many common weaknesses, notably to Water-, Rock-, and Steel-type moves such as Wave Crash, Rock Slide, and Iron Head from Basculegion, Garchomp, and Excadrill. Aerodactyl's Flying typing opens it up to other Rock Slides, especially from Choice Scarf Garchomp and Sand Rush-boosted Excadrill, which outspeed it and resist Aerodactyl's Rock Slide. Excadrill can also use Iron Head to avoid Wide Guard and deal more damage to Aerodactyl. Choice Scarf Basculegion can similarly easily bring it Aerodactyl to Focus Sash before it moves. Non-Choice Scarf Basculegion, while not able to outspeed Aerodactyl, can use Wave Crash or Liquidation to bring it down to Focus Sash, and then attack with Aqua Jet the following turn to finish it off. Priority moves can easily dispatch Aerodactyl after its Focus Sash is broken. Notably, Aerodactyl's typing makes it weak to Bullet Punch from Mega Scizor. Kingambit's unboosted Sucker Punch deals upwards of half Aerodactyl's health, making it similarly effective at finishing off Aerodactyl. Both Kingambit and Aegislash can use Iron Head to easily bring Aerodactyl to Focus Sash before finishing with Sucker Punch and Shadow Sneak, respectively, while resisting Rock Slide and Dual Wingbeat. Wide Guard from Aegislash, Pelipper, and opposing Aerodactyl blocks Rock Slide and is similarly annoying for Aerodactyl's common partners like Heat Wave Mega Charizard Y and Earthquake Garchomp.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y weakens Water-type moves and hits Basculegion super effectively with the sun and Solar Beam, respectively. Garchomp covers Steel-types and other common Rock Slide users such as Tyranitar and Excadrill with Earthquake, which it can freely use next to Aerodactyl. Mega Floette and Sylveon are effective Tailwind recipients with their spread Fairy-type attacks and pair well with Dual Wingbeat Aerodactyl, as it can quickly dispatch Sneasler before it can threaten them with Dire Claw.

  • How to Overcome Aerodactyl's Weaknesses: Aerodactyl's checks can actually answer themselves when used in tandem with Aerodactyl. Garchomp and Basculegion can hit opposing Garchomp and Basculegion super effectively with their STAB Dragon Claw or Scale Shot and Last Respects, and hitting first with these moves is easier with Aerodactyl's Tailwind support. Similarly, Kingambit can check opposing Kingambit with Low Kick and threaten an OHKO with Sucker Punch against the ever-present Basculegion. Tailwind generally has a problem with Trick Room, so being able to KO or Taunt Trick Room setters before they can set up is vital. Mega Charizard Y can easily clear Sinistcha and more cleanly KO Farigiraf after Aerodactyl's Rock Slide damage. Kingambit similarly threatens Trick Room users such as the aforementioned two and Mega Gardevoir, hits first regardless of Trick Room with Sucker Punch, and takes advantage of Trick Room itself with its low base Speed. If Trick Room does go up, Wide Guard Aerodactyl can help stall for turns against some common Trick Room attackers such as Primarina, Mega Gardevoir, and Sylveon, all with Hyper Voice, as well as Eruption Torkoal.

Tailwind Setter.description:
• Mega Aerodactyl is the fastest unboosted Pokemon in the metagame, which makes it an incredibly consistent Tailwind setter while also outspeeding and threatening OHKOs on common Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler.

  • Rock Slide: Mega Aerodactyl is an exceptional user of Rock Slide, since it is able to outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y. Thanks to its incredible Speed, Mega Aerodactyl can consistently threaten flinches with Rock Slide.

  • Dual Wingbeat: Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat is incredibly strong thanks to Tough Claws, making it a solid neutral attack against Pokemon like Basculegion-M. Dual Wingbeat is able to OHKO Sneasler, Venusaur, and Whimsicott through their Focus Sash and deal huge damage to Sinistcha and Mega Venusaur.

  • Mega Evolving Aerodactyl: In its base forme, Aerodactyl can still function well as a fast Tailwind setter, so it can be brought to a battle to support another Mega Evolution. Base forme Aerodactyl can also make use of Unnerve to prevent Sitrus Berry on Pokemon like Incineroar and Farigiraf and Chople Berry on Kingambit from activating.

Other Options

  • Ice Fang: Mega Aerodactyl's Ice Fang is able to OHKO Garchomp but isn't very useful against other Pokemon. This move can be run over Tailwind or Protect, which will either remove Mega Aerodactyl's ability to support its teammates or make it more vulnerable to Fake Out.

  • Wide Guard: Wide Guard can be used over Protect to shield partner Mega Charizard Y from opposing Rock Slide and stop other spread moves like Mega Froslass's Blizzard or Garchomp's Earthquake. Dropping Protect makes Mega Aerodactyl more vulnerable, making positioning with it much harder.

Abilities

  • Tough Claws: Tough Claws boosts Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Ice Fang, allowing the former to OHKO Sneasler and Whimsicott and the latter to OHKO Garchomp.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Aerodactyl is incredibly weak to Steel-types like Kingambit, Archaludon, and Excadrill, which can easily tank any of its attacks and OHKO it back with their Steel-type attacks. Without Ice Fang, Garchomp can be problematic, since it can deal big damage with Rock Slide, and hitting it with Dual Wingbeat will trigger Rough Skin twice. Other Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar and Rotom-Wash can easily tank Mega Aerodactyl's attacks and then threaten big damage back. Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash can be a particularly bad matchup for Mega Aerodactyl, since it can outspeed and threaten heavy damage to Mega Aerodactyl with Thunderbolt or Hydro Pump or slow it down with Electroweb. Mega Aerodactyl is also susceptible to having its damage output reduced by Incineroar's Intimidate and Mega Scovillain's Spicy Spray.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp is an excellent partner for Mega Aerodactyl, since it can freely use Earthquake next to it and threaten the Steel-types that Mega Aerodactyl struggles against. Sylveon is a great beneficiary of Mega Aerodactyl's Tailwind, with it being able to spam powerful Hyper Voices that threaten Garchomp while Mega Aerodactyl deals with common threats to Sylveon such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler. Kingambit is able to deter Pokemon like Incineroar and Farigiraf, which could otherwise slow down Mega Aerodactyl with Intimidate and Trick Room, respectively, while also threatening to deal heavy damage to opposing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar with Low Kick. Mega Charizard Y works as a great alternative Mega Evolution for Mega Aerodactyl, since it melts through Steel-types and works well with Aerodactyl's base forme. Mega Charizard Y can also handle Mega Evolutions that Mega Aerodactyl might struggle against, such as Mega Scovillain and Mega Floette, while Mega Aerodactyl can deal with Mega Dragonite in return. Farigiraf can block Fake Out thanks to Armor Tail, which is very useful for Mega Aerodactyl sets that aren't running Protect. Farigiraf also blocks Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Basculegion-M's Aqua Jet while being able to reverse Trick Room.

  • How to Overcome Mega Aerodactyl's Weaknesses: Pair Mega Aerodactyl with powerful sweepers to make full use of its fast Tailwind. Pokemon like Garchomp and Sylveon can threaten powerful spread damage on the field while also threatening some of Mega Aerodactyl's checks, such as Archaludon and Mega Tyranitar. Use Mega Aerodactyl to threaten Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and Sinistcha, which could otherwise disrupt your offense. Use an alternative Mega Evolution like Mega Charizard Y and Pokemon like Garchomp and Kingambit to deal with matchups where Mega Aerodactyl shouldn't be brought, such as against rain, sand, and Trick Room teams.

Bulky Support.description:
• Snorlax leverages its impressive bulk and ability to shrug off Fire-, Ice-, and Ghost-type damage from metagame staples such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Froslass, and Basculegion-M to provide consistent value to its team over several turns through disruption and chip damage.

  • Abilities: Thick Fat is crucial in allowing Snorlax to comfortably take attacks from common threats in the metagame such as Heat Wave from Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox and Blizzard from Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales.

  • Yawn: Yawn allows Snorlax to put opposing Pokemon into the awkward position of either staying in and letting themselves be put to sleep or switching out and giving Snorlax and its partner a turn to do as they please. In either situation, opponents are forced to essentially pause for a turn while their Pokemon either takes time to wake up or switches out.

  • Fissure versus High Horsepower: Fissure is a high-risk, high-reward move that punishes opponents by threatening to remove key pieces from their side if they can't KO Snorlax quickly or opt to ignore it and focus down its partner; it is sometimes able to secure an otherwise unobtainable victory. High Horsepower offers a much more consistent option that deals good damage to Steel- and Rock-types that otherwise resist its Normal-type STAB moves such as Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Hisuian Arcanine.

  • Double-Edge versus Heavy Slam: Double-Edge is Snorlax's highest damage attack, allowing it to secure KOs against neutral targets that have been worn down by its partners. Heavy Slam deals less damage to neutral targets and is resisted by the Fire-types that Snorlax often finds itself facing such as Mega Charizard Y and Ceruledge, but it threatens Fairy- and Ice-types super effectively while preserving Snorlax's health with the absence of recoil.

Other Options

  • Encore: Snorlax can reasonably forgo a coverage move to opt for Encore, further enhancing its disruptive capabilities. Because of Snorlax's low Speed, it can use Encore to lock its foes into moves on the same turn as they use them. This contrasts with Encore users with Prankster or that are fast such as Whimsicott and Alolan Ninetails that give the opponent the window to switch out or Protect to avoid their Pokemon being locked into a move. Additionally, Snorlax can use Encore as a niche counter to Farigiraf and other Trick Room setters, underspeeding them and forcing them to use Trick Room again to undo the field effect. However, slow Encore users often have to correctly guess the move that their opponent is going to use, risking the chance that the opposing Pokemon gets locked into a move that they are more than happy to keep using.

SP Spreads

  • 21 HP / 32 Def / 13 SpD with Relaxed: This combination of HP and Defense investment allows Snorlax to survive Close Combat from Adamant Sneasler and Jolly Mega Staraptor. The rest of the SPs are put into Special Defense instead of HP to optimize bulk.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Snorlax struggles to stomach powerful physical Fighting-type attacks such as Close Combat from Mega Blaziken and Mega Staraptor and Low Kick from Kingambit and Dragonite. Toxapex also poses an immense problem for Snorlax, threatening to use Toxic and prevent Snorlax from sitting on the field for several turns.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Gengar pairs fantastically with Snorlax, as it is able to trap foes that Snorlax has targeted with Yawn and isolate and eliminate Fighting-type threats that would otherwise give Snorlax a hard time, while Snorlax is immune to the Ghost-type attacks that would hit Mega Gengar for super effective damage. Snorlax also slots nicely into Perish Song teams, disrupting opponents who aim to try and finish the game before the Perish Song counter reaches zero with Yawn and Protect. Perish Song conveniently also punishes less offensive opponents like Toxapex that Snorlax struggles into. Toxapex also pairs well with Snorlax, using Infestation to trap drowsy targets and chip away at them while they're asleep.

  • Sinistcha complements Snorlax, with the former being able to redirect or switch into threatening Fighting-type moves; meanwhile, Snorlax can switch into the Fire-, Ice-, and Ghost-type moves that threaten Sinistcha. Sinistcha also sets Trick Room to take advantage of Snorlax's low Speed and heals Snorlax with Hospitality and Life Dew to help it stay on the field and continue to put foes to sleep and deal chip damage.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Dragonite is a strong anti-metagame pick with respectable offensive coverage into common threats and access to a strong priority move in Extreme Speed. Its well-rounded offensive and defensive profile gives it favorable matchups into metagame staples such as Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit, while its two viable abilities let it adapt to their common teammates, such as Incineroar and Garchomp.

  • Extreme Speed: Extreme Speed is valuable not only to finish off weakened foes; with a Life Orb, it can threaten 2HKOs on opposing Fairy-types such as Mega Floette and Sylveon after an ally has used Fake Out. Extreme Speed's ability to meaningfully threaten these Fairy-types is important because they are immune to Dragon Claw and resist Low Kick.

  • Low Kick versus Fire Punch: Low Kick provides Dragonite a reliable way to threaten metagame staples such as Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Incineroar. Fire Punch, while not being able to OHKO Kingambit, allows Dragonite to hit a wider variety of threats, notably incuding Gholdengo, Whimsicott, and Alolan Ninetales.

  • Inner Focus versus Multiscale: Inner Focus grants Dragonite an immunity to common defensive tools like Intimidate and Fake Out, allowing Dragonite to power through teams that rely on Fake Out from Incineroar and Sneasler to protect an offensive sweeper like Mega Delphox and Mega Blastoise. A bulkier spread with Multiscale allows Dragonite to have a better matchup against faster Dragon-types like Garchomp while also providing a safety net against other threats such as boosted Kingambit.

  • Life Orb versus Dragon Fang: Life Orb is the preferred item on Inner Focus sets as it significantly powers up all of Dragonite's moves, allowing Dragonite to 2HKO Incineroar with Low Kick even after Sitrus Berry recovery and pick up 2HKOs on most neutral targets with the combination of Dragon Claw and Extreme Speed. On Multiscale sets, Dragon Fang is used instead to secure the OHKO on most variants of Garchomp while not incurring the recoil from Life Orb that would break Multiscale.

Other Options

  • Superpower: On Inner Focus sets, Superpower's increased power over Low Kick allows Dragonite to OHKO Incineroar while also putting bulkier Steel-types such as Chople Berry Kingambit and Archaludon in KO range of an ally's attack such as Moonblast from Whimsicott. However, the Defense drop does put Dragonite in range of some moves like 100 Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion.

  • Lum Berry: Multiscale sets running Fire Punch over Low Kick can run Lum Berry to better deal with Sleep Powder from Venusaur and Zap Cannon from Mega Raichu-Y, as well as burns from Sinistcha's Matcha Gotcha and Mega Scovillain's Spicy Spray. Dragonite can then pick them off before they can spread their status further. However, this does leave Dragonite unable to KO bulkier variants of Garchomp with the combination of Dragon Claw and Extreme Speed.

  • Tailwind: Tailwind can be used on a Multiscale set to provide speed control to the team while allowing Dragonite to outpace Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon without allied support. However, this does come at the expense of an important coverage move or Protect.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread allows Dragonite to outrun Adamant non-Choice Scarf Basculegion and Mega Blastoise. Basculegion is immune to Extreme Speed and can threaten huge damage with Last Respects. Outspeeding Mega Blastoise allows Dragonite to weaken its Water Spout with Dragon Claw; even if Mega Blastoise has already used Shell Smash, Dragonite will attack first if it has Tailwind support.

  • 18 HP / 32 Atk / 16 Spe with Adamant: Since Dragonite has access to a strong priority attack in Extreme Speed, maximum Speed investment is not strictly necessary. This spread allows Dragonite to outpace even the fastest Kingambit while also outspeeding Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon under Tailwind. If running Multiscale, the added bulk allows Dragonite to survive Mega Floette's Moonblast and Mega Froslass's Blizzard, giving Dragonite a turn to retaliate.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Due to its typing and Speed tier, Dragonite can often struggle into faster Fairy and Ice-types like Mega Floette, Mega Froslass, and Alolan Ninetales; the latter two are also able to set up Aurora Veil to further dampen Dragonite's damage. However, Dragonite can hit bulkless variants of Mega Floette and Alolan Ninetales with Fire Punch to put them into range of Extreme Speed if holding Life Orb.

  • Without Multiscale, opposing Dragon-types like Hydreigon and Garchomp can easily outspeed and threaten a KO on Dragonite. Garchomp partnered with another faster attacker can break Dragonite even through Multiscale.

  • As Dragonite heavily utilizes Extreme Speed to finish off foes, Farigiraf can stop Dragonite from fulfilling its role as a cleaner due to Armor Tail.

  • As a physical attacker lacking spread moves, Dragonite can struggle to pick off its intended targets if they are protected by Rage Powder from partners like Sinistcha and Mega Scovillain. Due to Spicy Extract, Mega Scovillain completely throws off Dragonite's offensive presence; not only does the resultant burn severely weaken Dragonite's physical attacks, but it also breaks Multiscale, allowing its partner to set up and finish Dragonite off.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Poison-types like Mega Gengar and Sneasler can eliminate faster Fairy-types for Dragonite, while Dragonite complements them defensively with its immunity to Ground. Sneasler in particular can offer Fake Out pressure to allow Dragonite more easily deal with faster threats like Garchomp while also possibly using Coaching to boost Dragonite.

  • Steel-types like Kingambit likewise help Dragonite pressure opposing Fairy-types and excel into opposing Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales, giving Dragonite more freedom to run Low Kick over Fire Punch. Due to its powerful Dark-type STAB moves and low Speed, Kingambit is also a great deterrent for opposing Farigiraf from switching into Dragonite to block Extreme Speed or setting up Trick Room. In return, Dragonite helps eliminate opposing Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, and Sneasler.

  • Dragonite also greatly appreciates Tailwind, which allows it to outspeed other Dragon-types and also lowers its reliance on Extreme Speed to pick up KOs. Whimsicott is a natural partner, as it resists STAB moves from the likes of Garchomp and Hydreigon, allowing it to come in on attacks intended for Dragonite or, if Dragonite uses Protect, its partner Whimsicott also capitalizes on Fairy Aura from opposing Mega Floette and can assist in putting it in the range of Extreme Speed with Moonblast.

Special Attacker.description:
• Mega Dragonite is a strong special attacker with endless coverage and Multiscale, which lets it trade well against offensive teams while being difficult to revenge kill at full health. Its ability to threaten Pokemon such as Corviknight, Garchomp, and Primarina without needing setup gives it immediate value over Dragon Dance variants.

  • Draco Meteor: Draco Meteor is Mega Dragonite's strongest attack, giving it immediate damage against neutral targets and Dragon-types such as Garchomp, Hydreigon, and opposing Mega Dragonite. Its Special Attack drop can make Mega Dragonite easier to take advantage of afterward, so it is best used when picking up a KO or forcing major damage on a key target.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt pressures Water- and Flying-types such as Primarina, Corviknight, Basculegion-M, and Mega Gyarados, preventing them from switching into Mega Dragonite safely.

  • Flamethrower versus Air Slash: Flamethrower is preferred for hitting Steel-types such as Aegislash, Kingambit, and Mega Scizor, which otherwise resist Draco Meteor and can take advantage of Mega Dragonite lacking Fire-type coverage. Air Slash is an alternative that gives Mega Dragonite a Flying-type STAB move to pressure Fighting- and Grass-types such as Mega Lopunny, Sneasler, Meowscarada, and Mega Venusaur.

  • Ice Beam versus Air Slash versus Roost: Ice Beam is preferred alongside Thunderbolt to give Mega Dragonite the coveted BoltBeam coverage, letting Mega Dragonite hit Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon, Garchomp, and opposing Mega Dragonite while also pressuring Mega Meganium. Air Slash can be used here if Mega Dragonite is already running Flamethrower but still wants a Flying-type STAB move. Roost trades coverage for longevity, letting Mega Dragonite preserve or reactivate Multiscale.

  • Modest versus Timid: A Modest nature maximizes Mega Dragonite's damage output while letting it outspeed positive-natured Archaludon, Rotom-Wash, Hisuian Samurott, and Ceruledge. A Timid nature trades power to make it outspeed faster positive-natured threats such as Hydreigon, Mimikyu, and Excadrill while Speed tying with positive-natured Charizard and Mega Kangaskhan.

Other Options

  • Hurricane versus Air Slash: Hurricane can be used over Air Slash for a stronger Flying-type STAB move, but its low accuracy makes it unreliable without rain support from Pelipper.

SP Spreads

  • 31 HP / 1 Def / 32 SpA / 1 Spe: This bulkier spread gives Mega Dragonite more opportunities to take advantage of Multiscale and trade hits with offensive Pokemon. However, the lack of Speed investment leaves it slower than threats the faster spread lets it outspeed, such as positive-natured Mega Gyarados, Mamoswine, Basculegion-M, and Mega Blastoise, so this spread should only be used when the extra bulk is more valuable than speed control.

Dragon Dance.description:
• Dragonite uses Multiscale to find setup opportunities with Dragon Dance, letting it become a threatening late-game sweeper with strong priority in Extreme Speed and the ability to break past common defensive Pokemon such as Toxapex and Aegislash with Earthquake.

  • Scale Shot versus Outrage: Scale Shot is preferred for boosting Dragonite's Speed further after Dragon Dance, making it harder to revenge kill without requiring multiple Dragon Dance boosts. Unlike Outrage, Scale Shot does not make contact, helping Dragonite avoid contact damage from Garchomp's Rough Skin. Outrage is a much stronger Dragon-type attack, but locking Dragonite into it can make it easier for Fairy-types like Primarina, Sylveon, and Mega Floette to punish it.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake gives Dragonite important coverage against Steel-, Fire-, Rock-, and Poison-types such as Aegislash, Kingambit, Mega Charizard X, Mega Tyranitar, and Toxapex.

  • Extreme Speed versus Roost: Extreme Speed gives Dragonite strong priority, letting it pick off weakened faster threats such as Sneasler, Mega Lopunny, and Greninja without relying on Scale Shot boosts. Roost is an alternative that helps Dragonite preserve Multiscale and set up more reliably against defensive Pokemon, but dropping Extreme Speed makes it easier to revenge kill.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: On Lum Berry sets, a Jolly nature lets Dragonite outspeed threats Adamant Dragonite cannot after Dragon Dance, such as Mega Gengar, Mega Delphox, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Greninja. An Adamant nature gives Dragonite more power while still outspeeding threats such as Meowscarada, Sneasler, Garchomp, and Hydreigon after a boost. On Dragoninite sets, Adamant Mega Dragonite already outspeeds the faster unboosted threats Jolly regular Dragonite aims for, while a Jolly nature improves Mega Dragonite's matchup against opposing boosted sweepers such as Adamant Scale Shot Garchomp, Dragon Dance Mega Tyranitar and Mega Charizard X, and Quiver Dance Volcarona.

Other Options

  • Thunder Punch: Thunder Punch lets Dragonite pressure Water- and Flying-types, such as Primarina, Azumarill, Corviknight, and Mega Clefable, but it is difficult to justify over Extreme Speed due to its revenge killing utility.

  • Fire Punch: Fire Punch can be used to hit Steel- and Grass-types such as Corviknight, Mega Scizor, Skarmory, and Mega Meganium more directly, but Earthquake is generally preferred for its stronger coverage.

Items

  • Lum Berry versus Dragoninite: Lum Berry gives Dragonite more freedom to set up through status from Pokemon such as Rotom-Wash, Umbreon, and Hippowdon. Dragoninite trades Dragonite's higher base Attack for Mega Dragonite's improved Speed tier, making it harder to revenge kill after a Dragon Dance.

Bulky Attacker.description:
With high Special Attack, good natural bulk, and a fantastic ability in Mega Sol, Mega Meganium functions as a potent bulky attacker and balance breaker. Mega Sol further boosts Mega Meganium, with strong attacks like Solar Beam and reliable recovery with Synthesis ensuring that it is a consistent check to Water- and Ground-types like Primarina, Rotom-Wash, Mega Swampert, and Hippowdon. Weather Ball threatens Steel-types such as Corviknight, Aegislash, and Kingambit while also doing sizable damage to Galarian Slowking. Dazzling Gleam enables Mega Meganium to threaten Dragon-types that resist Weather Ball and Solar Beam, such as Dragonite and Hydreigon. Earth Power can be used instead to threaten potential switch-ins like Galarian Slowking, Skeledirge, and Mega Dragalge at the expense of no longer doing significant damage to the aforementioned Dragon-types. Mega Meganium should run 13 Speed SPs to outspeed Jolly Kingambit and Adamant Aegislash. 21 HP SPs allow Mega Meganium to survive an Iron Head from Excadrill, a Brave Bird from Corviknight, and a +1 Ice Spinner from Dragonite.

Mega Meganium functions best on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its offensive and defensive capabilities. It is a good teammate to sweepers like Dragon Dance Dragonite and Swords Dance Garchomp due to how it can threaten Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, which often give these Pokemon trouble. Ghost-types like Aegislash and Dragapult also appreciate its ability to switch into Dark-type attacks from Hisuian Samurott, Kingambit, and Hydreigon. Mega Meganium appreciates strong Ground-types, such as Garchomp and Excadrill, to threaten the Poison- and Fire-types that can wall sets lacking Earth Power, such as Galarian Slowking, Mega Dragalge, and Ceruledge. In return, Mega Meganium directly threatens the Water- and Grass-types that can give these Pokemon trouble, like Primarina, Rotom-Wash, and Meowscarada. It also appreciates entry hazard setters such as Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott to apply pressure to its switch-ins like Galarian Slowking and Toxapex. Hisuian Samurott in particular is a fantastic teammate thanks to its great type synergy and its ability to bring Mega Meganium in on physically bulky Pokemon, such as Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, with Flip Turn. Corviknight also makes a good partner, as it can easily switch into Poison-type moves while also switching into Triple Axel from Mega Lopunny and Meowscarada as well as Meteor Mash from Mega Metagross, which typically force Mega Meganium out. In return, Mega Meganium can reliably switch into attacks from Mega Raichu Y and Rotom-Wash. Bulky Water-types such as Primarina, Toxapex, and Rotom-Wash that can switch into the Fire-types that threaten Mega Meganium, like Blaziken, Ceruledge, and Volcarona, are also great teammates. Mega Meganium is also valued on rain teams that appreciate its unique defensive profile and ability to patch up rain's weaker matchups against Kingambit, Swords Dance Hisuian Samurott, and Hippowdon.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Mega Meganium is able to leverage its high bulk and Special Attack to deal large amounts of damage while healing off incoming attacks with Synthesis bolstered by Mega Sol. It particularly is adept at threatening common defensive cores featuring the likes of Corviknight, Primarina, and Hippowdon.

  • Solar Beam: Mega Sol allows Mega Meganium to viably run Solar Beam, which fires off in a single turn to deal massive damage, notably OHKOes Primarina and Hippowdon, and ignores the latter's Sand Stream.

  • Weather Ball: Weather Ball is similarly enabled by Mega Sol, making it a potent coverage option that notably threatens Steel-types like Corviknight and Aegislash.

  • Dazzling Gleam: While it isn't the most powerful move, Dazzling Gleam gives Mega Meganium a crucial second STAB option that can threaten common Dragon-types that can otherwise take its Fire- and Grass-type moves such as Garchomp and Hydreigon, with the latter getting OHKOed.

Other Options

  • Earth Power: Earth Power can be used as an extra coverage option for Fire-types such as Ceruledge, which resist all of Mega Meganium's other attacks, as well as hitting Archaludon for super effective damage.

Rain Support.description:
• For rain teams, Politoed is a bulky support Pokemon that enables Archaludon while also threatening with Perish Song late-game. Politoed's Drizzle allows it to do well against Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y, Incineroar, and Mega Delphox by weakening their attacks and allowing Politoed to pressure them with Weather Ball. Meanwhile, Perish Song pressures foes late-game, as they have limited opportunities to switch.

  • Weather Ball: Weather Ball gives Politoed a reliable single-target attack in rain, letting it pressure Fire-types such as Incineroar, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Delphox without relying entirely on its partner for damage. On teams with Mega Froslass, Weather Ball allows Politoed to pressure Garchomp if rain has been replaced with snow.

  • Perish Song: Perish Song forces opponents to reposition their Pokemon or risk losing both of them. Mega Gengar can trap targets so that they cannot escape Perish Song normally. Protect helps Politoed stall turns and avoid being removed before the Perishing count finishes.

  • Hypnosis versus Ice Beam versus Encore: Hypnosis can temporarily remove a key threat from play and give Politoed's partner room to attack or set up, though its poor accuracy makes it unreliable. Ice Beam gives Politoed consistent coverage against Garchomp, Dragonite, and Sinistcha regardless of the active weather. Encore punishes passive moves like Protect, Trick Room, and setup moves, which is especially useful when the opponent attempts to stall out rain.

Other Options

  • Muddy Water: Muddy Water can be used over Weather Ball for spread damage and accuracy drops, which can be useful when Politoed wants to support its partner while still attacking. However, Muddy Water's lower power makes Politoed worse at immediately pressuring Fire-types like Incineroar and Mega Charizard Y.

  • Helping Hand: Helping Hand compensates for Politoed's limited offensive presence by boosting a partner's attack. It notably amplifies Archaludon's wallbreaking power, allowing +1 Flash Cannon to OHKO bulky Mega Floette and Sylveon and Electro Shot to OHKO bulky Rotom-Wash.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry, in combination with the given defensive spread, gives Politoed the longevity to use Perish Song and stall its turns with Protect while remaining healthy enough to switch out and reset rain later. It notably prevents Adamant Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Timid Mega Floette's Moonblast from 2HKOing Politoed.

  • Mystic Water: Mystic Water should be used with an offensive spread, as it further strengthens Politoed's rain-boosted Weather Ball. This gives Politoed much greater immediate offensive pressure at the cost of Sitrus Berry's longevity.

SP Spreads

  • 31 HP / 23 Def / 12 SpD with Calm: 31 HP SPs let Sitrus Berry activate immediately after Politoed gets hit by Maushold's Super Fang. 12 Special Defense SPs let Politoed survive Modest Mega Floette's Light of Ruin from full health. The remaining SPs are invested in Defense, giving Politoed a solid chance to survive Adamant Basculegion-M's 150-Base Power Last Respects while improving its ability to take physical attacks from Garchomp and Sneasler.

  • 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpA with Modest: This spread maximizes Politoed's Special Attack while maintaining bulk. It should be used with Mystic Water to strengthen Politoed's rain-boosted Weather Ball enough to guarantee OHKOs on offensive Sneasler and specially bulky Incineroar. The Special Attack investment also allows Ice Beam to always OHKO offensive Garchomp.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Politoed struggles against strong Electric- and Grass-type attacks from Pokemon such as Archaludon and Sinistcha, both of which take little damage from Weather Ball. Opposing weather setters like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Torkoal can also remove rain, stopping your own Archaludon from using Electro Shot. Without Ice Beam, Politoed also struggles to threaten Dragon-types such as Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite, which can deal heavy damage to it with Draco Meteor and Dragon Pulse, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Archaludon is the main rain sweeper, using Politoed's rain to fire off Electro Shot immediately and threaten Water- and Flying-types such as Basculegion-M, Milotic, and Aerodactyl. Espathra is a great partner on Baton Pass rain teams, passing Speed and Calm Mind boosts to Archaludon so that it can snowball much more easily once Politoed sets rain. Mega Gengar is the main partner on Perish Song archetypes; it traps foes so that they cannot freely switch out. Incineroar and Sneasler provide Fake Out support to help Politoed use Perish Song or land Hypnosis. Sinistcha gives Politoed teams redirection and Hospitality recovery, while Mega Froslass can set Aurora Veil and reset rain later with Rain Dance.

  • How to Overcome Politoed's Weaknesses: Politoed should be preserved carefully in weather wars against Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, and Mega Froslass, as maintaining weather control makes these foes far easier for Politoed to deal with. Mega Dragonite can handle Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler threatens Mega Tyranitar with Close Combat, and Kingambit deals with Mega Froslass. Additionally, your own Mega Froslass can use Rain Dance to restore rain without forcing Politoed back onto the field. Against Electric- and Grass-types, Politoed should avoid sitting on the field and instead use Protect, Encore, or Hypnosis, or it should switch out to better position itself later on. Archaludon resists both Electric- and Grass-type attacks and can switch into moves such as Electro Shot from opposing Archaludon and Matcha Gotcha from Sinistcha, accumulating Stamina boots to make itself progressively more difficult to remove with physical attacks, while Incineroar resists Grass-type attacks and threatens Sinistcha. Perish Song should usually be saved for late-game scenarios or situations where the opponent has limited switching options, such as times when Mega Gengar is trapping a target. Sneasler’s Fake Out and Politoed’s Protect can also safely stall turns of the Perishing count.

That's Amore! (Defensive Wish Passer).description:
• Owing to its high natural bulk, especially in a format without Assault Vest, Umbreon is able to carve out a role on bulky offense and stall teams as a Wish passer capable of taking on threats such as Dragapult, Hydreigon, and Mega Gengar.

  • Foul Play: Umbreon's most reliable attack, Foul Play heavily punishes physical setup sweepers that attempt to take advantage of its passivity. Because of Umbreon's low offensive stats, Foul Play typically does more damage against even special attackers than other options like Dark Pulse and Crunch.

  • Yawn: Yawn forces the opponent to either switch out their Pokemon, which gives Umbreon a free turn to benefit from Wish and Leftovers and can create an opening for one of Umbreon's teammates to come in, or let it stay in and stomach the sleep.

  • Wish + Protect: The combination of Wish and Protect gives Umbreon a consistent way to heal, letting it not only not have to worry about damage on the turn it uses Protect but also buy itself a turn for Leftovers recovery. The knowledge that Umbreon has Protect can also be used to bait your opponent into setting up on a turn they believe Umbreon will be inactive, allowing it to disrupt their Pokemon with Yawn.

  • Inner Focus versus Synchronize: While Synchronize is able to punish status spreaders like Rotom-Wash and defensive Dragapult, it comes with the detriment of potentially preventing Umbreon and its teammates from inflicting their own statuses. Inner Focus avoids this issue and allows Umbreon to consistently cycle Wish without having to worry about disruption from flinches.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt allows Umbreon to take on stall Pokemon such as Toxapex by removing their access to status and recovery moves. With 3 Stat Points invested in Speed, physically defensive Umbreon sets can outpace and duel with uninvested Corviknight, which can be a problem Pokemon for defensive teams, by denying it usage of Iron Defense and Roost.

  • Toxic: Giving up the utility of Yawn for the deadlier option in Toxic can allow Umbreon to wear down Pokemon it would otherwise struggle with, especially when Toxic is combined with Protect. Passive teammates that can't use Toxic themselves also appreciate the damage Umbreon provides.

  • Baton Pass: Though Umbreon is not typically passing stat boosts, Baton Pass can still be useful as a slow pivoting option to bring in a weakened teammate that needs to be healed with Wish. It also gives Umbreon a way to escape from Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag if need be.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is Umbreon's most generally useful item, providing it with passive healing and reducing its reliance on Wish to stay healthy.

  • Mental Herb: Mental Herb is an alternative defensive item that prevents Taunt users from denying Umbreon the use of Wish, which can be crucial late-game. Mental Herb also allows Umbreon a little more consistency against Encore users it is otherwise unthreatened by like Skeledirge.

  • Chople Berry: Chople Berry improves Umbreon's matchups against a few Pokemon that run Fighting-type coverage, such as Focus Blast Mega Gengar and Close Combat Aegislash. It can, in return, 2HKO and OHKO these Pokemon with Foul Play, respectively.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpD with Bold vs. 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpD with Calm: Umbreon can succeed with investment in either of its defenses, which depends on the needs of its team. Physical sets do better against the likes of Kingambit and Dragon Darts Dragapult, while special sets do better against Pokemon like Mega Gengar and Hydreigon.

Defensive Pivot.description:
With great special bulk, solid typing, and the ability Regenerator, Galarian Slowking excels as one of the tier's best defensive pivots, able to repeatedly check a large number of special attackers, such as Primarina, Rotom-Wash, Mega Floette, and Mega Meganium, and punish them with a Sludge Bomb. Chilly Reception combined with its low Speed allows Galarian Slowking to pivot out and safely bring in a teammate. Future Sight, in combination with Chilly Reception, allows Galarian Slowking to apply delayed pressure to targets like Toxapex, Clefable, and Hippowdon, which teammates like Mega Lopunny and Sneasler can take advantage of. Psyshock can be used instead to immediately threaten Fighting- and Poison-types such as Sneasler, Glimmora, and Mega Dragalge while also doing the most damage to opposing Galarian Slowking. Thunder Wave can cripple threats like Volcarona, Hydreigon, and Mega Delphox for teammates that can take advantage of their lowered Speed. The combination of Ice Beam and Shuca Berry allows Galarian Slowking to withstand super effective Earthquakes from Garchomp and Dragonite and retaliate, often OHKOing offensive variants of the former, as well as KOing the latter with its Multiscale broken. Flamethrower can be used instead to do the most damage to Corviknight, Kingambit, and Aegislash, which can easily switch into Galarian Slowking’s other options. Toxic can put potential setup sweepers like Primarina, Skeledirge, Volcarona, and Mega Floette on a timer. Slack Off is another option that gives Galarian Slowking immediate recovery and helps it match up better against Quiver Dance Volcarona and Calm Mind Mega Floette. Colbur Berry lets Galarian Slowking stay in on its would-be checks, such as Meowscarada, Hydreigon, and Hisuian Samurott, and punish them with a Thunder Wave. Colbur Berry also lets Galarian Slowking survive a +2 Throat Chop from Sneasler and OHKO it with Psyshock. Sitrus Berry can be used as well for one-time recovery, helping Galarian Slowking remain healthy when it needs to stay in rather than pivot out. Kasib Berry is a more niche option that allows Galarian Slowking to stay in on threats like Dragapult, Ceruledge, and Annihilape and punish them with a Thunder Wave or Toxic.

Because of its defensive utility, Galarian Slowking can find its way on nearly any balance or bulky offense team. Offensive Fighting-types like Mega Lopunny, Blaziken, and Quaquaval can pressure the Dark- and Steel-types that commonly switch into Galarian Slowking while also appreciating its ability to bring them in safely with Chilly Reception and hit their would-be switch-ins like Toxapex, Mega Dragalge, and Clefable with Future Sight. They also appreciate Galarian Slowking's ability to absorb Toxic Spikes, which can otherwise hinder their longevity. Sweepers like Swords Dance Garchomp and Sneasler, as well as Nasty Plot Mega Delphox and Mega Raichu Y, also appreciate Galarian Slowking's ability to bring them in safely and allow them to get off a crucial boost. Galarian Slowking greatly appreciates partners like Garchomp, Hippowdon, Rotom-Wash, and Corviknight that can switch in on common physical attackers that threaten Galarian Slowking out, such as Excadrill, Hisuian Samurott, and Mega Metagross. Corviknight, in particular, can also clear entry hazards with Defog, allowing Galarian Slowking to switch in more frequently, while forming a great pivot core with U-turn. In return, Galarian Slowking checks Rotom-Wash, Mega Meganium, and Primarina for Corviknight. Dark-types like Kingambit, Hydreigon, and Hisuian Samurott are also valuable teammates, as they can easily switch in on Dark- and Ghost-type attacks from Meowscarada, Aegislash, and Dragapult, while Galarian Slowking can switch in on Fighting-type attacks. Slower attackers like Hisuian Samurott, Mega Meganium, and Aegislash also appreciate Galarian Slowking's ability to spread paralysis onto faster threats like Mega Metagross, Mega Lopunny, and Dragapult.

Bulky Swords Dance.description:
Mega Scizor uses its great defensive typing, high Attack, solid bulk, and powerful STAB Technician-boosted Bullet Punch to serve as an effective wallbreaker and cleaner, revenge killing weakened, fast, frail threats such as Dragapult, Mega Lopunny, and Sneasler. It can also find opportunities to set up Swords Dance against foes like non-Iron Defense Corviknight while checking wallbreakers like Mega Floette and Mega Metagross due to its bulk. Roost gives it much more longevity and more chances to set up. Close Combat tears down Steel-resistant Pokemon such as Archaludon, Excadrill, and most importantly Kingambit. Knock Off is an alternative to let Mega Scizor hit Aegislash, which is otherwise a huge roadblock, as well as Mega Delphox and Ceruledge on the switch in, which can shrug off its STAB Bullet Punch or Close Combat. 18 Speed SPs let Mega Scizor outpace Adamant Aegislash and Jolly Kingambit, while the HP SPs ensure that it doesn't get 2HKOed by Mega Floette's Moonblast and Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge.

Bulky offense and balance teams best appreciate Mega Scizor's ability to provide strong priority against foes like Sneasler. It also brings high defensive value, which allows it to answer dangerous wallbreakers like Mega Floette, Mega Mawile, and Mega Metagross. Mega Scizor's 4x weakness to Fire-type attacks from the likes of Ceruledge, Mega Delphox, Skeledirge, and Volcarona means that it appreciates teammates that can help against these particular foes. Water-types such as Hisuian Samurott, Rotom-Wash, and Primarina stand out, with Hisuian Samurott setting up Spikes and pressuring Ceruledge and Mega Delphox with Ceaseless Edge while using Flip Turn to bring Mega Scizor in safely against Fairy-types like Clefable and Mega Floette. Other entry hazard setters such as Garchomp and Glimmora make useful partners, with Stealth Rock chipping down the Fire-types that try to switch in on Mega Scizor and helping it guarantee the 2HKO on Dragapult. Dark-types such as Hydreigon and Meowscarada appreciate Mega Scizor's ability to dent Fairy-type foes with its STAB Bullet Punch. In return, Hydreigon can switch in on the Fire-type moves from the likes of Ceruledge and Mega Delphox while outpacing and pressuring the former with STAB Dark Pulse; Meowscarada helps against Water-types like Hisuian Samurott and Rotom-Wash. Special attackers like Volcarona, Hydreigon, and Primarina breaking down physically bulky Pokemon like Hippowdon and Rotom-Wash is appreciated by Mega Scizor, which, in return, can revenge kill faster threats to those special attackers like Garchomp and Sneasler.

Swords Dance.description:
• Scizor serves as an excellent revenge killer within the tier thanks to its powerful STAB priority Bullet Punch, enabling it to clean up against weakened foes and Fairy-types such as Mega Lopunny, Mega Gengar, and Sylveon.

  • Scizorite versus Lum Berry: Scizor is versatile enough that it can forgo its Mega Stone to allow for a different Mega Evolution on the team, while Scizor uses Lum Berry to switch into Yawn from Sylveon and Hippowdon safely and set up a free Swords Dance. However, Mega Scizor is a significant improvement over Scizor, as it can always OHKO Archaludon with Close Combat after a Swords Dance.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat can allow for Scizor to majorly threaten Corviknight after a Swords Dance and potentially OHKO Archaludon.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off lets Scizor handle Aegislash and deals with Mega Delphox as it tries to switch in.

  • U-turn: U-turn allows Scizor to do respectable damage as it pivots out of foes that can handle it, such as Umbreon.

  • Roost: Roost enables Scizor to recover as it sets up against threats unable to reliably threaten it, such as Mega Venusaur, Meowscarada, and Sylveon.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can be used on non-Scizorite sets, granting Scizor recovery when not running Roost.

Sand Attacker.description:
• Mega Tyranitar bolsters a team against opposing weather strategies while boasting good matchups against common Fire-types like Mega Delphox and Incineroar as well as Trick Room staples like Farigiraf and Torkoal.

  • Low Kick versus Dragon Dance: Low Kick threatens Kingambit and opposing Mega Tyranitar. Low Kick Mega Tyranitar is a good Kingambit check, as it outspeeds Kingambit, resists Sucker Punch, and has great physical bulk. Dropping Low Kick for Dragon Dance turns Mega Tyranitar into a game-ending threat when given support in the form of redirection from Sinistcha and damage mitigation from Rotom-Wash and Incineroar. Dragon Dance also enables Mega Tyranitar to go for Rock Slide flinches against a greater number of Pokemon. However, the rest of the team must have a better matchup against Kingambit without Tyranitar's Low Kick.

  • Mega Evolving Tyranitar: Tyranitar should look to Mega Evolve when it knows that it can win the weather war. If it leads against a Froslass holding Froslassite or Charizard holding Charizardite Y, then it should try to Mega Evolve either on the same turn as them or a turn after them. This ensures that sand will be up and these Pokemon cannot benefit from the weather they set. The state of the weather when leading against Pelipper is a bit tricky; fast Tyranitar sets will always concede the early weather advantage, and slow, bulky Pelipper sets will always seize weather control. Tyranitar can Mega Evolve to re-establish weather should rain win out after the lead.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 13 Atk / 4 Def / 17 Spe with Adamant: 17 Speed SPs allow Mega Tyranitar to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M under Tailwind. The physical bulk ensures that Mega Tyranitar always survives Jolly Adaptability Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. This bulky spread is best used with Low Kick.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Maximizing Speed and power lets Mega Tyranitar make the most of the boosts granted by Dragon Dance.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fighting-types like Sneasler and Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon directly threaten Mega Tyranitar; it struggles to effectively hit these Pokemon, especially Sneasler. Mega Tyranitar is also not particularly fast, so many attackers get the chance to attack it before it can respond. This includes threats like Garchomp, which is also unthreatened by Mega Tyranitar's attacks, even surviving Knock Off from Mega Tyranitar at +1 Attack. While Mega Tyranitar is excellent at disrupting rain, Pokemon on rain teams like Archaludon and Basculegion-M threaten it with their STAB attacks. Finally, Chople Berry variants of Kingambit can turn the tables on Mega Tyranitar by surviving Low Kick and OHKOing it in return with Iron Head.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Tyranitar benefits from having Ghost- and Steel-types that can check the Fighting- and Fairy-types it is afraid of. One of its best partners is Sinistcha, which can redirect away Fighting- and Water-type attacks and set Trick Room to let Mega Tyranitar outspeed Pokemon it otherwise could not, such as Archaludon. Corviknight is strong against Fairy- and Fighting-types, packs Speed control in the form of Tailwind, and resists Garchomp's STAB moves. Pokemon like Rotom-Wash, Hydreigon, and the aforementioned Sinistcha that threaten common Pokemon on rain teams ensure that Mega Tyranitar does not entirely rely on winning the weather war. Similarly, Pokemon that can back up Mega Tyranitar in the fight against Mega Charizard Y's sun, like Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Incineroar, ensure that it isn't alone in attempting to hold off dangerous sun threats. Mega Tyranitar's sand also enables Sand Rush Excadrill, a fast cleaner that beats Mega Tyranitar checks like Sneasler and Mega Floette.

  • How to Overcome Mega Tyranitar's Weaknesses: Mega Tyranitar has a middling Speed tier, meaning that it is slower than many Pokemon. Speed control in the form of Sinistcha's Trick Room or Corviknight's Tailwind lets Mega Tyranitar threaten a greater number of Pokemon. Sinistcha's redirection also allows Mega Tyranitar to bypass otherwise super effective attacks. Steel-types like Corviknight and Excadrill threaten Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon that threaten Mega Tyranitar.

Special Wall.description:
• Tyranitar uses Sand Stream, excellent special bulk, and Stealth Rock to function as a special wall that can check attackers such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Gengar, and Mega Delphox while making progress with item removal and chip damage.

  • Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock helps punish common switch-ins and breaks Focus Sash, which is especially valuable against offensive Pokemon such as Sneasler, Meowscarada, and Ceruledge. It also pressures Pokemon weak to Rock, such as Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona.

  • Knock Off versus Foul Play: Knock Off gives Tyranitar a consistent way to make progress by removing items from switch-ins such as Corviknight, Hippowdon, and Rotom-Wash. Foul Play is an alternative that punishes physical attackers and setup sweepers such as Dragonite, Mega Charizard X, and Garchomp without requiring much Attack investment.

  • Rock Blast versus Rock Tomb: Rock Blast gives Tyranitar a multi-hit Rock-type attack that can break Substitute and pressure Dragonite through Multiscale while still threatening targets such as Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona. Rock Tomb is a weaker alternative, but its Speed drop can punish switch-ins and allow Tyranitar or its teammates to more easily outspeed foes.

  • Earthquake versus Ice Punch: Earthquake gives Tyranitar coverage for grounded Steel- and Rock-types such as Kingambit, Archaludon, and opposing Tyranitar, especially when catching them on the switch. Ice Punch instead targets Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon and Garchomp, which can otherwise take advantage of Tyranitar.

  • Rest: Rest can be used over coverage to give Tyranitar more longevity. However, dropping Earthquake leaves Tyranitar unable to reliably pressure Kingambit and Archaludon, while dropping Ice Punch makes Garchomp and Hippowdon much safer switch-ins.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry gives Tyranitar general recovery, helping it stay healthy enough to set Stealth Rock and continue checking special attackers throughout a game.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry should be used with Rest, letting Tyranitar fully heal once without being forced to stay asleep afterward.

  • Shuca Berry: Shuca Berry fits best on Ice Punch sets, letting Tyranitar survive physical Ground-type attacks from Pokemon such as Garchomp and punish them in return.

Setup Sweeper.description:
• Mega Tyranitar uses its excellent bulk, Sand Stream-boosted Special Defense, and Dragon Dance to turn forced switches and favorable trades into setup opportunities. This lets it set up or trade against special attackers it threatens, such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Delphox, Mega Gengar, Volcarona, and even would-be checks like Primarina, which can be forced to respect a boosted Stone Edge.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off is Mega Tyranitar's most consistent Dark-type STAB move, letting it heavily pressure Pokemon such as Aegislash, Mega Gengar, and Mega Delphox while removing items from defensive switch-ins like Corviknight, Hippowdon, and Primarina.

  • Stone Edge: Stone Edge gives Mega Tyranitar a strong Rock-type STAB move to OHKO Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Volcarona, Pelipper, Gyarados, and Dragonite with prior sand chip damage.

  • Ice Punch versus Fire Punch: Ice Punch is preferred for hitting Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon and Garchomp, which can otherwise stomach Mega Tyranitar's STAB attacks. Fire Punch is an alternative for pressuring Steel-types such as Corviknight, Mega Scizor, and Kingambit more directly, though it leaves Mega Tyranitar worse off against common Ground-types.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature gives Mega Tyranitar better Speed after Dragon Dance, letting it outspeed threats such as Mega Gengar, Meowscarada, and Sneasler after a boost. An Adamant nature gives Mega Tyranitar more immediate power while still letting it outspeed threats such as Garchomp, Mega Floette, and Gengar after a Dragon Dance.

Other SP Spread

  • 26 HP / 16 Atk / 1 SpD / 23 Spe with Adamant or Jolly: This bulkier spread lets Mega Tyranitar survive Meowscarada's Flower Trick, Corviknight's Body Press, and Garchomp's Earthquake, giving it more setup opportunities against these threats. Mega Tyranitar's Speed is kept high enough to outspeed uninvested Mega Venusaur and Mega Meganium before boosting. After a Dragon Dance, Adamant Mega Tyranitar still outspeeds positive-natured Garchomp, Mega Floette, and base 100s such as Mega Charizard X, Mega Charizard Y, and Volcarona. A Jolly nature can be used instead to outspeed Gengar and Mega Lucario after a Dragon Dance, though the lower Attack investment and nature make Mega Tyranitar noticeably weaker.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Mega Tyranitar uses its excellent bulk, Sand Stream, and immediate power to pressure bulkier teams without needing Dragon Dance; it uses Knock Off and coverage to punish defensive Pokemon such as Corviknight, Skarmory, Hippowdon, and Mega Meganium.

  • Rock Blast versus Stone Edge: Rock Blast trades raw power for better accuracy and multi-hit utility, letting Mega Tyranitar break Substitute and Focus Sash while pressuring Dragonite through Multiscale. Stone Edge maximizes Mega Tyranitar's immediate Rock-type damage, making it better for punishing neutral targets and bulky switch-ins.

  • Ice Punch versus Fire Punch: Ice Punch hits Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon, Garchomp, and Hydreigon. Fire Punch is an alternative that pressures Steel-types such as Corviknight, Mega Scizor, Skarmory, and Kingambit more directly.

  • Superpower: Superpower lets Mega Tyranitar hit Dark- and Steel-types such as Umbreon, Kingambit, opposing Tyranitar, and Archaludon.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt can be used to stop defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon, Hippowdon, Skeledirge, and Corviknight from using Yawn, Will-O-Wisp, recovery, and phazing moves. Taunt pairs especially well with Superpower against Umbreon, since Superpower is Mega Tyranitar's strongest move against it but can be stalled out by Wish and Protect. However, fitting Taunt usually means dropping Ice Punch, Fire Punch, or a STAB move, making Mega Tyranitar easier for Ground-types, Steel-types, and Fairy-types to handle, respectively.

Other SP Spread

  • 32 HP / 20 Atk / 14 SpD with Adamant: This spread keeps Mega Tyranitar bulky while still letting it hit hard, as the extra Special Defense investment lets it almost always survive Timid Mega Gengar's Focus Blast at full HP while sand is active. The drop in Attack is noticeable compared to maximum Attack variants, but the improved Mega Gengar matchup can justify the trade-off.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Mega Blaziken's high Speed and Attack give it a good matchup against metagame staples like Incineroar, Kingambit, and Gholdengo. With Speed Boost, it can essentially guarantee it is the fastest Pokemon on the field after enough turns have passed, outspeeding Mega Aerodactyl and slower Pokemon like Sylveon even if they have a boost from Tailwind.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide OHKOes Mega Charizard Y. Combined with Speed Boost, Rock Slide lets Mega Blaziken threaten flinches before foes can move.

  • Detect: Detect is mandatory to safely gain Speed boosts.

Other Options

  • Swords Dance: Swords Dance can be used to offset Intimidate from Incineroar and make Mega Blaziken strong enough to OHKO Garchomp with Close Combat at +1 Attack. It can replace Rock Slide on teams that have another way to cover Mega Charizard Y, such as Mega Aerodactyl.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: Speed Boost allows Adamant Mega Blaziken to outspeed Mega Aerodactyl after one turn.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Opting for a Jolly nature allows Mega Blaziken to always outspeed Sylveon under Tailwind after one turn.

Teambuilding

  • Rain Matchup: Mega Swampert threatens to OHKO Mega Blaziken with either STAB attack, and Swift Swim lets it outspeed Mega Blaziken in the rain even after a turn of Speed Boost. Basculegion-M and Pelipper resist both of Mega Blaziken's STAB attacks and respond with an OHKO from Wave Crash and Hurricane or Weather Ball, respectively; Pelipper also weakens Flare Blitz while enabling Mega Swampert with Drizzle.

  • Other Weaknesses: Garchomp threatens an OHKO with Earthquake, which cannot be redirected by Sinistcha's Rage Powder. Mega Aerodactyl threatens an OHKO with Dual Wingbeat and can use Tailwind before Mega Blaziken gets its Speed Boost to deny Mega Blaziken's Speed advantage. Whimsicott has Tailwind to negate Mega Blaziken's Speed advantage and Encore to punish it for using Detect to gain Speed Boosts. Opposing Trick Room uses Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost against it, and Farigiraf threatens to OHKO it with Psychic. Mega Staraptor enters the field with Intimidate, threatens an OHKO with Brave Bird, and is often paired with Whimsicott to negate Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost with Tailwind. Mega Delphox threatens an OHKO with Psychic or Psyshock. Ceruledge completely walls both of Mega Blaziken's STAB attacks.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M has a better matchup against rain teams and Mega Aerodactyl, while Mega Blaziken helps it against Archaludon. Weather setters like Alolan Ninetales and Torkoal overwrite rain; Alolan Ninetales handles Garchomp with Blizzard; and Torkoal is useful in Trick Room while providing sun to let Flare Blitz OHKO bulky variants of Sylveon and offensive variants of Farigiraf. Sinistcha can nearly OHKO Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha and use Rage Powder to redirect threatening attacks like Pelipper's Weather Ball and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. It can also redirect neutral attacks that threaten Mega Blaziken due to its low bulk, like Sneasler's Dire Claw and Close Combat. Sinistcha helps offset Flare Blitz recoil with Hospitality and can also reverse Trick Room. Mega Blaziken, in turn, handles Kingambit, which threatens Sinistcha.

  • Kingambit threatens to OHKO Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch and is comfortable against Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Delphox, and Ceruledge, as it can survive their attacks and either OHKO them in return or deal enough damage to finish them off with Sucker Punch. Due to Defiant, Kingambit's presence can also deter Incineroar from switching in and activating Intimidate against Mega Blaziken. In return, Mega Blaziken handles Mega Charizard Y for Kingambit with Rock Slide. Sylveon is a strong answer to Garchomp, and Mega Blaziken, in turn, handles Steel-types that threaten Sylveon, such as Gholdengo and Mega Metagross.

  • Alternative Mega Evolutions: Mega Aerodactyl can take the place of Mega Blaziken against teams with nuisances like Garchomp, Mega Delphox, Ceruledge, and opposing Mega Aerodactyl. Mega Blaziken complements Mega Aerodactyl by beating its counters: Mega Tyranitar, Mega Metagross, and Mega Mawile. Mega Froslass has a better matchup against rain teams by setting snow over rain, and it is also strong against Garchomp and the combination of Mega Staraptor and Whimsicott. Mega Blaziken also plays well against Mega Froslass's counters: Mega Charizard Y, Kingambit, and Incineroar.

Fast Offense.description:
• Mega Swampert gives rain teams a clear choice of Mega Evolution, using its newly granted access to Wave Crash to hit incredibly hard. It is able to OHKO most Pokemon in Regulation M-B that do not resist Wave Crash in rain, albeit at the cost of a large portion of its own HP. It boasts a strong matchup against Regulation M-B staples such as Incineroar, Mega Metagross, and Sneasler.

  • Swift Swim: Swift Swim allows Mega Swampert to outrun every unboosted Pokemon in the tier when rain is active. This means it outspeeds the likes of Garchomp and Mega Raichu Y, two Pokemon that would otherwise greatly burden its partners. Mega Swampert can OHKO them before Garchomp threatens partner Archaludon with Earthquake or Mega Raichu Y threatens Archaludon and Pelipper with Focus Blast and Zap Cannon, respectively.

  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch allows Mega Swampert to threaten the Grass-types that OHKO it, such as Sinistcha, as well as Garchomp, which would otherwise deal a large amount of damage to Mega Swampert through the combination of Wave Crash recoil and Rough Skin contact damage. Notably, it is able to OHKO Whimsicott after Fake Out breaks its Focus Sash, preventing it from setting Tailwind and allowing Mega Swampert to maintain its Speed advantage in rain. It also allows Mega Swampert to hit the occasional Mega Dragonite for heavy damage.

  • Ground-type moves: While some Mega Swampert opt to run only Earthquake, others run High Horsepower to hit Steel-types such as Kingambit without threatening their partner.
