  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb, similar to Rock Slide, provides coverage against Mega Charizard Y but avoids Wide Guard from the likes of Aerodactyl. It also provides a form of Speed control but is really only useful against Mega Charizard Y because of its inability to fish for flinches or damage both foes.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry grants Garchomp far more longevity by allowing it to avoid 2HKOs from attacks such as Close Combat from Sneasler.

  • Roseli Berry: Roseli Berry allows Garchomp to take on the format's Fairy-types when used in combination with Poison Jab in one-on-one scenarios.

Abilities

  • Rough Skin: Rough Skin punishes attacks like Close Combat and Liquidation from Sneasler and Basculegion-M, respectively, breaking their Focus Sashes. It also punishes Fake Out from Incineroar; at low HP, Incineroar often cannot afford to use Fake Out on Garchomp without KOing itself.

SP Spreads

  • 19 HP / 26 Atk / 21 Spe with Jolly: The Attack investment allows Garchomp to OHKO uninvested Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide, while the Speed investment lets it outrun maximum Speed Hisuian Arcanine. The bulk allows Garchomp to almost always survive Last Respects from Basculegion-M after two of its allies have fainted and always survive Knock Off from Jolly Mega Tyranitar after a Dragon Dance.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Even with Roseli Berry, Garchomp can struggle against Fairy-types, as Poison Jab doesn't OHKO them, leaving Garchomp vulnerable to being OHKOed by Mega Floette's Light of Ruin and Sylveon's Hyper Beam. Garchomp also struggles to damage Mega Froslass, which can OHKO it with Blizzard. Opposing Dragon-types like Mega Dragonite, Archaludon, and Hydreigon can be issues for Garchomp, as they can survive Dragon Claw or Earthquake and retaliate with Draco Meteor. Without an offensive item like Soft Sand, Garchomp may also struggle to deal damage to the likes of Incineroar and Mega Scovillain, especially after being affected by Intimidate or a burn, respectively.

Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is a great partner for Garchomp, resisting the Fairy-type attacks that threaten Garchomp, OHKOing Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales, and, when the two are next to each other, allowing Garchomp to use Earthquake freely. Fairy-type partners like Whimsicott and Mega Floette can threaten opposing Dragon-types, while partners like Mega and base Glimmora and as well as Sneasler can threaten opposing Fairy-types.

  • How to Overcome Garchomp's Weaknesses: Keeping Garchomp in the back and removing threats to it early on are good ideas, as its amazing coverage lets it easily clean up a lot of the format's common Pokemon. Having switch-ins to Fairy-types is also a must, as they pose a huge threat to Garchomp even with Roseli Berry. Garchomp also appreciates allies that can stay on the field alongside it while it continuously deals damage with Earthquake, such as Mega Aerodactyl, which can provide Tailwind, use Rock Slide to hit opposing Flying-types, and use Dual Wingbeat to weaken and threaten Sinistcha, a Pokemon Garchomp can struggle to hit.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Garchomp is able to leverage its high offensive stats, good typing, and coverage to become a versatile threat fit for many teams; thanks to its Choice Scarf, it can outspeed and deal heavy damage to otherwise faster Pokemon like Mega Gengar and Sneasler.

  • Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum: Earthquake gives Garchomp a strong spread damage option, while Stomping Tantrum offers single-target Ground-type damage when trying to avoid Wide Guard or when positioned next to a Pokemon that is not immune to Earthquake. Knowing when to pick either one is vital, as locking into Earthquake when Garchomp's partner cannot safely take it can lose the game; alternatively, locking into Stomping Tantrum against redirection from the likes of Sinistcha and Vivillon can render Garchomp nearly useless.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide allows Garchomp to OHKO or deal heavy damage to Mega Charizard Y. Thanks to Choice Scarf, Garchomp can fish for flinches against fast Pokemon like Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Delphox, a role Garchomp without Choice Scarf is incapable of fulfilling.

Other Options

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb is an alternative to Rock Slide, offering speed control and still offering a way to hit Mega Charizard Y hard. It loses the ability to cause flinches and deal spread damage, however.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Garchomp to outrun faster foes such as Mega Froslass and Aerodactyl, allowing it to revenge kill the aforementioned foes before they threaten it with Blizzard or set up Tailwind, respectively.

Abilities

  • Rough Skin: Rough Skin punishes Fake Out from foes like Incineroar and Sneasler, providing chip damage and, in Sneasler's case, potentially breaking its Focus Sash.

SP Spreads

  • 29 Atk / 15 SpD / 22 Spe with Adamant: The SPs invested in Special Defense allow Garchomp to survive Dazzling Gleam from Timid Mega Floette, while the Speed investment lets Garchomp outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M when holding a Choice Scarf of its own. The remaining SPs are invested in Attack.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread opts for more Speed and power, ensuring that Garchomp at least Speed ties other Choice Scarf Garchomp, outspeeds Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash and Mega Aerodactyl, and deals as much damage as possible.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fairy-types like Mega Floette, Sylveon, Mega Gardevoir, and Whimsicott all threaten Garchomp with OHKOs or 2HKOs from their Fairy-type STAB attacks while also boasting an immunity to Dragon Claw, easily taking advantage of Garchomp's inability to switch moves. Whimsicott in particular also resists Garchomp's Ground-type STAB attacks and can use Tailwind to allow partners like Mega Floette to outspeed and OHKO Garchomp with Moonblast. Mega Froslass is able to easily OHKO Garchomp with Blizzard, while Fake Out from Sneasler and Incineroar can take advantage of Garchomp's inability to use Protect, leaving it vulnerable to attacks such as Draco Meteor from Hydreigon and Archaludon. Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite can easily take advantage when Garchomp locks into a Ground-type move, threatening it with Draco Meteor and Dragon Pulse, respectively, while Archaludon and opposing Garchomp are able to switch in on Rock Slide and threaten Garchomp with Draco Meteor and Dragon Claw, respectively. Rotom-Wash can also easily take attacks from Garchomp while threatening to burn it with Will-O-Wisp, and Mega Scovillain is able to redirect Garchomp's attacks, burning it in the process. Sinistcha and Farigiraf can set up Trick Room right in front of Garchomp, turning the Speed boost from Choice Scarf into a hindrance. Corviknight resists or, in the case of Ground-type attacks, is immune to all of Garchomp's STAB options, can shrug off Rock Slide, and can either set up Tailwind or use Bulk Up in the face of Garchomp, setting up an ally for success or turning itself into a win condition, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is able to sit next to Garchomp while it freely uses Earthquake and make Blizzard from Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales inaccurate by setting sun. Additionally, it is able to resist Fairy-type attacks and fire back with Weather Ball and Heat Wave while threatening to OHKO Mega Froslass and Sinistcha with the same moves. Incineroar also threatens Mega Froslass and Sinistcha and can safely switch into their attacks while using Fake Out against foes like Hydreigon to keep Garchomp safe for another turn or Parting Shot to safely bring in Garchomp. In return, Garchomp is able to threaten Rock-types like Mega Tyranitar and Lycanroc-D and deal with opposing non-Choice Scarf Garchomp. Mega Froslass, Sinistcha, and Farigiraf are all threatened by Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave; Fairy-types fear Iron Head; and Hydreigon and Archaludon take solid damage from Low Kick. Kingambit appreciates Garchomp's positive matchup against Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler. Mega Floette is able to threaten the Dragon-types Garchomp fears with heavy damage, as well as easily take out Rotom-Wash and take attacks from Mega Froslass before retaliating with Moonblast or Light of Ruin. Mega Aerodactyl deals heavy damage to Sinistcha with Dual Wingbeat, deterring it from attempting to redirect Garchomp's attacks; Mega Aerodactyl is also capable of using Ice Fang to OHKO opposing Garchomp.

  • How to Overcome Garchomp's Weaknesses: Bringing Choice Scarf Garchomp alongside offensive threats that complement it well, such as Mega Charizard Y, is a must to ensure it isn't easily stopped by Pokemon that resist or are immune to whatever move it has decided to lock into. When teambuilding, placing Garchomp on a team with Fairy-, Dragon-, and Ice-type damage is preferred, though not necessary thanks to Garchomp's flexibility, as it often functions as glue for teams. Mega Charizard Y threatens the Fairy- and Ice-type Pokemon that scare away Garchomp and, more importantly, appreciates Garchomp's ability to threaten opposing Mega Charizard Y and Dragon-types with Rock Slide and Dragon Claw, respectively. Mega Floette and Sylveon appreciate Garchomp's Ground-type attacks threatening Kingambit and Sneasler and, in return, provide coverage against problematic Dragon-types like Mega Dragonite. Kingambit and Mega Aerodactyl perform similar roles against Ice-types and other foes that trouble Garchomp, appreciating the wide array of coverage Garchomp has at its disposal to dispatch nearly any Pokemon. Kingambit has the added benefit of deterring Trick Room from Sinistcha and Farigiraf thanks to its naturally low Speed and can hit them hard with Kowtow Cleave.

Mixed Life Orb.description:
Garchomp can invest into its Special Attack to become a highly threatening mixed attacker, capable of breaking most defensive cores while also finding many opportunities to switch in thanks to its great defensive typing and natural bulk. Draco Meteor functions as a great neutral option, 2HKOing foes like Rotom-Wash, Glimmora, and Mega Staraptor while also OHKOing Meowscarada and Hisuian Samurott after entry hazard chip damage. Flamethrower allows Garchomp to 2HKO Corviknight and Skarmory, which are unphased by Garchomp's other options. Due to the fact that Garchomp greatly threatens common hazard removal options like Corviknight, Excadrill, and Glimmora, it is great at setting Stealth Rock and making sure the hazard stays up for its teammates to take advantage of the passive chip damage. If the team has a different Stealth Rock setter, like Glimmora or Excadrill, Poison Jab can be run instead to threaten Fairy-types like Mega Meganium and Mega Clefable, which can otherwise withstand Garchomp's attacks. A Life Orb allows Garchomp to reach important benchmarks like 2HKOing Corviknight with Flamethrower and OHKOing Mega Meganium with Poison Jab.

Mixed Garchomp is one of the most defining Pokemon on offensive teams and can easily find its place on nearly any team thanks to its ability to break defensive cores while also keeping entry hazards up. It greatly appreciates Water- and Grass-type attackers, like Primarina, Rotom-Wash, Mega Meganium, and Meowscarada, that can apply pressure to mixed defensive Hippowdon, which can survive two Draco Meteors and recover off the damage. Hisuian Samurott is also a great partner, as its Spikes allow Garchomp to reach important benchmarks like KOing opposing Hisuian Samurott with Draco Meteor, OHKOing Mega Dragalge and offensive Kingambit with Earthquake, and 2HKOing Hatterene with Earthquake. In return, Hisuian Samurott appreciates Garchomp's ability to pressure Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, which can otherwise give it trouble. Garchomp also appreciates support from Healing Wish users like Hatterene, as it can get worn down quickly from hazards and constant Life Orb recoil. Galarian Slowking, Rotom-Wash, and Corviknight are great teammates, as they can bring Garchomp in safely with their pivoting moves, reducing the amount of damage it would otherwise take from switching in while also allowing it to fall back on them after a Draco Meteor Special Attack drop. Galarian Slowking can also switch in on Fairy-types that commonly force Garchomp out, like Primarina, Clefable, and Mega Floette. Additionally, Corviknight can switch into threats like Mega Lopunny, Meowscarada, and Dragapult that can attempt to revenge kill Garchomp. Many sweepers like Swords Dance Scizor, Sneasler, and Mega Mawile, as well as Bulk Up Annihilape, appreciate its ability to pressure the aforementioned Corviknight and Rotom-Wash.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Garchomp is blessed with a Speed tier that allows it to outrun common sweepers such as Volcarona and Mega Charizard X after a Speed boost, as well as other fast attackers such as Mega Raichu Y and Mega Delphox, and swiftly KOes them with its powerful STAB moves and coverage. It also lets it avoid having to Speed tie with Mega Floette. Outrage is an incredibly powerful STAB option that can clean up games once Pokemon that resist or are immune to it have been dealt with. Stone Edge targets common Ground-immune foes such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Delphox, and Mega Clefable. It also OHKOes Volcarona, a threat that Earthquake does not OHKO. Rock Tomb is a much more accurate option that still OHKOes offensive Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y. Its Speed drop can also leave setup sweepers such as Dragonite and Mega Froslass easier for teammates to revenge kill. However, Rock Tomb cannot OHKO Mega Delphox, even after Stealth Rock, and cannot 2HKO Mega Clefable. Poison Jab is the strongest option available to hit Fairy-types, most notably OHKOing Mega Meganium, which would otherwise counter Garchomp, after Stealth Rock damage. It also does slightly more damage to Fairy-types than an unresisted Earthquake, which can be relevant when looking to KO foes such as Mega Floette and Clefable. Stealth Rock may let Garchomp act as a secondary setter if its team already handles Mega Meganium effectively, though locking into it gives up momentum.

Choice Scarf Garchomp can easily find its place on offense and balance teams looking for solid Speed control to deal with the likes of Volcarona, Mega Charizard X, and Mega Raichu Y. It also boasts a solid defensive typing that lets it switch into various attacks it resists or is immune to. Corviknight is Garchomp's main obstacle when trying to make progress, so teammates most apt at pressuring it and making progress against it, such as Black Glasses Hisuian Samurott, Rotom-Wash, and Shadow Ball Aegislash, are of utmost importance. Defensive teammates Garchomp can fall back on after being locked into a move, such as Corviknight, Galarian Slowking, and Rotom-Wash, are highly valuable. They also have the added benefit of having pivoting moves to bring Garchomp back in safely. In return, Garchomp handles their answers, such as Mega Raichu Y, Excadrill, and Mega Dragalge, respectively. Galarian Slowking in particular is one of the rare switch-ins to Mega Meganium, and is, for this reason, one of Choice Scarf Garchomp's best teammates. Stealth Rock setters such as Glimmora, Clefable, and Tinkaton are a great fit to fix various key interactions, such as breaking Dragonite's and Mega Dragonite's Multiscale, breaking Focus Sash from Ceruledge, and putting Mega Meganium in range of Poison Jab, so Garchomp can reliably KO them. Garchomp appreciates particularly strong physical wallbreakers such as Blaziken, Mega Mawile, and Mega Metagross overpowering physical walls such as Corviknight, Hippowdon, and Clefable, so that Garchomp may clean up late-game. In return, Garchomp can switch into Fire-type attacks targeting the latter two. Offensive Poison- and Steel-type teammates such as Mega Glimmora, Mega Metagross, and Mega Mawile are able to proactively switch into Fairy-types such as Mega Floette and Clefable and immediately pressure them, though they must be careful of Mega Meganium's coverage options.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Offensive Stealth Rock.description:
• Garchomp's excellent Speed tier and power make it one of the premier offensive choices for setting up Stealth Rock.

  • Outrage: Despite this set usually being used early-game to set up Stealth Rock, Outrage still gives Garchomp good cleaning potential and makes it a decent revenge killer if Focus Sash is still intact.

  • Rock Tomb versus Poison Jab: Rock Tomb is a perfect fit for the early-game playstyle of this set, ensuring foes like Mega Gyarados and Dragonite won't be able to set up Dragon Dance freely after Garchomp's Focus Sash is broken, in addition to being a great response to both Mega Charizard formes.

  • Focus Sash: Despite Garchomp's above average bulk, its sheer prominence means enough Pokemon are aiming to OHKO it, which makes Focus Sash worth using for the more reliable Stealth Rock setup.

Other Options

  • Poison Jab: If Mega Meganium is a serious issue for your team, Poison Jab can potentially flip that matchup.

  • Dragon Tail: While usually better sorted towards more defensive Garchomp sets, Dragon Tail still has merit due to preventing bulky Steel-types like Iron Defense Corviknight and Swords Dance Mega Scizor from setting up.

Swords Dance.description:
• Garchomp's good bulk and coverage place it near the top of the food chain of Swords Dance sweepers!

  • Scale Shot: Scale Shot's reliability issues and reduction of Garchomp's bulk may make it seem like a strange choice for a sweeper, but the Speed boost makes Garchomp so much harder to revenge kill that it's worth it overall.

  • Poison Jab versus Fire Fang: Poison Jab punctures through Mega Meganium, which otherwise can wall and revenge kill Garchomp fairly easily, as well as dealing with the rare Mega Clefable. Fire Fang, however weak it may be, is Garchomp's best shot of chewing through a weakened Corviknight, which otherwise is a strong Garchomp check.

Other Options

  • Outrage: Outrage makes Garchomp very vulnerable to being revenge killed, but its perfect accuracy and sheer power make it worth considering. Outrage pairs especially well with Lum Berry to cure confusion and block Yawn from Hippowdon, which is almost always 2HKOed by boosted Outrage even when it chomps down on a Sitrus Berry!

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash severely punishes teams that are unable to set up Stealth Rock, in addition to enhancing Garchomp's revenge killing capabilities. The vulnerability to entry hazards does sometimes conflict with this set's preference for late-game sweeping, though.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry is an excellent response to common status users like Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash, leaving even less defensive answers for Garchomp.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb gives Garchomp a tremendous power boost, now being able to OHKO offensive Mega Metagross without a boost! This comes at the cost of the recoil making Garchomp more vulnerable to priority attacks.

  • Haban Berry: Choice Scarf Dragon-types such as opposing Garchomp and Hydreigon are common enough where Haban Berry can be useful to put less pressure on boosting Speed with Scale Shot.

  • Roseli Berry: Roseli Berry can be a deadly surprise for Fairy-types like Mimikyu and bulky Primarina that are expecting to revenge kill Garchomp.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Garchomp's impressive power, Speed, and bulk make it arguably among the apex Choice Scarf revenge killers of Pokemon Champions Singles!

  • Outrage: While locking Garchomp into a Rampaging state makes it easy prey for Fairy-types like Primarina and Mimikyu, the power Outrage offers turns Garchomp into a ferocious late-game cleaner and an effective revenge killer of most Dragon-type foes.

  • Poison Jab: Poison Jab is Garchomp's preferred Fairy-type deterrent, OHKOing offensive Mega Meganium after Stealth Rock and usually 2HKOing the rare Mega Clefable as well.

  • Rock Tomb versus Dragon Claw: Rock Tomb not only OHKOes Mega Charizard Y but also ensures that fast setup sweepers that may come in after the KO such as Dragon Dance Dragonite and opposing Swords Dance Garchomp will be easier to revenge kill thanks to the Speed drop. Dragon Claw, on the other hand, is Garchomp's most reliable Dragon-type STAB move, perfect for revenge killing weakened Dragon-types without fearing the wrath of Fairy-types getting a free KO.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: Opposing Choice Scarf Garchomp are common enough that Jolly is the safer nature to use; Jolly also lets Garchomp outspeed Jolly Mega Dragonite. However, Adamant's power boost does make Garchomp a better late-game cleaner, granting it a good chance of OHKOing Mega Delphox with Outrage for example.

Other Options

  • Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock may seem nonsensical on a revenge killer, but it does give Garchomp some early-game utility if fitting in a more dedicated Stealth Rock setter is difficult for your team, at the cost of some revenge killing prowess. It also can be used to fool your opponent into thinking this set doesn't have Choice Scarf.

  • Rock Slide: While it offers less utility than Rock Tomb, Rock Slide's flinch chance has the potential to flip a bad matchup.

  • Iron Head: Poison Jab is usually preferred due to OHKOing Mega Meganium, but Iron Head's flinch chance could flip matchups against Fairy-types Garchomp can't OHKO, such as Mega Clefable, Mega Floette, and Sylveon. Additionally, Iron Head KOes Mimikyu after Disguise is broken without Stealth Rock support.

Chonky Chomp (Phazer).description:
• Garchomp uses its fantastic bulk to inflict double trouble, placing entry hazards and using Dragon Tail to disrupt and rack up damage on opposing teams.

  • Spikes: Combining Spikes with Stealth Rock can make it much harder for defensive staples like Hippowdon to stay healthy throughout a match.

  • Rock Slide: Even without Attack investment, Rock Slide is still strong enough to OHKO offensive Mega Charizard Y.

  • SP Spread: The given SP spread has enough physical bulk to avoid the OHKO from opposing Jolly Garchomp's Outrage as well as Mega Kangaskhan's Ice Punch if using Sitrus Berry. The special bulk investment allows Garchomp to dodge the OHKO from Modest Primarina's Moonblast and Mega Gengar's Icy Wind. The leftover SPs are put into Speed.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst recovery helps Garchomp stay healthy and continue to be a nuisance. Particularly after big attacks like Primarina's Moonblast, Garchomp can heal out of range of a follow-up Aqua Jet.

  • Haban Berry: Haban Berry is the most reliable method of letting Garchomp tank Draco Meteor from the likes of Archaludon and Hydreigon.

Swords Dance.description:
• Mega Lucario is a nearly unwallable breaker, threatening physical walls like Hippowdon after a Swords Dance and minimal chip. Mega Lucario also has access to priority moves that prevent faster threats like Mega Raichu Y from revenge killing it and an above-average Speed tier that lets it outpace Mega Metagross and Garchomp, making it a great late-game cleaner. However, Mega Lucario struggles to find openings to set up without taking too much damage, cannot deal with certain Ghost- and Water-types like Aegislash and Toxapex, and falls short of OHKOing physically defensive Mega Venusaur and Hippowdon. Alolan Ninetales can provide Mega Lucario with Aurora Veil, while pivots like Rotom-Wash and Choice Scarf Meowscarada can help it find more opportunities to set up. Alternative Mega Evolutions that deal with Aegislash, like Mega Gyarados and Mega Delphox, also pair well with Mega Lucario, as do teammates that provide entry hazard support like Hippowdon and Garchomp.

  • Swords Dance: Swords Dance gives Mega Lucario the power it needs to pummel bulky walls like Corviknight and Rotom-Wash.

  • Meteor Mash versus Earthquake: Meteor Mash breaks through Fairy-types like Primarina and Mega Meganium. It also gives Mega Lucario a chance to gain an additional Attack boost, which would let it outright OHKO physically defensive Mega Venusaur with Meteor Mash at +3. Alternatively, Earthquake allows Mega Lucario to power through Ceruledge and Aegislash.

  • Extreme Speed versus Bullet Punch: At +2, Extreme Speed OHKOes offensive Mega Raichu Y and picks off faster Pokemon that resist Steel, like Mega Greninja and Mega Blaziken. However, Bullet Punch can be considered to threaten Mega Gengar and Mimikyu.

  • Mega Evolving Lucario: Lucario should usually Mega Evolve as soon as possible unless it expects Gyarados or Staraptor to come in and neutralize its Swords Dance boost, as Inner Focus prevents Intimidate from affecting it. With Intimidate blocked, Lucario can Mega Evolve the next turn and OHKO them with Close Combat and Meteor Mash, respectively.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Maximum Attack and Speed investment with a Jolly nature lets Mega Lucario outspeed and deal with Mega Metagross, Mega Staraptor, and Alolan Ninetales.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: An Adamant nature gives Mega Lucario a better chance to OHKO Hippowdon and Mega Venusaur at +2 after Stealth Rock damage. It also makes Mega Lucario's priority moves more threatening, allowing it to OHKO offensive checks like Choice Scarf Hydreigon, Mega Delphox, and Mega Gengar at +2 after minimal chip. However, Mega Lucario will be slower than Mega Metagross, Garchomp, and Mega Charizard Y.

Special Sweeper.description:
• Nasty Plot Mega Lucario is a deadly setup sweeper that can be hard to prepare for, ripping down weakened teams with its STAB moves, high Special Attack, Adaptability, and good offensive and defensive typing. With these traits, it can become very difficult to stop once checks such as Skeledirge and Toxapex have been removed.

  • Nasty Plot: Nasty Plot gives Mega Lucario more power, ensuring that it can OHKO bulky Pokemon like Rotom-Wash.

  • Aura Sphere: This is Mega Lucario's primary STAB move, ensuring that it gets a small chance to OHKO specially defensive Corviknight with +2 Aura Sphere after Stealth Rock damage.

  • Flash Cannon: Flash Cannon serves as Mega Lucario's main way of hitting Fairy-type foes like Mimikyu and Mega Floette for super effective damage. With this, it can also guarantee an OHKO on the latter after Stealth Rock damage.

  • Vacuum Wave: Vacuum Wave is useful for picking off weakened metagame threats such as Hydreigon and Mega Lopunny. It also has a high chance to OHKO Meowscarada after Stealth Rock chip damage.

Other Options

  • Steel Beam: Mega Lucario can opt for Steel Beam to deal bigger damage to Fighting-resistant or -immune foes like Mimikyu. However, the move's extreme recoil results in Flash Cannon being the overall better STAB move.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse can catch Aegislash, Gholdengo, and Mega Starmie off-guard, as these three resist both of Mega Lucario's STAB moves. However, Dark Pulse has poor coverage aside from that, and its STAB moves are generally better against most of the metagame.

Mixed Wall.description:
Hippowdon is a sturdy wall that differentiates itself from other common Ground-types thanks to its access to reliable recovery in Slack Off and its ability to stave off some of the scariest wallbreakers in the tier that otherwise have great matchups against slower teams. Such threats include Mega Glimmora and Mega Metagross, as well as Mega Charizard Y and Archaludon thanks to Sand Stream removing opposing weather. Whirlwind forces Stealth Rock damage onto the opposing team and phazes dangerous sweepers such as Mega Staraptor and Dragonite. The SP investment allows Hippowdon to tank two unboosted Draco Meteors or one +1 Draco Meteor from Archaludon, two Flamethrowers from Mega Charizard Y, two Draco Meteors from mixed Life Orb Garchomp, and two unboosted Meteor Mashes or Ice Punches from Mega Metagross. Leftovers and Sitrus Berry guarantee Hippowdon can reliably achieve these feats, even after Stealth Rock chip damage. Holding no item is an option if both Leftovers and Sitrus Berry are already taken by teammates, as doing so ensures that Hippowdon can reliably switch into Poltergeist users such as Ceruledge and Aegislash.

This set's ability to handle key wallbreakers makes it a good fit on bulkier teams ranging from balance to stall. Since Hippowdon invites opposing Defog Corviknight in frequently, teammates able to make the most out of that matchup, such as Shadow Ball Aegislash, Ceruledge, and Mega Meganium, are important to have. Poison-type walls such as Galarian Slowking, Mega Dragalge, and Poison Jab Toxapex take pressure off of Hippowdon and are excellent answers to Mega Meganium, as well as Mega Clefable, which completely stops Hippowdon from making progress. They can also set Toxic Spikes, which makes Whirlwind much more irritating. In the same vein, Spikes setters such as Hisuian Samurott and Meowscarada are good teammates, increasing the chip damage Whirlwind can accumulate. Corviknight is a key partner, acting as a secondary physical wall and using Defog to remove the Spikes and Toxic Spikes that would otherwise cut into Hippowdon's longevity and prevent it from switching into key wallbreakers. Rotom-Wash brings momentum with Volt Switch, is able to switch into Mega Swampert, and makes progress against Corviknight. Blaziken, Ceruledge, and Mega Mawile are incredible wallbreakers that can easily dismantle defensive teams and have a chance to OHKO Hippowdon after a Swords Dance. As such, if running Hippowdon on a stall team, Skeledirge, Unaware Clefable, and Ditto are invaluable teammates to deal with them.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Stealth Rock.description:
• With impressive bulk, a great defensive typing, and a useful ability that wears foes down, Hippowdon is the premier setter of Stealth Rock!

  • Yawn: Yawn is the secret ingredient to Hippowdon's success, punishing sweepers that lack Lum Berry such as Iron Defense Mega Metagross and working well with Stealth Rock to rack up even more residual damage with switches.

  • Slack Off versus Whirlwind: Slack Off would normally be a given on such a defensive Pokemon, but Hippowdon can justify going without it to cause even more Stealth Rock damage with Whirlwind. Whirlwind also punishes Pokemon that may run Lum Berry to set up on Hippowdon, such as Garchomp and Kingambit.

Other Options

  • Rock Tomb: Not only does Rock Tomb provide utility in Speed reduction against common Ground-type switch-ins like Gyarados, but it also ensures that Hippowdon isn't totally walled by Flying-types.

  • Protect: Protect pairs well with Yawn and Leftovers, potentially letting Hippowdon incapacitate switch-ins that can otherwise threaten to seriously harm it such as Meowscarada and Hydreigon while also providing a small serving of free recovery.

  • Fissure: When your back is up against a wall, Fissure could potentially flip matchups by OHKOing switch-ins Hippowdon has no business beating, such as Mega Meganium. However, its low reliability makes it hard to fit in compared to Whirlwind.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's quick burst of recovery usually fits Hippowdon the best, giving it a chance to let loose a Yawn more easily. It also helps specially defensive variants deal with White Herb Archaludon.

  • Leftovers: If Sitrus Berry is held by another teammate, Leftovers's slower recovery still benefits Hippowdon, especially variants that run Slack Off.

  • Mental Herb: If both Sitrus Berry and Leftovers are needed on other teammates, Mental Herb can be justified for letting Hippowdon set up Stealth Rock even when hit by Taunt. It can be particularly helpful in preventing Taunt Mega Gyarados from easily setting up.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpD with Impish: Maximizing Hippowdon's tanky Defense stat gives it the best chance of stopping powerful physical sweepers like Garchomp late-game with Yawn or Whirlwind.

  • 32 HP / 5 Def / 29 SpD with Careful: This specially defensive spread lets Hippowdon survive Primarina's Mystic Water-boosted Sparking Aria.

  • 32 HP / 10 Def / 24 SpD with Careful: This spread should be paired with Sitrus Berry, as it allows Hippowdon to avoid a 2HKO from White Herb Archaludon's Draco Meteor while also surviving Garchomp's +2 Outrage after Stealth Rock damage.

  • 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpD with Careful: Maximizing Hippowdon's Special Defense gives it a good shot of avoiding an OHKO from Modest Mega Charizard Y's Overheat in the sun.

Sash Attacker.description:
• Mamoswine is a very threatening attacker due to its high Attack, immunity to Intimidate, and STAB combination that allows it to threaten many common Pokemon including Incineroar, Sinistcha, Garchomp, and Mega Aerodactyl.

  • Ice Shard: Ice Shard is a very powerful priority option against Garchomp. It isn't able to OHKO Garchomp, but it can put Garchomp in range of its own Life Orb recoil. Ice Shard is also able to threaten 2HKOs on common Pokemon that are hard to outspeed such as Whimsicott, Mega Aerodactyl, Venusaur, and Choice Scarf Hydreigon.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash lets Mamoswine tank the many strong super effective attacks in the format that would OHKO it such as Sneasler's Close Combat and Mega Raichu Y's Focus Blast and retaliate with High Horsepower.

Other Options

  • Earthquake: Earthquake can be used over High Horsepower as an alternative Ground-type attack that can deal consistent spread damage and get around redirection. Earthquake should always be used alongside partners with Protect or Ground-immune partners such as Mega Charizard Y and Hydreigon so Mamoswine doesn't hit its partner.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide can be used over Icicle Crash, sacrificing strong Ice-type damage for the ability to deal big damage to Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox. Without Rock Slide, Mamoswine has no way of dealing meaningful damage to Mega Delphox.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb can be used over Focus Sash, increasing Mamoswine's damage at the cost of its survivability. Life Orb allows Mamoswine's Ice Shard to always OHKO Garchomp and its Rock-type coverage to always OHKO Mega Charizard Y. It also allows Mamoswine's High Horsepower to OHKO Archaludon and Incineroar. Without Focus Sash, though, Mamoswine loses its ability to beat Pokemon like Sneasler, Gholdengo, and Mega Raichu Y without speed control.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mamoswine's poor defensive typing and middling Speed make it susceptible to being outsped and 2HKOed by foes that double target it. It is also susceptible to having its Focus Sash broken by priority moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Basculegion-M's Aqua Jet, making Mamoswine much easier to deal with.

  • Mega Delphox is an incredibly poor matchup for Mamoswine, since it resists Ice, is immune to Ground, and can 2HKO Mamoswine with Heat Wave or set up a Nasty Plot while Mamoswine can't threaten it. Mega Charizard Y similarly can 2HKO Mamoswine with Heat Wave while not being seriously threatened by variants without Rock Slide.

  • Mega Froslass can outspeed and 2HKO Mamoswine with Blizzard or reduce its damage output with Aurora Veil. Mega Scovillain can redirect any of Mamoswine's attacks, burn it with Spicy Spray, and threaten it with Overheat and Giga Drain.

  • Rain teams often feature Pokemon like Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-M that can threaten Mamoswine, while it can't do much damage back. Rain teams also commonly feature Grimmsnarl with Reflect to reduce Mamoswine's damage output.

  • Rotom-Wash resists Ice, is immune to Ground, and can threaten Mamoswine with Hydro Pump or reduce its damage output with Will-O-Wisp. Corviknight and Milotic are both too bulky for Mamoswine to comfortably 2HKO and can threaten it with Iron Head and Muddy Water, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Since Mamoswine is frail and likely won't stay on the field for long, it fits best on hyper offense teams that appreciate its unique STAB combination and ability to deal strong priority damage. Mamoswine is also a great beneficiary of Tailwind from Pokemon like Whimsicott and Mega Aerodactyl thanks to its great damage output. With Tailwind, Mamoswine can outspeed and OHKO Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl, Garchomp, and Sneasler before they can remove its Focus Sash.

  • Mega Charizard Y is an excellent partner for Mamoswine. Mega Charizard Y resists the Grass-, Fire-, and Fighting-type moves that threaten Mamoswine while threatening strong spread damage, shutting off rain, and threatening Pokemon like Mega Froslass, Mega Scovillain, and Corviknight. In return, Mamoswine can threaten common checks to Mega Charizard Y such as Garchomp, Incineroar, Mega Aerodactyl, and Dragonite.

  • Venusaur in the sun can outspeed and threaten Pokemon like Mega Swampert and Basculegion-M. Incineroar resists the Fire-type attacks that threaten Mamoswine and can safely switch in on any of Mega Delphox's attacks, threatening it with Throat Chop. Toxapex can protect Mamoswine from opposing Heat Wave with Wide Guard and trap Pokemon with a poor matchup into Mamoswine on the field with Infestation.

  • Choice Scarf users like Hydreigon and Garchomp can make up for Mamoswine's middling Speed. Hydreigon is stronger against rain teams and Basculegion-M because it resists Water and threatens the latter with its Dark-type STAB attacks, while Garchomp is stronger into Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Raichu Y because of its fast Ground-type damage. Mamoswine can use Ice Shard to put another Pokemon in range of a KO. For example, Mamoswine's Ice Shard into Choice Scarf Garchomp's Rock Slide can KO Mega Aerodactyl before it can move.

Curly Brace's Machine Gun (Offensive).description:
• Mamoswine shows off its offensive face-to-face capabilities against a wide array of targets, including powerhouse Pokemon like Garchomp and Mega Dragonite! It also carves a niche as the only Stealth Rock user in the format with Oblivious, which allows it to safely set entry hazards without worrying about getting Taunted!

  • Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock breaks Garchomp's and Meowscarada's Focus Sash and Dragonite's Multiscale. Other relevant targets that can have their survivability severely compromised by Stealth Rock include Volcarona and Charizard.

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb provides speed control against faster foes and will always OHKO Mega Charizard Y. The Speed drop becomes particularly useful for aiding an ally Choice Scarf user like Garchomp or Meowscarada to move before their counterparts.

  • Icicle Spear: If Mamoswine is used as a lead or an early-game attacker and there's no opportunity for it or an ally to set Stealth Rock in order to attempt to break a foe's Focus Sash, Icicle Spear is the best option to take on these users. A two-hit Icicle Spear will always OHKO Garchomp, and three hits OHKO Protean Meowscarada as long as it retains its Grass typing. Three hits also OHKO Dragonite, even with Multiscale. Another noteworthy target is Mimikyu, as the first hit can get around Disguise. However, OHKOing Mimikyu often requires a total of four or five hits with high damage rolls.

  • Icicle Crash: Despite the shaky accuracy compared to Icicle Spear's, the power of Icicle Crash is not conditioned by a total number of hits. Thus, it can deliver reliably high amounts of damage, potentially 3HKOing physically defensive Hippowdon after Sitrus Berry recovery. The moderate flinch chance can also potentially buy extra turns for Mamoswine against a slower foe.

  • Ice Shard: Ice Shard allows Mamoswine to pick up KOs and revenge kill Choice Scarf users like Garchomp, Meowscarada, and Hydreigon. Preserving Mamoswine after it's used its Focus Sash can also be valuable late-game for picking up a KO against the aforementioned foes. Ice Shard also takes out faster Pokemon that do not use or learn priority moves, such as Garchomp and Hydreigon. Ice Shard can also take care of Mega Mawile and Kingambit if they're put in KO range with Earthquake.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake can potentially OHKO Mega Mawile and also covers various relevant Pokemon like Mega Raichu Y, Mega Metagross, Aegislash, Archaludon, Kingambit, and Bellibolt.

  • Watch Out for Glimmora and Archaludon: Toxic Debris Glimmora can potentially switch in on Icicle Spear and set two layers of Toxic Spikes in the process. Meanwhile, Stamina Archaludon can switch in and snowball with a Defense boost per each successive hit, which makes it significantly harder to deal with.

Other Options

  • Freeze-Dry: If a rain archetype is particularly troublesome when leading, Freeze-Dry can be used to significantly damage Pelipper and Mega Swampert.

  • Endeavor: At low HP, Endeavor can make muscling through a more resilient Pokemon easier for Mamoswine or its teammates.

Abilities

  • Oblivious: Oblivious ensures Mamoswine is not affected by Mawile's and Gyarados's Intimidate. It also blocks Taunt so that Mamoswine can safely set up Stealth Rock.

  • Thick Fat: With Thick Fat, Mamoswine becomes capable of surviving a +2 Torch Song from Skeledirge. It can even survive the combination of Flamethrower and Extreme Speed from Modest Mega Dragonite after taking Stealth Rock damage!

Aurora Veil Setter.description:
• Mega Froslass uses its excellent Speed, Fake Out immunity, and Snow Warning to reliably set Aurora Veil for offensive teams without being too passive, using an accurate Blizzard in snow to pressure both foes and potentially freeze them while using Shadow Ball to threaten a metagame staple in Basculegion-M. This makes Mega Froslass a strong fit on offensive teams that can use Aurora Veil to stomach attacks and trade more aggressively.

  • Aurora Veil: Aurora Veil is Mega Froslass's main selling point, making it much harder for foes to remove it and its ally. This is especially valuable for teammates such as Sneasler, Kingambit, Basculegion-M, Garchomp, Hisuian Arcanine, and Kommo-o that appreciate the extra bulk when forcing trades, setting up, or staying on the field to keep offensive pressure. Aurora Veil can also make bulkier partners like Corviknight much harder to break through, but Mega Froslass gains more value by supporting aggressive teams rather than passive teammates.

  • Modest versus Timid: A Modest nature is preferred for the extra damage output, notably guaranteeing an OHKO on Basculegion-M with Shadow Ball while still allowing Froslass to outspeed major threats such as Garchomp, Mega Floette, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Dragonite as well as Speed tie Adamant Sneasler. A Timid nature can be used instead to Speed tie Jolly Sneasler while outspeeding Maushold and opposing Modest Mega Froslass, but the loss in power is noticeable.

  • Mega Evolving Froslass: Mega Froslass can forgo immediately Mega Evolving to ensure snow is active on the turn it uses Aurora Veil if the opponent has a slower weather setter like Mega Charizard Y, Pelipper, or Tyranitar. Staying in base forme can also give Cursed Body a chance to punish moves like Mega Aerodactyl's Rock Slide while Froslass positions to Mega Evolve and set snow later.

Other Options

  • Rain Dance: Rain Dance can be used over Shadow Ball to give Mega Froslass additional defensive utility against Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal while allowing Archaludon to use Electro Shot, but it removes Mega Froslass's own snow, making Aurora Veil unusable.

Abilities

  • Snow Warning: Snow Warning enables Mega Froslass to use Aurora Veil and makes Blizzard a perfectly accurate spread STAB attack against targets such as Garchomp, Whimsicott, Mega Dragonite, and Aerodactyl. Snow also boosts Mega Froslass's Defense, helping it helps Froslass take physical attacks like Rock Slide from Aerodactyl and Knock Off from Tyranitar more comfortably while trying to set Aurora Veil. Snow Warning also lets Mega Froslass contest weather from opposing setters such as Mega Charizard Y, Pelipper, and Mega Tyranitar if Mega Evolution is timed correctly.

SP Spreads

  • 30 HP / 21 Def / 15 Spe with Timid: This bulkier spread still outspeeds Garchomp, Mega Floette, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Dragonite while giving Mega Froslass much better physical bulk with snow active. With Aurora Veil up, Aerodactyl's Rock Slide becomes a 4HKO, while Incineroar's Flare Blitz and Aegislash's Poltergeist become guaranteed 3HKOs, and even a 200-Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion-M fails to OHKO Froslass. Even without Special Attack investment, Mega Froslass still 2HKOes Archaludon with Blizzard and OHKOes uninvested Mega Gengar with Shadow Ball while heavily pressuring Garchomp and Dragonite.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Froslass struggles most against Pokemon that either remove snow or threaten it before it can set Aurora Veil. Mega Charizard Y removes snow with Drought and threatens heavy spread damage with Heat Wave, while Mega Tyranitar overwrites snow with sand and pressures Mega Froslass with Rock- and Dark-type attacks. Hisuian Arcanine is especially dangerous because Head Smash and Flare Blitz can OHKO even bulkier Mega Froslass through snow's Defense boost and Aurora Veil. Kingambit and Incineroar also pressure Mega Froslass directly while walling its STAB attacks and threatening it back with their own STAB moves, making it difficult for Mega Froslass to do much beyond setting Aurora Veil. Kingambit is especially troublesome, as Sucker Punch can pick off Mega Froslass once it has been weakened, while Incineroar disrupts Mega Froslass's physical partners with Intimidate. Archaludon can take Blizzard well and retaliate with Flash Cannon, and Aerodactyl can outspeed Mega Froslass and threaten it with Rock Slide.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Froslass fits best with offensive teammates that can use Aurora Veil to stay on the field longer and force trades more aggressively. Sneasler is one of Froslass's best partners, using Fake Out to protect itself while Aurora Veil is being set and Close Combat to threaten Kingambit, Incineroar, and Mega Tyranitar. Kingambit appreciates Aurora Veil making it harder to remove while setting up Swords Dance or trading with faster teams. It threatens Ghost-types that pressure Mega Froslass, using Kowtow Cleave for consistent damage against Aegislash and Farigiraf as well as Sucker Punch to pick off faster threats such as Mega Gengar and opposing Basculegion-M once they are in range. Garchomp appreciates Aurora Veil giving it more room to attack, using Earthquake to threaten Steel-, Fire-, and Rock-types such as Kingambit, Archaludon, Incineroar, Hisuian Arcanine, and Mega Tyranitar. Rock Slide also lets Garchomp pressure Mega Charizard Y and Hisuian Arcanine while giving it a spread move that can punish both foes. Hisuian Arcanine gives Mega Froslass teams immediate pressure against opposing Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y with Head Smash and Rock Slide while threatening Steel-types such as Kingambit with Flare Blitz. Whimsicott provides Tailwind and Encore, letting Mega Froslass's offensive teammates overwhelm faster teams while punishing Protect, Fake Out, and setup attempts. Kommo-o can use Aurora Veil to set up more safely and pressure Kingambit, Incineroar, and Archaludon with Aura Sphere. Basculegion-M uses Aurora Veil to survive revenge killing attempts from priority users like Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Aeiglash's Shadow Sneak as well as faster attackers like Mega Gengar while pressuring Fire- and Rock-types such as Mega Charizard Y, Incineroar, Hisuian Arcanine, and Mega Tyranitar. Archaludon can fit on Rain Dance variants with Politoed and Basculegion-M, as Mega Froslass can support it with Aurora Veil and set rain later on in the game. Aurora Veil makes Archaludon even harder to remove, while Rain Dance lets it use Electro Shot consistently to threaten targets such as Mega Floette and Mega Charizard Y.

  • How to Overcome Mega Froslass's Weaknesses: Against opposing weather teams, avoid Mega Evolving early if the opponent can still overwrite snow with Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, and Pelipper. Against Kingambit and Incineroar, pair Mega Froslass with teammates such as Sneasler, Garchomp, Basculegion-M, and Hisuian Arcanine that can immediately threaten them instead of letting them attack freely. Against faster Rock Slide users such as opposing Aerodactyl, use Protect and Tailwind support from Whimsicott or Wide Guard from partners such as Aerodactyl to stop Mega Froslass from being flinched before it can set Aurora Veil.

Special Attacker.description:
Mega Froslass secures a niche in the tier as a solid wallbreaker thanks to its unique offensive coverage as well as great Speed and Special Attack. Its ability, Snow Warning, gives it a Defense boost, allowing it to survive Meowscarada's Knock Off even after Stealth Rock chip damage, as well as Shadow Sneak from +2 Adamant Ceruledge. Additionally, with Snow Warning, Blizzard can bypass accuracy checks, letting Mega Froslass threaten many common foes like Garchomp, Dragonite, Mega Meganium, and Corviknight. Shadow Ball allows it to damage common Ice-resistant foes like Aegislash, Mega Metagross, and Ceruledge as well as bulky Pokemon like Galarian Slowking super effectively. Nasty Plot lets Mega Froslass become an insanely powerful wallbreaker; after a boost, it OHKOes physically defensive Clefable and Corviknight. Thunderbolt can be used to hit Greninja and Hisuian Samurott super effectively, which otherwise resist Mega Froslass's STAB moves. Will-O-Wisp can be useful to cripple physically offensive answers to Mega Froslass such as Kingambit, Tyranitar, and Mega Scizor. It also synergizes very well with the Defense boost provided by snow; Mega Froslass is able to survive a Meteor Mash from a burned Mega Metagross when snow is active, and Bullet Punch's damage output is greatly reduced when Mega Scizor is affected by Will-O-Wisp. This makes it easier for Mega Froslass to pressure them with Shadow Ball. Aurora Veil is another option that lets Mega Froslass have an easier time boosting with Nasty Plot and allows its teammates to enter the field more safely.

Mega Froslass finds its way on all types of offense teams that appreciate its ability to break common defensive cores. Physical sweepers such as Dragonite, Kingambit, and Quaquaval benefit from Mega Froslass pressuring physically bulky Pokemon like Clefable, Corviknight, and Rotom-Wash as well as the damage reduction provided by Aurora Veil. Quaquaval, in particular, shines as a partner due to its ability to break past common Dark- and Fire-types like Hisuian Samurott, Kingambit, and Volcarona that Mega Froslass struggles against while also bringing Mega Froslass in with Flip Turn and removing entry hazards, especially Stealth Rock, with Rapid Spin. Other entry hazard removers like Corviknight, Excadrill, and Glimmora are all great partners as well, with Corviknight providing Mega Froslass with safe entry via its slow U-turn. On the other hand, entry hazards of your own help Mega Froslass break its foes more easily, so hazard setters like Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott along with the aforementioned Excadrill and Glimmora work extremely well as teammates, with Stealth Rock ensuring that Mega Froslass's Thunderbolt OHKOes Greninja and Hisuian Samurott. Hatterene is another useful partner, providing paralysis support with Nuzzle to slow down faster threats such as Dragapult, Greninja, and Meowscarada as well as entry hazard control with Magic Bounce. It can also check Mega Lopunny decently well, which Mega Froslass benefits from. Bulky Water-types like Toxapex, Rotom-Wash, and Primarina that can switch into repeated Fire-type attacks from the likes of Blaziken, Ceruledge, and Volcarona are also greatly appreciated as teammates.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Offensive Pivot.description:
• With a Choice Scarf, Rotom-Heat becomes a speedy pivot and disruptor. Levitate also lets Rotom-Heat switch in on Pokemon that often use Ground-type attacks such as Choice-locked Garchomp, Mega Metagross, and Mega Venusaur, and revenge kill them if they're weakened enough.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge: Thunderbolt is preferred for higher damage. Discharge can be used instead for the higher chance of paralysis.

  • Volt Switch: This turns Rotom-Heat into an offensive pivot, allowing it to leave matchups where it can't do much damage and safely bring another teammate in the process.

  • Overheat: This is the best and only option for Rotom-Heat to threaten Meowscarada and Scizor. If Rotom-Heat is using a Modest nature, Overheat has a very high chance to OHKO Mega Meganium with maximum HP investment and also deals massive damage to specially defensive Corviknight, but it narrowly misses a chance to land the OHKO even with Stealth Rock damage. In the event Mega Meganium and Corviknight survive, they can use their recovery moves to offset the damage they receive as Rotom-Heat's Special Attack decreases with every use of Overheat, so this should only be used to pick up the KO if they're weakened enough.

  • Trick: Even though Choice Scarf is a highly coveted item for speed control, Trick can be used to lock a defensive Pokemon into a move and make it virtually useless for the rest of the battle.

  • Modest versus Timid: On one hand, a Modest nature allows Rotom-Heat's Thunderbolt to have a very low chance to OHKO Mega Charizard Y, as well as 2HKOing specially defensive Corviknight after Leftovers recovery. On the other hand, a Timid nature can be used for outspeeding Jolly Gyarados that has used Dragon Dance.

Bulky Support.description:
• Rotom-Wash is able to leverage its great bulk and defensive typing alongside healing items to become very difficult for the opponent to remove from the field, using Will-O-Wisp against the many physical attackers in the format such as Garchomp and Kingambit while being able to deal good damage to staples like Basculegion-M and Incineroar.

  • Hydro Pump: Hydro Pump is Rotom-Wash's only option for Water-type STAB, enabling it to handle Ground-types, namely Garchomp, while also hitting Incineroar.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp allows Rotom-Wash to beat Kingambit and physical attackers like Mega Tyranitar; after burn damage, Hydro Pump will always 2HKO Garchomp.

Other Options

  • Volt Switch: Volt Switch allows Rotom-Wash to play as a slow, bulky pivot, similarly to Incineroar. This does, however, come at the cost of Rotom-Wash losing either reliable Electric-type STAB in Thunderbolt or Protect.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry grants Rotom-Wash solid healing, allowing it to avoid 2HKOs from Sneasler's Close Combat and Sylveon's Hyper Voice.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers provides Rotom-Wash with more consistent recovery, though it requires Rotom-Wash to stay on the field longer to provide good value; it also allows Rotom-Wash to always avoid a 2HKO from Glimmora's Sludge Bomb.

Abilities

  • Levitate: Levitate not only allows Rotom-Wash to be a good ally for Garchomp, letting Garchomp use Earthquake without fear of damaging its partner, but also allows Rotom-Wash to switch in on opposing Garchomp rather freely.

SP Spreads

  • 31 HP / 12 Def / 1 SpA / 20 SpD / 2 Spe with Bold: With the given bulk, Rotom-Wash survives Solar Beam from Timid Mega Charizard Y and Sucker Punch from +2 Black Glasses Kingambit while having a chance to survive Last Respects from Adamant Basculegion-M after two of Basculegion-M's allies have fainted. The HP SPs give Rotom-Wash an even HP stat to optimize Sitrus Berry recovery. The Speed investment allows Rotom-Wash to outspeed Jolly Choice Scarf Basculegion-M under Tailwind, and the remaining SP is invested in Special Attack.

  • 31 HP / 14 Def / 16 SpA / 3 SpD / 2 Spe with Modest: This spread is more offensively oriented, allowing Rotom-Wash to guarantee a 2HKO on minimum-bulk Garchomp with Hydro Pump and avoid a 2HKO from Garchomp's Dragon Claw; it also survives Kowtow Cleave from +1 Kingambit, such as after an Intimidate. The same Speed benchmark as above is reached, and the remaining SPs are invested in Special Defense.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash trades most of its bulk investment for greater offensive investment, while still being able to tank hits thanks to its naturally high defensive stats. With Choice Scarf, Rotom-Wash can more consistently take on the likes of Aerodactyl, Mega Delphox, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M.

  • Electroweb: Thanks to Choice Scarf, Rotom-Wash can consistently use Electroweb to provide Speed control for its team, slowing down fast threats like Aerodactyl and Alolan Ninetales.

  • Volt Switch: As opposed to the bulkier sets, Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash can use Volt Switch to quickly pivot out of unfavorable situations while dealing chip damage, possibly breaking a Focus Sash on a Sneasler, Basculegion-M, Aerodactyl, or Whimsicott.

Other Options

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp can cripple physical attackers and, with Choice Scarf, be used on fast Pokemon like Sneasler before they move. It is generally forgone, however, as locking Rotom-Wash into a status move is undesirable. Running Will-O-Wisp also requires dropping Thunderbolt, Rotom-Wash's most consistent Electric-type STAB option.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Rotom-Wash to outrun faster Pokemon such as Talonflame, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Gengar. Thanks to the Speed boost from Choice Scarf, Rotom-Wash becomes a reliable revenge killer, switching in to take out low-HP Pokemon with either Electroweb, which also hits the other foe and provides Speed control, or Volt Switch, which improves positioning.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest: This spread maximizes Rotom-Wash's Speed and Special Attack, allowing it to outpace the likes of Mega Delphox and Adamant Mega Aerodactyl.

  • 14 HP / 27 SpA / 25 Spe with Timid: With the given Speed investment, Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash always outruns Choice Scarf (RC) Basculegion-M while surviving Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette; the remaining SPs are invested in Special Attack.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: While Rotom-Wash has an amazing defensive typing, it struggles against Grass-types, mainly Sinistcha and Mega Venusaur, which resist all of its common attacks. Sinistcha can also redirect these attacks, preventing Rotom-Wash from dealing meaningful damage or burning foes like Kingambit, while Sinistcha and Mega Venusaur can heavily damage Rotom-Wash with Matcha Gotcha and Giga Drain, respectively. Dragon-types like Archaludon and Hydreigon can also shrug off a burn, resist all of Rotom-Wash's common attacks, and retaliate with Electro Shot and Dark Pulse, respectively. Mega Floette and Mega Scovillain pose issues for Rotom-Wash as well, setting up in front of it or heavily damaging it with Giga Drain, respectively; Mega Floette can easily take Rotom-Wash's attacks thanks to its naturally high Special Defense and retaliate with Moonblast or Light of Ruin, with the latter threatening an OHKO.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp works well with Rotom-Wash, freely using Earthquake and threatening opposing Dragon-types with Dragon Claw. Excadrill can also use Earthquake next to Rotom-Wash, as well as Iron Head to beat Mega Floette and Rock Slide to hit Mega Charizard Y, which can threaten to OHKO Rotom-Wash with Solar Beam. Corviknight is another great ally that threatens Sinistcha and Mega Floette, while Mega Tyranitar can deal heavy damage across the board to offset Rotom-Wash's passivity and appreciates Rotom-Wash's ability to threaten Basculegion-M. In return, Mega Tyranitar threatens Mega Charizard Y and Sinistcha, both of which boast Grass-type attacks that threaten Rotom-Wash. When building with Rotom-Wash and Mega Tyranitar, however, it is important to keep in mind that they share a weakness to Mega Floette. To counteract this, the aforementioned Steel-types, Excadrill and Corviknight, can be used to take down Mega Floette.

  • How to Overcome Rotom-Wash's Weaknesses: Bringing safe switch-ins to attacks that target Rotom-Wash's weaknesses is recommended; Pokemon like Corviknight work well in this role. Offensive Pokemon like Excadrill and Garchomp work well alongside Rotom-Wash, combining Earthquake with Hydro Pump or Electric-type moves to deal solid damage. Playing Rotom-Wash as a supporting pivot is best, burning foes or providing Speed control and chip damage throughout the game.

Defensive Pivot.description:
With serviceable bulk, a fantastic defensive typing supported by Levitate, and a good utility movepool, Rotom-Wash can function as a great defensive pivot. Hydro Pump threatens Fire- and Ground-types, like Ceruledge, Blaziken, Garchomp, and Hippowdon. Volt Switch serves as Rotom-Wash's primary Electric-type STAB move, hitting Flying- and Water-types like Corviknight, Hisuian Samurott, and Primarina while also allowing it to safely bring in a teammate. Will-O-Wisp can immediately threaten most physical attackers, such as Dragonite, Kingambit, Mega Metagross, and Mega Staraptor. Pain Split, combined with Rotom-Wash's low HP stat, allows it to recover health against its common switch-ins, like Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge, ensuring it stays healthy throughout the game. Rest, alongside Chesto Berry, can be used instead as a more immediate recovery option. Sitrus Berry gives Rotom-Wash a one-time recovery option instead, preventing it from spending a turn using Pain Split or Rest. Leftovers can alternatively be used to let Rotom-Wash have a more passive recovery option while also taking advantage of passive foes like Galarian Slowking and Clefable. Rotom-Wash can also opt for no item to let it best stand up to Poltergeist users like Ceruledge and Aegislash, at the cost of giving up item-based recovery. 7 Speed SPs allow Rotom-Wash to outspeed Adamant Aegislash and Jolly Kingambit to potentially get off a Will-O-Wisp or pivot out to a teammate.

Thanks to its defensive utility as well as its ability to pivot to a teammate, Rotom-Wash works well on both balance and bulky offense teams. Special walls like Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge make great teammates, as they can switch in against the special attackers that commonly force it out, like Primarina, Mega Meganium, Mega Raichu Y, and Mega Floette. In return, Rotom-Wash can switch in against and burn foes that threaten them, like Garchomp, Dragonite, Hisuian Samurott, and Mega Metagross. Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge also have excellent type synergy with Rotom-Wash and can form a great pivot core with their access to Chilly Reception and Flip Turn, respectively. Rotom-Wash also appreciates support from Fairy-type attackers like Primarina, Mega Floette, and Mega Meganium in order to pressure Dragon-types like Dragapult, Hydreigon, and Mega Dragonite, which resist both of Rotom-Wash's attacks. Physical wallbreakers like Blaziken, Dragonite, Mega Metagross, and Mega Lopunny are also good teammates, as they can take advantage of Galarian Slowking, Mega Meganium, and Mega Dragalage, which can commonly switch in on Rotom-Wash. Due to the fact that Rotom-Wash greatly threatens Corviknight, physical attackers like Meowscarada, Scizor, and Excadrill appreciate its presence while also being brought in safely by its Volt Switch. Ghost-types like Dragapult and Aegislash also appreciate Rotom-Wash's ability to threaten burn on Dark-type attackers like Hisuian Samurott, Meowscarada, and Kingambit, while they can do super effective damage to Galarian Slowking in return. Rotom-Wash struggles against Mold Breaker Excadrill, which can hit it through Levitate; therefore, Corviknight, Garchomp, and Hippowdon make great teammates, with Corviknight switching into Excadrill while providing Defog and U-turn support and the latter two immediately threatening it with their Ground-type STAB moves.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Pivot.description:
• The combination of an excellent defensive typing, fantastic ability, and solid bulk lets Rotom-Wash act as a great pivot that can handle physical attackers such as Garchomp, Dragonite, Mega Gyarados, and Scizor.

  • Volt Switch: Volt Switch lets Rotom-Wash maintain momentum, allowing its teammates to get on the field safely.

  • Hydro Pump: Hydro Pump gives Rotom-Wash reliable damage against the Ground-types that try to switch into Volt Switch.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp acts as a deterrent for physically offensive foes, such as Sneasler, Dragon Dance Dragonite, Aegislash, and Garchomp.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge: Thunderbolt has more Base Power than Discharge, but Discharge can be used to paralyze foes faster than Rotom-Wash, such as Mega Lopunny, Sneasler, and Greninja.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry provides quick healing to Rotom-Wash, especially after surviving high-Base Power moves from strong foes.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers can be used as an alternative option over Sitrus Berry, providing Rotom-Wash passive healing, which makes up for its lack of reliable recovery. Additionally, Leftovers synergizes with a Bold nature and the secondary stat spread better than Sitrus Berry.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 SpA / 2 Spe with Modest: Maximizing Rotom-Wash's decent Special Attack stat allows it to roll a very small OHKO chance on Mega Charizard Y, as well as letting Rotom-Wash reliably 2HKO Dragonite after Stealth Rock and specially defensive Hippowdon.

  • 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpA with Bold: When fully invested in Defense, Rotom-Wash can stop powerful physical sweepers, such as Garchomp and Kingambit, while threatening them with Will-O-Wisp.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf turns Rotom-Wash into a fast pivot and revenge killer, letting it outspeed key threats such as Charizard, Mega Lopunny, and Garchomp.

  • Volt Switch: Volt Switch lets Rotom-Wash take advantage of its Choice Scarf by dealing chip damage to faster threats such as Mega Gengar and Sneasler before pivoting into a teammate that can handle them. It also helps Rotom-Wash keep momentum against Pokemon it forces out, such as Corviknight and Mega Charizard Y.

  • Trick: Trick lets Rotom-Wash cripple defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon and Hippowdon by locking them into one move, making it easier for teammates to take advantage of them.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge: Thunderbolt gives Rotom-Wash a stronger Electric-type attack when it does not want to pivot out with Volt Switch, notably helping against Primarina, Corviknight, and Mega Gyarados. Discharge trades power for a higher paralysis chance, which can punish switch-ins and support slower teammates.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp gives Rotom-Wash a way to punish physical attackers such as Garchomp, Kingambit, and Mega Scizor. However, it is harder to justify than an Electric-type attack because Rotom-Wash usually needs to use Trick first, as being locked into Will-O-Wisp can leave it easy to take advantage of.

Bulky Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance alongside a boosting item allows Hisuian Samurott to take its damage output to new highs, functioning as a wallbreaker and sweeper off the strength of its powerful Dark-type STAB moves. Sharpness-boosted Ceaseless Edge is one of the strongest Dark-type moves in the tier, and it also sets Spikes that make progress even against Pokemon like Mega Meganium, Primarina, and Mega Floette that resist the move. This not only accentuates Hisuian Samurott's own gameplan of taking down teams but also supports its teammates in the process. Sucker Punch circumvents Hisuian Samurott's middling Speed and allows it to handle offensive threats such as Dragapult, Mega Delphox, and Mega Metagross; entry hazards allow even unboosted Sucker Punch to OHKO Pokemon like Mega Raichu Y. Black Glasses helps with Hisuian Samurott's damage output, helping it OHKO bulky foes such as Rotom-Wash with a +2 Ceaseless Edge after minor chip damage and fast offensive ones such as Mega Glimmora with a +2 Sucker Punch after entry hazard damage. With hazard removers like Corviknight, especially if Hisuian Samurott's set is unknown to the opponent, Hisuian Samurott can use them as an opportunity to set up a Swords Dance and either use Encore to lock the target into a disadvantageous move, allowing for further usage of Swords Dance, or block status moves with Taunt to maintain hazards or prevent setup. Sacred Sword is another option, allowing Hisuian Samurott to OHKO certain Pokemon that resist its Dark-type moves such as Kingambit and opposing Hisuian Samurott; its secondary effect allows Hisuian Samurott to break through Archaludon regardless of how many Defense boosts from Stamina it has accrued. Hisuian Samurott's SP spread maximizes its Attack, uses 8 Speed SPs to outspeed Jolly Kingambit and neutral-natured Aegislash, and invests the remainder in HP.

Hisuian Samurott's potent offensive typing and ability to immediately threaten foes or force progress makes it a great piece on a variety of archetypes, as it helps out against some of the most effective offensive Pokemon such as Aegislash, Ceruledge, and, if it can lock it into a disadvantageous move with Encore or has Sacred Sword, Kingambit. Stealth Rock users such as Garchomp and Excadrill synergize with Hisuian Samurott greatly, being immune to Electric-type attacks from Pokemon such as Mega Raichu Y and Rotom-Wash while assisting in an entry hazard stacking strategy. Other Stealth Rock users, such as Glimmora, can work quite effectively alongside Hisuian Samurott on more hyper offensive builds. With its bulk, this set works as an effective switch-in to Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking; this quality assists potent specially offensive teammates such as Volcarona, Mega Meganium, and Mega Floette. Such teammates, in return, help out Hisuian Samurott by dealing with Fighting-type threats such as Mega Lopunny, which threatens to outspeed and OHKO Hisuian Samurott. Fellow Dark-types such as Kingambit, Meowscarada, and Hydreigon appreciate Hisuian Samurott wearing down shared answers such as Corviknight and Hatterene.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf allows Hisuian Samurott to compress roles as both speed control and a strong Spikes setter for balance and bulky offense teams due to its access to Ceaseless Edge. The item gives Hisuian Samurott the jump on faster foes such as Dragapult and Mega Delphox, allowing it to revenge kill them with Ceaseless Edge; Mega Raichu Y and Mega Metagross can also be picked off once weakened. Flip Turn allows Hisuian Samurott to act as a pivot against switch-ins such as Clefable, Corviknight, and Mega Meganium. Razor Shelloffers frequent Defense drops and higher Base Power, but Aqua Cutter is a viable alternative due to it not making contact against Rough Skin Garchomp as well as its high critical hit rate and perfect accuracy. Sacred Sword serves as coverage against Kingambit, Hydreigon, and opposing Hisuian Samurott. Aqua Jet allows Hisuian Samurott to snipe frailer foes that outspeed it, such as boosted Volcarona and Blaziken. It also allows Hisuian Samurott to get around Mach Punch Mega Lopunny if weakened. Finally, Knock Off is a more niche alternative to the two, removing valuable held items such as Dragonite's Lum Berry and Clefable's Leftovers and allowing Hisuian Samurott to discourage direct switch-ins more.

Hisuian Samurott's entry hazard-setting capability gives it major utility for its team, which makes Stealth Rock setters such as Garchomp and Glimmora valuable partners. Stealth Rock is especially key for chipping Flying-types such as Corviknight and Dragonite, which avoid Spikes, and Garchomp can help Hisuian Samurott overwhelm shared checks in Corviknight and Clefable. While Hisuian Samurott can set up Spikes quite easily, it struggles to maintain them versus the aforementioned Corviknight, making Fire-types such as Volcarona, Mega Delphox, and Ceruledge all great teammates to discourage Corviknight from switching into Hisuian Samurott. Ceruledge and Annihilape can also block a predicted Rapid Spin from Excadrill. Other wallbreakers and cleaners such as Mega Lopunny, Sneasler, and Kingambit all appreciate Hisuian Samurott's hazard support, and the former two additionally appreciate it beating Psychic-types such as Galarian Slowking and Mega Delphox; in return, they beat Dark-types such as opposing Hisuian Samurott and Hydreigon. Kingambit appreciates overwhelmed checks such as Sneasler, while it can pick off foes faster than Hisuian Samurott, such as boosted Mega Charizard X. Galarian Slowking can serve as a switch-in to Fairy-types such as Primarina, Clefable, and Mega Floette while supporting Hisuian Samurott with Future Sight. In return, Hisuian Samurott can threaten the Ghost- and Ground-types that Galarian Slowking may bring in, such as Aegislash and Excadrill. Finally, Mega Meganium is a useful ally, doing well against the aforementioned Primarina and Quaquaval while overwhelming a shared check in Corviknight. In return, Hisuian Samurott can slice past Galarian Slowking and Ceruledge, which Mega Meganium does not like dealing with.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Offensive Spikes Setter.description:
• Hisuian Samurott serves an important role in the metagame as an excellent lead and the tier's premier Spikes setter through Ceaseless Edge while also being able to threaten the likes of Mega Metagross, Hippowdon, and Gholdengo with its good movepool.

  • Sacred Sword: Sacred Sword lets Hisuian Samurott chunk opposing Dark-types such as Mega Gyarados and Hydreigon along with ignoring Archaludon's Stamina Defense boosts.

  • Razor Shell vs. Aqua Cutter: Although the choice is mostly your preference, Razor Shell hits a bit harder, notably always 2HKOing physically defensive Hippowdon and potentially 2HKOing Mega Scizor with a Defense drop. Aqua Cutter is, however, perfectly accurate, making it a safer cleanup tool.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch can pick off weakened or faster targets such as Garchomp, Mega Delphox, and Basculegion-M.

  • Flip Turn: Flip Turn can be used to pivot out and keep up momentum should Hisuian Samurott be up against problematic walls like Primarina and Mega Meganium.

  • Encore: Encore can punish more passive options like Corviknight's Roost or Umbreon's Wish, allowing Hisuian Samurott to freely slice away at them.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This is a basic spread that lets Hisuian Samurott hit hard and move quickly.

  • 14 HP / 32 Atk / 8 SpD / 12 Spe with Jolly: This spread will let Hisuian Samurott nearly always survive Modest Archaludon's Draco Meteor while outspeeding bulkier Mimikyu sets.

Items

  • Black Glasses: Black Glasses increases the power of Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge and Sucker Punch. It allows the former to potentially OHKO Shield forme Aegislash and Mega Metagross, while the latter will always OHKO uninvested Basculegion-M and nearly always OHKO Mega Starmie.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash allows Hisuian Samurott to work as an incredible lead, usually enabling at least a layer of Spikes to be set up, and it can allow Hisuian Samurott to successfully trade against opposing leads such as Glimmora.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott provides excellent role compression through speed control and entry hazard support from Ceaseless Edge. It can remove threats such as Mega Starmie, Mega Delphox, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M.

  • Ceaseless Edge: Ceaseless Edge sets entry hazards, lets Hisuian Samurott generate progress against bulkier teams, and breaks opposing Pokemon's Focus Sash. It also lets Hisuian Samurott deal with Mega Gengar and Gholdengo. However, Hisuian Samurott is unable to beat Aegislash one-on-one from full HP because King's Shield lowers its Attack.

  • Sacred Sword: Sacred Sword cuts through Mega Lucario and Mega Lopunny. Hisuian Samurott is OHKOed from full HP by +2 Mach Punch from Mega Lopunny but not by +2 Vacuum Wave from Mega Lucario. It also ignores Defense boosts, which allows Hisuian Samurott to finish off Archaludon in a pinch.

  • Flip Turn: Flip Turn preserves momentum for Hisuian Samurott's teammates by allowing it to switch out of checks like Corviknight, Primarina, and Toxapex. It also deals some chip damage to Mega Metagross, allowing Hisuian Samurott to OHKO it later with Ceaseless Edge.

  • Razor Shell versus Aqua Cutter: Razor Shell gives Hisuian Samurott a chance to break through physically defensive Hippowdon with a Sitrus Berry over two turns if it lowers Hippowdon's Defense. It also guarantees an OHKO on offensive Mega Raichu Y. On the other hand, Aqua Cutter has perfect accuracy at the cost of slightly less power. Either move OHKOes Mega Delphox and all except the bulkiest variants of Volcarona.

  • Potential Partners: Hisuian Samurott is relatively weak and not that fast even with a Choice Scarf, leaving it unable to OHKO threats such as Mega Gyarados and Mega Metagross or outspeed +1 Mega Blaziken; teammates that can reliably handle these threats, such as Garchomp and Mega Blaziken, are greatly appreciated. Pokemon like Mega Gengar and Swords Dance Scizor that benefit from Hisuian Samurott's pivoting capabilities also make for great teammates.

SP Spreads

========

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Maximum Attack and Speed investment with a Jolly nature lets Hisuian Samurott outspeed +1 Mega Gyarados and fast threats like Mega Greninja and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: An Adamant nature may be considered, as it allows Hisuian Samurott to guarantee an OHKO on Mega Raichu Y with Aqua Cutter and plausibly 2HKO Corviknight on the switch if Razor Shell lowers Corviknight's Defense. However, the reduced Speed means Hisuian Samurott Speed ties with Mega Lopunny and is outsped by +1 Mega Gyarados, though it can still outspeed and remove Mega Delphox.

Sand Sweeper.description:
• Excadrill is a staple of sand teams due to its ability and STAB combination allowing it to outspeed the metagame and threaten common threats to its sand-setting partner, Mega Tyranitar, including Sneasler, Archaludon, Mega Floette, and Sylveon.

  • Earthquake versus High Horsepower: Earthquake gives Excadrill an incredibly powerful spread move; however, it can't be safely used next to partners without a Ground immunity and makes Excadrill susceptible to Wide Guard. High Horsepower can be safely used next to any partner, but it comes at the cost of Excadrill's ability to deal big spread damage and leaves Excadrill more susceptible to redirection.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide gives Excadrill an option to hit Mega Charizard Y for big damage and works as an alternative spread option that doesn't hit partners. Excadrill can also effectively fish for flinches with Rock Slide due to its high Speed in sand.

Items

  • Focus Sash: The extra survivability given by Focus Sash is necessary to let Excadrill fire off more attacks before being KOed. Focus Sash lets Sand Rush-boosted Excadrill 2HKO Choice Scarf Basculegion-M while surviving Wave Crash; it also allows Excadrill to tank a Close Combat from Unburden-boosted Sneasler deal an OHKO in return with Earthquake or High Horsepower.

Abilities
