  • Sand Rush: While sand is active, Sand Rush allows Excadrill to outspeed every Pokemon in the metagame besides Sneasler with an Unburden boost.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Without sand, Excadrill is relatively slow, allowing Pokemon like Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, Sneasler, and Mega Charizard Y to outspeed and threaten it if sand is stalled out or overwritten by another weather. Excadrill commonly wants to be led alongside Tyranitar to activate Sand Rush; however, this lead can be exploited because the two share weaknesses to Water-, Fighting-, and Ground-type moves. Garchomp can be a particularly bad matchup, since Rough Skin can break Excadrill's Focus Sash if Excadrill goes for Iron Head or High Horsepower, allowing Garchomp to OHKO it with Earthquake. Basculegion-M is another tough matchup, as non-Choice Scarf variants can bring Excadrill down to its Focus Sash with Wave Crash, tank an attack, and then KO it before it can move with Aqua Jet. Excadrill is unable to deal meaningful damage to both Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, and it's also susceptible to being burned and redirected by Mega Scovillain's Spicy Spray and Rage Powder, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Tyranitar is a must-have partner for Excadrill, since it sets up sand and threatens Mega Charizard Y and Basculegion-M with Rock Slide and Knock Off, respectively. Excadrill really appreciates Ground-immune partners because they can freely switch into Garchomp and let Excadrill use Earthquake with no drawback. Corviknight is excellent for this role; it effectively walls Garchomp, threatens Grass-types with Brave Bird, and can set up with Bulk Up while Excadrill puts on offensive pressure. Hydreigon and Rotom-Wash are other great options for Ground-immune partners. Hydreigon can offensively threaten Garchomp, Mega Scovillain, and Basculegion-M, while Rotom-Wash can threaten Water-types with Thunderbolt and physical attackers with Will-o-Wisp. Sinistcha can be a great partner, since it resists all the weaknesses that Excadrill and Mega Tyranitar share while providing redirection to protect Excadrill from attacks like Sneasler's Close Combat and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash.

  • How to Overcome Excadrill's Weaknesses: Mega Tyranitar and Excadrill should always be chosen together during Team Preview. Use Excadrill as an immediately deadly sweeper, especially to outspeed and OHKO Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Floette that would otherwise be huge threats to Mega Tyranitar. Against opposing weather teams, time Tyranitar's Mega Evolution so that it can keep sand up, and position it well to keep it out of danger and preserve sand. Use the rest of the team to deal with threats to this duo, most importantly Garchomp, while keeping up offensive pressure.

Disruptive Support.description:
• Whimsicott leverages its Prankster ability and deep support movepool to help teammates outspeed crucial foes; for example, it allows non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M to outspeed and hit Mega Charizard Y with Wave Crash. It is also able to output meaningful chip damage with Moonblast.

  • Moonblast: Moonblast ensures Whimsicott can contribute to the battle even when affected by Taunt or having already set up Tailwind without any good targets for Encore being present. Notably, Whimsicott is able to break Focus Sashes on Pokemon such as Hisuian Arcanine, Sneasler, and Kingambit or threaten foes such as Garchomp, Mega Staraptor, and Dragonite.

  • Encore: Encore allows Whimsicott to essentially bar foes from using any setup moves like Bulk Up and Calm Mind while being a deterrent against moves like Fake Out. This allows Whimsicott to be a very effective member of teams weak to setup strategies, as Whimsicott's Grass typing means Encore cannot be redirected by the likes of Sinistcha. Encore also deters foes from trying to use Protect to stall out Tailwind.

  • Items: Focus Sash allows Whimsicott to get off more than one move in a battle, as it would otherwise quickly drop to foes like Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler. This allows players to preserve Whimsicott to get another chance to set Tailwind later in the game, use Whimsicott's borrowed time to put an enemy in range of a partner's attack with Moonblast, or use Encore to deter foes from using moves such as Substitute, Fake Out, and setup moves like Bulk Up.

Other Options

  • Charm: Charm is only seen when Whimsicott is paired with Mega Staraptor, as it allows Whimsicott to boost Mega Staraptor's Attack due to Contrary. It also allows Whimsicott to survive certain attacks, such as Flare Blitz from Jolly Hisuian Arcanine, even if its Focus Sash is broken. It is almost always used over Encore.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Poison-types such as Glimmora and Mega Gengar threaten to bring Whimsicott down to Focus Sash and are potentially able to KO Whimsicott in one turn due to Sludge Bomb's considerable poison chance.

  • Damage Struggles: Whimsicott struggles to contribute damage towards resisted targets such as Mega Charizard Y and Venusaur, while these also threaten it in return with Weather Ball or Heat Wave and Sludge Bomb, respectively.

  • Foes with Dual Wingbeat, such as Mega Staraptor and Mega Aerodactyl, threaten to OHKO Whimsicott through Focus Sash while being able to match Whimsicott's Tailwind. Additionally, Gholdengo threatens Whimsicott with Make It Rain and is able to safely set up in front of Whimsicott because Good as Gold blocks Encore. Additionally, Hisuian Arcanine is able to take down Whimsicott before it can move with Extreme Speed if it had been taken down to Focus Sash beforehand, or it can use Flare Blitz first to so itself. Incineroar is able to use Fake Out to allow partners to bypass Encore on a crucial turn, such as after using Calm Mind. Additionally, Fake Out can break Whimsicott's Focus Sash if Whimsicott does not use Protect, while Incineroar does not fear Encore due to its Dark typing; Incineroar's Flare Blitz also deals significant damage to Whimsicott. Additionally, Armor Tail Farigiraf completely blocks Prankster Encore and can thus safely set up Trick Room in spite of it.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Pokemon with a middling Speed such as Basculegion-M greatly benefit from Tailwind, as it allows them to invest heavily into their offense and bulk without worrying too much about their Speed stat. It also allows them to outspeed their and Whimsicott's checks and potentially threaten them instead; under Tailwind, Mystic Water Basculegion-M threatens heavy damage onto Mega Charizard Y with Wave Crash without getting outsped and OHKOed by Solar Beam. Whimsicott is also able to chip foes for KOs that Mystic Water Basculegion-M barely misses, such as Incineroar after an Intimidate and bulky Mega Charizard Y in the sun.

  • **HyperOffensive Teams **: These teams generally aim to outspeed opposing Pokemon at all times and can struggle if facing a faster foe. Whimsicott can allow these teams to function against opposing teams with speed control, such as Trick Room from Sinistcha and Tailwind from Mega Staraptor, either through using Tailwind itself to maintain the Speed advantage or using Encore to dissuade opponents from using Trick Room or Tailwind. It is also able to effectively disrupt other defensive strategies such as Calm Mind Mega Floette with Encore.

  • Mega Floette: Whimsicott excels with Mega Floette as a partner, allowing bulky Mega Floette to outspeed Pokemon such as Garchomp and Sneasler. Mega Floette also has issues dealing with Bulk Up Corviknight, which Whimsicott can deter from setting up with Encore. Attempts to dampen Mega Floette's damage output with Aurora Veil from Mega Froslass or Ninetales-A are also disincentivized by Encore. In return, Mega Floette boosts Whimsicott's damage output to considerable levels with Fairy Aura, allowing Whimsicott to threaten an OHKO on Garchomp with Moonblast and a 2HKO on Sneasler. This also allows Whimsicott to put bulkier foes such as Kingambit and Archaludon into range of Moonblast or Dazzling Gleam from Mega Floette.

  • Other Mega Evolutions: Whimsicott also finds an excellent partner in Mega Charizard Y, as Tailwind allows Mega Charizard Y to outspeed threats such as Choice Scarf Basculegion-M. Garchomp is threatened by Moonblast, further disincentivising Garchomp from staying in and using Rock Slide on Mega Charizard Y. Mega Charizard Y also threatens the Steel- and Ice-type Pokemon that Whimsicott fears, such as Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Mega Froslass, with Weather Ball in the sun and Heat Wave.

  • Non-Mega Pokemon: Kingambit and Garchomp check the Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon that threaten Whimsicott. Kingambit is able to resist both of these types while also threatening most relevant Poison-types, such as Mega Gengar and Glimmora, with Kowtow Cleave and Iron Head, respectively, and is able to use Sucker Punch to deal heavy damage to Gholdengo and Mega Metagross before they can move. Garchomp is able to use Stomping Tantrum or Earthquake to OHKO most Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon and can use Rock Slide to threaten opposing Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox. Additionally, Whimsicott checks opposing Garchomp, which could otherwise threaten Garchomp with Dragon Claw. However, Garchomp cannot safely use Earthquake next to Whimsicott, as it would break Whimsicott's Focus Sash.

Tailwind Support.description:
• Whimsicott is able to provide crucial Tailwind support to many Pokemon that rely on it, such as Mystic Water Basculegion-M, offensive Mega Floette, and bulky Garchomp. At the same time, it can shut down almost any attempts at setting up with Encore, making Whimsicott ideal for both support and disruption.

  • Encore: While Tailwind teams can sometimes struggle with setup Pokemon or moves such as Fake Out, Encore attaches a risk to these moves by forcing foes to switch out or prevent Encore in other ways risk being locked into a useless move. It synergizes well with Whimsicott's Grass typing, which allows it to ignore Rage Powder from Sinistcha attempting to redirect Encore. Encore can also be used to lock foes into resisted attacks, such as opposing Basculegion-M's Wave Crash instead of Last Respects, protecting Whimsicott and potentially its partner.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash allows Whimsicott to run more Speed but means it cannot be as offensive as Fairy Feather variants, as quite a few SPs are still required in bulk to survive Dual Wingbeat from Aerodactyl.

  • Fairy Feather: Fairy Feather allows Whimsicott to threaten a 2HKO on bulky Sitrus Berry Garchomp with Moonblast while leaving room for a lot of SPs in bulk. This item is mostly used when Focus Sash is used by a different Pokemon.

SP Spreads

  • 18 HP / 6 Def / 10 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: This spread is only run by Focus Sash variants. Whimsicott will survive Dual Wingbeat from Jolly Aerodactyl almost the entire time, with the rest of the SPs prioritized towards Speed in order to Speed tie other Whimsicott.

  • 30 HP / 17 Def / 9 SpA / 10 SpD with Bold: This spread is only run by Fairy Feather variants, as Focus Sash variants do not need to hit as many benchmarks. Whimsicott is guaranteed to survive Iron Head from Adamant-natured Kingambit and will almost always survive Moonblast from Mega Floette. The offensive investment allows Whimsicott to almost always 2HKO bulky Sitrus Berry Garchomp.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: When combined with Mega Floette's Fairy Aura, this SP spread allows Whimsicott to deal a large amount of damage. Whimsicott can afford to run this spread when holding Focus Sash, as Dual Wingbeat from Aerodactyl is the only attack it needs bulk to survive.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: While Whimsicott is almost never totally useless, as Encore will almost always achieve something, it struggles against Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox, as they usually don't mind being Encored and resist Moonblast from Whimsicott. Venusaur, in a similar vein, resists Moonblast and is not bothered by Encore too much. However, Moonblast can break Venusaur's Focus Sash, so attacking Venusaur can still be worthwhile. Additionally, Incineroar can pose problems for Whimsicott due to its immunity to Encore, that allows it to shrug off Moonblast, and access to Fake Out to stop Whimsicott from using Encore.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: While there are many Pokemon that appreciate Whimsicott's support and improve its performance in return, Mega Floette stands out as one of the best. Tailwind allows Mega Floette to outspeed nearly every other Pokemon barring other Tailwind-supported threats, while Fairy Aura allows Whimsicott to deal a surprisingly large amount of damage with Moonblast. Encore also helps Mega Floette beat foes it can struggle with, such as setup Corviknight and Aurora Veil Mega Froslass. Mega Charizard Y is another good partner, as Whimsicott's Tailwind lets even bulky variants outspeed Garchomp, one of Mega Charizard Y's biggest threats. Garchomp resists Weather Ball and Heat Wave, and Solar Beam isn't strong enough to take it out, but Whimsicott can bring Garchomp in range of Weather Ball with Moonblast. Garchomp itself is also a great partner, as it has a very good matchup against Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox, which Whimsicott struggles with.

  • How to Overcome Whimsicott's Weaknesses: When using Whimsicott, well-placed Encores can get its team out of many bad positions. Leveraging Whimsicott's presence on the field with Protect is also important for this, as the opponent may feel locked out of several moves while Whimsicott is present. Moves such as Aqua Jet and Aurora Veil, as well as Earth Power from Venusaur, are examples of options that require positioning around Encore. Certain moves are only used in specific situations, such as when Venusaur uses Earth Power against Glimmora or when Aqua Jet picks off a foe at low HP, while others, such as Protect, can render a Pokemon useless if it is forced to use them multiple turns in a row. As such, these moves require much more precise positioning when Whimsicott is on the field. Leveraging this pressure alongside Whimsicott's Protect and the opportunity cost of manually switching can exponentially increase Whimsicott's usefulness. The partners mentioned in the previous section can help cover Whimsicott's common switch-ins, with Garchomp beating Incineroar using Earthquake or Stomping Tantrum as well as Mega Delphox and Mega Charizard Y using Rock Slide. When facing opposing Tailwind teams, using defensive options such as an allied Incineroar or bulky Pokemon may be more consistent than attempting to win Speed ties against opposing Whimsicott and lock it into Tailwind.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Hydreigon finds its place in the metagame as an excellent Choice Scarf user, outspeeding and being a good answer to Choice Scarf Basculegion-M as well as other common Pokemon such as Garchomp, Sinistcha, Mega Froslass, Mega Delphox, and Mega Gengar. Hydreigon's typing is also helpful against Mega Charizard Y, allowing it to resist Heat Wave, sun-boosted Weather Ball, and Solar Beam while hitting it back hard with STAB Draco Meteor.

  • Earth Power vs. Heat Wave: Both Earth Power and Heat Wave can hit Steel-types, with Earth Power having the advantage of dealing more damage to Kingambit and Archaludon. On the other hand, Heat Wave being a spread move allows Hydreigon to hit Kingambit on teams that have redirection while also threatening Corviknight and Whimsicott.

  • Snarl: Snarl can weaken a plethora of special attackers, such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Floette, Archaludon, Sylveon, and Mega Dragonite. After inducing a Special Attack drop, Hydreigon can always survive Mega Froslass's Blizzard as well as Archaludon's and Mega Dragonite's Dragon Pulse.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Hydreigon to always outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Aerodactyl.

Abilities

  • Levitate: Levitate provides Hydreigon with a helpful Ground immunity, making it a good partner for Pokemon that like spamming Earthquake like Excadrill.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon are the easiest and best way to keep Hydreigon in check, always OHKOing it with their STAB moves, while it can only slow them down with Special Attack drops from Snarl. After activating Unburden with White Herb or Focus Sash, Sneasler will always outspeed Hydreigon and OHKO it with Close Combat. Sneasler can also use Fake Out on Hydreigon, which is incredibly helpful for Sneasler's teammates like Garchomp and Basculegion-M, allowing Garchomp in particular to OHKO Hydreigon with Dragon Claw. Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Corviknight are huge roadblocks for Choice Scarf Hydreigon: Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar can take any hit Hydreigon throws at them and retaliate with Low Kick or set up with Dragon Dance and Swords Dance. Alternatively, Corviknight can always survive a few Heat Waves and set up Tailwind.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Choice Scarf Hydreigon is a great piece on sand teams, as they appreciate its ability to threaten and potentially OHKO Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and most Garchomp sets, which they can struggle against. In return, Excadrill, a common feature on sand teams, threatens both Fairy- and Steel-types for Hydreigon with its STAB moves. Rotom-Wash also works well with Hydreigon, threatening damage on Corviknight as well as crippling Garchomp, Kingambit, and Mega Tyranitar with Will-O-Wisp. Mega Charizard Y is also a potential partner that appreciates Hydreigon threatening and removing Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Garchomp while helping it in return by removing Steel-types, resisting Fairy-type attacks, hitting Fairy-types especially hard with sun-boosted Weather Ball, and cleanly removing Sneasler.

  • *How to Overcome Hydreigon's Weaknesses: Hydreigon appreciates partners that can threaten and deal huge damage to the Fairy- and Steel-types that wall it. Pokemon like Sneasler, Mega Charizard Y, Hisuian Arcanine, Corviknight, and Excadrill are all great against Fairy-types; some are also great against Kingambit and opposing Corviknight. Sneasler in particular is a good Hydreigon partner, hitting most Steel-types incredibly hard with Close Combat as well as having a great matchup against Fairy-types with Dire Claw or Gunk Shot. Mega Froslass and Corviknight have a great matchup against Sneasler, with Mega Froslass being immune to Close Combat and resisting Dire Claw while hitting Sneasler hard with either of its STAB moves. Corviknight is immune to Dire Claw and removes Sneasler with Brave Bird.

• Choice Scarf Hydreigon serves as a solid speed control option and revenge killer for teams, being able to outspeed and remove the likes of Mega Gengar, Ceruledge, and non-Choice Scarf Garchomp.

  • U-turn: U-turn enables Hydreigon to keep up momentum against switch-ins it cannot threaten, such as Sylveon and Primarina.

  • Flamethrower: Flamethrower allows Hydreigon to threaten foes such as Mega Meganium, Scizor, and Kingambit.

  • Timid Timid enables Hydreigon to outspeed threats such as Choice Scarf Adamant Garchomp and Adamant Mega Charizard X after a Dragon Dance.

Other Options

Natures

-Modest: Modest lets Hydreigon always OHKO Mega Starmie and gives it a much better chance to OHKO Basculegion outright.

Offensive.description:
• Hydreigon can serve as a pivotal offensive piece for teams using its high Special Attack and solid natural Speed. Its good typing and ability enable it to safely come in against the likes of Hippowdon and Ceruledge, then proceed to break apart the opposition.

  • Flamethrower can help Hydreigon break through the likes of Corviknight and Scizor.

  • U-turn: U-turn enables Hydreigon to keep up momentum against checks such as Primarina and Sylveon.

  • Taunt: Taunt can shut down the likes of Hippowdon and Umbreon, preventing them from forcing Hydreigon out with tools like Yawn.

  • Nasty Plot: Nasty Plot enables Hydreigon to threaten OHKOs on foes such as Mega Venusaur with Draco Meteor.

  • Modest: With a Modest nature, Hydreigon can threaten an OHKO on specially defensive targets like Hippowdon and Corviknight after a Nasty Plot boost with Draco Meteor and Flamethrower, respectively.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash allows Hydreigon to trade against threats such as Sneasler and Mega Starmie with Draco Meteor and Dark Pulse, respectively.

  • White Herb: White Herb enables Hydreigon to fire off two full-power Draco Meteors in a row, potentially overwhelming a would-be check such as Umbreon.

  • Lum Berry: With a Lum Berry, Hydreigon can safely switch into Hippowdon or Umbreon going for Yawn and set up a Nasty Plot in their face.

Other Options

Natures

  • Timid: A Timid nature enables Hydreigon to outspeed threats such as Jolly Mimikyu and prevents a Speed tie with Timid Archaludon and Jolly Ceruledge.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Mega Delphox serves as a strong setup threat in the M-B metagame. Its excellent Speed enables it to outspeed and check key targets such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, Sneasler and Toxapex, and it also makes good use of its solid special bulk and typing to combat opposing Mega Evolutions like Mega Metagross and Mega Floette.

  • Psyshock vs. Psychic: Psyshock enables Mega Delphox to always 2HKO Mega Floette and Sylveon, while Psychic deals higher damage, 2HKOing Garchomp and being able to OHKO Mega Staraptor with little bulk investment before it gets a Special Defense boost. Both options cleanly handle Poison-types like Sneasler and Toxapex.

SP Spreads

  • 5 HP / 32 SpA / 29 Spe with Timid: Mega Delphox's SP spread enables it to outspeed Mega Gengar while slightly increasing its bulk, giving it good odds of surviving Kingambit's non-Black Glasses-boosted Sucker Punch with Friend Guard support and always surviving Mega Aerodactyl's Rock Slide.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Delphox is terrified of Pelipper, as Drizzle shuts down its ability to do reliable spread damage with Heat Wave, while its partners like Mega Swampert and Archaludon can easily eliminate Mega Delphox.

  • Dark-types like Incineroar and Mega Tyranitar easily take Mega Delphox's attacks and threaten to OHKO it with Darkest Lariat and Knock Off.

  • Mega Delphox struggles greatly under Trick Room, which leaves it easily picked off by the likes of Mega Mawile. Kingambit can prove to be an especially dangerous Trick Room attacker, as even outside of Trick Room, it can pick Mega Delphox off with Sucker Punch.

  • Basculegion-M can effortlessly remove Mega Delphox before it can do anything, as Basculegion-M can either use a Life Orb-boosted Aqua Jet or hit it with Wave Crash if Basculegion-M is holding Choice Scarf.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Blastoise and Mega Floette can handle the matchups Mega Delphox struggles against, with both doing wonders against Trick Room and rain teams. After a Shell Smash, Mega Blastoise easily decimates the likes of Mega Swampert and Mega Mawile, while Mega Floette obliterates Farigriaf and Archaludon with Light of Ruin. In return, both enjoy Mega Delphox handling their checks such as Mega Venusaur, Toxapex, and Mega Metagross.

  • Mega Staraptor can focus down Dark-types such as Incineroar and Kingambit for Mega Delphox while appreciating its ability to scare away foes like Toxapex, Mega Gengar, and Gholdengo.

  • Sinistcha and Maushold provide vital redirection support for Mega Delphox, enabling it to set up Nasty Plot and protecting it from Kingambit's Sucker Punch. Sinistcha can also check Water-type foes such as Mega Swampert and Milotic.

  • Kingambit can provide support with Sucker Punch to pick off faster threats aiming to eliminate Mega Delphox such as Choice Scarf Basculegion-M. It can also help Mega Delphox deal with Trick Room by removing Farigiraf before it can set up Trick Room or by outspeeding it if Trick Room goes up.

  • Garchomp can serve as an excellent partner, as it is capable of freely using Earthquake thanks to Mega Delphox's Levitate while also threatening the likes of Incineroar and Mega Tyranitar. In return, Mega Delphox can eliminate foes such as Sinistcha and Mega Froslass that pose a problem for Garchomp.

  • Sneasler can provide Fake Out support to help Mega Delphox get a Nasty Plot off; it can also use Quick Guard to block Kingambit's Sucker Punch, enabling Mega Delphox to remove it with Heat Wave.

Wallbreaker.description:
Thanks to its insanely high Speed and Special Attack as well as its solid type coverage, Mega Delphox works as one of the tier's deadliest wallbreakers and cleaners. Flamethrower is the preferred choice of Fire-type STAB move because of its perfect accuracy, but Fire Blast can be run, at the expense of that accuracy, for greater damage output, which lets Mega Delphox have a chance to 2HKO no bulk Hisuian Samurott and OHKO Careful Excadrill after Stealth Rock. Psyshock is used to deal more damage to common special walls, most notably to OHKO Galarian Slowking and 32 HP Primarina after Nasty Plot and Stealth Rock damage, as well as to OHKO Mega Dragalge after Stealth Rock. Dazzling Gleam is used to hit Dragon- and Dark-types like Hydreigon, Hisuian Samurott, and Greninja that otherwise resist or are immune to Mega Delphox's STAB moves. Substitute is a solid option that can ease prediction, avoid status from the likes of Galarian Slowking, Hatterene, and Toxapex, and avoid Sucker Punch from Hisuian Samurott and Kingambit, though it does come at the cost of either Nasty Plot's breaking potential or Dazzling Gleam's coverage. Similarly, Encore is a utility option that can be used to lock opponents into non-damaging moves, giving Delphox free turns to use Nasty Plot. It can also situationally work well in tandem with Mega Delphox's ability Levitate, locking Pokemon like Garchomp into Earthquake. Focus Blast and Grass Knot are niche coverage choices that can be used to deal with specific walls like Tyranitar, Slowbro, and Slowking. Timid is the preferred nature to outspeed Mega Raichu Y, Greninja, and Sneasler. 1 SP in Defense and HP lets Mega Delphox survive Shadow Sneak from Adamant Spell Tag Aegislash and Adamant Life Orb Ceruledge.

Mega Delphox fits best on offense, bulky offense, and balance teams that can provide ample support in the form of pivoting and entry hazard control for Mega Delphox to effectively break and clean late-game. Hence, Pokemon like Galarian Slowking and Corviknight are solid partners, as they are able to bring Mega Delphox safely onto the field using Chilly Reception and U-turn, respectively. Corviknight also supports Mega Delphox by removing Stealth Rock using Defog; similarly, other Stealth Rock removers like Excadrill and Glimmora can also make for good partners. On the other hand, Mega Delphox itself appreciates hazards that help chip the opposing team down and let Mega Delphox achieve, for instance, a guaranteed OHKO on Hisuian Samurott using Dazzling Gleam and a guaranteed OHKO on Galarian Slowking using +2 Psyshock. For that reason, Pokemon like Garchomp, Glimmora, and Hisuian Samurott are crucial teammates. Bulky partners that can deal with faster threats like Mega Lopunny and Dragapult, such as Primarina, Toxapex, and Clefable, are appreciated. Mega Delphox is often revenge killed using super effective priority moves like Shadow Sneak and Sucker Punch from Aegislash, Ceruledge, and Kingambit; therefore, Dark-types that can handle these moves like Hisuian Samurott, Hydreigon, and Meowscarda are all great teammates. Meowscarada, in particular, has amazing offensive synergy with Mega Delphox, as it has U-turn to pivot out against common Steel-type switch-ins like Corviknight, Scizor, and Mega Metagross to bring Mega Delphox in, giving Mega Delphox opportunities to either set up freely or deal a lot of damage. Meowscarada also pressures physically bulky Rotom-Wash, which Delphox may struggle against. Skeledirge is another Pokemon that walls Mega Delphox, due to Unaware, so Pokemon that can easily pressure it like Primarina, Rotom-Wash, and Hydreigon are appreciated. The former two also help in tanking Water-type attacks aimed at Mega Delphox. Finally, late-game sweepers that can take advantage of Mega Delphox weakening the opposing team like Kingambit, Dragonite, and Sneasler all work well as teammates.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Crimson Maiden (Offensive Mega).description:
• Mega Delphox works as an excellent wallbreaker, with its blazing base 134 Speed and strong STAB combination enabling it to outspeed and handle threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Charizard Y, and Corviknight without much issue.

  • Psychic-type STAB Moves: For its secondary STAB move, Mega Delphox has plenty of choice options. Psychic does the overall highest damage, allowing Mega Delphox to 2HKO Hippowdon and OHKO Mega Venusaur after Stealth Rock. However, Psyshock deals with more specially bulky targets like Primarina, while Psychic Noise can bypass the Substitute Mega Gengar loves to hide behind.

  • Dazzling Gleam: If you're looking for coverage, Dazzling Gleam serves as Mega Delphox's best option to handle pesky Dark-types such as Hydreigon and Umbreon.

  • Encore: Encore serves as Delphox's premier utility option; it locks foes such as Kingambit and Sneasler into options like Sucker Punch and Swords Dance, allowing Mega Delphox to set up a Substitute or Nasty Plot safely.

  • Nasty Plot: Nasty Plot can turn Mega Delphox's already powerful moves into immense bombs, enabling Mega Delphox to OHKO foes such as Garchomp with Psychic.

  • Substitute: Substitute can punish threats incapable of hurting Mega Delphox like Corviknight and Sylveon, allowing it to stay in on foes such as Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Mega Lopunny that could threaten it out otherwise, and can help it out against Sucker Punch users such as Kingambit and Focus Sash Meowscarada.

Other Options

  • Focus Blast: If you wish to go gambling on unreliable moves, Focus Blast serves as a much cleaner check to Dark-types overall compared to Dazzling Gleam, notably OHKOing Tyranitar and 2HKOing Umbreon.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: A very basic and standard spread, it leaves Mega Delphox lacking any real bulk but lets Mega Delphox just hit hard and fast.

  • 1 HP / 4 Def / 29 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: An overall bulkier spread that, at the cost of a small bit of damage output, grants Mega Delphox a nearly guaranteed chance to survive Choice Scarf Garchomp's Outrage.

Torrent Focus Sash.description:
• Focus Sash guarantees Greninja survives any single attack, allowing it to reliably reach the HP range needed to activate Torrent, which boosts its Water-type attacks to trade damage or secure KOs against foes it would otherwise struggle against.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse is Greninja's most reliable STAB move, pressuring Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Mega Delphox, Basculegion-M, Mega Gengar, Aegislash, and Ceruledge. Its decent flinch chance is useful after Focus Sash activates to potentially prevent Greninja from being KOed.

  • Surf versus Hydro Pump: Surf provides accurate and consistent damage against targets like Hippowdon and Glimmora. Hydro Pump is much stronger, allowing Greninja to secure crucial KOs on bulky checks like Tyranitar and Corviknight that Surf fails to pick up, though its low accuracy makes it less reliable.

  • Water Shuriken: Water Shuriken becomes incredibly threatening when boosted by Torrent, allowing Greninja to pick off faster threats that have been brought down to their Focus Sash such as Meowscarada and Sneasler.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam is crucial coverage for heavily damaging Dragon- and Ground-types such as Dragonite and Garchomp.

  • Toxic Spikes versus Taunt versus Counter: Toxic Spikes wears down checks like Umbreon and Primarina over time. Taunt shuts down defensive Pokemon like Corviknight and prevents Glimmora from setting entry hazards up. Counter allows Greninja to heavily punish physical attackers, notably securing an OHKO against Meowscarada from the lead position.

  • Modest versus Timid: A Modest nature is preferred because Focus Sash guarantees Greninja survives hits from faster attackers, which makes the extra damage output for Torrent-boosted attacks more valuable. Even without a Speed-boosting nature, Modest Greninja outspeeds Jolly Garchomp, Timid Mega Charizard Y, and Jolly Mega Kangaskhan. A Timid nature can be used to outspeed faster threats such as Adamant Meowscarada, Jolly Mega Lucario, and Sneasler.

Other Options

  • Sludge Wave: Sludge Wave can be used to hit Fairy-types such as Primarina, Mega Meganium, and Clefable, but without Protean's STAB boost and defensive type change, it is generally less justifiable for this set over other coverage options.

Protean Focus Sash.description:
• Focus Sash ensures Greninja avoids being OHKOed; this ensures it can utilize Protean to defensively pivot or offensively retaliate with STAB-boosted moves.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam is mandatory, as it provides excellent coverage for OHKOing Dragon-types like Garchomp and Mega Dragonite.

  • Sludge Wave: Sludge Wave pressures Fairy- and Grass-types such as Primarina, Mega Floette, and Meganium, with Protean also changing Greninja's typing to Poison to resist their attacks.

  • Mud Shot: Mud Shot is the primary way to punish Steel-types like Archaludon and Kingambit for super effective damage. Notably, the Speed drop acts as team support when Greninja is about to be KOed, as lowering a foe's Speed allows a teammate to come in and finish off a threat that might otherwise outspeed the rest of the team.

  • Water Shuriken: For teams that lack a priority option, Water Shuriken allows Greninja to act as a revenge killer after the Focus Sash is consumed, enabling it to pick off opposing Focus Sash users like Sneasler and Meowscarada or clean up weakened foes like Mega Gengar that would otherwise outspeed and KO it.

  • Toxic Spikes: Toxic Spikes provides good utility against bulkier teams and allows Greninja to wear down defensive foes like Umbreon and Primarina that it cannot break through directly, providing support for the rest of the team to clean up later.

  • Modest versus Timid: With a Modest nature, Greninja remains faster than threats such as Garchomp, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Kangaskhan. A Timid nature is an alternative option if moving first against faster Pokemon like Meowscarada, Mega Lucario, and Sneasler is more important than the extra power.

All-out Attacker.description:
• Greninja uses its excellent Speed, Protean-boosted coverage, and either Greninjite or Choice Scarf to revenge kill offensive threats and pressure teams with its endless range of coverage.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam is one of Greninja's most important attacks, dealing heavy damage to Dragon- and Ground-types such as Garchomp, Dragonite, and Hydreigon.

  • Sludge Wave: Sludge Wave lets Greninja pressure Fairy- and Grass-types such as Mega Floette, Primarina, Sylveon, Mega Clefable, and Mega Meganium.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse gives Greninja a reliable attack against Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Mega Gengar, Aegislash, Mega Delphox, and Ceruledge.

  • Hydro Pump versus Surf: Hydro Pump is preferred on Greninjite sets for its higher damage output, notably giving Greninja a stronger attack against Hippowdon. Surf is weaker but more accurate, making it more reliable when Greninja needs to revenge kill without risking a miss.

  • Low Kick versus Grass Knot versus U-turn: Low Kick lets Greninja punish heavier Dark- and Steel-types such as Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Archaludon while also chipping Snorlax, Mega Kangaskhan, and Mega Lucario hard. Meanwhile, Grass Knot is Greninja's strongest option against Hippowdon and Basculegion-M while also hitting Mega Blastoise hard. U-turn is especially useful on Choice Scarf sets, letting Greninja pivot out of unfavorable matchups and keep momentum against switch-ins like Umbreon, Mega Scizor, and Gyarados.

  • Mega Evolving Greninja: Greninjite sets do not always need to Mega Evolve immediately, as staying in base forme gives Greninja one extra Protean type change before Mega Evolving. This can help Greninja play around foes' attacks or boost the power of a specific coverage move, but delaying Mega Evolution also means giving up Mega Greninja's improved stats for that turn.

Items

  • Greninjite versus Choice Scarf: Mega Greninja boasts the freedom to switch moves and better immediate attacking stats, making it harder for opponents to play around its coverage. Choice Scarf's extra Speed gives Greninja stronger revenge killing utility, letting it outspeed boosted threats that Mega Greninja cannot.

Other Options

  • Extrasensory: Extrasensory can be used to hit Mega Venusaur and the uncommon Toxapex, which otherwise handles many of Greninja's common coverage options.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide can be used on mixed sets to counter Mega Charizard Y, notably OHKOing maximum HP variants even with a negative Attack nature. However, fitting it means giving up one of Greninja's more useful coverage moves.

SP Spreads

  • 8 HP / 32 SpA / 26 Spe with Timid or Naive: This spread lets Mega Greninja outspeed Mega Lopunny while giving it a decent chance to survive Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp's Outrage. A Naive nature should be used on mixed sets to avoid weakening physical coverage moves such as Low Kick.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest or Rash: This spread maximizes Greninja's Speed and Special Attack investment, giving Mega Greninja's Hydro Pump and Grass Knot the power to OHKO specially defensive Hippowdon. A Rash nature should be used on mixed sets to avoid weakening physical coverage moves such as Rock Slide.

Offensive Support.description:
• Talonflame can consistently set the pace of the battle due to the priority boost on Tailwind granted by Gale Wings. Gale Wings also gives it immediate offensive pressure with its primary STAB Flying-type moves. With its high Speed, Talonflame can threaten many prominent Pokemon like Kingambit, Sneasler, and Whimsicott with its STAB Fire- and Flying-type attacks.

  • Flare Blitz vs. Will-O-Wisp: Flare Blitz can threaten large damage onto Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Mega Froslass, while Will-O-Wisp provides damage reduction against physical attackers like Garchomp and Corviknight. Furthermore, Will-O-Wisp and Flare Blitz are Talonflame's only ways to pressure Kingambit and Aegislash.

  • Brave Bird vs. Dual Wingbeat vs. Acrobatics: Brave Bird, when boosted by Gale Wings, becomes a powerful priority attack, giving Talonflame immediate pressure. It is much stronger than Dual Wingbeat and Acrobatics, as only Brave Bird can OHKO Scovillain. However, Dual Wingbeat can also be valuable due to its ability to KO Pokemon such as Sneasler and Whimsicott through Focus Sash without breaking Gale Wings. Finally, the lack of recoil damage from Acrobatics allows no-item Talonflame to threaten heavy Flying-type damage without deactivating Gale Wings.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt can be used over Flare Blitz or Will-O-Wisp for an extra tool against Trick Room teams. Furthermore, Taunt can be used to disrupt redirectors like Maushold and Sinistcha as well as setup Pokemon such as Calm Mind Mega Floette.

  • Quick Guard: Quick Guard is a niche move that can be used over Protect, Flare Blitz, or Will-O-Wisp. It protects allies against Fake Out users like Incineroar as well as other priority attacks like Aqua Jet from Basculegion-M and Sucker Punch from Kingambit.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Pokemon with Intimidate, such as Incineroar, severely weaken Talonflame's damage output. Rock Slide users like Garchomp, Tyranitar, and Aerodactyl are strong checks to Talonflame, as they are able to OHKO it. Garchomp is notable, as Rough Skin breaks Gale Wings regardless of what Flying-type move Talonflame is carrying. Furthermore, Mega Tyranitar's sand works similarly in breaking Gale Wings. Archaludon is also a great check to Talonflame, resisting its Flying-type moves and boosting up with Stamina. Fake Out users like Incineroar can break Talonflame's Gale Wings, removing the option to use priority Tailwind.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp and Mega Floette are some of the best Pokemon to pair Talonflame with. Talonflame's priority Tailwind and immunity to Earthquake allows Garchomp to put immense pressure on opponents. Additionally, Garchomp's Rock Slide in Tailwind lets it act as a great check against prominent Mega Charizard Y compositions by always outspeeding Mega Charizard Y in Tailwind. Mega Floette and Mega Gardevoir also benefit greatly from Tailwind, and Talonflame's STAB moves cover Sneasler and Kingambit for both. In return, their STAB Fairy-type moves handle Dragon-types like Garchomp and Dragonite. Kingambit discourages Pokemon with Intimidate from switching in with Defiant and provides high priority damage with Sucker Punch, which can OHKO opposing Basculegion-M. Finally, Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can take advantage of Tailwind by capitalizing on its powerful STAB attacks to KO threats such as Mega Aerodactyl. Additionally, bulky variants with Sitrus Berry or Mystic Water can use Tailwind to outspeed Mega Charizard Y, Mega Froslass, and Mega Gengar.

  • How to Overcome Talonflame's Weaknesses: Protecting Talonflame and preserving Gale Wings is a viable strategy against other Tailwind setters such as Aerodactyl and Whimsicott. Another viable strategy is to preserve Gale Wings for late-game scenarios, mainly by manually switching out. Kingambit can be used to threaten Basculegion-M and Mega Aerodactyl, which would otherwise use Aqua Jet or Rock Slide on Talonflame. Mega Floette also helps Talonflame, as its Light Of Ruin can quickly KO Archaludon and Garchomp.

Redirection Support.description:
• Vivillon is a fast supporter that gives offensive teams both disruption and redirection, forcing opponents to respect Compound Eyes-boosted Sleep Powder while using Rage Powder to protect teammates trying to set up or attack. These give it a niche different from bulkier redirection users such as Sinistcha and Maushold. Vivillon is useful next to teammates such as Mega Blastoise, Farigiraf, Kingambit, and Basculegion-M, which appreciate Vivillon creating openings without giving up too much offensive momentum.

  • Sleep Powder: Sleep Powder is Vivillon's main disruption tool, preventing a foe from acting and giving its partner room to set up or attack the other foe. Compound Eyes makes it reliable enough to threaten metagame staples such as Incineroar, Farigiraf, Kingambit, and Mega Charizard Y.

  • Hurricane: Hurricane prevents Vivillon from being completely passive after using its support moves, pressuring targets such as Sneasler, Kommo-o, Mega Venusaur, and Sinistcha. Even without Special Attack investment, Hurricane has a chance to OHKO Sneasler and always 2HKOes Kommo-o and Mega Venusaur. Hurricane also gives Vivillon something meaningful to do when Sleep Powder is blocked by Grass-types.

  • Pollen Puff versus Rain Dance versus Protect: Pollen Puff gives Vivillon a way to heal partners such as Mega Blastoise, Kingambit, and Basculegion-M after redirecting or forcing a sleep turn. Rain Dance is mainly for teams with Mega Blastoise or Basculegion-M, strengthening their Water-type attacks while removing sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal. Protect should only be used on Focus Sash sets, as this lets Vivillon avoid Fake Out, stall opposing Pokemon's speed control, or preserve itself to use its powder moves later.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf is preferred to make Vivillon a fast disruptor, letting it outspeed threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Aerodactyl, Sneasler, Mega Froslass, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M before putting them to sleep with Sleep Powder. However, being locked into Rage Powder or Sleep Powder can make Vivillon exploitable, especially if the opponent has Grass-types, which are immune to both moves, or spread attackers that can ignore Rage Powder.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash trades Choice Scarf's Speed for more flexible move use, letting Vivillon switch between support and offense more freely. It is especially useful if Vivillon needs to survive a strong attack and still redirect an attack or put a foe to sleep, but it leaves Vivillon vulnerable to faster threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Aerodactyl, and other Choice Scarf users.

Abilities

  • Compound Eyes: Compound Eyes makes Sleep Powder and Hurricane accurate enough for Vivillon to reliably disrupt and threaten Pokemon such as Sneasler, Incineroar, Farigiraf, Kingambit, and Mega Charizard Y. It also makes Hurricane much safer to use, letting Vivillon consistently punish targets like Sneasler, Kommo-o, Sinistcha, and Whimsicott instead of being limited to support moves. Compound Eyes is especially important on Choice Scarf sets, where missing Sleep Powder can make Vivillon's team lose a lot of momentum by giving the target a free turn to attack, set speed control, or reposition.

  • Friend Guard: Friend Guard can be used on Focus Sash sets if Vivillon's teammates value extra damage reduction, especially against spread moves that Rage Powder cannot redirect. However, losing Compound Eyes makes Sleep Powder and Hurricane much less reliable, so Friend Guard is usually worse.

SP Spreads

  • 24 Def / 5 SpA / 5 SpD / 32 Spe with Timid: This bulkier spread is mainly for Choice Scarf Vivillon. It keeps maximum Speed investment to outspeed key fast threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Froslass, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, as well as getting the jump on Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp. The defensive investment lets Vivillon survive Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Sylveon's Hyper Voice, and it gives Vivillon an extremely good chance to survive Jolly Talonflame's Dual Wingbeat. Focus Sash sets can also consider this spread if they want to avoid being KOed by Talonflame's Dual Wingbeat.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Vivillon relies heavily on Sleep Powder to force progress, so Pokemon that can ignore Sleep Powder are its biggest obstacles. Sinistcha and Whimsicott are immune to Sleep Powder entirely. Whimsicott can use Prankster Encore to lock non-Choice Scarf Vivillon into Rage Powder, Sleep Powder, or Protect, while Sinistcha can set or remove Trick Room to disrupt Vivillon's team. Fake Out from Pokemon such as Sneasler, Incineroar, and Mega Kangaskhan can stop Vivillon before it uses its powder moves, which is especially punishing for Choice Scarf sets because they can't use Protect. Tailwind robs Vivillon much of its Speed advantage and makes it easier to KO. Gale Wings Talonflame is particularly threatening, as it can set priority-boosted Tailwind and can also threaten Vivillon directly with Flying-type STAB moves. Vivillon is also weak against strong spread damage moves, as Rage Powder cannot redirect moves like Garchomp's and Aerodactyl's Rock Slide, Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave, Sylveon's Hyper Voice, and Mega Froslass's Blizzard. Rock-types can be major problems for Vivillon because they resist Hurricane, while Rock Slide hits it extremely effectively, bypasses Rage Powder, and pressures its partner all at the same time. Aerodactyl outspeeds non-Choice Scarf Vivillon and can KO Vivillon through Focus Sash or set Tailwind, and Mega Tyranitar can nullify Vivillon's Focus Sash with sand chip damage. Sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal makes Hurricane much less reliable, limiting Vivillon's ability to deal respectable damage.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Vivillon should be paired with teammates that can immediately take advantage of the free turns it creates with its powder moves. Farigiraf is one of Vivillon's best partners, as Armor Tail blocks Fake Out, which would otherwise stop Vivillon from using Sleep Powder. In return, Vivillon can help Farigiraf set Trick Room through Rage Powder or by putting a foe to sleep. Mega Blastoise is one of Vivillon's strongest partners, as Vivillon's powder moves can create opportunities for it to use Shell Smash, while Pollen Puff can restore its HP to keep Water Spout strong. Rain Dance also strengthens Water Spout and removes sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal. Basculegion-M similarly appreciates Rain Dance support, while Rage Powder can redirect Kingambit's Sucker Punch and give it safer turns to use Wave Crash or Last Respects. Sneasler threatens Rock- and Steel-types such as Mega Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Archaludon, which Vivillon struggles to damage. Incineroar can weaken physical attackers with Intimidate, which is especially useful for Choice Scarf Vivillon because Intimidate allows it to sometimes survive attacks it normally could not, such as Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. Additionally, Incineroar's Parting Shot can bring Vivillon or one of its offensive partners onto the field more safely. Kingambit appreciates Vivillon pressuring Fighting-types such as Sneasler and Kommo-o with Hurricane, while Vivillon can redirect Fighting-type attacks that threaten Kingambit. Mega Floette and Sylveon can pressure some Rock Slide users such as Mega Tyranitar and Garchomp with Fairy-type spread damage, while Vivillon helps them by threatening Sneasler with Hurricane and disrupting faster threats with Sleep Powder.

  • How to Overcome Vivillon's Weaknesses: Vivillon should avoid trying to use its powder moves against teams that can easily counter it. If Grass-types such as Sinistcha or Whimsicott are on the field, Hurricane is usually the better option, while Rage Powder should be saved for turns where it enables Vivillon's partner to attack or set up safely. Armor Tail from Farigiraf blocks Fake Out, Whimsicott's Prankster Encore, and Talonflame's Gale Wings Flying-type attacks while also letting Farigiraf set Trick Room in front of Tailwind teams. Incineroar can help Vivillon by using Fake Out to stop one foe while Vivillon puts the other to sleep. Because Rage Powder cannot redirect spread damage, Vivillon needs partners that can pressure common spread attackers directly. Mega Blastoise and Basculegion-M threaten Rock Slide and Heat Wave users such as Aerodactyl, Mega Charizard Y, and Torkoal, while Kingambit pressures Mega Froslass, Sylveon, and Mega Floette. Teammates such as Mega Blastoise, Basculegion-M, and Kingambit can pressure Rock-types like Mega Aerodactyl and Tyranitar, limiting their opportunities to force Vivillon out.

Sun Attacker.description:
• Mega Pyroar is a devastating sun attacker in Regulation M-B, taking advantage of Fire Mane and the sun to deal monstrous amounts of damage. Mega Pyroar's typing makes it immune to Basculegion-M's Last Respects and resistant to Gholdengo's and Mega Charizard Y's main STAB attacks as well as Fairy-type attacks from Mega Floette, Mega Gardevoir, and Sylveon.

  • Overheat: Overheat allows Mega Pyroar to OHKO nearly everything in the metagame with enough damage multipliers, including Pokemon that may resist Overheat, such as Incineroar and Garchomp.

  • Solar Beam: Solar Beam is used to hit Water-types like Basculegion-M, Mega Blastoise, and Mega Swampert for super effective damage.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Pelipper and Politoed can decrease Mega Pyroar's damage output with Drizzle while threatening it with rain-boosted Weather Ball. Rain allows Mega Swampert to outspeed and threaten Mega Pyroar with either STAB attack while denying Solar Beam as a coverage option.

  • Focus Sash Sneasler can survive one attack from Mega Pyroar and OHKO it back with Close Combat. Unburden-boosted Sneasler can also outspeed and OHKO Mega Pyroar. Sneasler's Fake Out can also slow down Mega Pyroar's momentum.

  • Garchomp and Basculegion-M resist Mega Pyroar's Fire-type moves while threatening to OHKO it with Life Orb-boosted Earthquake and Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash, respectively.

  • Mega Aerodactyl can outspeed Mega Pyroar, survive a sun- and Fire Mane-boosted Overheat, block Heat Wave with Wide Guard, 2HKO Mega Pyroar with Rock Slide, and set up Tailwind for other Mega Pyroar checks such as Garchomp to outspeed it. Mega Tyranitar can shut off the sun, reducing Mega Pyroar's damage output while resisting its Fire-type attacks and threatening it with Rock Slide.

  • Ceruledge soaks up Mega Pyroar's Fire-type attacks while resisting Solar Beam. Ceruledge also takes advantage of the sun while setting up with Bulk Up in the face of Mega Pyroar. Notably, at +1 Attack, Bitter Blade in the sun 2HKOes Mega Pyroar.

  • Choice Scarf Hydreigon resists all of Mega Pyroar's moves while outspeeding it and weakening it with Snarl or threatening it with Earth Power. Mega Dragonite also resists all of Mega Pyroar's moves while setting up Tailwind in its face and chunking it with Dragon Pulse.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Torkoal enables Mega Pyroar's immense damage output with Drought. It also provides a Trick Room mode with Farigiraf as well as Helping Hand support, allowing Mega Pyroar to OHKO no-bulk Garchomp and Impish Incineroar with Overheat and 2HKO most Mega Charizard Y sets with Heat Wave if sun is up.

  • Farigiraf nullifies Fake Out, preventing it from stalling out Mega Pyroar's sun turns or disrupting its momentum, and can set up Trick Room for Mega Pyroar's partner Torkoal. Farigiraf can OHKO Sneasler through Focus Sash with Twin Beam and threaten Water-types like Pelipper, Politoed, and Basculegion-M with Thunderbolt.

  • Venusaur threatens Basculegion-M with Solar Beam and can put foes to sleep with Sleep Powder. Whimsicott gives Mega Pyroar speed control with Tailwind and weather control with Sunny Day. Whimsicott resists both of Garchomp's STAB attacks while chunking it with Moonblast. Vileplume also utilizes Sleep Powder but has access to After You, allowing allied Torkoal to fire off Eruption almost immediately. However, Vileplume is forced to run Focus Sash and does not hit as hard as Venusaur.

  • Mega Floette can threaten the Dragon-types that may hinder Mega Pyroar with Fairy Aura-boosted Dazzling Gleam and Moonblast.

Offensive.description:
• Mega Floette's high Special Defense and Special Attack stats allow it to be a strong Calm Mind sweeper, with decent physical bulk to patch matchups against Pokemon such as Sneasler and Kingambit. Its Fairy Aura ability allows it to threaten Garchomp, Mega Tyranitar, and Dragonite even without any boosts. Mega Floette's respectable base Speed can also allow it to outspeed Mega Charizard Y and Speed tie with Garchomp.

  • ** Moonblast vs. Draining Kiss**: Moonblast allows Mega Floette to OHKO uninvested Sneasler most of the time, as well as 2HKOing Archaludon. It consistently deals high damage, whereas Draining Kiss needs Calm Mind boosts to really be effective, notably failing to OHKO Garchomp without any boosts. However, Draining Kiss can allow Mega Floette to recover some health after spending time setting up. This can allow it to take an attack like Dire Claw from Sneasler without being permanently crippled.

  • Calm Mind vs. Light of Ruin: Calm Mind allows Mega Floette to become very hard to remove for metagame threats such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Raichu Y, and Archaludon. The offensive boost allows Mega Floette to OHKO Kingambit with Moonblast at +1 and almost always 2HKO specially defensive Incineroar with Dazzling Gleam at +1. Light of Ruin can allow it to OHKO threats such as Archaludon and Kingambit, as well as dealing devastating damage to even resisted targets, such as Mega Gengar. Light of Ruin deals similar damage to +1 Moonblast but has considerable consequences to Mega Floette's longevity on the field due to the large amount of recoil damage.

SP Spreads

  • 10 HP / 32 Def / 15 SpA / 9 Spe with Modest: This spread allows Mega Floette to outspeed all Adamant non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and almost always OHKO bulky Basculegion-M with Moonblast at +1. It is also able to OHKO Kingambit with Moonblast at +1 while always surviving Iron Head from the aforementioned Kingambit and Dire Claw from Sneasler.

  • 10 HP / 17 Def / 23 SpA / 16 Spe with Modest: The extra Speed investment allows Mega Floette to outrun Modest Archaludon and Jolly Mega Tyranitar while still surviving Dire Claw from Jolly Sneasler.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest or Timid: This spread pairs well with Whimsicott's Tailwind, as Mega Floette needs to move first to account for the lack of defensive investment. Whimsicott is usually chosen over a different Tailwind setter like Aerodactyl due to Whimsicott's synergy with Mega Floette's Fairy Aura.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Given Mega Floette's lack of coverage, it struggles to deal with Poison- and Fire-types such as Glimmora and Mega Charizard Y, the former of which is also able to 2HKO it with Sludge Bomb. Physical threats such as Kingambit and Sneasler, which have their Fairy-type weakness covered by their secondary typing, can provide issues for Mega Floette due to its mediocre Defense. Basculegion-M, especially Mystic Water variants, are able to deal massive damage to Floette-E with Wave Crash.

  • Opposing Mega Evolutions: Mega Charizard Y can overpower Mega Floette despite any boosts provided by Calm Mind due to the power boost from the sun, while Mega Delphox is able to resist its attacks and hit through Special Defense boosts with Psyshock. Mega Metagross can OHKO Mega Floette with Iron Head, and Mega Gengar can trap it on the field and 2HKO it with Sludge Bomb. Mega Mawile resists Floette-E's moves and can retaliate with Iron Head while also being able to use Fairy Aura against its partners with Play Rough. Mega Swampert can deal huge damage to Floette-E with rain-boosted Wave Crash.

  • Other Threats: Toxapex is able to use its high Special Defense alongside its Poison typing to stall out Mega Floette, dealing fixed damage with Infestation and Toxic. This is especially strong against Calm Mind sets, as they usually lack an immediately strong single-target move in the form of Light of Ruin, which could deal a respectable chunk of damage to Toxapex. Calm Mind sets also need to worry about Whimsicott, as its Encore can lock Mega Floette into an unfortunate move choice such as Calm Mind or an unboosted Draining Kiss. Whimsicott's Encore also cannot be redirected by an allied Rage Powder user such as Sinistcha. Furthermore, Steel-types such as Gholdengo and Excadrill are able to play around Calm Mind's Special Defense boosts through either Nasty Plot or physical attacks and OHKO Mega Floette with Make It Rain and Iron Head while resisting its attacks.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Calm Mind Mega Floette appreciates partners that can support its longevity, such as Incineroar with Intimidate and Fake Out and Sinistcha with Hospitality and Life Dew. Sinistcha is also able to set Trick Room, which can allow Mega Floette to outspeed faster threats such as Sneasler, Mega Swampert in the rain, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M. Meanwhile, Incineroar is able to use Flare Blitz to OHKO most Gholdengo and Whimsicott. In addition to its offensive presence, Incineroar's defensive typing allows it to take on Mega Delphox, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Metagross or weaken them with Parting Shot and, in Metagross's case, Intimidate.

  • Specialized Needs: Non-Calm Mind Mega Floette wants to be paired up with other offensive Pokemon, such as Basculegion-M and Kingambit, which are able to cover for Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar, respectively. Both of them also boast a good matchup against Mega Metagross. This set also appreciates speed control, such as Tailwind from Whimsicott. Whimsicott shares an extra synergy with Mega Floette, as Fairy Aura can allow Whimsicott to reach benchmarks such as a 2HKO on uninvested Basculegion-M with Moonblast. Additionally, Fairy Aura-boosted Moonblast from Whimsicott combined with Light of Ruin from Mega Floette can KO Glimmora before it can move if Tailwind is up. Other strong partners are Farigiraf, which also provides speed control and covers Poison-types, and Glimmora, which is able to OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Power Gem.

  • Partner Mega Evolutions: Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox are great partners for Mega Floette, as they can be used in matchups that it struggles with such as Mega Metagross, Mega Mawile, and Mega Venusaur. Floette-E can be used against Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar, Mega Staraptor, and Mega Dragonite, Pokemon that Charizard or Delphox would struggle against. Mega Raichu Y fulfills a similar role, being able to take on opposing Mega Charizard Y, Toxapex, and non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M.

Bulky Calm Mind.description:
Mega Floette can run heavy Defense investment to leverage its fantastic defensive typing and multiple recovery options to act as a durable tank and sweeper. This bulk investment allows Mega Floette to avoid OHKOs from threatening attacks such as Sneasler's Dire Claw and Blaziken's Flare Blitz and then strike back. Calm Mind increases Draining Kiss's recovery and makes Mega Floette extremely difficult to take down on the special side. Synthesis acts as a secondary recovery option to help against threats that take little damage from Draining Kiss such as Galarian Slowking and Mega Delphox. Moonblast is a strong secondary attacking option with much higher damage output than Draining Kiss. It helps take down weakened threats before they can act or simply punches holes into frailer teams with no solid switch-in, scoring an OHKO on offensive Garchomp and Annihilape while having a small chance to OHKO uninvested Archaludon. Alternatively, Substitute and Misty Terrain prevent poison spreaders such as Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge from putting Mega Floette on a timer; this preparation may allow Mega Floette to beat Galarian Slowking.

This bulky Mega Floette variant can act as a solid switch-in to a wide array of key Pokemon such as Annihilape, Hisuian Samurott, most Garchomp variants, and Mega Lopunny. Balance and bulky offense teams especially enjoy Mega Floette's ability to both defensively answer Dark- and Fighting-types and easily threaten a sweep once key defensive answers such as Galarian Slowking, Toxapex, and Skeledirge are KOed. Mega Floette needs teammates that can put pressure on defensive Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon, especially Galarian Slowking and Toxapex. As such, Ground-type teammates such as Garchomp, Excadrill, and Hippowdon, are necessary. Dark-type attackers such as Hydreigon and Hisuian Samurott are able to put pressure on Galarian Slowking and Skeledirge, and the latter may set Spikes through Ceaseless Edge, chipping at grounded Steel-type foes such as Excadrill, Aegislash, and Mega Metagross. In return, Mega Floette can switch into Fighting-type attacks that threaten them. Hisuian Samurott is also capable of threatening a weakened Mega Metagross with Sucker Punch or Choice Scarf Ceaseless Edge. Mega Metagross is an extremely dangerous threat as a balance breaker that also beats Mega Floette. As such, Hippowdon is one of Mega Floette's best teammates as one of the few reliable switch-ins to Mega Metagross while threatening a strong Earthquake against Steel- and Poison-type foes. Since Mega Floette is particularly vulnerable to all entry hazards that can make it unable to switch into various attackers, hazard removal in the form of Corviknight, Scizor, or Excadrill is important; these Pokemon also switch into Poison- and Steel-type attacks. Grounded Poison-type teammates, such as Galarian Slowking, Toxapex, and Sneasler, can reliably clear Toxic Spikes, which otherwise heavily undermines Mega Floette's staying power. While decent with investment, Mega Floette's physical bulk is too low to reliably take on strong physical attackers that can hit Mega Floette for neutral or super effective damage such as offensive Garchomp, Mega Scizor, Sneasler, and Blaziken. Therefore, secondary physical walls such as Hippowdon and Corviknight for the first three, as well as Slowbro for Blaziken, alleviate a lot of pressure.

X: Life Giver (Bulky Setup).description:
• Mega Floette's deceptively decent bulk and access to Fairy Aura-boosted Draining Kiss make it an incredibly sturdy late-game sweeper on bulky offense teams, as it's able to quickly snowball into high damage and healing. However, its shallow movepool means that it typically needs opposing Pokemon that resist its Fairy-type STAB attacks to be weakened beforehand.

  • Calm Mind + Draining Kiss: The combination of Calm Mind and Draining Kiss gives Mega Floette amazing longevity, letting it set up on and subsequently defeat even special attackers that hit it super effectively like Archaludon.

  • Moonblast: Moonblast is more immediately threatening than Draining Kiss, giving Mega Floette a consistent damaging option in situations where it's unable to boost its Special Attack. Moonblast is also particularly useful for picking off Pokemon that have already been weakened by Draining Kiss but would not be KOed by the weaker move.

  • Light of Ruin: Light of Ruin is a nuclear option that provides similar offensive utility to Moonblast. Owing to its higher Base Power, it's a lot more potent for closing out games than Moonblast—for example, Light of Ruin can always OHKO Basculegion-M and has a good chance of doing the same to maximum HP Kingambit—though its recoil damage can make Mega Floette more prone to being revenge killed.

  • Synthesis: Synthesis provides consistent healing, granting more time for Mega Floette to boost its stats before Draining Kiss can threaten the opponent's Pokemon. Synthesis can also be used to stall out Mega Charizard Y's sun if needed, buying an opportunity for Mega Floette to set up.

Other Options

  • Psychic: Psychic has a niche use in giving Mega Floette a way to deal with defensive Poison-types—in particular Toxapex, which otherwise can shrug off its Fairy-type attacks and remove its stat boosts with Haze—though giving up the consistent offensive power of Moonblast or Light of Ruin can greatly limit its damage output in situations where it can't use Calm Mind.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 29 Def / 5 SpA with Modest: This spread aims to patch Mega Floette's lower physical bulk, ensuring Garchomp's Earthquake is a 3HKO, while the investment in Special Attack allows it to always OHKO even maximum HP sets in return with a +1 Draining Kiss.

Y: Life Taker (Offensive).description:
• With enough Speed to outpace common threats like Mega Dragonite and both of Charizard's Mega Evolutions, as well as Speed tying with Garchomp, Mega Floette can act as a powerful sweeper capable of doing immense damage with Fairy Aura-boosted Moonblast and Light of Ruin.

  • Moonblast versus Draining Kiss: Mega Floette greatly appreciates the additional damage provided by Moonblast, notably OHKOing offensive Archaludon and all Garchomp sets without needing to use Calm Mind, though Draining Kiss can still be useful to help Mega Floette avoid being worn down especially if you're choosing to forgo Synthesis.

  • Psychic: Psychic gives Mega Floette an option to hit Poison-types that would otherwise wall it, notably 2HKOing physically defensive Mega Venusaur and OHKOing Mega Gengar after Stealth Rock damage, though be aware that Mega Gengar has a good chance of OHKOing Mega Floette itself with Sludge Wave if it hasn't already buffed its Special Defense.

  • Substitute: Mega Floette can use Substitute to take advantage of passive Pokemon like Umbreon and Hippowdon that lack Whirlwind by blocking their status moves, letting it set up with Calm Mind. Substitute can also be useful to prevent being worn down by Fake Out cycling from the likes of Mega Lopunny and Sneasler.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Aegislash solidifies its place in the metagame as a prominent answer to Fairy-types, helping check Sylveon and Mega Floette while being immune to Fake Out and walling Sneasler. Aegislash takes advantage of its high offensive and defensive capabilities to tank an attack and retaliate with its powerful STAB moves and Fighting-type coverage. It also picks off weakened foes with access to Shadow Sneak.

  • Iron Head versus Fighting-type coverage: Iron Head makes it easier for Aegislash to remove Fairy-types like Sylveon and Mega Floette, while Fighting-type coverage helps Aegislash deal with Dark- and Steel-types, most commonly Kingambit.

  • Close Combat versus Sacred Sword: Sacred Sword is preferred for the bulkier set because it avoids the defensive drawback of Close Combat, and it can be useful against Archaludon to bypass its Stamina boosts. Close Combat is generally better, especially for the glass cannon set, as it deals more damage than Sacred Sword, notably allowing Aegislash to OHKO Hydreigon.

  • King's Shield versus Wide Guard: King's Shield is typically preferred, as it not only shields Aegislash from attacks but also allows it to switch back to Shield forme after attacking. Wide Guard can be used on the Focus Sash set because Aegislash is already guaranteed to survive an attack, so it does not need to switch formes often. Wide Guard also protects both Aegislash and its teammates from moves like Rock Slide and Earthquake from Garchomp and Heat Wave from Mega Charizard Y.

Items

  • Spell Tag: Spell Tag greatly boosts the power of Poltergeist and Shadow Sneak, allowing Aegislash to OHKO physically defensive non-Kasib Berry Sinistcha with Poltergeist and KO uninvested Garchomp with the combination of Poltergeist and Shadow Sneak.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash allows Aegislash to withstand a powerful attack such as Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave or Weather Ball in the sun.

Abilities

  • Stance Change: After Aegislash attacks, it is extremely vulnerable because its Blade forme has low defenses. This means that it must often alternate between attacking and using King's Shield to change formes. Additionally, using priority Shadow Sneak can be dangerous, since it leaves Aegislash vulnerable before foes have had a chance to attack.

SP Spreads

  • 27 HP / 32 Atk / 7 Spe with Adamant: The Speed investment allows Aegislash to outrun Adamant Sneasler and Modest Mega Froslass in Tailwind. The remaining SPs are invested in HP and Attack to maximize its damage output and ability to take hits.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This SP spread should only be used with a Focus Sash set because it neglects bulk in favor of striking first. The speed investment notably allows Aegislash to outspeed uninvested Archaludon and, in Tailwind, Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Aerodactyl.

  • 32 HP / 11 Atk / 23 Spe with Adamant: The Speed investment allows Aegislash to outspeed Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar in Tailwind. The remaining SPs are invested in HP and Attack, but with more investment in HP because Spell Tag Aegislash already secures the OHKOs it needs, including an OHKO on most bulky Mega Gengar variants with Poltergeist even at -1.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Kingambit can be problematic for Aegislash, even for variants that run Fighting-type coverage, as Kingambit often has Chople Berry, allowing it to survive the hit and OHKO Aegislash in return with Kowtow Cleave while Aegislash is in Blade forme. Few threats can outright OHKO Aegislash in Shield forme from full HP, but exceptions include Mega Charizard Y with Heat Wave or Weather Ball in sun and Basculegion-M with a 100-Base Power Last Respects. Garchomp is not a full counter, but it deals a hefty amount of damage with its Ground-type STAB moves, and Aegislash cannot even 2HKO Sitrus Berry variants.

  • Maushold is one of the more problematic support Pokemon for Aegislash because it is immune to Ghost-type attacks and commonly uses either Chople Berry or Focus Sash, forcing Aegislash to attack it twice and leaving Aegislash vulnerable for longer. Additionally, Maushold can lock Aegislash into King's Shield with Encore, preventing it from switching to Shield forme unpunished. In general, Aegislash struggles because its need to switch between Blade and Shield formes is predictable. Mega Scovillain is another redirector that Aegislash struggles against because Aegislash's offensive presence is greatly diminished by the burn from Spicy Spray, and Mega Scovillain also threatens an OHKO with Overheat. Intimidate from Incineroar is also quite troublesome for Aegislash, as it reduces the value Aegislash gets from its attacking turns. In addition, Parting Shot bypasses King's Shield, and if Incineroar is slower, it can also threaten to OHKO Aegislash with its STAB attacks while Aegislash is in Blade forme. Aegislash can struggle against Pokemon that are itemless or have already used their item. Talonflame may choose to run no item, while common Pokemon like Garchomp and Sinistcha can consume their Sitrus Berry or resist Berry. This prevents Aegislash from hitting them with Poltergeist, which is its most powerful option.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Aerodactyl and Pelipper can provide Tailwind support, allowing Aegislash to reach the previously mentioned Speed benchmarks. They also help against Mega Charizard Y, with Aerodactyl threatening it with Rock Slide and Pelipper able to change the weather upon switching in, weaken its Fire-type attacks, and threaten an OHKO with Weather Ball. Garchomp is one of Aegislash's best partners because it threatens Kingambit and Incineroar with its Ground-type STAB attacks, and it often carries Rock Slide to pressure Mega Charizard Y. In return, Aegislash resists attacks from and threatens Ice- and Fairy-types such as Mega Froslass and Sylveon, which would otherwise OHKO Garchomp. Additionally, Garchomp can freely use Earthquake when paired with Wide Guard Aegislash. Mega Floette also pairs well with Aegislash, as it threatens opposing Garchomp, which can deal significant damage to Aegislash. In return, Aegislash handles Sneasler, one of Mega Floette's biggest threats. Furthermore, unlike Aegislash, Mega Floette is not hindered by Intimidate, making it a strong offensive partner. Mega Charizard Y can also pair well with Aegislash, as it can threaten Kingambit as well as OHKO most Maushold with Weather Ball. Rotom-Wash is another solid partner, as it can use Will-O-Wisp to cripple physical threats such as Garchomp and Kingambit while pressuring Basculegion-M and Incineroar with Thunderbolt and Hydro Pump, respectively. In return, Aegislash can handle Pokemon like Sinistcha that wall Rotom-Wash, and it can pick off weakened foes with Shadow Sneak, as Rotom-Wash often falls just short of scoring OHKOs.

  • How to Overcome Aegislash's Weaknesses: Aegislash's problematic matchups against Kingambit and Mega Charizard Y are greatly improved by partner Garchomp's Ground- and Rock-type coverage. The Focus Sash set itself is an adaptation to work around the predictability of using King's Shield to switch formes because it does not need to focus on bulk and typically drops King's Shield in favor of Wide Guard. However, the predictability of the bulkier set might force riskier plays to prevent Aegislash's partners from being targeted without punishment. Generally speaking, it is much better to pair Aegislash with special-attacking threats like Mega Floette because Incineroar can easily cycle in and out of the field against Aegislash.

battlestadiumsingles.comments:
Speed SP Benchmarks

  • 1 Speed: This Speed investment allows Aegislash to outspeed uninvested Primarina and Clefable.

  • 2 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Tyranitar.

  • 6 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Scizor and Umbreon.

  • 7 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Skeledirge.

  • 8 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Corviknight.

  • 16 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Mega Scizor.

  • 21 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Mega Meganium and Mega Venusaur.

Physical Attacker.description:
• With its incredible stats, boasting sets of some of the highest offensive and defensive stats of any non-Mega Evolved Pokemon in the format; access to a powerful STAB attack with little drawback in Poltergeist; and its amazing typing, Aegislash is a potent physical wallbreaker that few Pokemon can switch in on without taking serious damage. Shadow Sneak also gives it the option to act as a revenge killer, allowing it to clean up weakened teams and remain useful late-game.

  • Swords Dance: With a Swords Dance boost, Aegislash is able to tear through even defensive teams, and thanks to Shield forme's stellar defenses, it can often find opportunities to set up, especially against common Pokemon like Corviknight, Archaludon, Mega Floette, and Sneasler. At +2, Poltergeist OHKOes bulky Primarina and Rotom-W sets, and Shadow Sneak OHKOes the likes of Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar.

  • King's Shield: At the cost of some offensive power, King's Shield provides Aegislash with much greater longevity, particularly when combined with Leftovers. By using King's Shield to first lower their Attack, Aegislash can take hits from and subsequently OHKO physically attacking counters that commonly run all-out attacking sets like Mega Lopunny and Meowscarada, making it much more difficult for offensive teams to reliably deal with.

  • Close Combat versus Sacred Sword: Aegislash appreciates Fighting-type coverage, which lets it hit Dark- and Normal-type Pokemon for super effective damage. Sets lacking King's Shield typically prefer the additional damage that Close Combat provides, which gives Aegislash the ability to always OHKO Mega Lucario as well as Mega Lopunny and Hydreigon on the switch in. Such sets don't care about Close Combat's drawback thanks to Blade forme's already low defensive stats. With this said, Swords Dance sets can still benefit from Sacred Sword ignoring stat boosts, which prevents Iron Defense Corviknight from using Aegislash to set up.

Other Options

  • Brave Nature: King's Shield variants of Aegislash can run a Brave nature, allowing them to always be slower than neutral-nature Primarina and therefore always be in the more defensive Shield forme when taking damage from its attacks. This comes at the cost of a worse matchup against opposing Adamant Aegislash, however, as the one-on-one is often decided by which Pokemon hits Poltergeist first.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head provides a STAB attack that, unlike Poltergeist, doesn't rely on the opposing Pokemon holding an item. This allows Aegislash to deal consistent damage throughout the game if it's paired with a Knock Off user like Meowscarada, as well as against common Sitrus Berry users like Hippowdon. Iron Head's lower Base Power can hinder Aegislash's ability to sweep, however.

Items

  • Spell Tag: Spell Tag makes Aegislash's Ghost-type STAB attacks even more potent, making Poltergeist a guaranteed OHKO on Primarina after Stealth Rock damage and giving it a chance to OHKO physically defensive Corviknight after a Swords Dance.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is generally preferred on King's Shield variants, which greatly appreciate passively healing while they protect themselves. However, Leftovers can still be useful on Swords Dance sets thanks to the pressure Aegislash's massive damage output puts on the opponent to make defensive switches, which often buys it free turns to heal.

  • Focus Sash: Swords Dance sets can make use of Focus Sash to set up on would-be threats like Mega Gengar and threaten a sweep against frail teams with a boosted Shadow Sneak.

Mixed Attacker.description:
