• Aegislash is a popular threat in BSS thanks to its good defensive typing and priority. This set trades damage for coverage and better offensive versatility against physical walls.

  • Shadow Ball: With Shadow Ball and Special Attack investment, Aegislash fares better against Corviknight and Archaludon due to their low Special Defense. Since Corviknight is prone to using U-turn, Aegislash's Quiet nature allows it to hit the incoming Pokemon instead. Aegislash also heavily threatens Iron Defense Mega Metagross by running Shadow Ball instead of Poltergeist.

  • Shadow Sneak: Aegislash's high offensive stats in Blade Forme mean that Shadow Sneak still has wide utility for revenge killing or dealing damage to faster foes like Basculegion-M, Mega Delphox, Mega Gengar, and Focus Sash Greninja.

  • King's Shield: King's Shield is useful against physical attackers like Meowscarada, Mega Lopunny, and Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott. Lowering a foe's Attack allows Aegislash to win many one-on-one scenarios it otherwise wouldn't. However, Contrary users like Mega Staraptor can gain an Attack boost from King's Shield when using Blaze Kick.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat still deals heavy damage to Mega Lucario, Mega Lopunny, Mega Greninja, and Meowscarada. The lack of full Attack investment does mean that Aegislash won't consistently OHKO the first two without chip damage, so having an entry hazard setter is generally recommended with this set.

Other Options

  • Flash Cannon versus Iron Head: Flash Cannon provides an additional STAB option against Fairy-types like Alolan Ninetales and makes use of Aegislash's investment in Special Attack. It does well against Mega Floette, though Iron Head deals more damage even without Attack investment and has a chance to KO offensive variants. Flash Cannon also deals the most damage against Mega Scrafty and Mega Staraptor.

  • Sacred Sword: Sacred Sword does well against Archaludon and provides coverage without the cost of lowering Aegislash's defensive stats.

Items

  • Spell Tag: Spell Tag provides a blanket boost to Ghost-type attacks, allowing Shadow Ball to consistently 2HKO uninvested Archaludon and Corviknight and OHKO Mega Metagross.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers has good synergy with King's Shield, allowing Aegislash to recover out of KO range while protecting itself. King's Shield lowering the Attack of foes that use contact moves can also give Aegislash more opportunities to recover with Leftovers.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb provides a helpful damage boost against Pokemon that Aegislash cannot quite OHKO with coverage. Examples include Hisuian Samurott, Mega Lucario, and Mega Lopunny with Close Combat, as well as Mega Floette with Flash Cannon. However, this cuts heavily into Aegislash's longevity.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Mega Dragalge's unique defensive typing, incredible special bulk, ability Regenerator, and access to Flip Turn make it an excellent defensive pivot. Mega Dragalge uses these traits to check numerous special threats such as Mega Meganium, non-Psychic Volcarona, Mega Raichu Y, and Rotom-Wash and even physical threats such as Sneasler, generating momentum with Flip Turn by forcing switches. Flip Turn also allows Mega Dragalge to take advantage of passive Pokemon, notably underspeeding Corviknight's U-turn. Sludge Bomb lets Mega Dragalge pressure Fairy-types such as Clefable, Primarina, Mega Meganium, and Mega Floette while threatening to poison non-immune foes. Draco Meteor is a powerful STAB option that prevents fellow Dragon-types from coming in freely, such as Garchomp and Dragapult, while also dealing enormous damage to most foes that do not resist it, such as Archaludon, Sneasler, and Rotom-Wash. Scald lets Mega Dragalge threaten burns, discouraging physical threats such as Mega Metagross, Kingambit, and Aegislash from switching in. It can also cripple opposing defensive Pokemon such as Toxapex, Galarian Slowking, and Corviknight with passive chip damage. Toxic is an alternative to Scald, allowing Mega Dragalge to more reliably check Volcarona, Calm Mind Primarina, and Mega Floette by putting them on a timer. Toxic Spikes is an option as well to target teams without an absorber. The SP spread allows Mega Dragalge to survive Garchomp's Earthquake and Mega Delphox's Psyshock while still avoiding the 2HKO from Moonblast by Calm Mind-boosted Primarina or Mega Floette.

Mega Dragalge faces competition from Toxapex and Galarian Slowking, which can similarly function as specially defensive pivots that absorb Toxic Spikes. Therefore, Mega Dragalge best fits on balance teams in search of a defensive pivot that can cover most of the roles filled by the aforementioned Pokemon while reliably handling Mega Raichu Y and Mega Charizard Y, which are otherwise quite difficult to check defensively. Mega Dragalge is threatened by numerous physical threats such as Mega Metagross, Excadrill, and Garchomp, so it should be paired with a strong physical wall, such as Corviknight or Hippowdon, both of which benefit from how Mega Dragalge checks Mega Raichu Y, Mega Meganium, and Rotom-Wash. Powerful wallbreakers that appreciate switch-in opportunities against Steel- and Poison-types, such as Aegislash, Ceruledge, and Garchomp, would complement Mega Dragalge's ability to bring them in safely with Flip Turn. Galarian Slowking is particularly annoying for Mega Dragalge, as none of Mega Dragalge's moves threaten it, allowing Galarian Slowking to set up Future Sight and pivot out with a slower Chilly Reception. Thus, Hisuian Samurott and Meowscarada make great partners with Mega Dragalge, taking advantage of many Pokemon that threaten it like Galarian Slowking, Aegislash, and Mega Delphox while benefiting from how Mega Dragalge checks Fighting- and Fairy-types in return. Mega Dragalge is less reliable at checking certain Fairy-types such as Calm Mind Mega Floette than other Poison-types; therefore, a secondary answer such as Excadrill or Aegislash is appreciated.

Bulky Offensive.description:
• Sylveon is a bulky offensive sweeper that fires off powerful Fairy-type attacks like Hyper Voice and Hyper Beam thanks to Pixilate. In addition to its bulk, Sylveon's middling Speed lets it make use of both Tailwind and Trick Room, ensuring it moves before its foes. Sylveon's Fairy-type attacks are devastating in the metagame, threatening KOs on Dragon- and Dark-types like Garchomp, Mega Tyranitar, and Hydreigon as well as dealing strong neutral damage against foes like Kingambit and Archaludon.

  • Hyper Voice: Hyper Voice is Sylveon's most commonly used attack. It provides strong spread damage, OHKOing low-bulk Garchomp and 2HKOing bulky Sitrus Berry and Roseli Berry Garchomp variants as well as Sneasler. This attack, however, can be neutralized by Incineroar's Throat Chop.

  • Hyper Beam vs Moonblast: Both of these moves provide Sylveon with a powerful single-target Fairy-type attack, allowing it to still deal damage when facing potential Wide Guard users like Aerodactyl and Pelipper. They also allow Sylveon to OHKO Soundproof Kommo-o. Hyper Beam is used as a powerful attack, potentially OHKOing bulkier foes such as Kingambit, Archaludon, and Mega Dragonite through Multiscale as well as Garchomp through its Roseli Berry. Using Hyper Beam is risky, as it leaves Sylveon vulnerable, although it can potentially KO a major threat. Moonblast, on the other hand, deals significantly less damage and has no drawbacks. Moonblast lets Sylveon 2HKO Sinistcha and bulky Pelipper.

  • Quick Attack: Quick Attack provides a priority Fairy-type attack that can finish off weakened foes and break Focus Sashes. It can also be used to cause Kingambit's Sucker Punch to fail if it targets Sylveon.

Other Options

  • Yawn: Sylveon occasionally runs Yawn, usually over Quick Attack, to put foes to sleep, disrupt them, and slow the pace of the game for its team. This lets Sylveon secure KOs or gives its partners chances to set up safely. Yawn is also great at disrupting setup sweepers like Calm Mind Mega Floette and Bulk Up Ceruledge, forcing them to switch out or be put to sleep.

Items

  • Fairy Feather: Fairy Feather increases the damage of Sylveon's Fairy-type attacks. It is a vital item to ensure that Sylveon can 2HKO Basculegion-M with Hyper Voice and OHKO bulky foes like Archaludon with Hyper Beam.

SP Spreads

  • 25 HP / 24 Def / 12 SpA / 5 Spe with Modest: The defensive investment lets Sylveon almost always survive Dire Claw from Adamant Sneasler. The Speed investment lets Sylveon outrun Garchomp under Tailwind. The remaining SPs are invested in Special Attack to maximize Sylveon's damage.

  • 6 HP / 32 SpA / 28 Spe with Modest: The Speed investment allows Sylveon to outrun Jolly Choice Scarf Basculegion-M while Tailwind is active. The HP investment lets Sylveon take Moonblast from +1 Modest Mega Floette with 15 Special Attack SPs invested, while Sylveon's given Special Attack investment with Modest maximizes its damage output.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Sylveon struggles most against hard-hitting foes that move before it, such as Mega Charizard Y and Basculegion-M. They deal a lot of damage, helping their partners easily pick off Sylveon or even outright OHKO it. Mega Charizard Y in particular resists Sylveon's attacks and threatens it with Weather Ball. Mega Gengar and Sneasler easily outrun Sylveon and threaten it with Sludge Bomb and Dire Claw, respectively. Mega Venusaur and Glimmora are also problematic, since they are bulky, resist all of Sylveon's attacks, and threaten it with heavy damage from Sludge Bomb. Steel-types like Kingambit and Aegislash threaten Sylveon with massive damage from Iron Head. Wide Guard from Aerodactyl and Pelipper is troublesome, as it forces Sylveon to rely on its single-target attacks instead of Hyper Voice, most commonly Hyper Beam and Quick Attack, leaving Sylveon open to taking huge damage after using Hyper Beam or dealing little damage when using Quick Attack. Sableye's dual screens and Mega Froslass's Aurora Veil prevent Sylveon from achieving important OHKOs with Hyper Beam against foes such as Archaludon and bulky Basculegion-M.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Incineroar is one of Sylveon's best partners. It can threaten Steel-types that Sylveon can't threaten at all, like Aegislash, with Flare Blitz while providing damage reduction via Intimidate and Fake Out support. Sneasler also works well with Sylveon, applying more pressure to Kingambit and Archaludon while providing Fake Out support. Sneasler also threatens to OHKO Mega Floette, which is particularly valuable against Calm Mind sets that can beat Sylveon one-on-one. Aerodactyl provides Tailwind support, letting Sylveon outspeed faster foes like Garchomp. Aerodactyl and its Mega Evolution also threaten Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide and Sneasler with Dual Wingbeat. Garchomp threatens Poison- and Steel-types like Mega Gengar and Aegislash with Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum, as well as Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide. Farigiraf provides Trick Room support, letting Sylveon move before faster foes, and Armor Tail helps prevent Fake Out. Farigiraf also threatens Poison-types like Sneasler and Glimmora with Psychic and Twin Beam.

  • How to Overcome Sylveon's Weaknesses: Sylveon often relies on its partners to defeat faster, powerful foes, such as Garchomp and Aerodactyl OHKOing Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide and Kingambit OHKOing Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch. If Sylveon is caught in a bad position where a partner that typically threatens the foes that threaten it is not on the field, Sylveon can use Detect for the turn while pivoting a partner onto the field to threaten those foes the following turn. Setting up Tailwind or Trick Room lets Sylveon move before faster threats like Basculegion-M. Fake Out support from Incineroar and Sneasler also helps Sylveon deal damage without fear of being double-targeted.

Fake Out Pivot.description:
• Incineroar is the premier support Pokemon in all of VGC, using Fake Out to deny attacks and constantly cycling said Fake Out while also applying offense stat drops with Parting Shot and Intimidate to gain control of the damage on the board. Thanks to its good natural bulk and exceptional typing, it can switch in with ease on attacks such as the powerful Ghost-type onslaught from the likes of Aegislash and Mega Gengar as well as Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y.

  • Flare Blitz: Flare Blitz allows Incineroar to make use of its high Attack stat, preventing foes from ignoring it especially when the sun is up. Flare Blitz notably threatens Kingambit, which usually scares away Incineroar due to Defiant.

  • Throat Chop versus Darkest Lariat: Throat Chop deals a decent chunk of damage while also preventing sound-based moves; this means common moves such as Sylveon's and Primarina's Hyper Voice and opposing Incineroar's Parting Shot are blocked. Darkest Lariat, on the other hand, ignores Archaludon's Stamina boosts, though that is rather irrelevant in most matchups; the most enticing part of Darkest Lariat is its higher Base Power, allowing Incineroar to always 2HKO Shield forme Aegislash.

  • Parting Shot: Parting Shot allows Incineroar to continuously lower foes' damage. Using Parting Shot also typically allows Incineroar to switch out last due to its low Speed, allowing frailer allies like Sneasler to come in safely.

Other Options

  • Protect: By dropping one of Incineroar's STAB attacks, Protect allows it to better position itself around the board. This is almost exclusively seen on Perish trap teams, where Incineroar plays a key role of in using Fake Out and Protect to stall Perish Song turns and then using Parting Shot to pivot around.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp allows Incineroar to further weaken physical attacks on top of Intimidate and allows Incineroar to cripple Pokemon immune to Intimidate, namely Defiant Kingambit and Inner Focus Dragonite.

  • Taunt: Taunt notably allows Incineroar to deny Trick Room from Farigiraf and Sinistcha, as well as crippling Pokemon that thrive off of their status moves, especially Whimsicott and Sableye.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry grants Incineroar more sustainability, allowing it to avoid a 2HKO from Modest Mega Dragonite's Hurricane and almost always avoiding a 2HKO from Timid offensive Mega Floette's Moonblast.

  • Chople Berry: While this is mostly used when Sitrus Berry has already been taken, Chople Berry still has its uses; most notably, it allows Incineroar to survive Close Combat from Sneasler, though only once.

Abilities

  • Intimidate: Intimidate is what makes Incineroar so strong; it can switch in, drop the foes' Attack stat, switch out, and repeat that same process over and over again.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 20 Def / 12 SpD / 2 Spe with Careful: With the given bulk, Incineroar, after an Intimidate, survives Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M. Additionally, it avoids a 2HKO from Timid Mega Gengar's Sludge Bomb, and it survives Hyper Beam from Sylveon and Light of Ruin from Mega Floette. The Speed investment allows Incineroar to outspeed non-invested Tyranitar, possibly letting it get off a crucial Parting Shot.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Incineroar is very prone to the rain teams that plague the format, where Pokemon such as Pelipper, Politoed, and Basculegion-M can all OHKO Incineroar when they're in the rain. Incineroar also struggles against White Herb Sneasler and the less popular White Herb Garchomp, since thanks to White Herb, they can ignore Intimidate and fire back with Close Combat and Stomping Tantrum or Earthquake, respectively. Incineroar also struggles against Rock-type Pokemon due to its inability to damage them hard; these Rock-type Pokemon include Mega Tyranitar, Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Glimmora, and their base formes.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Sinistcha is a great defensive partner for Incineroar, switching into the many Fighting-, Ground-, and Water-type moves that would threaten Incineroar, while Incineroar can switch into the Fire-, Dark-, and Ghost-type attacks that threaten Sinistcha. Sinistcha also provides Trick Room for Incineroar to circumvent its relatively low Speed. Offensively, Basculegion-M threatens the many Rock-types that beat Incineroar and opposing Fire-types as well as walling most Sneasler out entirely. Mega Gengar can do the same to Sneasler, while Mega Aerodactyl can outspeed and OHKO Sneasler with Dual Wingbeat. Mega Charizard Y can prevent Pelipper and Politoed from hitting Incineroar with a super effective Weather Ball and can threaten Water-types with Solar Beam. Incineroar also functions well on Perish trap teams, working as a slow pivot that can use Fake Out to prevent foes from doing much while their Perish Song counters ticks down.

  • How to Overcome Incineroar’s Weaknesses: Bringing Pokemon that heavily benefit from the support Incineroar provides, such as Calm Mind Mega Floette and Mega Charizard Y, allows you to use it to its full potential; these Pokemon deal huge damage, compensating for Incineroar's passivity and allowing your team to break through would-be threats like Garchomp and Archaludon. Building your team with some way to circumvent rain is also advised, as this lets Incineroar avoid the powerful Water-type Weather Ball from Pelipper. Mega Charizard Y is the most effective, as it also matches up well against Sneasler that decide to forego Rock Slide; however, Incineroar doesn't typically fit on Mega Charizard Y structures due to stacking of Fire-types, so alternative weathers from the likes of Mega Froslass and Mega Tyranitar can also work.

battlestadiumsingles.comments:
Special Defense SP Benchmarks

  • 32 HP and 15 Special Defense: With Sitrus Berry, this allows Primarina to avoid the 2HKO from Modest Mega Dragonite's Thunderbolt.

  • 32 HP and 17 Special Defense: This allows Primarina to avoid the OHKO from Timid Mega Gengar's Sludge Wave.

Speed SP Benchmarks

  • 6 Speed: This lets Primarina outspeed uninvested Scizor and Umbreon.

  • 7 Speed: This lets it outspeed uninvested Skeledirge.

  • 8 Speed: This lets it outspeed uninvested Corviknight.

  • 16 Speed: This lets it outspeed uninvested Mega Scizor.

Offensive Utility.description:
• With excellent natural bulk and a stellar typing combination, Primarina is a premier balance attacker that can provide both excellent offensive trading and strong support options.

  • Aqua Jet: While somewhat weak on Primarina, Aqua Jet is still an excellent move for picking off weakened foes and finishing off Focus Sash users like Garchomp.

  • Flip Turn versus Encore: Flip Turn lets Primarina function as a bulky pivot against faster threats, while Encore lets Primarina disrupt slower, bulkier threats like Hippowdon.

  • Modest versus Quiet: Even if it does weaken Aqua Jet, Modest is the no-nonsense option especially if Primarina is running Encore. On the other hand, Quiet can be run to preserve Aqua Jet's power while also making Primarina a slower pivot with Flip Turn.

Other Options

  • Ice Beam: Despite Moonblast already hitting Dragon-types very hard, Ice Beam can be used to catch bulkier Garchomp sets that survive Moonblast by surprise. It’s also a good tool to pressure Mega Meganium on a predicted switch, as Modest Primarina's Ice Beam can 2HKO maximum HP builds.

  • Psychic Noise: Psychic Noise is Primarina's only hope of taking on Mega Venusaur, dealing respectable damage and temporarily stopping any Synthesis or Leech Seed healing.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is the most reliable source of recovery for attacking sets.

  • Mystic Water: Mystic Water is an alternative to healing items that synergizes better with Torrent, allowing Primarina's Sparkling Aria to hit extra hard once it's at low health.

  • Leftovers: If Sitrus Berry is needed elsewhere on the team, Leftovers is a decent alternative for healing.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash can be used with fully offensive spreads, allowing Primarina to activate Torrent more easily against targets such as Mega Gengar.

Other SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 2 SpA / 32 SpD with Calm or Sassy: With this spread, Primarina can lean harder into being a special cushion for its team. In particular, it almost always avoids the 2HKO from Modest Mega Dragonite's Thunderbolt.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest: A fully offensive spread should always be used for Focus Sash sets. It also greatly increases Primarina's ability to disrupt with Encore.

Glass Cannon.description: The set for Lycanroc-D does not significantly change from Regulation M-A to M-B, nor does its teammates and method of play. To see the analysis information, please refer to the Regulation M-A analysis.

Defensive Support.description:
• Toxapex finds itself serving a unique role within the Regulation M-B metagame as a supportive wall thanks to its valuable Water / Poison dual typing and sky-high defensive stats. These allow it to sit in front of and greatly limit offensive threats such as Mega Charizard Y, Garchomp, and Sylveon.

  • Infestation: Infestation enables Toxapex to provide some level of offensive pressure along with trapping foes on the field, messing up attempts to reposition.

  • Wide Guard: Wide Guard can protect Toxapex and teammates like Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit from spread moves such as Rock Slide and Earthquake.

  • Toxic: Toxic forces timers onto foes such as Milotic and Mega Staraptor, preventing them from being able to setup and win games safely.

  • Infestation, Toxic, and Baneful Bunker Synergy: This trio of moves synergizes well with each other and turns Toxapex into an active threat, as the combination of Infestation and poison does immense amounts of damage over time, softening up foes for partners to KO them.

  • Regenerator: Regenerator helps keep Toxapex healthy throughout a match to let it maintain pressure with trapping and spreading poison.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 16 Def / 18 SpD with Bold: This spread allows Toxapex to take Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M's 200-Base Power Last Respects at full HP in addition to Mega Delphox's Psychic.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Toxapex can be greatly annoyed by Steel- and Poison-types, as their immunity to Toxic prevents them from being worn down quickly and leaves Toxapex with only Infestation to whittle away at them. Archaludon, Mega Metagross, and Venusaur can prove especially problematic for Toxapex because they can also threaten it with powerful attacks like Electro Shot, Psychic Fangs, and Earth Power. Psychic- and Ground-types such as Mega Delphox, Farigiraf, and Mega Swampert, while not immune to Toxic, can still scare Toxapex through their STAB moves.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y greatly appreciates Toxapex's Wide Guard blocking Rock Slide from Garchomp and Aerodactyl, and in return, it can melt through Steel-types such as Kingambit and Gholdengo.

  • Kingambit and Incineroar can prey on the Psychic-types that break Toxapex like Mega Delphox and Farigiraf, and they also can deal with Ghost-types such as Mega Gengar and Sinistcha, which can escape Infestation's Bound effect. In return, Toxapex can come in against Fighting-types that handle them such as Sneasler and Mega Staraptor. Additionally, Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot complement Toxapex by making it much more troublesome to remove.

  • Garchomp removes Poison-types such as Mega Gengar and opposing Toxapex while also helping it handle threats such as Mega Delphox and Mega Raichu Y. Toxapex for its part can use Wide Guard to prevent Sinistcha and Mega Froslass from reliably threatening Garchomp with Matcha Gotcha and Blizzard. Wide Guard also allows Garchomp to use Earthquake without worrying about it hurting Toxapex.

  • Venusaur can pair well with Toxapex by scaring away Ground- and Water-types that cause Toxapex problems such as Garchomp, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-M with its Grass-type STAB moves. Meanwhile, Toxapex protects Venusaur from Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Mega Froslass's Blizzard with Wide Guard.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Swords Dance.description:
• Disguise's incredible power in a format where Item Clause is in effect makes Mimikyu an excellent sweeper and revenge killer despite its mediocre stats!

  • Shadow Sneak: Despite its paltry power, Shadow Sneak is perfect for picking off weakened threats like Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox.

  • Shadow Claw: When Disguise is still intact, Shadow Claw paired with Life Orb or Spell Tag lets Mimikyu OHKO offensive Mega Metagross, offensive Mega Gengar, and Mega Delphox.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb's power boost makes it by far Mimikyu's best item, beefing up its mediocre Attack stat enough to KO key threats after a boost, such as offensive Primarina and Mega Blaziken.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Mimikyu prefers to juice up its Attack stat with Adamant to pick off as many threats as possible with Shadow Sneak, but Jolly is still worth considering for outspeeding opposing Mimikyu and Modest Mega Dragonite.

Other Options

  • Curse: Curse is effective at punishing foes that may attempt to set up on Mimikyu like Mega Scizor, Iron Defense Mega Metagross, and Iron Defense Corviknight. Sacrificing Mimikyu with Curse when its weakened can also be an effective way to bring in dangerous sweepers like Garchomp and Mega Delphox. Finally, Curse lets Mimikyu put your opponent's last remaining Pokemon on a timer, potentially clinching you a win if Mimikyu doesn't have enough power to KO them.

  • Wood Hammer: Wood Hammer crushes even the most defensive Hippowdon after a boost when using an Adamant nature and Life Orb, a threat Mimikyu usually has little business breaking through early on. It also allows Mimikyu to revenge kill offensive Primarina.

  • Drain Punch: Drain Punch's healing isn't particularly helpful for such an offensive Mimikyu set, but it's the only way to OHKO Kingambit after a boost.

Other Items

  • Mimikyu should almost always use Life Orb, but other options can be considered if another teammate needs it.

  • Spell Tag: Spell Tag is Mimikyu's second best offensive item, turning Shadow Claw into an effective revenge killing option with an Adamant nature against Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox, as well as retaining the key OHKO after a boost against offensive Mega Metagross.

  • Scope Lens: Scope Lens gives Shadow Claw a 50% chance to land a critical hit, meaning boosted Mimikyu can potentially ruin Iron Defense Mega Metagross attempting to stonewall a sweep.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry is a great response against status inducers, with Yawn Umbreon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash being particularly big targets for Mimikyu to surprise.

Swiss Army Knife (Trick Room Support).description:
• Mimikyu offers role compression with its Disguise ability to stop foes from sweeping, Shadow Sneak to pick up KOs, disrupting resilient foes with Curse, and speed control as a Trick Room setter!

  • Trick Room: Trick Room provides speed control for very slow Pokemon like Mega Mawile, Aegislash, and Kingambit. Variants of naturally fast Pokemon like Garchomp and Meowscarada that do not fully invest in Speed or use a Choice Scarf also appreciate Trick Room, as it lets them move before faster variants of themselves. With Disguise, Mimikyu can absorb a hit from an opposing Trick Room sweeper and use Trick Room to restore the normal Speed order, thus allowing its team to countersweep!

  • Curse: At low HP, Curse grants a clean exit for Mimikyu and lets it safely bring in another teammate. It can also put opposing defensive Pokemon and Baton Pass chains or recipients on a timer.

  • Shadow Sneak: Shadow Sneak lets Mimikyu pick up KOs against faster or problematic foes that can threaten Mimikyu's partners. With Life Orb, Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak always 2HKOes Basculegion-M, Mega Starmie, and Mega Gengar.

  • Play Rough: With Life Orb, Mimikyu's Play Rough has a good chance to OHKO Mega Gyarados and usually OHKOes uninvested Garchomp.

Items

  • Life Orb: Life Orb's boost improves or guarantees the odds of achieving the aforementioned OHKOs and 2HKOs, which would otherwise be harder to achieve with type-enhancing items. If Mimikyu is in range of fainting from Life Orb recoil, it can attack the foe, faint, and make way for another teammate, which can come in clutch if Taunt prevents Mimikyu from using Curse!

  • Mental Herb: Mental Herb gives Mimikyu a second chance to set Trick Room or use Curse if Taunted. For team modes that rely on Trick Room sweepers as a win condition, this can be a more consistent option.

SP Spreads

These SP spreads minimize Stealth Rock damage and let Mimikyu use Curse twice without fainting. With Disguise, it can also survive a five-hit Icicle Spear from Adamant Mamoswine; if Disguise is broken, Mimikyu can still take Triple Axel from Adamant Protean Meowscarada. As Disguise is ignored by Mold Breaker, Mimikyu will always survive Waterfall or Crunch from Jolly Mega Gyarados at full HP after a Dragon Dance.

  • 29 HP / 30 Atk / 7 Def with Adamant: This spread can be used with Life Orb. The additional investment in Defense improves Mimikyu's survivability alongside Life Orb recoil, giving it a small chance to survive Bullet Punch from Adamant Mega Metagross after its Disguise is broken.

  • 29 HP / 32 Atk / 5 Def with Adamant: This spread can be used with Mental Herb. If Disguise is broken, Mimikyu has a good chance to survive Bullet Punch from Adamant Mega Metagross.

Setup Sweeper.description:
• Kommo-o has the potential to sweep through teams after using Clangorous Soul. It boasts good matchups against metagame staples like Kingambit and Incineroar while its defensive typing gives it an edge versus Mega Charizard Y and Mega Blastoise.

  • Clangorous Soul: It is necessary for Kommo-o to use Clangorous Soul to ensure crucial OHKOs, such as with Clanging Scales against Garchomp and Aura Sphere against Archaludon. However, given the fact that Clangorous Soul leaves Kommo-o vulnerable for a turn and damages it, Kommo-o has to have support from teammates like Incineroar and Sinistcha in order to set up safely. The HP loss can allow foes Kommo-o is normally comfortable against, like Kingambit and Sneasler, to threaten a double-target KO, making support necessary to set up.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers aids Kommo-o's survivability, helping offset the HP loss from Clangorous Soul and allowing Kommo-o to avoid an OHKO from Adamant Sneasler's Close Combat after using Clangorous Soul and receiving one turn of Leftovers recovery.

Abilities

  • Soundproof: Soundproof allows Kommo-o to ignore Hyper Voice from Sylveon and Parting Shot from Incineroar, which would otherwise threaten an OHKO or negate most of Clangorous Soul's benefit, respectively. Soundproof also grants Kommo-o an immunity to Perish Song, improving its matchup against Mega Gengar while also making it a good partner.

SP Spreads

  • 8 Def / 29 SpA / 29 Spe with Modest: At +1, the Special Attack investment lets Kommo-o almost always OHKO Chople Berry Kingambit with Aura Sphere. The Speed investment allows it to outrun Aerodactyl and Mega Gengar after using Clangorous Soul. The Defense investment optimizes Kommo-o's chance of surviving 150-Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion-M after its Defense is boosted.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: The Speed investment allows Kommo-o to outrun Mega Aerodactyl and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M after a Speed boost, while the Special Attack investment maximizes its chance of OHKOing Chople Berry Kingambit with Aura Sphere after a Special Attack boost.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fairy-types like Mega Floette, Whimsicott, and Sylveon threaten to OHKO Kommo-o while it cannot do much damage in return. Mega Floette in particular uses Dazzling Gleam to prevent Sinistcha's Rage Powder from saving Kommo-o. Whimsicott threatens an OHKO with Moonblast, which also cannot be redirected by Sinistcha, and can use Encore to lock Kommo-o into Clangorous Soul. Mega Froslass threatens heavy damage with Blizzard, which cannot be redirected, and can survive Clanging Scales even after two boosts to Kommo-o's Special Attack. Aegislash resists Kommo-o's attacks and blocks Clanging Scales with Wide Guard. Mega Aerodactyl and Garchomp can threaten an OHKO or heavy damage before Kommo-o moves, preventing it from using Clangorous Soul.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Sinistcha's Hospitality and Life Dew help recover HP lost from Clangorous Soul and may allow Kommo-o to use Clangorous Soul a second time, and Rage Powder redirects attacks like Dragon Claw from Garchomp and Dragon Pulse from Archaludon to make it easier for Kommo-o to use Clangorous Soul in the first place. Kommo-o is immune to Mega Gengar's Perish Song, while Mega Gengar handles the aforementioned Fairy-types and Mega Froslass. In exchange, Kommo-o beats Dark-types like Kingambit and Incineroar that threaten Sinistcha and Mega Gengar. Incineroar provides Fake Out support and Parting Shot to weaken foes, making it easier for Kommo-o to use Clangorous Soul. Kommo-o in turn covers for Mega Tyranitar with Aura Sphere and is better versus Mega Blastoise.

  • How to Overcome Kommo-o's Weaknesses: Poison-type attacks like Sludge Bomb from Mega Gengar and Dire Claw from Sneasler deal with threatening Fairy-types, and Mega Gengar has Shadow Ball to handle Mega Froslass and Aegislash. Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag allows it to trap and KO these threats before Kommo-o comes in to sweep. Redirection from Sinistcha is effective against Sylveon, as Kommo-o blocks Hyper Voice, leaving Sylveon without spread moves that can ignore Rage Powder; this redirection is also useful against foes without spread attacks like Basculegion-M and Archaludon. Incineroar has offensive options against Mega Froslass and Aegislash with Flare Blitz and Throat Chop while also having Fake Out and Intimidate to help Kommo-o set up in the face of Mega Aerodactyl and Garchomp.

Bulk Up.description:
• Corviknight leverages its amazing defensive profile to become a strong late-game sweeper, using Bulk Up and Roost to easily stand in front of the format's biggest beasts like Mega Floette and Garchomp.

  • Brave Bird: Brave Bird offers huge damage against Grass- and Fighting-type Pokemon like Sneasler and Sinistcha, though it reduces Corviknight's longevity; to counteract this, Corviknight runs Roost and Leftovers to heal off the recoil damage.

  • Bulk Up: Bulk Up, in conjunction with Roost, makes Corviknight immovable against the format's physical attackers, eventually letting it shrug off attacks from the likes of Kingambit. After using Bulk Up twice, Corviknight usually OHKOes Mega Floette that run little to no bulk investment, and after just one Bulk Up, it secures a 2HKO on most Garchomp.

Other Options

  • Body Press: Body Press offers coverage against Steel- and Rock-type Pokemon like Kingambit, Archaludon, and Mega Tyranitar, OHKOing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar at +2. However, this does come at the cost of dropping Roost or Tailwind, which either significantly cuts Corviknight's longevity or makes it lose out on a valuable speed control option. Note that all moves in this section call for dropping either Roost or Tailwind.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head allows Corviknight to hit Fairy-types like Sylveon without having to take recoil from Brave Bird.

  • Protect: Protect allows Corviknight to stall turns to recover with Leftovers and time out weather conditions, Tailwind, and Trick Room, all while allowing Corviknight and its team to position Corviknight for a potential win.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers further increases Corviknight's longevity, allowing it to have good chances at avoiding a 2HKO from 100-Base Power Last Respects from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M.

Abilities

  • Mirror Armor: Mirror Armor allows Corviknight to deflect stat drops, namely those coming from Incineroar's Intimidate and Alolan Ninetales's Icy Wind, preventing it from being weakened after using Bulk Up or slowed down after using Tailwind.

SP Spreads

  • 19 HP / 10 Atk / 29 Def / 8 SpD with Careful: The given HP SPs are optimized for Leftovers recovery and, in combination with the Defense and Special Defense SPs, allow Corviknight to survive Black Glasses Kingambit's +2 Kowtow Cleave, withstand Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M's Wave Crash in the rain, and avoid a 2HKO from Modest Mega Froslass's Blizzard. The remaining SPs are dropped into Attack for maximum damage. Do note that an alternative spread with an Impish nature and possibly more Defense SPs can be used to deal more damage with Body Press if you opt for that move.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Delphox, and Ceruledge all hit Corviknight hard with Heat Wave and Bitter Blade. Ceruledge in particular can even match Corviknight's boosts with Bulk Up of its own. Strong special attackers like Mega Blastoise, which has access to Shell Smash to make it even stronger, and Mega Dragonite, which has super effective coverage in the form of Heat Wave, Flamethrower, or Thunderbolt, can hit Corviknight on its weaker defensive stat, ignoring the boosts from Bulk Up. Without boosts or after only one Bulk Up, double targeting from strong physical attackers like Basculegion-M and Sneasler can bring Corviknight to low HP, making it much harder to reliably use Bulk Up. Archaludon and Rotom-Wash threaten high Electric-type damage and can easily tank Corviknight's Brave Bird.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Tyranitar is able to thwart the plans of any Fire-type Pokemon, shutting off sun from Mega Charizard Y and hitting them hard with Rock Slide while resisting their Fire-type attacks. Mega Tyranitar also shuts off rain, making Archaludon far more manageable. In return, Corviknight beats Garchomp and Fairy-types like Sylveon and Mega Floette that would otherwise give Mega Tyranitar big trouble. Rotom-Wash also helps against Fire-types and has Electric-type STAB moves to threaten the likes of Basculegion-M and Mega Blastoise. Furthermore, since Rotom-Wash carries Will-O-Wisp to prevent physical attackers from overwhelming it, Corviknight becomes near-impossible to remove with physical blows after a Bulk Up or two. In return, Rotom-Wash appreciates Corviknight's ability to threaten common Fairy-type Pokemon, as they are able to tank attacks from Rotom-Wash and target its typically lower Special Defense with their strong STAB moves. Mega Froslass shuts down other weather and helps against Mega Dragonite, being commonly run alongside Corviknight thanks to its good matchups against Mega Aerodactyl and, after boosting and when using Body Press, Kingambit. Excadrill and Garchomp are good partners for Corviknight, with the former also pairing well with Mega Tyranitar and both carrying Earthquake and Rock Slide to threaten Fire-types. They're also able to offset Corviknight's passive nature before it can set up. Corviknight, thanks to its Earthquake immunity, can sit next to them while they use Earthquake.

  • How to Overcome Corviknight's Weaknesses: Teams with Corviknight should always have ways to beat sun and rain teams; Mega Tyranitar and Mega Froslass are able to do this well by changing the weather. Meanwhile, offensive partners like Excadrill and Garchomp help make dents into teams early-game, removing threats to Corviknight like Mega Charizard Y, which allows it to set up more easily and bring you closer to a good win condition. Sinistcha can provide redirection and recovery in the form of Rage Powder and Hospitality, creating bigger opportunities for Corviknight to set up and get rolling.

IronPress.description:
Iron Defense Corviknight is an excellent defensive Pokemon and wincon. It can boost alongside setup sweepers such as Kingambit, Dragonite, and Garchomp, allowing it to continue checking them while threatening significant damage with Body Press. Corviknight's fantastic typing, resilience to entry hazards, and key resistances grant it many opportunities to set up throughout a game. Corviknight can extend its utility with Defog, given its great matchup against foes like defensive Garchomp and Hippowdon, thanks in part to Pressure. Alternatively, Corviknight can run Brave Bird to hit threats that would otherwise check it, such as Volcarona, Mega Meganium, and Mega Delphox, as well as Ghost-types like Annihilape and Ceruledge, preventing them from switching in. Leftovers is Corviknight's preferred item, with the passive healing over time being crucial for checking hazard setters and limiting how often it needs to use Roost. Sitrus Berry is also a good option if another teammate is already using Leftovers, and has the added benefit of allowing Corviknight to avoid Poltergeist from Pokemon such as Aegislash after it is consumed. Occa Berry allows Corviknight to survive an otherwise lethal Fire-type attack from Pokemon such as Blaziken, Mega Meganium, and Volcarona. Occa Berry pairs especially well with Brave Bird, as Corviknight can lure in Blaziken, Mega Meganium, and Volcarona and potentially KO them in return. 16 Speed SPs can be used to allow Corviknight to outrun maximum Speed Adamant Kingambit and use Iron Defense before Kingambit attacks. However, this requires Corviknight to sacrifice a notable amount of physical bulk, and it already outspeeds bulkier Kingambit variants without the investment. Mental Herb is another option, allowing Corviknight to avoid being locked into a move by Encore from users such as Maushold and Hisuian Samurott. However, because Encore is uncommon, other items are typically more effective.

Corviknight can fit on a wide variety of teams thanks to its ability to clear entry hazards and check a number of dangerous Pokemon such as Garchomp, Sneasler, and Kingambit, though it will find particular success on balance and bulky offense teams. Corviknight benefits greatly from entry hazard support because many of its answers, such as Mega Delphox, Ceruledge, and Mega Raichu Y, lack reliable recovery or are weak to Stealth Rock. Bulky entry hazard setters such as Garchomp and Hippowdon are thus great partners, as they can set up Stealth Rock to wear down Corviknight's key checks while also handling certain Fire-types such as Blaziken and Ceruledge and switching into Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon. Corviknight also fits well on hazard-centric teams because Pressure punishes Defog from opposing Corviknight, and Corviknight itself is a great counter to Rapid Spin Excadrill. Key Regenerator Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking, Mega Dragalge, and Toxapex greatly appreciate Corviknight's ability to handle physical attackers such as Kingambit and Garchomp as well as remove entry hazards with Defog. In turn, they can handle special attackers that threaten Corviknight, such as Mega Meganium, Mega Charizard Y, Primarina, and Mega Raichu Y. With or without Brave Bird, Corviknight can find itself struggling against Ghost-types such as Annihilape, Ceruledge, Dragapult, and Aegislash. Hisuian Samurott is a fantastic partner, as it can switch into many of these Ghost-types as well as Fire-type attacks aimed at Corviknight and capitalize on this to begin setting up entry hazards with Ceaseless Edge. It can also revenge kill key threats such as Mega Delphox and Mega Raichu Y either with a Choice Scarf set or by using Sucker Punch. Hydreigon can similarly switch into many of these Pokemon and revenge kill them with Dark Pulse on a Choice Scarf set. However, both Pokemon struggle against Annihilape, so another partner to handle it, such as Clefable or Mega Meganium, is recommended.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Physically Defensive.description:
• Corviknight serves as an excellent physical wall, with its incredible typing enabling it to handle physical attackers and Ground-types such as Tyranitar, Garchomp, and Hippowdon with ease.

  • Body Press: Body Press is the main offensive option, weaponizing Corviknight's good natural bulk to dispose of threats such as Meowscarada, Excadrill, and Umbreon safely.

  • Iron Head: If a secondary offensive option is needed, Iron Head allows Corviknight to actually threaten Mimikyu and Sylveon along with Primarina and Mega Floette in a pinch.

  • Iron Defense: Iron Defense improves Corviknight's Defense and Body Press's damage, enabling it to shrug off physical attackers like Dragonite and Sneasler completely.

  • Taunt: Taunt allows Corviknight to shut down Umbreon and Hippowdon, preventing them from forcing Corviknight out with tools such as Yawn, and prevents multiple turns of setup from the likes of Dragon Dance Dragonite.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers allows Corviknight to safely stay on the field for multiple turns while it accrues Iron Defense boosts.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can provide a solid quick burst of healing, enabling Corviknight to have HP to spare while combating foes such as Tyranitar and Mega Gyarados.

Abilities

  • Pressure: Pressure punishes Pokemon reliant on low-PP moves like Garchomp, which needs Stone Edge to reliably damage Corviknight, by quickly draining their moves' PP; Pressure also helps Corviknight handle opposing Corviknight by letting it outlast their Body Press's PP.

  • Mirror Armor: Mirror Armor punishes Intimidate from Gyarados, forcing it to set up with Dragon Dance longer, along with Special Defense drops from the likes of Espathra's Lumina Crash and Gengar's Shadow Ball, which can help force them out as Corviknight pivots to a special attacker.

Specially Defensive.description:
• With a specially defensive SP spread, Corviknight can still maintain its role of checking Ground-types like Hippowdon as with the a physically defensive spread while also expanding its reaches and allowing it to directly take on special attackers such as Mega Meganium and Gengar.

  • Body Press and Iron Defense: Body Press and Iron Defense can allow Corviknight to still check more physically leaning threats such as Mega Lopunny once it gets going while also making it capable of directly combating Archaludon that lack Electro Shot.

  • Brave Bird: Brave Bird is an alternative offensive tool for Corviknight to bust up Mega Venusaur and Primarina.

  • Taunt: Taunt shuts down Hippowdon and Sylveon's attempts to force it out with Yawn and prevents Corviknight from being safely set up on by the likes of Hydreigon.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers can soften the blow of the recoil from Brave Bird.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst healing helps Corviknight take on Mega Meganium and quickly recover from an untimely bit of Brave Bird recoil.

Abilities

  • Pressure: Pressure helps Corviknight handle Primarina by depleting its Sparkling Aria PP more quickly as well as allowing it to quickly expend Garchomp's Stone Edge PP.

  • Mirror Armor: Mirror Armor annoys Gyarados by turning Intimidate against it, along with bouncing Special Defense drops back against the likes of Lumina Crash Espathra and Shadow Ball Gengar as Corviknight pivots to a special attacker.

Prankster Support.description:
• Grimmsnarl utilizes its access to Prankster and dual screens to become a premier support Pokemon within Regulation M-B, supporting big threats like Archaludon and having a favorable type matchup against the likes of Basculegion-M and Garchomp.

  • Parting Shot: Thanks to Prankster, Parting Shot turns Grimmsnarl into a fast pivot option, allowing it to easily get out of sticky situations like a regular swap with the added benefit of lowering the opponent's offenses. Although it acts before most moves, Parting Shot does occur after players switch or Mega Evolve their Pokemon, allowing Grimmsnarl to bring in an ally weather setter on the same turn the opponent attempts to set up weather by one of the aforementioned methods.

  • Spirit Break versus Foul Play: Spirit Break allows Grimmsnarl to hit Dragon-types like Garchomp and Hydreigon hard while reducing the Special Attack of foes like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Floette, usually when they are switching in due to Grimmsnarl's low Speed. Spirit Break also deals significant damage to Mega Floette. Foul Play, on the other hand, is capable of OHKOing Basculegion-M and 2HKOing Mega Swampert and most Garchomp.

  • Light Clay: Thanks to Light Clay, partners like Archaludon and Gholdengo have more time to set up safely behind dual screens.

Other Options

  • Fake Out: Fake Out can be used over its attacking moves, allowing Grimmsnarl to provide further support by giving partners like Gholdengo an opportunity to set up. However, this leaves it vulnerable to moves like Taunt from Maushold.

  • Scary Face: Scary Face can be used over Spirit Break or Foul Play to grant Grimmsnarl an option of speed control, though it leaves Grimmsnarl entirely passive.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 14 Def / 20 SpD with Careful: The given SPs allow Grimmsnarl to survive Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M and, when Light Screen is set up, Moonblast from Mega Floette. The Defense SPs allow Grimmsnarl to always survive Dire Claw from Jolly Sneasler. A Calm nature can be run when using Foul Play to decrease damage from confusion and opposing Foul Play.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Steel-type Pokemon like Kingambit, Mega Metagross, Archaludon, and Gholdengo threaten Grimmsnarl with Iron Head, Flash Cannon, and Make It Rain. Kingambit can switch in on Spirit Break to activate Defiant, while Gholdengo is immune to Parting Shot and can use Nasty Plot to offset the Special Attack drops from Spirit Break, which does minimal damage to it.

  • Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten huge damage onto Grimmsnarl through dual screens, especially against sets without Spirit Break.

  • Farigiraf, thanks to Armor Tail, denies Parting Shot and, if it's run, Scary Face from affecting Farigiraf's allies, severely hindering Grimmsnarl's effectiveness.

  • Fake Out from the likes of Sneasler and Incineroar prevent Grimmsnarl from setting up dual screens, leaving it vulnerable to another attack like Moonblast from Mega Floette. Sneasler itself threatens huge damage onto Grimmsnarl with Dire Claw, while Incineroar is immune to Prankster moves and easily tanks any attacks that Grimmsnarl carries.

  • Outside of pressuring a few select targets like Basculegion-M, Grimmsnarl struggles to carry an offensive presence on the field, leaving itself to be rather easily ignored.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Offensive partners like Gholdengo are recommended to offset Grimmsnarl's passivity. Gholdengo is able to threaten Fairy-types and walls out Farigiraf and Sneasler, as well as having a good matchup against Mega Metagross without Stomping Tantrum. Archaludon fills this role well as well, acting as a bulkier partner that exchanges Gholdengo's good Fairy-type matchup for a better matchup against physical attackers like Kingambit thanks to a combination of Reflect and Stamina.

  • Mega Staraptor threatens Steel-types with Close Combat. In return, Grimmsnarl not only provides dual screens but can also use Parting Shot on Mega Staraptor to make it even stronger thanks to Contrary. Grimmsnarl can also use Spirit Break to offset boosts granted to opposing Archaludon by Electro Shot, allowing Mega Staraptor to feel less threatened.

  • Sinistcha creates a strong supportive core alongside Grimmsnarl, healing up common partners behind dual screens and allowing them to easily set up and sweep games.

  • Mega Swampert can use Earthquake or High Horsepower to hit Steel-types, Sneasler, and Incineroar hard while also threatening big damage onto the format's Fairy-types with Wave Crash. Grimmsnarl, in return, can easily pivot to Pelipper against opposing weather setters with Parting Shot. Archaludon also appreciates this to become a dangerous sweeper thanks to the combination of dual screens, Stamina, (AC) and Electro Shot.

Dual Screens.description:
• Thanks to Prankster, Grimmsnarl is a consistent dual screens setter that can enable sweepers like Mega Gyarados, Nasty Plot Mega Delphox, and Swords Dance Garchomp to safely set up. Though it lacks the Speed and offensive presence of Aurora Veil setter Alolan Ninetales, Grimmsnarl's defensive typing and access to useful disruption moves help it find a place on bulkier teams.

  • Spirit Break: Spirit Break has greater accuracy than Play Rough, with both moves 2HKOing offensive Garchomp and Mega Gyarados, and its secondary effect can punish specially offensive checks like Primarina and Archaludon that want to switch in on Grimmsnarl.

  • Parting Shot: Prankster gives Parting Shot increased priority, allowing the otherwise slow Grimmsnarl to build momentum on top of providing it with another way to reduce the damage dealt by the opposing Pokemon. However, Parting Shot will fail if used against a Pokemon with Good as Gold or Clear Body, preventing Grimmsnarl from switching, so it should be used with caution if the opponent can switch in a Gholdengo or a non-Mega-Evolved Metagross.

  • Taunt: Taunt shuts down supportive Pokemon like Hippowdon and defensive Garchomp, letting Grimmsnarl act as an effective counter lead. It can also prevent Pokemon like Volcarona and Mega Blaziken from taking advantage of Grimmsnarl's passivity by setting up on it.

  • Foul Play: Foul Play provides an alternative attack that can punish setup and is particularly effective against Mega Metagross and Aegislash. However, opting to stay in against these Pokemon will often result in Grimmsnarl taking significant damage, which can compromise its ability to set up dual screens late-game.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpD with Impish: Running a physically defensive SP spread allows Grimmsnarl to always survive a Bullet Punch followed by a second Bullet Punch behind Reflect from Adamant Mega Metagross and Mega Lucario, brings Adamant Life Orb Mimikyu's Play Rough to a 3HKO behind Reflect, and helps it act as a late-game check to Basculegion-M.

  • 32 HP / 18 Def / 16 SpD with Careful: Running some Special Defense brings Timid Glimmora's Sludge Wave and Modest Archaludon's Flash Cannon to a 3HKO behind Light Screen and gives Grimmsnarl a very good chance to avoid the 2HKO from Modest Primarina's Moonblast under the same conditions. Investing the rest of its Stat Points in Defense allows Grimmsnarl to always survive Adamant Mega Scizor's Bullet Punch.

Hex.description: Hex Dragapult works well on offense teams, with its Ghost typing preventing entry hazard removal from Rapid Spin users such as Excadrill. Dragapult's high Speed alongside Clear Body makes it a crucial asset against Sticky Web Araquanid. Alternatively, Infiltrator allows Hex Dragapult to cripple Pokemon with Will-O-Wisp behind Substitute such as Bulk Up Annihilape and Dragonite with status, racking passive damage to bring them into revenge killing range. Hisuian Samurott is one of its best partners, setting Spikes with Ceaseless Edge, while Garchomp and Glimmora can set Stealth Rock; these hazards chip down switch-ins to the range of an OHKO by Hex, with Glimmora being able to set Toxic Spikes, allowing Hex to receive a doubled power boost immediately. Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott, Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Kingambit can threaten to revenge kill Dragapult, making Fairy-types such as Mega Meganium good partners. Mega Meganium threatens to deal significant damage with Dazzling Gleam, resists Dark- and Dragon-type attacks thrown at Dragapult, and has Weather Ball to OHKO Kingambit. Ghost-types such as Ceruledge pair nicely as offensive partners to chip down Dark-type Pokemon trying to switch in, whereas Mega Lopunny serves as a physical attacker that handles Kingambit while appreciating Dragapult dealing with Corviknight and Galarian Slowking. Dragapult being able to burn Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott assists Psychic-types such as Mega Delphox and Mega Metagross. Will-O-Wisp can cripple defensive Pokemon such as Corviknight, opening up Dragapult's teammates such as Swords Dance Garchomp and Blaziken to sweep while boosting the power of Hex against Pokemon such as Primarina, Galarian Slowking, and Toxapex. Burn's physical damage reduction also allows Dragapult to soft check Pokemon such as Mega Staraptor and Mega Swampert, and its multitude of resistances help spread paralysis to prevent a sweep against Pokemon such as Swords Dance Blaziken and Quaquaval. Hex Dragapult also works well on bulky balance teams as their main speed control and progress maker, soft checking threatening Pokemon such as Mega Raichu Y while bulky partners such as Clefable and Umbreon can sponge Dark-type attacks as well as threaten with status moves such as Thunder Wave and Toxic.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Dragapult provides amazing speed control by outspeeding Choice Scarf Meowscarada and even +2 Blaziken while also providing good damage output with its Ghost and Dragon-type STAB moves, allowing it to clean late-game. Choice Scarf allows Dragapult to gain a higher Speed tier to revenge kill boosted sweepers while remaining an effective spinblocker and a fast pivot with U-turn. Shadow Ball is its spammable STAB option, while Draco Meteor provides a one-time nuke, stopping sweepers such as Swords Dance Garchomp and Blaziken. U-turn allows Dragapult to maintain momentum by pivoting while also chipping down switch-ins such as Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and Primarina. Dragapult also outspeeds Meowscarada and OHKOes it. Flamethrower allows Dragapult to chip Pokemon such as Kingambit and Excadrill and deal massive damage against Corviknight and Scizor. However, Dragon Darts can be slotted to make Dragapult a mixed attacker allowing it to lock into a Dragon-type STAB option without being left extremely exploitable as it would be with Draco Meteor and to deal more damage to Multiscale Dragonite. A Special Attack-boosting nature is preferred due to it allowing Dragapult to still outspeed most of the metagame.

Choice Scarf Dragapult is run on bulky offense teams, as it can provide unparalleled speed control, luring in Pokemon such as Dragonite and Ceruledge and revenge killing them. Clear Body allows it to ignore the Speed lowering of Sticky Web, while Infiltrator allows Dragapult to bypass Substitute users such as Annihilape and Mega Delphox. Dragapult enjoys entry hazard support from setters such as Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott to chip down foes. With its Ghost typing allowing it to spinblock against Pokemon such as Excadrill, it can maintain hazards, helping it OHKO Pokemon such as Dragonite. Choice Scarf Dragapult appreciates defensive teammates with pivoting moves such as Corviknight and Galarian Slowking, with the latter checking Fairy-type attackers such as Mega Floette and Primarina, which threaten an OHKO on Dragapult and take little damage from its attacks in return. Corviknight, especially with Body Press, serves as a good switch-in to Dark-types, which can be otherwise difficult to handle with Dragapult due to the threat of priority Sucker Punch. It also threatens significant damage with U-turn. Fighting and Fairy type partners such as Mega Lopunny, Mega Floette, and Mega Meganium cover Dragapult's weaknesses well, as all three can switch into Dark-type attacks, while Mega Floette and Mega Meganium can also switch into Dragon-type attacks. In return, they benefit from Dragapult chipping common defensive pieces such as Corviknight, Mega Dragalge, Galarian Slowking, and Hippowdon. Dragapult also appreciates hazard removal from the likes of Corviknight and Excadrill in order to have multiple entry opportunities to fire off its spammable STAB attacks. Volt Switch Rotom-Wash and Mega Raichu Y are excellent VoltTurn partners with Dragapult pressuring Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge, while Rotom-Wash and Mega Raichu Y pressure Water-type switch-ins to Dragapult, such as Toxapex and Primarina, allowing it to clean up with Shadow Ball.

• Choice Scarf Basculegion-M aims to punch holes early in the game, using Wave Crash to chunk and KO threats like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Aerodactyl. It can then clean up late-game with Last Respects, outspeeding and breaking through opposing late-game sweepers like Mega Floette and Gholdengo.

  • Last Respects: Last Respects is what turns Basculegion-M into one of the scariest threats in Regulation M-B, easily OHKOing foes like Gholdengo at 100 Base Power and Mega Floette at 150 Base Power.

  • Flip Turn: Flip Turn allows Basculegion-M to easily pivot out, dealing chip damage to put foes like Mega Tyranitar and Sylveon in range of Wave Crash and 100-Base Power Last Respects.

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Basculegion-M to outspeed foes like Mega Froslass and Sneasler.

  • Adaptability: Adaptability allows Basculegion-M to OHKO non-Kasib Berry Sinistcha with 100-Base Power Last Respects.

Teambuilding

========

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Grass-type Pokemon like Mega Venusaur can easily tank Wave Crash, while non-Mega Venusaur can outspeed and threaten to OHKO Basculegion-M with Solar Beam when in the sun. Whimsicott and Sinistcha can use Tailwind and Trick Room, respectively, to allow partners like Gholdengo and Mega Staraptor to outspeed and threaten Basculegion-M with Shadow Ball and Brave Bird, respectively.

  • Toxapex can easily swap in on Basculegion-M's Water-type attacks and punish Basculegion-M with Baneful Bunker. Other bulky Water-type Pokemon like Mega Blastoise and Rotom-Wash also give Basculegion-M trouble, hitting it with Dark Pulse and Thunderbolt, respectively. Milotic, after setting up Coil a couple of times, can safely put Basculegion-M to sleep with Hypnosis and either chip it down with Muddy Water or allow partners like Kingambit to OHKO it.

  • Kingambit can tank Wave Crash and OHKO Basculegion-M with Kowtow Cleave or even use Sucker Punch to deal huge damage to it before it can move. Hydreigon also causes issues, resisting all of Basculegion-M's attacks and retaliating with Dark Pulse or outspeeding and KOing it thanks to its own Choice Scarf.

  • Trick Room is an issue for Basculegion-M, exploiting the Choice Scarf to make it move last; slower Pokemon like Kingambit that already threaten Basculegion-M become even more threatening. Tailwind similarly allows otherwise slower Pokemon like Mega Floette to outspeed and OHKO Basculegion-M with Light of Ruin.

  • Because of Basculegion-M's Choice Scarf, it becomes very easy to exploit; when Basculegion-M is locked into Last Respects, Normal-type Pokemon like Farigiraf can easily chunk it down with Thunderbolt, but when Basculegion-M is locked into Wave Crash, the aforementioned Water- and Grass-type Pokemon as well as Dragon-type Pokemon, like Mega Dragonite, become far scarier.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Kingambit deters Trick Room thanks to its low Speed, threatens opposing Ghost-type Pokemon like Basculegion-M with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch, and hits opposing Kingambit hard with Low Kick. Sneasler can hit opposing Dark-type Pokemon hard while also doing well against Venusaur that don't carry Earth Power and Whimsicott thanks to Dire Claw. Sneasler can also form a potent combination with Basculegion-M, threatening the Normal-type Pokemon that annoy it with Close Combat. Both Kingambit and Sneasler appreciate the support against opposing Sneasler and Mega Aerodactyl, respectively. Garchomp can easily switch in on Thunderbolt from Rotom-Wash and hits foes like Toxapex hard with Earthquake.

  • Mega Charizard Y can OHKO Grass-type Pokemon like Venusaur that give Basculegion-M trouble while using Solar Beam to deal with Water-types, gaining an extra layer of support against Rock-type Pokemon in return. Basculegion-M also provides good coverage against opposing Fire-type Pokemon like Mega Delphox and Mega Charizard Y, which Mega Floette greatly appreciates. To return the favor, Mega Floette hits Dragon- and Dark-type Pokemon hard.

  • Whimsicott and Grimmsnarl both help against opposing speed control; Whimsicott helps match Tailwind and lock Trick Room users into Trick Room with Encore, while Grimmsnarl sets up dual screens, allowing Basculegion-M to survive otherwise lethal attacks like Sucker Punch from Kingambit. Both also have access to Fairy-type STAB moves, while Basculegion-M helps out against the aforementioned Fire-type Pokemon as well as Gholdengo.

Revenge Killer.description:
• Basculegion-M is one of the strongest revenge killers in the metagame, able to function both with and without rain. Along with acting as an offensive pivot against opposing frail leads, Basculegion-M also offers the ability to constantly threaten an OHKO on several common threats and Mega Evolutions, such as Aerodactyl, Talonflame, Mega Tyranitar, and Mega Charizard Y. Basculegion-M also possesses relatively decent natural bulk, allowing it to survive the occasional neutral hit. Basculegion-M's bulk also lets it act as a late-game sweeper more reliably by making use of its allies to remove its checks in the early game or to ultimately expend enough of the opponent's resources to allow Basculegion-M to enter, outspeed, and then brute force stragglers through the use of Last Respects or Wave Crash.

  • Last Respects: Last Respects's damage, when powered up by fallen allies, is often enough to OHKO most of the common non-Ghost-resistant metagame threats even after defensive investment. Still, it is generally recommended to avoid locking into the move before allies have started fainting to allow Last Respects to reach its coveted OHKO capabilities. 150 Base Power is a reliable goal to hit once Basculegion-M settles on the field, as Last Respects becomes able to OHKO common Water-resistant foes such as Pelipper and Rotom-Wash, which would otherwise survive a Wave Crash even under rain.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet is used to allow Basculegion-M to finish off low-health targets and ensure damage when you're on the back foot, with the added benefit of allowing Basculegion-M to potentially evade Kingambit's Sucker Punch.

  • Positioning: Flip Turn is Basculegion-M's primary tool to pivot and reset momentum. Basculegion-M largely prefers not being led with, due to the predictability of being locked into a move and lack of Base Power. Flip Turn, when combined with Choice Scarf, also allows Basculegion-M to put in some chip damage and reset unfavorable positioning before the opponent's Pokemon can move. The set thrives on picking off weakened foes, so priority should be placed on removing threats to Basculegion-M.

Other Options

  • Icy Wind: Icy Wind may be used as a speed control replacement over Aqua Jet, sacrificing a priority option for the ability to drop the foe's Speed before they can move and break Focus Sash with its chip damage. It also heavily chips Garchomp, which is particularly vulnerable to it in the early-game. If you opt for this move, greater caution should be exercised when positioning Basculegion-M, as it will offer very little damage while locked into the move and will also invite opposing switch-ins. Kingambit and Milotic are potentially catastrophic; not only do they resist Icy Wind, but it will also trigger Defiant and Competitive, respectively.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: A Choice Scarf will allow Basculegion-M to reach Talonflame's Speed and outspeed the most common options above base 100 Speed, such as Sneasler, Mega Floette, and Mega Froslass.

Abilities

  • Adaptability: Adaptability allows Basculegion-M to pick up several key OHKOs; Wave Crash threatens a reliable OHKO on Aerodactyl, its Mega Evolution, and Excadrill. Meanwhile, 150-Base Power Last Respects will reliably remove many common neutral targets, like Sneasler and Talonflame, and it also threatens a potential OHKO against most Mega Floette sets.

SP Spreads

  • Jolly: A Jolly nature may be chosen to outpace Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox, which would otherwise outspeed Basculegion-M and, in Mega Gengar's case, threaten it with super effective damage. This will also allow Basculegion-M to outspeed Aerodactyl and Talonflame, which allows Basculegion-M to potentially deny them from setting Tailwind.

  • Adamant: An Adamant nature allows Wave Crash to OHKO uninvested Mega Floette as well as Maushold and 150-Base Power Last Respects to OHKO Mega Scovillain semi-reliably.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Priority attackers pose the biggest threat to Basculegion-M. Kingambit is at the forefront of said threats, as it can threaten Basculegion with Sucker Punch for an OHKO while often having enough bulk to survive a rain-boosted Wave Crash. Basculegion-M is also threatened by bulky Water-resistant pokemon, particularly Grass-types such as Mega Venusaur that can hit it for super effective damage in return. Archaludon poses a serious threat to Basculegion-M in the rain with its Electro Shot and high physical bulk supplemented by Stamina. Basculegion-M's Speed tier means it will often be outran by other Choice Scarf users, like Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, and Vivillion, and especially speedy threats such as Mega Aerodactyl, and it's also particularly vulnerable to foes' Tailwind if it's unmatched. Common sun leads, such as Whimsicott with its Prankster ability, can specifically pose an indirect threat to Basculegion-M, nullifying its Speed advantage or forcing weather control through Sunny Day.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M is part of a known core made up of Sneasler, Kingambit, and itself. Basculegion-M appreciates Sneasler's capability to remove threats such as Kingambit and Incineroar with its Close Combat while also offering Fake Out support to help Basculegion-M with repositioning. Sneasler can cover many of Basculegion-M's weaknesses while being a fine choice to lead, which Basculegion-M specifically tends to avoid. Archaludon walls Basculegion-M early-game but lacks Stamina's Defense boost, which makes it particularly susceptible to Sneasler leads. Kingambit rounds out the trio by discouraging Intimidate through its Defiant ability and threatening Farigiraf, which is immune to Basculegion-M's Last Respects, while also discouraging Trick Room thanks to its lower Speed tier. Kingambit also renders the matchup against opposing Choice Scarf Basculegion-M less volatile by pressuring them with Sucker Punch, letting Basculegion-M avoid a Speed tie. Basculegion-M appreciates Pelipper's ability to set rain, which boosts its damage output and enables it to outspeed faster Choice Scarf users by setting Tailwind. Also, Pelipper's Hurricane provides coverage against bulky Grass-types that may otherwise threaten Basculegion-M like Sinistcha and Venusaur.

  • How to Overcome Basculegion-M's Weaknesses: Basculegion-M's primary weakness to priority and susceptibility to Intimidate and common sun leads means it greatly appreciates being with partners with access to pivoting moves such as Incineroar with Parting Shot, which through its typing and bulk can be an effective defensive pivot that can sponge hits, particularly from Dark-, Ghost-, and Grass-type attacks that threaten Basculegion-M. Redirection users such as Sinistcha and Mega Scovillain are also greatly appreciated as a way to keep Basculegion-M safe from priority such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and any threatening single-target damage. Fake Out users like Sneasler and the previously mentioned Incineroar can buy the time for Basculegion-M to pivot out safely or get a key attack off. Basculegion-M overall greatly appreciates being paired with Tailwind users like Talonflame and Pelipper, as they allow Basculegion-M to overcome its weakness to faster Choice Scarf users, as well as avoiding the Speed tie with other Choice Scarf Basculegion-M. Weather control options such as Pelipper with Drizzle and Sableye with Rain Dance bolster Basculegion-M's power, allowing Wave Crash to score otherwise unattainable OHKOs on Pokemon like Sylveon while also counteracting the potential damage loss incurred from opposing sun teams. Allies like Sneasler and Garchomp, with their Fighting- and Ground-type coverage, respectively, help deal with Basculegion-M's biggest obstacle: Kingambit.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Basculegion-M is able to output monstrous amounts of damage with the combination of Adaptability and its high-Base Power moves. This set takes advantage of its strong natural bulk to ease matchups that would otherwise heavily favor the opponent, such as Kingambit and Mega Gengar, while still maintaining offensive prowess through the use of Mystic Water or using Sitrus Berry to alleviate Wave Crash's recoil damage.

  • Wave Crash: Wave Crash is Basculegion-M's most consistent STAB move, allowing it to threaten Trick Room setters such as Farigiraf, as Basculegion-M's bulk usually isn't enough to outlast Trick Room, while also OHKOing or 2HKOing most Pokemon. Crucially, it lets Basculegion-M OHKO Sneasler. In combination with its defensive typing, Basculegion-M can almost always serve as a band-aid for Sneasler-weak teams.

  • Last Respects: This move allows Basculegion-M to function as a late-game sweeper, letting it OHKO most Pokemon in the format after two of its allies faint. However, it is also usable after just one ally has fainted, usually in situations where Wave Crash recoil needs to be avoided. At 100 Base Power, it is able to OHKO Pokemon such as non-Kasib Berry Sinistcha, Mega Froslass, and Sneasler.

Items

  • Mystic Water: Mystic Water allows Basculegion-M to reach OHKOs on important metagame threats such as bulky Mega Floette, bulky Mega Gengar, and medium-bulk Mega Charizard Y in the sun with Wave Crash.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry allows Basculegion-M to heal enough to safely use Wave Crash instead of knocking itself out due to recoil damage. This can be important against Pokemon such as Kingambit, which would invalidate Wave Crash as an option after a Sucker Punch.

Focus Sash Attacker.description:
• This Basculegion-M set utilizes Focus Sash to mitigate Basculegion-M's worst matchups, allowing it to deal consistent damage without having to reposition in front of Kingambit or Mega Gengar, as Focus Sash allows it to survive a hit and threaten heavy damage in return.

  • Liquidation: This set uses Liquidation instead of Wave Crash, as the recoil damage from Wave Crash would invalidate Focus Sash. While it does not threaten OHKOs in the same fashion as Wave Crash, Liquidation still allows Basculegion-M to threaten Dark-types such as Incineroar, Kingambit, and Tyranitar. It also allows Basculegion-M to threaten an OHKO on foes such as Mega Delphox at the start of the match.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash lets Basculegion-M safely threaten the likes of Mega Gengar and Mega Froslass, even without speed control or redirection. It pairs well with Basculegion-M's Ghost typing, preventing Fake Out from breaking Focus Sash. However, it does mean that Basculegion-M cannot attack Garchomp effectively until at least one ally has fainted due to Last Respects' low Base Power and Garchomp's Rough Skin breaking Focus Sash if Basculegion-M hits it with Liquidation or Aqua Jet.

SP Spreads

  • 16 HP / 24 Atk / 6 Def / 20 Spe with Adamant: This spread allows Basculegion-M to outspeed Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp in Tailwind while always surviving Sucker Punch from non-Black Glasses Kingambit. It is also able to almost always survive Shadow Ball from bulky Mega Gengar and Timid Mega Froslass. The Attack investment allows Basculegion-M to always OHKO bulky Mega Floette with Wave Crash when equipped with Mystic Water.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread is only used by Focus Sash Basculegion-M, as it does not need any bulk and instead prefers to maximize its damage output and Speed.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Kingambit is Basculegion-M's biggest enemy. It is bulky enough to survive Wave Crash while resisting Last Respects and not taking much damage from Liquidation. On top of that, it threatens Basculegion-M with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch, both of which are able to OHKO Basculegion-M when Kingambit is holding Black Glasses. Sinistcha is also able to take all of Basculegion-M's moves if Last Respects has no Base Power boosts, and it can redirect them while its partner takes out Basculegion-M. Alternatively, Sinistcha can threaten Basculegion-M directly with Matcha Gotcha. However, once one of Basculegion-M's allies has fainted, Last Respects will almost always OHKO Sinistcha unless it is holding Kasib Berry. If using Mystic Water or Sitrus Berry without speed control, opposing Basculegion-M and Mega Charizard Y also check it, as Basculegion-M is OHKOed by Last Respects and Solar Beam, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: While not necessary for Basculegion-M to function, it appreciates speed control such as Trick Room or Tailwind, as it lets Basculegion-M beat tough matchups such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Froslass, and Mega Gengar. Mega Floette is a great partner, as it threatens Kingambit and Archaludon with Light of Ruin. It is also able to OHKO Garchomp, which Basculegion-M can sometimes regret targeting due to the additional recoil from Rough Skin adding up quickly with Wave Crash's recoil. Kingambit can also support Basculegion-M, as it OHKOs opposing Ghost-types such as Basculegion-M and Sinistcha. Additionally, if Kingambit has Low Kick, it is able to help clear opposing Kingambit out for Basculegion-M while also covering Kingambit's biggest weakness, Sneasler. On top of that, Kingambit deters Intimidate from opposing Incineroar, which would otherwise be especially effective against Basculegion-M.

  • How to Overcome Basculegion-M's Weaknesses: Due to Basculegion-M's coverage and defensive options, very little can explicitly force it to switch out. While Sneasler and Mega Floette help with Sinistcha and Kingambit, an allied Kingambit can also take care of Mega Gengar and Mega Froslass. Additionally, it threatens Sinistcha, and, if holding Chople Berry, it can threaten opposing Kingambit with Low Kick. As such, when Basculegion-M is being threatened, it can use Protect while a partner mitigates the threat. Examples include setting speed control such as Tailwind with Whimsicott or Talonflame or simply knocking out the threat if Basculegion-M cannot hit it for significant damage. Setting up Basculegion-M for success in the late game is also a viable gameplan. When doing so, one should prioritize taking out the likes of Kingambit, Incineroar, and Sinistcha while setting some form of speed control to allow Basculegion-M to outspeed Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y and Mega Froslass.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Basculgion-M is enjoying a fantastic offensive type combination in the current metagame, which, when combined with Adaptability, makes it a standout pick as a late-game sweeper with Last Respects and a potent early-game scout with Flip Turn.

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf gives Basculegion-M the Speed it needs to chunk foes and get out safely early-game while also allowing you to bring it in late-game without spending a turn to set up Agility. However, Basculegion-M's pitiful base 78 Speed means that it will be outsped by most of the other Choice Scarf users in the format, as well as most Dragon Dance users, so you need to be careful when positioning Basculegion-M.

  • Wave Crash: Wave Crash will be Basculegion-M's primary early-game damage option if you elect to not pivot it out.
