  • Last Respects: Even after just one team member is KOed, Last Respects becomes an extremely potent move that's very difficult to switch into, and it gives Basculegion-M immense sweeping power once both allies have fainted.

  • Flip Turn: Adaptability allows Flip Turn to deal notable damage for a pivoting move.

  • Aqua Jet: Adaptability-boosted Aqua Jet does a considerable amount of damage and can get Basculegion-M out of trouble against other priority users or Speed-boosted foes.

Other Options

  • Ice Fang: Ice Fang provides coverage against Dragon-types and threatens Garchomp and Dragonite right out of the gate.

  • Head Smash: Head Smash gives Basculegion-M a heavily damaging coverage option that threatens Gyarados and Dragonite.

Offensive.description:
• This Agility set gives Basculegion-M the freedom to outspeed and threaten the majority of its metagame-relevant foes while enabling it to use multiple moves.

  • Opposing Priority Users: While setting up Agility can make Basculegion-M an absolutely terrifying sweeper, late-game checks such as Aegislash, Mimikyu, and Kingambit are quite popular in the current metagame, so be careful when you see these during Team Preview.

  • Adamant Nature: Agility's boost is going to give Basculegion-M plenty of Speed to set up its sweep. As Basculegion-M lacks an Attack-boosting setup move, an Adamant nature is preferred over Jolly. Adamant Basculegion-M is already outspeeding Choice Scarf Garchomp with an Agility boost, while a Jolly nature won't allow it to outspeed the likes of Choice Scarf Jolly Meowscarada.

Items

  • Mystic Water versus Spell Tag: These items will allow Basculegion-M's STAB moves to do hilariously high damage. Mystic Water allows Basculegion-M to OHKO physically defensive Hippowdon with Wave Crash and has the added bonus of juicing up Aqua Jet's damage when it needs to rely on priority. On the other hand, Spell Tag will allow Last Respects to tear through walls, letting it OHKO maximum HP Mega Scizor after Stealth Rock at 150 Base Power.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash ensures that Basculegion-M is going to tank a hit while it sets up Agility, but because entry hazards are very popular in the current metagame, saving your Focus Sash user for last can be a risky venture.

Disruptive Support.description:
• Sneasler is a fast yet frail offensive support Pokemon that most notably stops incoming attacks with Fake Out, enabling its allies to safely attack or set up. Its STAB combination helps it check prominent threats like Mega Floette, Whimsicott, and Kingambit.

  • Dire Claw: Beyond threatening Fairy-types like Sylveon and Grimmsnarl, Dire Claw's status effects can help turn the tide of a battle in your favor.

  • Protect vs. Quick Guard: Protect is generally used as the final move, but teams that revolve around setup sweepers like Mega Delphox and Mega Blastoise may prefer Sneasler to have Quick Guard. While giving up Sneasler's ability to defend itself is a notable drawback, Quick Guard's protection against priority attacks like Incineroar's Fake Out and Kingambit's Sucker Punch is incredibly useful to keep the aforementioned sweepers unharmed as much as possible. This is especially important for Mega Blastoise, as it needs to be healthy for Water Spout to hit hard.

  • Unburden: Unburden grants Sneasler unparalleled Speed, ensuring that it will move first unless it is interrupted by Fake Out or facing an opposing Unburden-boosted Sneasler. Activating the ability is important to let Sneasler outspeed weather sweepers like Venusaur, Mega Swampert, and Excadrill.

  • Focus Sash vs. White Herb: Opting for Focus Sash ensures the fragile Sneasler will survive at least one hit, though it will make triggering Unburden harder. White Herb sacrifices Focus Sash's insurance for synergy with Close Combat, simultaneously wiping away the defense drops and activating Unburden. It also lets Sneasler thwart Incineroar's and Staraptor's Intimidate once.

Other Options

  • Poison Jab and Poison Touch: Poison Jab can be used over Dire Claw if poison's residual damage is more useful for the team than paralysis or sleep. The secondary effect chance can be enhanced with Poison Touch, which also benefits Sneasler's other attacks, though Unburden's Speed boost is often too valuable to sacrifice.

  • Coaching: Coaching can be slotted over Protect to bolster physical allies like Kingambit and Basculegion-M, as the potential of these attackers with a +1 Attack boost can justify the inability to make defensive maneuvers.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide threatens the ubiquitous Mega Charizard Y with heavy damage, and with Sneasler's excellent Speed, it can let Sneasler game for flinches in desperate situations. Rock Slide usually replaces Fake Out on Focus Sash sets, as Sneasler can't afford to drop either of its STAB moves.

  • Gunk Shot: Gunk Shot is a somewhat unreliable alternative to Dire Claw that ensures the OHKO on most physically bulky variants of Sylveon and Mega Floette. Notably, an uninvested Gunk Shot still hits harder than a fully invested Dire Claw, which might prove useful for bulky Sneasler variants.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly or Adamant: A Jolly nature lets Sneasler outspeed Whimsicott and Modest variants of Mega Delphox and Mega Froslass. An Adamant nature ensures Sneasler OHKOes maximum HP Sylveon with Dire Claw and makes it possible to OHKO Chople Berry Kingambit with Close Combat.

  • 29 HP / 19 Def / 18 Spe with Jolly: A bulky spread can enable Sneasler to survive attacks it otherwise would not without investment, which helps incentivize the use of White Herb. This spread guarantees survival against Timid Mega Floette's Moonblast and grants a good chance to avoid the 2HKO from Adamant Life Orb Dragonite's Extreme Speed, while the Speed investment ensures Sneasler outspeeds Jolly Garchomp and opposing Adamant Sneasler. Even with no Attack investment, Close Combat is favored to 2HKO uninvested Garchomp.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Ghost-types are the most reliable defensive checks to Sneasler because they resist or are immune to its STAB attacks. Sneasler is practically useless against Gholdengo, which is immune to anything it can do and can go for a Nasty Plot as it switches out. Basculegion-M can switch into a predicted attack and proceed to threaten heavy damage with Wave Crash or Last Respects, though it risks getting statused by Dire Claw. Sinistcha can redirect any of Sneasler's attacks and is bulky enough to take its Poison-type moves despite lacking a resistance to them. Mega Gengar can easily trap and eliminate Sneasler, paving the way for an ally like Kingambit to clean up late-game. If it hasn't Mega Evolved yet, Gengar can still force Sneasler out with its presence so that it can Mega Evolve and KO Pokemon with the Perish trap strategy.

  • Ground-types like Garchomp, Mega Swampert, and Excadrill easily OHKO Sneasler with their STAB attacks, and they can use Choice Scarf or weather to outspeed it if Unburden isn't active. The former two examples are durable enough to withstand Close Combat, while the last of these usually sports Focus Sash to guarantee survival. Other foes like Mega Metagross and Mega Staraptor can also win against Sneasler one-on-one thanks to their defensive profiles and super effective STAB moves, and Staraptor can weaken non-White Herb sets with Intimidate before Mega Evolving.

  • Without an Unburden boost, faster attackers like Mega Delphox and Mega Aerodactyl can easily threaten Sneasler with an OHKO while generally being bulky enough to take at least one STAB attack from it. Notably, Mega Aerodactyl can bypass Focus Sash's insurance with Dual Wingbeat and neutralize Unburden's Speed boost with Tailwind. Farigiraf also can OHKO Sneasler with Psychic and turn its Speed and ability into hindrances by setting up Trick Room; additionally, Armor Tail prevents it from bothering Farigiraf's team with Fake Out.

  • Toxapex is a sturdy foe that resists Sneasler's STAB attacks and can trap it with Infestation. While Toxapex can't directly damage Sneasler much, the opponent will have an easier time eliminating it with other Pokemon like Garchomp and Mega Charizard Y once it has been trapped. This can force you to make difficult decisions on whether or not to switch Sneasler out.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Dark-types like Kingambit and Incineroar are ideal partners for Sneasler, as they can easily handle Ghost-types. Additionally, Kingambit's Sucker Punch allows it to support Sneasler against speedier attackers if Unburden isn't active, notably OHKOing Mega Delphox. Meanwhile, Incineroar's access to Fake Out allows it to work together with Sneasler in shutting down opposing Pokemon, and Intimidate and Parting Shot make it easier for Sneasler to switch in while not getting hurt too much.

  • Sneasler's good matchup against opposing Kingambit enables Basculegion-M to attack mid- or late-game more easily, as it will not have to worry about Sucker Punch. It can help Sneasler out in return by dealing with Fire-, Ghost-, and Ground-types like Mega Delphox, Gholdengo, and Excadrill. These two also pair well with Kingambit, forming an effective core of physical attackers that many players use.

  • Sneasler stands out as a secondary offensive piece in setup-oriented teams based around Mega Evolutions like Mega Delphox, Calm Mind Mega Floette, and Mega Blastoise. It can easily deal with Kingambit, a foe these Pokemon can have trouble beating one-on-one, and it can provide Fake Out and Quick Guard support to let them more easily set up or attack unhindered. In return, Mega Delphox can handle Sinistcha, Toxapex, and Mega Metagross; Mega Floette can deal with Garchomp and Mega Staraptor; and a set-up Mega Blastoise can help out against Excadrill, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-M. Furthermore, all of these Mega Evolutions have access to spread moves, which help Sneasler out against redirectors like the aforementioned Sinistcha.

Offensive Support.description:
• Sneasler is the fastest relevant Fake Out user in Regulation M-A, guaranteeing a threat will be halted so that Sneasler's ally can move safely, and it's undoubtedly the fastest Pokemon in the format with Unburden active. Thanks to its STAB combination, Sneasler also threatens many prominent Pokemon like Kingambit, Mega Floette, and Sylveon.

  • Close Combat: In addition to handling Dark- and Normal-types like Incineroar, Mega Tyranitar, and Maushold, Close Combat's drawback can be used with White Herb to grant Sneasler unparalleled Speed.

  • Dire Claw: Though it shouldn't be relied upon, Dire Claw's suite of status conditions can potentially push a critical situation in your favor.

Other Options

  • Coaching: Coaching can be slotted over Protect to provide support to physically offensive teammates like Garchomp, as the extra power and bulk granted to such Pokemon can justify the inability to make defensive plays.

  • Rock-type Coverage: Rock Slide and Rock Tomb can be considered to severely damage Mega Charizard Y and Talonflame. Rock Slide deals spread damage and can let you game for flinches, while Rock Tomb is a more reliable alternative that trades damage output for the potential to let Sneasler's teammates hit an otherwise faster foe like Mega Froslass before it moves.

  • Throat Chop: Throat Chop lets Sneasler threaten Ghost-types like Aegislash and Mega Gengar and act as a late-game emergency check to Choice Scarf Basculegion-M with Focus Sash.

  • Gunk Shot: Although it's less accurate than Dire Claw, Gunk Shot's ability to let even Jolly Sneasler one-shot most bulky variants of Mega Floette and Sylveon makes it worth considering. Additionally, Adamant Sneasler's Gunk Shot is very likely to OHKO Mega Delphox.

Items

  • White Herb: White Herb is the most common item on Sneasler, as the item grants it on-demand speed control with use of Close Combat. White Herb also gives it a buffer against stat drops incurred by Incineroar's Intimidate and Milotic's Icy Wind.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash generally ensures Sneasler will make at least one move before fainting, though it'll be harder to activate Unburden without a would-be fatal blow. Focus Sash is also a contested item that teammates like Aerodactyl may need to function effectively.

Abilities

  • Unburden: Unburden's Speed boost is crucial to outspeed faster foes like Choice Scarf Garchomp, Sand Rush Excadrill, and Chlorophyll Venusaur.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant or Jolly: An Adamant nature lets Sneasler OHKO maximum HP Sylveon with Dire Claw and have a favored chance to OHKO Chople Berry Kingambit with Close Combat while still outspeeding neutral-natured weather attackers like Venusaur and Excadrill with Unburden active. A Jolly nature allows Sneasler to outspeed opposing Adamant Sneasler, Maushold, and Alolan Ninetales, letting it use Fake Out first against the former; note that positive-natured variants of Venusaur and Excadrill are uncommon.

  • 32 HP / 4 Atk / 29 Def / 1 Spe with Jolly: A bulky spread is an option on White Herb sets to allow Sneasler to survive otherwise deadly attacks and still pack enough power to 2HKO neutral foes like Garchomp with Close Combat. This spread allows it to survive Aerodactyl's and Sharp Beak Talonflame's Dual Wingbeat and Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum while outspeeding Adamant Garchomp and Modest Mega Floette, as well as Jolly Sand Rush Excadrill with Unburden active.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Sneasler is walled by Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Aegislash; they resist Dire Claw and ignore Fake Out and Close Combat, letting them safely come in on predicted attacks. Mega Gengar is a very threatening Ghost-type, as Gengar can force Sneasler out and Mega Evolve to trap its teammates. Sinistcha, in particular, can set up Trick Room and render Sneasler very vulnerable to attacks; Farigiraf accomplishes the same while preventing Fake Out from hitting its team and directly threatening it with Psychic or Twin Beam. Without Unburden active, faster attackers like Choice Scarf Garchomp, Sand Rush Excadrill, Mega Delphox, and Aerodactyl can easily OHKO it, with the latter even bypassing Focus Sash with Dual Wingbeat and matching Unburden with Tailwind.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Kingambit is one of the best partners for Sneasler, as it threatens Ghost-types and prominent Trick Room setters with its STAB Dark-type moves. Basculegion-M appreciates Sneasler's good matchup against opposing Kingambit, which can threaten its late-game sweeps with Sucker Punch, while Dragon-types like Garchomp and Archaludon can safely let their STAB moves loose with opposing Fairy-types removed by Sneasler.

  • How to Overcome Sneasler's Weaknesses: Choosing Kingambit during Team Preview will give Sneasler security when facing Ghost-types alongside it or ensure you have a reliable switch-in to them. Kingambit also benefits from Trick Room, making it a potential counterlead against Sinistcha and Farigiraf. Against faster threats, aim to have Unburden activated by the time they come out; if that's not plausible, priority moves like Kingambit's Sucker Punch can help lessen their Speed advantage. Weather setters like Mega Charizard Y can also nullify the Speed advantage of opposing weather attackers like Excadrill, though keep in mind that opponents will often attempt to fight for weather control with their own setters like Mega Tyranitar.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Sneasler is one of the tier's most threatening sweepers with its high Attack and Speed, the latter being unparalleled with Unburden. Dire Claw is usually the preferred Poison-type STAB move to destroy targets such as Primarina and Mega Meganium; however, Gunk Shot is an option to get the OHKO on Clefable and Hatterene, at the expense of its lower accuracy. Throat Chop enables Sneasler to hit Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Aegislash and Galarian Slowking, while Shadow Claw can bypass the common Colbur Berry on Aegislash and Galarian Slowking and still hit Annihilape super effectively, at the expense of a lower Base Power. Acrobatics is another option, which is boosted by Unburden and hits Annihilape and opposing Sneasler super effectively. Adamant is the preferred nature, as Sneasler already outspeeds the entire unboosted metagame after Unburden while gaining important benchmarks such as the OHKO on Mega Metagross and Rotom-Wash with Close Combat at +2. Jolly is useful for outspeeding Mega Metagross and Mega Staraptor before Unburden activates. White Herb enables Sneasler to gain the Unburden boost after a Close Combat, whereas Focus Sash allows it to survive super effective hits such as Excadrill's Earthquake, Corviknight's Brave Bird, and Mega Delphox's Psyshock while giving Sneasler an opportunity to set up Swords Dance.

Swords Dance Sneasler best fits on offense teams where it is appreciated due to its ability to absorb Toxic Spikes while being naturally fast and threatening Fairy-type Pokemon such as Hatterene, Clefable, and Mega Floette. Sneasler enjoys having wallbreakers such as Blaziken and Ceruledge to chip down shared checks such as Corviknight, tank Garchomp, and Hippowdon. Special Attackers such as Mega Meganium, Mega Floette, and Primarina beat these checks outright. Moreover, Sneasler appreciates entry hazards such as Stealth Rock from Glimmora and Excadrill, which give it a chance to OHKO Corviknight with +2 Close Combat. Hisuian Samurott can set Spikes, improving rolls against tank Garchomp and Hippowdon. Focus Sash Sneasler also appreciates hazard control such as Rapid Spin Excadrill, Mortal Spin Glimmora, and Hatterene to preserve Focus Sash, while White Herb sets appreciate it preventing Sticky Web from prematurely activating White Herb. Sneasler struggles breaking Pokemon such as Aegislash and Toxapex, so Ground-types such as Garchomp and Excadrill are invaluable as teammates. Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott and Hydreigon benefit from Sneasler dealing with Fairy-types such as Clefable and Mega Floette and can switch into Psychic-types such as Mega Delphox. On more bulky teams, slow pivots such as Corviknight, Galarian Slowking, and Rotom-Wash are appreciated due to Sneasler's frailty and can bring it in freely to set up a Swords Dance.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Unburden Sweeper.description:
• With the powerful Unburden ability, Sneasler can become a dangerous cleaner that wrecks havoc on frailer teams.

  • Throat Chop versus Shadow Claw : When covering Psychic- and Ghost-types, Throat Chop is usually preferred for its higher power over Shadow Claw. However, Adamant Sneasler with Shadow Claw has about a 50/50 chance to knock out offensive Mimikyu after Disguise breaks.

  • Swords Dance : If allowed to set up a Swords Dance, Sneasler can quickly spiral out of control and even overpower Hippowdon and Corviknight if they have been chipped.

  • Fake Out: Fake Out can help get targets into KO range of its more powerful attacks, and the priority helps Sneasler catch faster foes prior to activating Unburden.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is usually preferred to maximize sweeping potential, and with Unburden active, Sneasler can effortlessly outrun even Choice Scarf Dragapult. WIth maximum investment, Adamant Sneasler also maintains enough Speed to outrun threats like Mega Glimmora and unboosted Garchomp before Unburden's boost. Jolly gives Sneasler a little more consistency, allowing it to outrun more threats such as Mega Starmie and Focus Sash Gengar before Unburden activates.

Other Options

  • Acrobatics: Acrobatics is Sneasler's best move against threats like Mega Venusaur, Volcarona, and opposing Sneasler, though the move's damage is reliant on Sneasler consuming its item beforehand.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide landing a clean OHKO on Mega Charizard Y is huge, but its uses are otherwise limited.

  • Fling: Fling with King's Rock or Light Ball is the most flexible method of triggering Sneasler's Unburden, but the sacrifice to damage and coverage makes it a hard sell.

Items

  • White Herb: White Herb synergizes fantastically with Sneasler, allowing it to activate Unburden through its best attack Close Combat while also nullifying the defense drops once. White Herb can also function as insurance against Intimidate users.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can give the somewhat frail Sneasler a bit more survivability, especially against priority attacks. However, it does make Sneasler reliant on the opponent to trigger Unburden for it.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry puts Sneasler into a more niche role for its team, focused on countering status users like Yawn Umbreon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash.

Choice Scarf.description:
Meowscarada can take advantage of its great Speed and Attack stats, good STAB and coverage moves, and ability Protean to function as a fantastic Choice Scarf user and offensive pivot. Choice Scarf notably lets Meowscarada outspeed Dragapult and Mega Raichu Y as well as boosted threats such as +1 Garchomp and Dragonite. Flower Trick can OHKO Grass-weak targets, like Hisuian Samurott and Primarina, as well as OHKOing Mega Raichu Y after Stealth Rock. Knock Off lets Meowscarada KO Dark-weak foes like Dragapult, as well as Mega Delphox and Galarian Slowking after Stealth Rock. Knock Off also makes progress by removing held items from Meowscarada's common switch-ins like Corviknight and Clefable. U-turn allows Meowscarada to maintain momentum against checks such as Blaziken, Kingambit, Corviknight, and Archaludon while also doing sizable damage to Bug-weak foes like Hisuian Samurott and Hydreigon. Triple Axel lets Meowscarada OHKO Dragon-types like Garchomp and Multiscale Dragonite, as well as Mega Staraptor if all three hits connect; after Stealth Rock, all three hits also remove bulky Mega Dragalge and Mega Meganium, which can otherwise switch in freely against it.

Meowscarada works well on both offensive and balance teams that appreciate a fast pivot that threatens more typical speed control options, like Dragapult, Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott, and Mega Raichu Y. Due to its immense frailty, Meowscarada greatly appreciates slow pivoting from the likes of Corviknight, Galarian Slowking, and Mega Dragalge to bring it in safely. Corviknight in particular is a great teammate, as it can clear entry hazards that can quickly wear Meowscarada down from constantly switching in while also threatening Fighting-types with Brave Bird, like Sneasler, Mega Lopunny, and Annihilape, that would otherwise force Meowscarada out. Meowscarada also appreciates Fighting-type teammates of its own like Blaziken, and the aforementioned Sneasler and Mega Lopunny to overwhelm its typical checks like Kingambit and Archaludon; Blaziken can additionally pressure Corviknight. In return, Meowscarada can threaten Dragapult and Rotom-Wash that can otherwise greatly threaten the aforementioned Fighting-types with a crippling burn or paralysis. Special attackers like Primarina, Volcarona, Mega Raichu Y, and Mega Delphox can also function as great teammates, as Meowscarada can deal with Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge, which can commonly give them trouble. In return, they can take advantage of the Pokemon Meowscarada commonly brings in, like Corviknight and Clefable, to set up. Mega Delphox can switch into and pressure Blaziken, which easily comes in on Meowscarada's attacks. Steel-types like Kingambit, Excadrill, and Aegislash also greatly appreciate Meowscarada's ability to threaten Ground-types, like Garchomp and Hippowdon, while they can threaten Fairy-types like Clefable and Mega Floette in return. Hisuian Samurott and Garchomp can provide Spikes and Stealth Rock, capitalizing on the switches Meowscarada forces and helping it secure KOs against targets such as Mega Raichu Y, Mega Dragalge, and Mega Meganium. Setup sweepers, like Swords Dance Garchomp, Scizor, and Mega Mawile, also appreciate Meowscarada's ability to bring them in with U-turn and chip down their checks like Rotom-Wash, Hippowdon, and Mega Metagross.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Meowscarada's ability Protean and good base Speed combined with Choice Scarf make it an extremely versatile solution to many speedy threats such as Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, Mega Gyarados after a Dragon Dance, and Mega Lopunny.

  • Flower Trick: Because it always lands a critical hit, Meowscarada's signature move is a very consistent source of damage against Intimidate Gyarados and Shell Smash Blastoise behind dual screens. It notably 2HKOes Hippowdon and Garchomp and OHKOes Basculegion-M and Primarina.

  • Triple Axel: Triple Axel covers targets that resist Grass- and Dark-type moves, OHKOing foes such as Multiscale Dragonite, Focus Sash Garchomp, Starapator, and Hydreigon. Triple Axel can also 2HKO both Mega Charizard X and Mega Charizard Y, making it very difficult for them to switch in and forcing Mega Charizard X to refrain from using Dragon Dance, as it still won't outspeed Meowscarada after one boost.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off allows Meowscarada to remove Leftovers and do decent damage to Aegislash. It can be used to remove Leftovers and Sitrus Berry from Archaludon and Leftovers from Corviknight as they switch in. It will also 2HKO Mega Evolutions such as Mega Delphox, Mega Starmie, and Mega Gengar.

  • Thunder Punch: Thunder Punch is useful against Mega Charizard Y, providing more consistent damage compared to Triple Axel. It can also be used to finish off a weakened Corviknight.

  • U-turn: U-turn maintains momentum against Meowscarada's checks and hard counters, such as Blaziken, Kingambit, Corviknight, Mega Scizor, Archaludon, and Mega Venusaur. It will also OHKO opposing Choice Scarf Meowscarada, leading to a coin flip for momentum.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature provides some niche benefits, as it is what allows Meowscarada to outspeed Timid Choice Scarf Greninja, but the main reason is to compete with opposing Meowscarada. As Meowscarada's Speed is already high with Choice Scarf, an Adamant nature allows it to more consistently OHKO Mega Gyarados with Flower Trick as well as Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar with Knock Off.

Other Options

  • Throat Chop: Throat Chop can be used as a substitute for Knock Off. It does more consistent damage against Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox, since Mega Stones can't be removed. It also stops Skeledirge from using Torch Song.

  • Low Kick: Low Kick can be useful against Archaludon and Kingambit.

Focus Sash.description:
• Focus Sash Meowscarada is useful thanks to its ability to 2HKO many foes and strike first with Sucker Punch. Focus Sash Meowscarada can take on Pokemon such as Glimmora, Mega Delphox, Mega Gyarados, Mega Greninja, and Mega Gengar one-on-one.

  • Flower Trick: Flower Trick is very helpful against Water- and Ground-type Pokemon, providing consistent damage against Gyarados, Primarina, and Hippowdon.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch gives Meowscarada an edge in finishing off faster Pokemon such as Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar. It also provides good damage against Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, and a strong chance to 2HKO offensive Mega Metagross

  • Triple Axel versus Knock Off: Triple Axel is great for beating Garchomp and Multiscale Dragonite, as well as hitting neutral targets such as Sneasler and both of Charizard's Mega Evolutions. Knock Off is a strong Dark-type move that doesn't count on Meowscarada's foe attacking first while also removing an item. It is particularly helpful against Ceruledge and Aegislash, as they will not always attack when Meowscarada uses Sucker Punch.

  • U-turn: U-turn maintains momentum against Meowscarada's hard counters, such as Archaludon or Corviknight.

  • Taunt: Taunt can avoid messy situations where your opponent's Pokemon tries to set up on Meowscarada, letting it stop Hippowdon and Mega Scizor from using Stealth Rock and Swords Dance, respectively.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature is heavily preferred for outspeeding Jolly Mega Metagross, a threat Meowscarada has the potential to surprise one-on-one.

Other Options

  • Toxic Spikes: Toxic Spikes can be strong in longer drawn-out games. This does little to alleviate Meowscarada's poor matchup against Steel-types, though.

  • Overgrow: Overgrow has good synergy with Focus Sash for boosting Flower Trick.

  • Low Kick: Low Kick is an option against Archaludon and Kingambit.

Physical Wall.description:
• Skeledirge's decent bulk and access to Unaware allow it to act as a check to some of the most threatening physical sweepers in the metagame, notably walling Mega Blaziken, Scizor, as well as IronPress variants of Mega Metagross and Corviknight. Its strong offensive typing and potential to snowball with Torch Song additionally keep it from being too passive to fit on offensive teams, setting it apart from other physical walls.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Burning physical attackers makes it even easier for Skeledirge to tank their attacks, allowing it to take on Pokemon like Mimikyu and Jolly Garchomp that can otherwise deal significant damage to it. The threat of Will-O-Wisp also makes it difficult for the opponent to safely switch in physical attackers that Skeledirge fears, like Mega Gyarados.

  • Yawn: Though Yawn lacks the potential to flip matchups that Will-O-Wisp has, it can be effective for buying free turns for Skeledirge to use Torch Song or Slack Off. Forcing switches with Yawn can also be useful to rack up entry hazard damage over the course of a game if Skeledirge is paired with an entry hazard setter.

  • Shadow Ball versus Hex: Shadow Ball lets Skeledirge deal consistent damage to Pokemon that it doesn't want to waste a turn inflicting status on and is especially useful against burn-immune Pokemon like Mega Delphox. Though more reliant on prediction, Hex pairs well with Will-O-Wisp against bulkier teams, and its greater power can help Skeledirge deal significant damage to Pokemon it typically struggles with, like Toxapex and Primarina, on the switch-in.

Other Options

  • Encore: After switching in, Skeledirge can potentially use Encore to lock slower Pokemon it struggles with into using ineffective moves, for example forcing Primarina to repeat Moonblast or Calm Mind, or Aegislash to repeat Swords Dance. This is, however, much less effective against faster Pokemon that typically won't give Skeledirge an opportunity to use Encore.

Items

  • Leftovers versus Sitrus Berry: Leftovers greatly increases Skeledirge's longevity, making it less reliant on Slack Off to stay healthy, and it can often find free turns to heal thanks to the switches it forces. Though Sitrus Berry's burst healing is less conducive to keeping a wall like Skeledirge healthy in the long run, it can make Skeledirge more consistent in certain matchups; for example, it allows Skeledirge to always avoid the 2HKO from Adamant Life Orb Mimikyu's Shadow Claw.

  • Kasib Berry: Kasib Berry allows Skeledirge to be more aggressive against Mimikyu, as it does not have to risk missing Will-O-Wisp to beat it, and provides utility by causing Poltergeist to fail once consumed, allowing Skeledirge to wall Ceruledge and physical Aegislash. If needed, Kasib Berry can also let Skeledirge stay in against special-attacking Ghost-types that could otherwise OHKO it, like Mega Gengar and Gholdengo, as well as opposing Skeledirge, and deal significant damage to them with its STAB attacks.

  • No Item: Running no item on Skeledirge causes Poltergeist to always fail against it, giving Skeledirge the same utility in this regard as Kasib Berry, and weakens Knock Off from the likes of Meowscarada and Scizor, at the cost of passive healing.

Redirection Support.description:
• Maushold is an excellent support option with moves like Follow Me to prevent its teammates from getting damaged and nullify Ghost-type attacks like Last Respects from Basculegion-M, helping allies such as Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar. With Friend Guard, its presence on the field will help its teammates survive, even against opposing spread moves that ignore Follow Me.

  • Super Fang: It is ideal, but not necessary, that Maushold be faster than its teammates in order to cut a foe's HP with Super Fang so a teammate can finish it off. Super Fang also lets Maushold continue to get value even if it is Taunted.

  • Feint versus Encore versus Helping Hand: Feint is useful for breaking a foe's Focus Sash or Wide Guard to let teammates like Mega Gardevoir continue to get value with spread moves like Hyper Voice; it also breaks Protect, preventing foes from stalling out turns of Tailwind and Trick Room. Encore can punish Fake Out from Incineroar and can be paired with Disable from Pokemon like Mega Gengar. Encore also pressures foes like Kingambit and Mega Floette not to set up with Swords Dance and Calm Mind, respectively. It is easiest to replace Feint with Encore because, like Feint, Encore is itself an answer to opposing Protect. Helping Hand will make Mega Floette's Moonblast always OHKO a bulky variant of Archaludon. It can replace the Feint slot on teams that lack spread attacks.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt shuts down Trick Room from Farigiraf, Parting Shot from Incineroar, support options from Sinistcha like Rage Powder and Life Dew, and setup options like Calm Mind from Mega Floette and Swords Dance from Kingambit. It can replace Feint, Encore, or Helping Hand.

  • Rain Dance: Rain Dance only appears on rain teams and is mainly used to overwrite sun after Mega Charizard Y activates Drought. It also overwrites Mega Tyranitar's sand to nullify its Special Defense boost and Mega Froslass's snow to make its Blizzard inaccurate. It can replace the Feint slot.

Items

  • Chople Berry: Chople Berry will essentially guarantee Maushold survives a Fighting-type attack like Close Combat from Sneasler, with enough HP left to survive extraneous damage like Fake Out or sand chip damage.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash will guarantee that Maushold survives almost any attack, but opposing Fake Out users may pressure it into using Protect, giving the opponent momentum. Using Focus Sash can make Maushold more comfortable investing less in bulk and more in Speed, allowing it to use Super Fang before an ally moves and punish faster foes with Encore, such as Mega Floette and Garchomp.

Abilities

  • Friend Guard: Friend Guard helps Maushold's less bulky teammates like Mega Delphox survive longer. Kingambit survives Heat Wave from Timid Mega Charizard Y, and Earthquake from Garchomp almost always becomes a 3HKO.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 10 Def / 24 Spe with Timid: The Speed investment allows Maushold to outspeed Garchomp and Mega Floette, with the remaining SPs dumped into HP and Defense to improve the chance of surviving Wave Crash from Basculegion-M. This spread works well with the Focus Sash set given the relative lack of bulk, though it can be used with Chople Berry too.

  • 32 HP / 17 Def / 17 SpD with Calm: Maushold will always survive Wave Crash from Basculegion-M with this defensive investment, and the remaining Special Defense SPs are used to survive Weather Ball from Mega Charizard Y most of the time. This spread is only intended for the Chople Berry set.

  • 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 Spe with Timid: This spread is only intended for Focus Sash builds. Its Speed investment allows it to outrun Lycanroc-D and Alolan Ninetales.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Taunt from Pokemon like opposing Maushold and Incineroar shuts down most of Maushold's options. Opposing Fake Out from Incineroar or Sneasler can shut down Maushold's Follow Me for a turn, which can leave the partner vulnerable. Hyper offensive options like Wave Crash in rain from Basculegion-M and Light of Ruin from Mega Floette can OHKO Maushold without Focus Sash. Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Sinistcha are immune to Super Fang and Feint.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Maushold is unable to provide high damage on its own; thus, it must be paired with high-damage partners like Mega Delphox, Kingambit, and Basculegion-M. Mega Delphox and Basculegion-M in particular appreciate Maushold's Follow Me to redirect threatening attacks like Sucker Punch from Kingambit. Friend Guard lets Mega Floette survive Dire Claw from Sneasler and lets Archaludon survive Moonblast from opposing Modest Mega Floette. Slower partners like Mega Floette and Archaludon appreciate Super Fang cutting down foes like Kingambit and opposing Mega Floette; after Super Fang, Mega Floette can KO Kingambit with Moonblast, while Archaludon can KO opposing Mega Floette with Electro Shot or Flash Cannon. Mega Blastoise benefits from Follow Me making it easier to set up with Shell Smash and Feint preventing Wide Guard from stopping Water Spout.

  • How to Overcome Maushold's Weaknesses: Mega Delphox covers opposing Fighting-types that threaten Maushold such as Sneasler and Kommo-o. Basculegion-M is a useful pivot if the opponent is threatening a Fighting-type attack. Though Maushold is commonly in the lead, bringing it in the back can help prevent its Focus Sash from being broken by Fake Out and help allies like Mega Delphox and Mega Floette clean up an endgame. Kingambit can use Kowtow Cleave to threaten the aforementioned Ghost-types Maushold cannot hit.

Setup Sweeper.description: The set for Ceruledge does not significantly change from Regulation M-A to M-B, nor does its teammates and method of play. To see the analysis information, please refer to the Regulation M-A analysis.

Focus Sash.description:
• Ceruledge's strong typing and access to Swords Dance make it a powerful offensive presence, which includes the ability to overwhelm targets like Corviknight and Volcarona that normally wall physical attackers well.

  • Weak Armor: The combination of Weak Armor and Focus Sash can turn Ceruledge into a deadly fast sweeper, making it risky for prominent physical threats like Mega Lopunny and Sneasler to attack it.

  • Shadow Sneak: Paired with Weak Armor, Ceruledge with Shadow Sneak can win priority wars it would otherwise lose, on top of being a strong cleaning attack in general.

  • Poltergeist: Poltergeist is Ceruledge's strongest STAB attack and best overall source of damage, but be careful against targets that potentially use Sitrus Berry or other consumable items; some checks like Toxapex will go without an item to render Poltergeist useless from the start!

  • Bitter Blade: Bitter Blade's strong recovery is useful after being taken down to its Focus Sash, potentially giving Ceruledge more of a buffer against priority moves. Against weaker attacks, it can also heal Ceruledge back to full so that it can still utilize Focus Sash.

  • Close Combat: After a Swords Dance, Close Combat has a high chance of OHKOing physically defensive versions of both Archaludon and Umbreon! It's also strong against Mega Gyarados, which will often Mega Evolve to resist Poltergeist and Shadow Sneak.

  • Beware of Garchomp: Be wary of Rough Skin Garchomp that try to switch into Ceruledge's Bitter Blade or Shadow Sneak, as the passive damage nullifies Focus Sash and leaves Ceruledge vulnerable. Scale Shot can also be problematic, since it can trigger Weak Armor's Defense drop several times, though usually four hits are required to OHKO.

Other Options

  • Jolly Nature: The loss in power can be problematic elsewhere, but going Jolly over Adamant with the given SP spread will allow Ceruledge to outrun Choice Scarf Meowscarada after a single Weak Armor activation.

  • Flash Fire: Flash Fire allows Ceruledge to create momentum from the back by switching in on Mega Charizard Y's Fire-type attacks. Furthermore, an undamaged Ceruledge can take Stealth Rock chip damage and still always survive Timid Mega Charizard Y's Scorching Sands.

Special Wall.description:
• With impressive special bulk, Bellibolt can soak up most of the special attacks in the format and turn them into fuel to boost its own damage and even heal itself!

  • Volt Switch: Volt Switch is Bellibolt's means of pivoting out of incoming Electric-resistant foes. Positioning is important, as all of Bellibolt's offensive options are Electric-type. In a pinch, it can be used to inflict the extra damage needed to secure a KO in the event Parabolic Charge lacks the power needed.

  • Parabolic Charge: When boosted by Electromorphosis, Parabolic Charge becomes Bellibolt's primary offensive option. Its amazing HP-draining effect drastically increases Bellibolt's survivability while it deals solid damage.

  • Soak: Soak is a powerful utility option that makes foes weak to Bellibolt's attacks and usually removes their STAB boost from their attacks. It can also be used preemptively against incoming Ground-types, making them much more manageable to deal with.

  • Slack Off: Slack Off grants Bellibolt reliable healing and increased longevity in the event Parabolic Charge isn't a wise move.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry allows in-a-pinch healing, which can be very useful for taking on powerful attackers with high-Base Power moves, such as Draco Meteor Mega Dragonite.

  • Magnet: Magnet boosts the power of Bellibolt's attacks and, in the case of Parabolic Charge, its healing.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is a great option for Bellibolt if you're intending to make it take on more defensive teams, as when paired with Parabolic Charge, the consistent healing makes Bellibolt exceptionally difficult to damage with the lower offensive power of defensive teams.

SP Spread

  • 29 HP / 4 Def / 2 SpA / 28 SpD / 3 Spe with Calm: 29 HP and 4 Defense SPs guarantee Bellibolt will survive Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake. 3 Speed SPs allow it to outspeed uninvested Hippowdon and use Soak to enable pivoting. 2 Special Attack SPs ensure the OHKO on uninvested Garchomp with Parabolic Charge after Soak and Electromorphosis. The rest is placed into Special Defense to maximize bulk.

Other Options

  • Toxic: Toxic allows Bellibolt to stack on an extra layer of offensive pressure during sustained battles. It can also punish incoming Ground-types by placing them on a timer.

  • Acid Spray: Acid Spray improves Bellibolt's matchup against more defensive teams and Calm Mind users that attempt to take advantage of Bellibolt's semi-passive toolkit.

Redirection Support.description:
• Mega Scovillain uses Spicy Spray and Rage Powder to punish physical attackers like Basculegion-M, Garchomp, and Kingambit while keeping its teammates safe. It also threatens high burst damage with Overheat against foes like Whimsicott and Sinistcha. Between burn's Attack drop, recovery from Leech Seed or Giga Drain, and even a lucky defensive boost from Moody before Mega Evolving, Mega Scovillain can make itself incredibly difficult to remove from the field.

  • Rage Powder and Spicy Spray: Rage Powder can force foes to attack Mega Scovillain and activate Spicy Spray, mitigating damage from physical attackers to keep its allies safe. Mega Scovillain is typically meant to be led to apply burn pressure early-game, which can also dissuade physical attackers from attacking, giving an ally like Kingambit room to set up Swords Dance to help it take out threats. Leading Mega Scovillain can pressure Basculegion-M to switch out, at which point saving Mega Scovillain for later may be necessary to burn it and stop it from sweeping with Last Respects.

  • Giga Drain versus Leech Seed: Giga Drain threatens good damage against Basculegion-M and Mega Blastoise while providing instantaneous healing. Leech Seed can rack up considerable passive damage, especially when combined with a burn. Leech Seed also allows Mega Scovillain to effectively ignore its Special Attack drop from Overheat by pivoting to a passive playstyle.

  • Mega Evolving Scovillain: Protect can be used before Mega Evolving to fish for useful Moody boosts. A Speed boost will allow Mega Scovillain to outrun Sneasler, a Defense boost will allow it to survive 200-Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion-M, and a Special Defense boost will allow it to survive Sludge Bomb from Mega Gengar. Delaying Mega Evolution can also prompt an opponent to consider whether a different Pokemon will Mega Evolve later.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 10 Def / 24 SpD with Bold: The defensive investment allows Mega Scovillain to always survive Dire Claw from Sneasler and avoid a 2HKO from Garchomp's Dragon Claw. The remaining SPs are put into Special Defense to survive Weather Ball from bulky Mega Charizard Y and Hurricane from Vivillon.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fire-types are unaffected by Spicy Spray, and Mega Charizard Y in particular threatens to deal heavy damage to Mega Scovillain. Incineroar can safely use Fake Out on Mega Scovillain, shutting down Rage Powder support for a turn, shrug off Overheat, and pivot out of Leech Seed easily with Parting Shot. Rain teams typically feature Pelipper, which threatens Mega Scovillain with Hurricane and weakens its Overheat with Drizzle. Mega Gengar threatens an OHKO with Sludge Bomb, counters Mega Scovillain's slower playstyle with a Perish trap strategy, and can use Disable on Rage Powder to stop Mega Gengar's teammates from getting burned. Most special attackers in general are comfortable against Mega Scovillain because they do not care about being burned.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Teammates like Basculegion-M and Kingambit appreciate Mega Scovillain's ability to redirect strong attacks like Sucker Punch and Close Combat, respectively, weakening the users in case they get another chance to attack later in the game. These are also offensive Pokemon that can make up for Mega Scovillain's lower damage output. Mega Froslass offers a more offensive playstyle, works better against Perish trap because it can freely switch out of Shadow Tag, and is a better option than Mega Scovillain against opposing rain. Mega Aerodactyl can be brought instead of Mega Scovillain against its biggest threats such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler, or Lycanroc-D can cover Mega Charizard Y without using Mega Evolution. Archaludon appreciates Sneasler's Close Combat being weakened by burn and improves the matchup against rain.

  • How to Overcome Mega Scovillain's Weaknesses: Rock-type coverage from teammates like Lycanroc-D and Mega Aerodactyl is mandatory for dealing with Mega Charizard Y. Steel-type coverage from Kingambit or Archaludon is appreciated to cover Rock-type foes like Aerodactyl or Glimmora that threaten Mega Scovillain, and both of them help the matchup against Incineroar. Archaludon covers Flying-type threats like Pelipper and Mega Charizard Y with Electro Shot.

Offensive.description:
• With its typing, Glimmora can resist the STAB moves of multiple attackers in the format, making it a good check to Mega Charizard Y, Mega Floette, and Aerodactyl. Furthermore, its own STAB moves can OHKO several common threats, such as Mega Charizard Y, Aerodactyl, and Whimsicott, while pressuring most of the metagame for super effective damage.

  • Earth Power is used to threaten Steel-types such as Archaludon and Kingambit that both resist its STAB moves and are immune to Toxic Spikes.

Ability

  • Toxic Debris punishes physical attackers that attack Glimmora. With Focus Sash, Toxic Spikes can be set up more reliably. This helps punish Pokemon that like to pivot in and out often, such as Incineroar.

Items

  • Focus Sash protects Glimmora from being OHKOed by some of the format's heavier hitters, such as Garchomp, Basculegion-M, and Mega Delphox. Focus Sash further helps Glimmora by granting it more opportunities to set up Toxic Spikes through its ability.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Metagame staples such as Garchomp and Mega Delphox reliably outspeed Glimmora, threatening major damage. Furthermore, even though it can hit many Pokemon for super effective damage, Glimmora can still fail to OHKO them. For example, Mega Floette requires two Sludge Bombs to be taken out. Similarly, Kingambit can tank an Earth Power and OHKO back with Iron Head. Special attackers like Mega Delphox and Rotom-Wash threaten to OHKO Glimmora without triggering Toxic Debris.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Whimsicott is a strong ally for Glimmora, using its Prankster-boosted Tailwind to reliably set the pace of the battle for Glimmora to outspeed threats such as Mega Floette while using STAB Fairy-type attacks to check Garchomp. Additionally, Glimmora can help OHKO Sneasler, which Whimsicott can struggle with. Mega Charizard Y is another good partner; its Fire-type STAB moves help check Steel-types, and its Drought protects Glimmora from Water-type attacks such as Wave Crash from Basculegion-M. Mega Charizard Y likewise benefits from Glimmora, as Glimmora's Power Gem can hit Incineroar , which would otherwise resist Mega Charizard Y’s attacks, for super effective damage.

  • How To Overcome Glimmora's Weaknesses: Partnering Glimmora with Mega Charizard Y helps it cover threats such as Basculegion-M and Rotom-Wash with Solar Beam, and the sun weakens their Water-type attacks. Additionally, Kingambit threatens Farigiraf and Mega Delphox, which can threaten Glimmora with Twin Beam and Psyshock, respectively.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Annihilape uses its excellent offensive coverage, solid Speed, and immunity to common defensive tools like Intimidate and Fake Out to dismantle opposing teams and create awkward situations for the opponent with Phantom Force. It also has incredible matchups against metagame staples like Incineroar, Sneasler, and Kingambit.

  • Phantom Force: Phantom Force forces common setup Pokemon like Mega Delphox, Gholdengo, and Mega Gengar to either switch out or take devastating damage. Phantom Force also breaks Protect, which can allow a slower partner to attack Annihilape's target even if they use Protect.

  • Rock Tomb vs. Rage Fist: Rock Tomb can be used for speed control and allows Annihilape to deal big damage to Mega Charizard Y. Rage Fist can be used as an alternate Ghost-type attack. Its damage output is slightly higher than Phantom Force after Annihilape gets hit once, and at 150 Base Power, Rage Fist can OHKO Sinistcha, Gholdengo, and Sneasler.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash is needed to let Annihilape check Pokemon like Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar that could otherwise outspeed and OHKO it with moves like Psychic and Shadow Ball respectively.

  • Defiant: Defiant makes Annihilape great at deterring Intimidate users. When combined with Annihilape's Fake Out immunity and Close Combat, it makes Annihilape a perfect counter to Incineroar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fast Fairy-types like Mega Floette, Whimsicott, and Sylveon under Tailwind can 2HKO Annihilape while tanking a Phantom Force or Rage Fist. Mega Staraptor can similarly outspeed and threaten Annihilape with Brave Bird while also being able to tank any of its attacks; however, it can take big damage from Phantom Force or a boosted Rage Fist combined with Brave Bird's recoil. Mega Aerodactyl can outspeed and OHKO Annihilape through its Focus Sash with Dual Wingbeat.

  • Redirection: Maushold and Mega Scovillain are particularly bad redirectors for Annihilape to deal with. Maushold can nullify Phantom Force's damage due to its Ghost immunity, while Mega Scovillain can burn Annihilape thanks to Spicy Spray, which not only reduces Annihilape's offensive prowess but also breaks its Focus Sash.

  • Farigiraf: Farigiraf can safely switch into Phantom Force while also being able to tank a Close Combat. Farigiraf can also remove Annihilape's Speed advantage with Trick Room and 2HKO it with Psychic.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is one of Annihilape's best partners due to its Fairy resistance and ability to deal big damage to Annihilape's checks. Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave ignores redirection and can 2HKO Maushold and Mega Scovillain, while Weather Ball can 2HKO Farigiraf through its Sitrus Berry healing. In return, Annihilape can force out Basculegion-M and Incineroar, which are common checks to Mega Charizard Y.

  • Poison-types: With Chlorophyll, Venusaur in the sun can outspeed and threaten Fairy-types with Sludge Bomb. If given a Life Orb, it can outspeed and OHKO Mega Aerodactyl with Solar Beam. Toxapex can sit in front of Fairy-types and take them down over time with the combination of Toxic and Infestation. Toxapex can also trap Pokemon on the field with Infestation, forcing them to get hit by Phantom Force. Phantom Force combined with Protect can let Annihilape stall out turns, letting Toxapex's Infestation and Toxic rack up damage before Phantom Force KOes the target.

  • Incineroar and Garchomp: Incineroar can use Fake Out to let Annihilape set up a Phantom Force and can threaten Farigiraf with Throat Chop. Intimidate also drops Mega Aerodactyl's Attack low enough so that it can't OHKO Annihilape with Dual Wingbeat. Incineroar appreciates Annihilape's good matchups against Sneasler and Basculegion-M. Choice Scarf Garchomp can outspeed and deal big damage to Mega Aerodactyl with Rock Slide, and it appreciates Annihilape's ability to threaten Hydreigon.

Trick Room Support.description:
• Farigiraf's solid resilience and unique ability to deny Fake Out give it a strong niche as a reliable Trick Room setter. Offensively, a Psychic typing grants it a great matchup against Poison-types like Sneasler, Glimmora, and Venusaur.

  • Psychic: Even with no Special Attack investment, Psychic will always 2HKO maximum HP variants of Mega Gengar and Mega Venusaur.

  • Thunderbolt vs. Hyper Voice: Thunderbolt pressures Flying- and Water-types like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Aerodactyl, and Basculegion-M, notably having a good chance to 2HKO the latter two with no investment. Hyper Voice sacrifices useful coverage for the ability to constantly pressure the opposing team with spread damage, especially if Farigiraf has the initiative under Trick Room.

  • Protect vs. Helping Hand: If Farigiraf's support is integral to your team, it can use Protect to defensively position itself and guard against double targeting. Helping Hand can be used over Protect if you can afford to sacrifice Farigiraf, allowing it to bolster the team's damage output even when it's about to be KOed. Farigiraf can run both moves in the last two moveslots only if it's supporting a Pokemon that can deal so much spread damage, like Torkoal or Mega Blastoise, that having an auxiliary attack isn't necessary.

Other Options

  • Twin Beam: Twin Beam is a weaker alternative to Psychic that's capable of OHKOing Focus Sash variants of Sneasler and, with enough investment, Glimmora.

  • Roar: Roar can be used in the last moveslot to deny setup sweepers like Mega Floette from gaining boosts and users of Trick Room like Sinistcha and opposing Farigiraf from setting it up.

  • Ally Switch: Although it's reliant on predicting your opponent's actions, Ally Switch's ability to essentially redirect an incoming attack away from Farigiraf's ally can make it a worthwhile consideration for the last moveslot.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst healing lets Farigiraf repeatedly survive strong attacks like Sneasler's Close Combat and handle double targeting much more easily, making it the preferred held item.

  • Colbur Berry: If Sitrus Berry isn't available, Colbur Berry can be used to guarantee survival against Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Mega Tyranitar's Knock Off.

Abilities

  • Armor Tail: Armor Tail's most notable application is denying Fake Out from users like Sneasler and Incineroar. Additionally, it protects Farigiraf's team from Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Prankster-boosted moves like Whimsicott's Encore and Sableye's Quash.

SP Spreads

  • Speed-reducing Natures: A Relaxed, Quiet, or Sassy nature can be used over a Bold, Modest, or Calm nature, respectively, if you want Farigiraf to outspeed neutral-natured base 60s like Sylveon and Incineroar under Trick Room.

  • 30 HP / 24 Def / 12 SpD with Bold or Relaxed: This is a physically defensive spread that lets Farigiraf survive Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Mega Scizor's Bug Bite. With Sitrus Berry, Farigiraf is also likely to avoid getting 2HKOed by Sneasler's Close Combat, Jolly Adaptability Basculegion-M's Wave Crash, and Modest Mega Floette's Dazzling Gleam.

  • 12 HP / 24 Def / 27 SpA / 3 SpD with Modest or Quiet: This offensive spread lets Farigiraf usually OHKO Focus Sash Glimmora with Twin Beam and potentially OHKO maximum HP Mega Gengar with Psychic. The bulk investment lets Farigiraf avoid the OHKO from non-Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Mega Floette's Moonblast, as well as the 2HKO from uninvested Incineroar's Throat Chop with either Berry.

  • 32 HP / 11 Def / 23 SpD with Calm or Sassy: With the heavy special bulk investment, Farigiraf cannot be OHKOed by Mega Floette's Light of Ruin and is unlikely to be OHKOed by its +1 Moonblast, while 11 Defense SPs give favorable odds to survive non-Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. Sitrus Berry lets Farigiraf dodge the 2HKO from Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Archaludon's Electro Shot, as well as the 3HKO from Jolly Garchomp's Dragon Claw almost all of the time.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Kingambit is the most threatening Pokemon to Farigiraf, as it can easily KO non-Colbur Berry variants with Kowtow Cleave, comfortably take Farigiraf's STAB attacks, and benefit from Trick Room with its low Speed. Additionally, Farigiraf is a sitting duck against other Dark-types like Mega Tyranitar and Incineroar; Mega Tyranitar can threaten an OHKO with Knock Off and proceed to set up as it switches out, while Incineroar can gradually wear it down and lock out Hyper Voice with Throat Chop. Steel-types like Aegislash and Corviknight easily tank Farigiraf's STAB attacks, which lets them freely attack and, in Corviknight's case, set up. Bug-types like Kleavor and Mega Scizor pressure Farigiraf with their STAB moves; additionally, Mega Scizor can set up Swords Dance and gain free recovery by eating its Sitrus Berry with Bug Bite. Although it's fairly bulky, Farigiraf can be easily KOed if it's targeted by a pair of very strong foes; a combination of attacks like Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball and Sneasler's Close Combat can put it out of commission if it attempts to set up Trick Room. Farigiraf's lack of coverage and Speed can make it passive outside of Trick Room, especially if it uses a bulky SP spread. This can put the burden on its on-field ally to pick up the slack offensively, which the opponent can exploit by double targeting the ally.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Farigiraf should be ideally paired with slow teammates like Kingambit and Sylveon, as they appreciate the ability to attack first and still tank a couple blows with their bulk investment. However, it's possible to use Farigiraf alongside moderately fast Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Floette, especially if the opposing team uses Tailwind support. In this case, a Tailwind setter like Whimsicott or Aerodactyl can be beneficial for an alternate team mode if Trick Room isn't needed, and Farigiraf can still contribute to this mode by blocking Fake Out with Armor Tail to preserve the setter's Focus Sash. This also prevents Pokemon that don't run Protect, like Choice Scarf Garchomp and most Chople Berry Kingambit variants, from getting disrupted and losing momentum.

  • Kingambit appreciates Farigiraf's ability to pressure Sneasler; in return, it can handle Aegislash and, with Low Kick, other Dark-types like opposing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar. Fairy-types like Sylveon and Mega Floette can repay Farigiraf's good matchup against Poison-types by handling Dark-types for it; Sylveon can use Trick Room to attack unimpeded, while bulky Calm Mind variants of Mega Floette can have an easier time setting up under it. Fire-types like Torkoal and Mega Charizard Y can blast through Steel- and Bug-types with their STAB moves. Torkoal especially stands out given its absolutely subpar Speed, which, in tandem with Armor Tail, makes it almost guaranteed to unleash a full-power Eruption under Trick Room. Incineroar can also handle these foes itself under Trick Room, and it can help protect Farigiraf from getting overwhelmed with Fake Out, Intimidate, and Parting Shot.

  • How to Overcome Farigiraf's Weaknesses: Farigiraf should be positioned in a way such that it won't be KOed if it attempts to set up Trick Room. When paired with it as the leading duo, Incineroar can prevent double targeting with Fake Out, letting Farigiraf set up Trick Room more easily. Once Trick Room is set up, Incineroar can pivot to an offensive teammate to maintain momentum. Under Trick Room, Farigiraf should ideally be paired with the teammate that threatens the opposing side the best or switch out if two offensive Pokemon can put up better pressure. Outside of Trick Room, it can get around its Speed with Helping Hand to still contribute to the team's damage output. If your team has a Tailwind setter alongside Farigiraf, determine the opposing team's means of speed control and potential priority users during Team Preview, then play off your selections from there. For example, if the opposing team has its own Tailwind setter and a Fake Out user, it may be wise to bench your setter and bring Farigiraf instead.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Kingambit is one of the top threats of Regulation M-B, trading damage comfortably and threatening many top threats such as Basculegion-M, Gholdengo, and Mega Floette. Additionally, Kingambit's typing allows it to defensively answer both Gholdengo's and Mega Metagross's STAB moves as well as making it immune to Toxapex's Toxic.

  • Items: Black Glasses allows Kingambit to deal more damage with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch. Black Glasses-boosted Sucker Punch always OHKOes Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and can OHKO Mega Froslass in the snow most of the time. Focus Sash allows Kingambit to sacrifice its defenses to patch up its lackluster Speed, and it enables Kingambit to survive strong attacks such as Mega Floette's Light of Ruin, Mega Staraptor's Close Combat, and Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball. Focus Sash Kingambit is utilized on Tailwind teams to take advantage of any Speed investment. Chople Berry lets Kingambit retain its great bulk and utilize Trick Room better while surviving Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat, Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar, and Mega Raichu Y's Focus Blast. Chople Berry Kingambit can also survive Mega Staraptor's Close Combat, but this isn't guaranteed.

  • Abilities: Defiant allows Kingambit to punish Incineroar's and Staraptor's Intimidate, Milotic's Icy Wind, and even the Special Attack drops from Mega Floette's and Whimsicott's Moonblast. Defiant's boost lets Kingambit always OHKO Sinistcha with Kowtow Cleave.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch makes up for Kingambit's poor Speed and threatens faster Pokemon such as Basculegion-M. Sucker Punch is also useful for late-game one-on-ones, as it pressures the opponent to guess whether Kingambit will choose Kowtow Cleave or Sucker Punch.

  • Iron Head versus Swords Dance versus Low Kick: Iron Head is used to threaten Mega Floette and Sylveon while dealing decent damage to Sneasler and Mega Staraptor and chunking Tyranitar. Swords Dance turns Kingambit into a setup sweeper; it's typically seen with Black Glasses to add another damage multiplier. A Black Glasses- and Swords Dance-boosted Sucker Punch can OHKO frailer Mega Charizard Y and Garchomp. Low Kick is used to threaten opposing Kingambit, Incineroar, and Tyranitar. However, Kingambit cannot damage Fairy-types or Sneasler much if it opts for Low Kick.

  • Protect versus Low Kick: Low Kick is an alternative coverage move if Kingambit doesn't necessarily need Protect on its team. This comes at the cost of Kingambit being unable to shield itself from Fake Out and attacks that may threaten it. Focus Sash and Chople Berry are typically seen with this option, because it allows Kingambit to trade damage more comfortably.

Other Options

  • Life Orb: Life Orb pushes Kingambit's power to the absolute limit, at the cost of some recoil. A Life Orb-boosted Sucker Punch OHKOes some Gholdengo.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def with Adamant: This is Kingambit's primary SP spread. Chople Berry and Black Glasses are typically seen with this spread.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread is used with a set utilizing four attacks and Focus Sash, allowing Kingambit to outspeed bulkier Pelipper and some Incineroar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Even with Chople Berry, Kingambit does not have the best matchup against Sneasler and Mega Staraptor. Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar threaten to OHKO Kingambit as well, and without speed control, Tyranitar will beat Black Glasses Kingambit. Despite Kingambit's ability acting as a check to Incineroar's Intimidate, its Flare Blitz still threatens Kingambit.

  • Without Iron Head or a Swords Dance boost, Mega Floette and Sylveon will outlast Kingambit in damage trades. Additionally, Mega Floette's Light of Ruin will OHKO non-Focus Sash Kingambit.

  • Mega Charizard Y is faster than Kingambit and will threaten to OHKO it, while Excadrill, Mega Swampert, and Garchomp are Ground-types that threaten Kingambit super effectively while also outspeeding it.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M and Sinistcha can block Sneasler's Close Combat, and the former can OHKO Sneasler with Wave Crash while resisting Dire Claw. Furthermore, Basculegion-M also threatens Incineroar for huge damage even with Intimidate. Sinistcha can set up Trick Room for Kingambit, allowing Kingambit to outspeed and beat threats to Sinistcha, such as non-Focus Sash Basculegion and Mega Froslass.

  • Sneasler can threaten opposing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar with Close Combat and provide Fake Out support so that Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance safely. Kingambit can deal with Gholdengo and Mega Metagross in return.

  • Mega Charizard Y can support Kingambit teams with its immunity to Garchomp's Earthquake and resistance to Incineroar's Flare Blitz, opposing Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and sun-boosted Weather Ball, and Mega Staraptor's Close Combat while pressuring opposing Kingambit and Mega Scovillain. In return, Kingambit can cover Mega Aerodactyl for it.

  • Garchomp can threaten opposing Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and Tyranitar. Kingambit boasts an excellent matchup against Mega Froslass, as well as Alolan Ninetales if it is running Iron Head, both of which Garchomp usually struggles with. However, Garchomp cannot safely use Earthquake next to Kingambit.

  • Mega Floette and Sylveon can threaten opposing Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Mega Staraptor. Their weakness to Poison-type moves such as Sneasler's Poison Jab and Venusaur's Sludge Bomb is in turn patched up by Kingambit's Steel typing.

Bulky Swords Dance.description:
Kingambit is one of the tier's most devastating late-game sweepers thanks to Supreme Overlord and its strong offensive profile, making it a potent option on multiple playstyles ranging from balance to hyper offense. Its typing and natural bulk allow it to set up with Swords Dance on Galarian Slowking, Espathra, and Meowscarada. Sucker Punch makes up for Kingambit's poor Speed, letting it snipe frailer foes such as Mega Alakazam and Mega Delphox. Kowtow Cleave is a consistent STAB move that deals heavy damage to slower foes such as Corviknight and Toxapex, while Iron Head hits Dark-resistant foes such as Clefable and Mega Lopunny. The SP spread maximizes Kingambit's natural bulk, notably letting it survive +1 Mega Gyarados's Earthquake. Leftovers increases Kingambit's longevity and makes better use of its natural bulk while punishing foes for playing around Sucker Punch by restoring health. Black Glasses amplifies Kingambit's power, notably allowing it to OHKO Mega Lopunny with +2 Sucker Punch and five fainted allies, as well as OHKO Multiscale Dragonite with +2 Kowtow Cleave and five fainted allies. Chople Berry minimizes the risk of Fighting-type coverage from foes such as Aegislash and Hisuian Samurott, while Lum Berry punishes foes that rely on status conditions such as Dragapult and Rotom-Wash. Shuca Berry can also be considered to punish Ground-types such as Garchomp and Excadrill alongside users of Ground-type coverage such as Dragonite. Occa Berry has a similar niche against Ceruledge, Mega Delphox, and Mega Meganium.

On offensive teams, Glimmora can provide entry hazard support to wear down checks such as Annihilape and Sneasler, making Kingambit's late-game sweep easier. Offensive teammates that help Kingambit overwhelm its counterplay, such as Corviknight and Skarmory, are appreciated, including Garchomp, Sneasler, and Hisuian Samurott. Specially offensive teammates such as Volcarona, Mega Floette, and Primarina can take advantage of the physically defensive walls Kingambit doesn't like dealing with, while Kingambit can break past Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge for all three. On balance and bulky offense teams, defensive pivots such as Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, both of which handle Ground-types such as Garchomp, can bring Kingambit in safely against foes it does well against, such as Dragapult and Meowscarada. Toxapex, Clefable, and Galarian Slowking all do well against Fighting-types that may offensively pressure Kingambit. The former two can provide hazard support, while Galarian Slowking's Future Sight can limit how easily Fighting-types switch into Kingambit.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.
battlestadiumsingles.comments:
Speed SP Benchmarks

  • Moving first means Kingambit can improve certain matchups like Primarina. Generally speaking, it is recommended to sacrifice bulk instead of offensive power if wanting to reallocate to Speed.

  • 3 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed negative Speed nature Aegislash.

  • 11 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested base 60 Speed targets such as Clefable before Mega Evolution, Primarina, and Aegislash.

  • 12 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Tyranitar.

  • 16 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Scizor before Mega Evolution.

  • 18 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Corviknight, though its superior bulk and access to Body Press mean that it is still overwhelmingly favored in the matchup.

  • 21 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Clefable, though keep in mind that Mega Clefable often receives Speed boosts from Baton Pass Espathra.

  • 26 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Scizor.

Swords Dance.description:
• With excellent typing, Supreme Overlord, and Sucker Punch, Kingambit is a powerful revenge killer and bulky attacker.

  • Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave: Sucker Punch helps pick off weakened attackers and is excellent insurance against late-game Choice Scarf users like Basculegion-M and Garchomp. Kowtow Cleave is usually needed as a second Dark-type attack, though, particularly for Substitute users like Mega Gengar that can play around Sucker Punch.

  • Swords Dance: Kingambit's amazing bulk allows it to consistently survive big hits such as Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake, letting it set up a Swords Dance and fire back with +2 Sucker Punch.

  • Iron Head versus Low Kick: Iron Head provides the best all-around power and coverage, allowing Kingambit to better threaten Primarina, Mimikyu, and Mega Floette. Low Kick is less flexible and leaves Kingambit vulnerable to Primarina, but it's the best way to take on opposing Kingambit and has a high chance to OHKO offensive Hydreigon after Stealth Rock damage.

Items

  • Black Glasses: Black Glasses doubles down on making Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave as deadly as possible. When combined with Supreme Overlord, +2 Sucker Punch + Black Glasses will always OHKO offensive Garchomp.

  • Lum Berry: If Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance ahead of time, Lum Berry will prevent Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-W from switching in and completely ruining its momentum.

  • Chople Berry: Chople Berry allows Kingambit to withstand some weaker Fighting-type attacks, such as Close Combat from Aegislash and Scizor and unboosted Body Press from Corviknight. With maximum HP investment, Kingambit also has a high chance to survive Jolly Mega Lopunny's Close Combat and an average chance to survive Timid Mega Gengar's Focus Blast.

Alternate EV Spread

  • 8 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def / 24 Spe with Adamant: This spread maintains enough bulk to almost always survive Adamant Life Orb Mimikyu's +2 Play Rough after Stealth Rock damage as well as Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake from full health. After maximizing Attack, the remaining SPs are invested into Speed, allowing Kingambit to outrun threats such as Mega Clefable with 2 Speed SPs.

Setup Sweeper.description:
• Gholdengo, thanks to its naturally strong defensive typing, easily walls out common Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Staraptor and helps beat top Pokemon like Mega Floette, Sylveon, Mega Aerodactyl, and Sinistcha. This typing allows Gholdengo to set up Nasty Plot, letting it sweep through teams with its STAB moves and threaten nearly all metagame staples with at least neutral damage.

  • Make It Rain: Make It Rain hits nearly anything that doesn't resist it for huge damage after a Nasty Plot, having a solid chance to OHKO Mega Tyranitar with Life Orb. When using Make It Rain, Gholdengo must be careful; using it at the wrong time late-game will leave Gholdengo too weak to contribute much . This forces Gholdengo to use Nasty Plot again and leave itself or its partner open to attacks.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb gives Gholdengo potential for large amounts of burst damage, allowing Gholdengo to OHKO most Mega Froslass with Make It Rain and Basculegion-M with Shadow Ball, though it comes at the cost of Gholdengo's longevity. For this reason, builds that use Life Orb Gholdengo tend to run faster and more offensive SP spreads to turn it into a strong and threatening attacker that doesn't require setup turns.

  • Spell Tag and Metal Coat: Spell Tag and Metal Coat save Gholdengo's longevity but only allow it to boost either Shadow Ball or Make it Rain. Spell Tag allows Gholdengo to 2HKO Sneasler, while Metal Coat allows Gholdengo to OHKO Mega Aerodactyl.

  • Good as Gold: Good as Gold gives Gholdengo good chances to switch into attacks like Parting Shot from Incineroar and Grimmsnarl as well as Sleep Powder from Venusaur.

Other Options

  • Leftovers: Leftovers allow Gholdengo to focus more on setting up by increasing its longevity, though the item sacrifices power.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 8 Def / 7 SpA / 3 SpD / 16 Spe with Timid: The given SP spread allows Gholdengo to outspeed Adamant Basculegion-M, almost always survive Earthquake from Jolly Life Orb Garchomp, and withstand Dark Pulse from Mega Blastoise, with the rest dumped into Special Attack.

  • 7 HP / 32 SpA / 27 Spe with Timid: This SP spread is tailored towards Life Orb sets. It lets Gholdengo outrun Jolly Basculegion-M and survive Wave Crash from Choice Scarf Adamant Basculegion-M, allowing Gholdengo to retaliate with Shadow Ball. The remaining SPs are put into Special Attack.

  • 17 HP / 1 Def / 15 SpA / 1 SpD / 32 Spe with Modest: With the SPs in HP, Defense, and Special Defense, Gholdengo can possibly survive Flare Blitz from Incineroar and has a high chance to survive Heat Wave from Timid Mega Delphox. The SPs in Special Attack allow Life Orb-boosted Shadow Ball to OHKO Mega Delphox and +2 Make It Rain to OHKO uninvested Mega Tyranitar, which typically uses Dragon Dance sets. The Speed SPs allow Gholdengo to outspeed all Mega Tyranitar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fire-type Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Blaziken, Incineroar, and Mega Scovillain threaten huge damage onto Gholdengo with Heat Wave, Weather Ball, Flare Blitz, and Overheat. Incineroar in particular resists both of Gholdengo's STAB options, tanking Make It Rain and Shadow Ball and retaliating with Throat Chop or Flare Blitz.

  • Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar outspeed and threaten to OHKO Gholdengo with Last Respects and Shadow Ball. Hydreigon, Kingambit, and Mega Tyranitar are Dark-types that OHKO Gholdengo with Dark Pulse, Kowtow Cleave, and Knock Off. Additionally, Hydreigon can opt for Snarl instead to slowly chip down Gholdengo and weaken it in the process, and Kingambit can use Sucker Punch to hit Gholdengo before it moves.

  • Ground-types like Mega Swampert and Garchomp threaten Gholdengo with Earthquake. Mega Swampert also resists Make It Rain and is placed on rain teams alongside Pokemon like Hydreigon and Archaludon, which can deal lots of damage to Gholdengo with Dark Pulse and Electro Shot. On the other hand, Garchomp's flexibility enables it to fit on many teams, meaning that it is a hurdle that Gholdengo often has to face.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp threatens Fire-types aside from Mega Scovillain with Earthquake, and it can handle Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide.

  • Incineroar and Kingambit can switch into Ghost-types and threaten them with Throat Chop and Kowtow Cleave, while Sneasler and Mega Staraptor can help Gholdengo handle Dark-types with Close Combat.

  • Sinistcha can heal up Gholdengo with Hospitality and redirect many attacks with Rage Powder; it can also switch into Ground-types and threaten Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha. Alolan Ninetales can threaten Ground-types with Freeze-Dry and Blizzard.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Gholdengo threatens Archaludon, Mega Staraptor, Starmie, and Mega Floette. Trick and Good as Gold allow it to punish slow defensive play by locking Pokemon like Hippowdon and Corviknight into one move. It struggles a bit with damage, as it won't OHKO other threats it outspeeds like Mega Delphox, Basculegion-M, Mega Metagross, and Skeledirge without a bit of chip damage first. Gholdengo's Speed tier can also be lackluster at times, meaning Pokemon that can boost their Speed like Mega Gyarados, Mega Charizard X, and Mega Blaziken can take advantage of Gholdengo and position themselves to sweep.

  • Trick: Trick is quite useful against more utility-oriented Archaludon sets by locking them into a move and taking their Sitrus Berry. It can lock bulky Pokemon like Hippowdon, Bellibolt, and Umbreon into their recovery moves or attacks, turning them into setup fodder for Gholdengo's teammates. Trick can also stop dual screen setters like Grimmsnarl by taking its Light Clay and setup sweepers like Kingambit from using Swords Dance.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt provides coverage against Flying- and Water-types, such as Pelipper, Mega Staraptor, Hisuian Samurott, Primarina, Greninja, and Mega Gyarados.

  • Power Gem: Power Gem OHKOes Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona. It also provides Flying-type coverage similarly to Thunderbolt but can hit Mega Dragonite and Fire-types like Mega Charizard X for super effective damage.

  • Timid vs. Modest: With a Timid nature, Gholdengo can outspeed +1 Mega Gyarados, Jolly Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, Jolly Mega Lopunny, and Timid Mega Delphox.
