Modest Gholdengo's Shadow Ball has a 50% chance to OHKO Mega Metagross without chip damage, and it additionally 2HKOes Garchomp so that Gholdengo doesn't have to be locked into Make It Rain. A Modest nature also enables the OHKO on Choice Scarf Meowscarada with Make It Rain, so it can no longer act as a check.

Other Options

  • Recover: Recover is a viable option even with Trick, as Gholdengo can heal up against targets locked into utility moves like Stealth Rock. This is particularly effective against Archaludon, which Gholdengo generally walls.

  • Dazzling Gleam: Dazzling Gleam can catch Hydreigon switching in off-guard, as it generally beats this set. However, this surprise only works once, as Gholdengo is slower than Choice Scarf Hydreigon and OHKOed by Dark Pulse. Dazzling Gleam also provides coverage against other Dragon- and Dark-types like Hisuian Samurott and Mega Gyarados, though its lower Base Power means Make It Rain and Gholdengo's other coverage moves are usually better options.

Redirection Support.description:
• Sinistcha is the go-to redirector in the Regulation M-A metagame, setting itself apart from other redirectors with its immunity to Fake Out, good defensive stats, access to Trick Room, and Hospitality. Its typing allows it to support metagame-defining threats well, redirecting away moves such as Sneasler's Close Combat and Dire Claw, as well as Water-type moves and Electro Shot from rain teams.

  • Trick Room versus Protect: Trick Room is useful to turn the tables on fast threats, like Chlorophyll Venusaur, and Tailwind, even when it necessarily isn't used for a Trick Room sweeper. However, Protect can be used over Trick Room if there is conflict with other speed control options on Sinistcha's team or to give Sinistcha another tool to assist with positioning itself or other teammates.

  • Life Dew versus Protect: Life Dew is great for partners with setup moves, particularly Calm Mind Mega Floette. When using Trick Room, Protect could be used over Life Dew to help position Sinistcha to safely set it up. For instance, Sinistcha can use Protect while its partner switches to a Fake Out user, which would then give it a better opportunity to set Trick Room.

Other Options

  • Strength Sap: Strength Sap is a rather effective self-healing option, in addition to being a way to manage physical threats such as Garchomp and Incineroar.

  • Shadow Ball: Shadow Ball is a more proactive tool to help manage the common Ghost-types in the metagame, such as other Sinistcha, Mega Gengar, Mega Froslass, and Ceruledge, as well as some Psychic-types like Mega Delphox.

Items

  • Kasib Berry: With Kasib Berry, Basculegion-M can't OHKO Sinistcha with a 150-Base Power Last Respects, while Sinistcha resists its Water-type STAB moves and threatens to both 2HKO Basculegion-M with Matcha Gotcha.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is useful for general healing and helps Sinistcha avoid 2HKOs from attacks such as Fairy Feather Sylveon's Hyper Voice, Mega Floette's Moonblast, Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat after Intimidate, and Incineroar's Flare Blitz after Intimidate.

  • Colbur Berry: Colbur Berry is most useful to help manage Kingambit, allowing Sinistcha to take a Kowtow Cleave more easily; instead of requiring Sinistcha to stay at full HP to survive Kowtow Cleave, it only needs half of its HP. This allows Sinistcha to more safely use Rage Powder in front of Kingambit, nullifying Sucker Punch and allowing its partner to attack safely.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 14 Def / 20 SpD with Bold: The Defense investment allows Sinistcha to avoid being OHKOed by Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. The rest of the SPs are invested into Special Defense for general bulk. A Relaxed nature could also be used for Trick Room, though it doesn't allow Sinistcha to underspeed anything noteworthy aside from other Sinistcha.

  • 32 HP / 11 Def / 23 SpD with Calm This spread allows Sinistcha to more effectively redirect special attacks, notably Timid Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball, with the remaining SPs invested into Defense. More Special Defense could be used to live attacks such as Timid Mega Floette's Light of Ruin, though it comes at the cost of taking more damage from common physical attackers like Kingambit and Incineroar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Sinistcha has many exploitable weaknesses, most notably Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave, which both ignores Rage Powder and OHKOes Sinistcha. Mega Froslass with Blizzard and Mega Delphox with Heat Wave are similarly effective against Rage Powder Sinistcha, (AC) even if they don't OHKO it. Mega Aerodactyl with Dual Wingbeat and Kingambit with Kowtow Cleave do significant damage to Sinistcha. Ceruledge can 2HKO Sinistcha with Bitter Blade or OHKO it after a Bulk Up while resisting Matcha Gotcha and being immune to burn. Basculegion-M, while being 2HKOed by Matcha Gotcha, can threaten an OHKO with a boosted Last Respects unless Sinistcha holds a Kasib Berry. Mega Tyranitar is similar; it can outright OHKO Sinistcha with Knock Off and is naturally faster than Sinistcha to avoid Matcha Gotcha. Incineroar both resists and cannot be burned by Matcha Gotcha, and it can chunk Sinistcha for around half its health with Throat Chop or for even more with Flare Blitz. Pelipper is often a rain team's first line of defense against Sinistcha, as its Hurricane OHKOes it after slight chip damage.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Hospitality makes Sinistcha a great partner for Mega Floette, which also appreciates redirection for threatening attacks like Sneasler's Dire Claw or Gunk Shot while it sets up. Mega Floette can then threaten to OHKO Sinistcha checks such as Kingambit with a +1 Moonblast or spread damage with Dazzling Gleam. Other Pokemon that use boosting moves can naturally make excellent use of Sinistcha's redirection and Hospitality. Black Glasses Swords Dance Kingambit and Dragon Dance Mega Tyranitar are a couple of Pokemon that appreciate being able to set up in the face of extremely effective Close Combats from Sneasler and can threaten Sinistcha's checks; they outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Sucker Punch and Rock Slide, respectively, after a boost. Slower Pokemon such as Kingambit and non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can most effectively take advantage of Sinistcha's Trick Room.

  • Overcoming Sinistcha's Weaknesses: Incineroar can both make use of the extra healing and complements Sinistcha's typing near-perfectly, forming a core that can switch into each other's weaknesses and repeatedly activate Intimidate and Hospitality. Fake Out can help ensure Trick Room is set up, and Parting Shot can also allow Sinistcha to heal a teammate in the same turn by switching out Sinistcha, using Parting Shot, then switching it back in again mid-turn. While Incineroar does give Kingambit a Defiant boost, it still resists Kingambit's STAB moves and threatens to 2HKO with Flare Blitz. Similar to Incineroar, Basculegion-M both resists Fire and has access to Flip Turn to pivot. Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can also threaten key threats to Sinistcha such as Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Delphox with its speedy Wave Crash, and although Mega Charizard Y can mitigate the damage with Drought, it will still be easily 2HKOed with Wave Crash while Sinistcha threatens to redirect its Solar Beam. Sneasler threatens Kingambit and other Dark-types with STAB Close Combat. Kingambit itself is a good source of Fighting-type damage with Low Kick and a partner Sinistcha is a great way to avoid Low Kick from opposing Kingambit. Kingambit additionally helps overcome Ghost-type threats such as Mega Froslass and Basculegion-M. Garchomp is an excellent check to both Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit, 2HKOing both with Rock Slide and Earthquake, respectively; Mega Charizard Y is even able to be OHKOed if it does not have Defense investment. Pelipper and Politoed effectively neuter Sinistcha's biggest check in Mega Charizard Y, as well as other Fire-types such as Incineroar and Mega Delphox.

Bulky Rain Sweeper.description:
• Acting as rain's main powerhouse in Regulation M-B, Archaludon has the ability to easily snowball out of control if left alone, thanks to Electro Shot, Leftovers, Stamina, and its naturally high physical bulk. Archaludon has a good matchup against Mega Aerodactyl, Basculegion-M, and Toxapex thanks to Electro Shot and its typing.

  • Leftovers: Archaludon utilizes Leftovers to increase its longevity. This allows Archaludon to sweep more effectively while making some attacks, such as Choice Scarf Garchomp's Earthquake, 3HKOs instead of 2HKOs.

  • Stamina: Archaludon can accumulate Stamina boosts to become nearly physically impenetrable. This allows Archaludon to take attacks such as bulky Garchomp's Earthquake and Kingambit's and Mega Tyranitar's Low Kick more effectively over time.

  • Electro Shot: Electro Shot allows Archaludon to snowball through teams while threatening the common Pelipper, Milotic, and Basculegion-M. However, Electro Shot is reliant on rain, which makes it easily punishable by changing the weather with Pokemon like Mega Froslass.

  • Positioning with Archaludon: Archaludon can switch into weaker attacks such as Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Mega Raichu Y's and Incineroar's Fake Out to accumulate Stamina boosts. Because Archaludon's Stamina and longevity permit it to stay on the field as long as possible, it is important to position Archaludon correctly so that it faces foes that don't threaten it to swap and drop its boosts such as Sneasler and Mega Charizard Y.

SP Spreads

  • 27 HP / 5 Def / 5 SpA / 26 SpD / 3 Spe with Calm: This is Archaludon's primary spread, allowing it to survive Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Weather Ball and Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat, outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M in Tailwind, and optimize HP for Leftovers recovery. The rest of the SPs are put into Special Attack to maximize offense.

  • 32 HP / 1 Def / 5 SpA / 25 SpD / 3 Spe with Modest: This more offensive spread allows Archaludon to survive the aforementioned Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat and outspeed the aforementioned Choice Scarf Basculegion in Tailwind. The Modest nature allows Archaludon to almost always OHKO Calm Milotic with Electro Shot.

  • 27 HP / 11 Def / 8 SpA / 17 SpD / 3 Spe with Bold: This physically defensive spread allows Archaludon to hit the same Speed benchmark, HP optimization, and Special Attack dump as the primary spread while letting it survive Mega Swampert's Helping Hand-boosted Earthquake, Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M's 200-Base Power Last Respects, and Timid Mega Floette's Moonblast.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Archaludon's middling Special Defense leaves it open to strong special attacks such as Mega Floette's Moonblast, Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Weather Ball, and Hydreigon's Draco Meteor and Earth Power.

  • Archaludon is extremely exploitable without any Stamina or Electro Shot boosts, and its reliance on rain can make it tough to use in weather wars against opposing setters like Mega Charizard Y. Archaludon is overwhelmed by double targeting with special attacks, such as the combination of Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Weather Ball and Venusaur's Life Orb-boosted Earth Power. Without rain, Electro Shot is extremely exploitable, leaving Archaludon to double targeting.

  • Despite Archaludon's great physical bulk, Sneasler and Mega Staraptor can threaten huge damage with Close Combat.

  • Mega Raichu Y can stall out its own Mega Evolution to soak up Archaludon's Electro Shot thanks to Lightning Rod and can threaten it with Focus Blast after Mega Evolving.

  • Excadrill resists all of Archaludon's moves and threatens it back with High Horsepower and Earthquake. Mega Swampert can turn Archaludon's own rain against it by outspeeding Archaludon, even if it's under Tailwind, and threatening huge damage with Earthquake. Garchomp can threaten huge damage on an unboosted Archaludon with Life Orb-boosted Earthquake, outspeeding and safely 2HKOing it if Archaludon is not already at +1 Special Attack.

  • Venusaur resists Archaludon's Electro Shot while threatening Archaludon with Life Orb-boosted Earth Power or thwarting its momentum with Sleep Powder. Mega Venusaur utilizes its bulk to outlast Archaludon that lack Electro Shot boosts.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Pelipper is the far more common rain setter for Archaludon; it handles Pokemon that give Archaludon trouble such as Sinistcha, Mega Staraptor, and Excadrill with Hurricane and rain-boosted Weather Ball. Pelipper can utilize Tailwind for speed control and Wide Guard to block Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave, Mega Swampert and Garchomp's Earthquake, and Sylveon's Hyper Voice. Politoed does not have access to STAB Hurricane but has greater bulk and Speed, and it also has access to Encore and Perish Song. Encore can lock Sneasler into Fake Out, while Perish Song can remove bulky threats to Archaludon such as Mega Staraptor and Mega Venusaur.

  • Basculegion-M acts as a switch-in to any Fighting-type move that may threaten Archaludon and threatens Ground-types like Garchomp and Excadrill. Basculegion-M has access to the powerful Last Respects to clean up games with ease once Archaludon has chipped foes down, and it can chunk foes early-game with Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash, allowing Archaludon to clean up. Mega Swampert's Earthquake and High Horsepower can chunk opposing Archaludon and OHKO Sneasler and Mega Raichu Y, and its Ice Punch can OHKO Garchomp. Mega Swampert can also outspeed and OHKO Mega Floette and Sylveon with rain-boosted Wave Crash, preventing them from dealing huge damage to Archaludon.

  • Sinistcha provides Archaludon with recovery in Hospitality and Life Dew, speed control in Trick Room, and redirection in Rage Powder. Sinistcha can also act as a switch-in to attacks Archaludon is weak to, handling Garchomp's Earthquake and Mega Raichu Y's Focus Blast comfortably. Furthermore, Sinistcha can check Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha. By providing dual screens support and Special Attack drops to with Spirit Break, Grimmsnarl can maximize Archaludon's bulk and weaken moves such as Sneasler's Close Combat and Mega Floette's Moonblast. Parting Shot can bring in Archaludon safely, weaken foes, and allow it to take moves that may threaten Grimmsnarl, namely Basculegion-M's Wave Crash and Kingambit's Iron Head, while gaining a Stamina boost.

  • Mega Charizard Y can threaten problematic foes like Venusaur and Excadrill with Weather Ball in and out of the rain, respectively. Hurricane can be used at times to threaten Grass-types that trouble Archaludon such as Sinistcha, Venusaur, and Mega Scovillain inside of rain. Under sun, Mega Charizard Y can utilize Weather Ball and Heat Wave to threaten Alolan Ninetales and Mega Froslass to win weather wars; these attacks also threaten Excadrill and Gholdengo to pave the way for Archaludon to sweep. In exchange for this utility, Archaludon can cover for the Rock-types that give Mega Charizard Y trouble, such as Mega Aerodactyl and Lycanroc-D. However, Archaludon cannot use Electro Shot as easily when brought alongside Mega Charizard Y.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Bulky Entry Hazard Setter.description:
• Archaludon is one of the best walls in the entire game thanks to its incredible bulk and Stamina. With access to Stealth Rock, phazing support, and Draco Meteor, Archaludon can efficiently wear down lineups that lack dedicated checks to it.

  • Thunderbolt versus Flash Cannon: Thunderbolt is Archaludon's best complementary move to Draco Meteor for its ability to hit key bulky targets Primarina and Corviknight, which comfortably check Archaludon otherwise, as well as hitting many other Steel-types neutrally. Flash Cannon is a more consistent damage source overall, but it doesn't help Archaludon against Steel-types like Corviknight, Scizor, and Aegislash.

  • Roar versus Dragon Tail: Roar is the preferred phazing option for racking up Stealth Rock damage, as Pokemon immune to it are extremely uncommon, and it works through Substitute. Dragon Tail is more generally oppressive by dealing direct damage and phazing at the same time, and it additionally cannot be shut down by Taunt. However, Dragon Tail can make Archaludon struggle against Substitute users and does not work at all on Mega Floette, which can set up on Archaludon and threaten to snowball out of control.

  • Mirror Coat: Archaludon's bulk makes it a viable user of Mirror Coat, which allows it to deal significant damage or completely take out targets such as Primarina and Mega Gengar.

  • Sitrus Berry versus Leftovers: Sitrus Berry's burst recovery is more effective at helping Archaludon survive multiple hits from big attacks, including super effective ones like Garchomp's Earthquake. On the other hand, Leftovers is superior when Archaludon can capitalize long-term on Stamina boosts from favorable defensive matchups against foes such as Meowscarada and Mega Starmie.

Other Options

  • Foul Play: Foul Play gives Archaludon a direct option against difficult physical attackers like Aegislash and Mega Metagross.

  • Rest and Chesto Berry: Restoring Archaludon to full health after receiving several Stamina boosts can completely ruin physically offensive lineups that rely on attrition to beat Archaludon.

SP Spreads

  • All 2HKOs mentioned below factor in Archaludon having a +1 Defense boost from Stamina for the second hit.

  • 32 HP / 23 Def / 11 SpD with Bold: With this spread, Archaludon is guaranteed to avoid the 2HKO from Jolly Basculegion-M's 150-Base Power Last Respects and, when using Sitrus Berry, Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake. Leftover SPs are put into Special Defense.

  • 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpD with Calm: Maximum special bulk investment allows Archaludon to avoid the 2HKO from Timid Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball and Modest Primarina's Moonblast, assuming no Fairy Feather on the latter. This spread works particularly well with Mirror Coat, as Archaludon also has a significant chance to survive +1 Moonblast from offensive Mega Floette.

Pseudo-Focus Sash.description:
• Archaludon can perform consistently as an offensive lead thanks to Sturdy, which lets it take full advantage of its respectable Speed and high-power attacks.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt provides strong overlapping coverage with Draco Meteor, in particular pressuring defensive mainstays Primarina and Corviknight.

  • Flash Cannon versus Steel Beam: Flash Cannon is the safest option for a Steel-type STAB attack and is more than sufficient against the likes of offensive Mimikyu and Glimmora. However, Steel Beam's massive Base Power makes dealing with bulkier threats like Hippowdon much more viable, even if it comes at the cost of survivability.

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere helps Archaludon win the mirror matchup while avoiding Draco Meteor usage, keeping its Special Attack stable and making it less likely to become setup bait. Even specially defensive Archaludon has a high chance to be 2HKOed. Aura Sphere is also the best option for taking on Kingambit.

  • Stealth Rock: The combination of Archaludon's Speed and Sturdy allows it to reliably set Stealth Rock.

  • Roar: Roar can disrupt dangerous setup sweepers like Iron Defense Mega Metagross and Swords Dance Mega Blaziken.

  • Timid versus Modest: Many offensive threats such as Adamant Mimikyu, Jolly Basculegion-M, Jolly Hisuian Samurott, and Jolly Mega Gyarados are at or just below Archaludon's positive-nature Speed tier. As such, a Timid nature is usually preferred. However, the power increase from a Modest nature is still worth considering; for example, it gives Archaludon a decent chance to OHKO offensive Mega Gengar with Draco Meteor.

Other Options

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse is offensive Archaludon's best means of pressuring Aegislash and Gholdengo directly.

  • Mirror Coat: Sturdy allows for more confident Mirror Coat usage, especially against targets like Gholdengo that boost their Special Attack, but it limits the direct offensive nature that this set likes to utilize and is very reliant on Sturdy being active.

Items

  • White Herb: White Herb allows Archaludon to fire off Draco Meteor once without worrying about the subsequent Special Attack drop, giving it incredible burst potential and generally making it less exploitable by setup attackers.

  • Sitrus Berry: Archaludon's defensive typing and stats are so strong naturally that Sitrus Berry can still be worth running on an offensive set. Sitrus Berry will also always activate after using Steel Beam, giving Archaludon an extra health buffer as well as the potential to fire off a second Steel Beam without fainting.

Rain Sweeper.description:
• When paired with a rain setter like Pelipper, Archaludon can build dangerous offensive momentum with Electro Shot.

  • Electro Shot : Thanks to the Special Attack boost, even the first Electro Shot used can be difficult to switch into without an Electric resistance, and it can also OHKO frailer targets like Mega Lucario.

  • Draco Meteor : Electro Shot may be the star of the show, but Draco Meteor is often Archaludon's best option when you're trying to play around Ground-type switch-ins such as Garchomp.

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere provides consistent coverage independent from the weather, pressuring Dark-types like Kingambit and opposing Archaludon.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt is an alternative Electric-type option to use outside of rain, which can be especially relevant for keeping pressure on Mega Charizard Y.

SP Spreads and Items

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: A standard offensive spread for use with Choice Scarf. A Timid nature is mandatory, as Archaludon wants to outrun Choice Scarf Jolly Basculegion-M.

  • 32 HP / 11 Def / 15 SpA / 8 Spe with Modest: Going with a bulkier spread along with a Sitrus Berry sacrifices immediate offensive pressure, but it eases the need for prediction and allows Archaludon more flexibility in and out of rain. Enough Special Attack investment is maintained to guarantee that Electro Shot OHKOes offensive Mega Gyarados, and the Speed investment is enough to outrun fully invested base 60s like Primarina. The remaining SPs go into HP and Defense, giving Archaludon a decent chance of avoiding the 2HKO from Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake after Sitrus Berry healing and a Stamina activiation.

Focus Energy.description:
• By utilizing Focus Energy and Scope Lens for guaranteed critical hits, not only can Archaludon ignore its own Draco Meteor's stat drops, but it can also rip through the defensive boosts of tanky threats like Clefable and its Mega Evolution!

  • Draco Meteor: Draco Meteor can still be used as an upfront burst option prior to using Focus Energy, allowing Archaludon to adapt to what works best in each matchup. This can make Focus Energy + Draco Meteor a nasty surprise for anything trying to set up on a "weakened" Archaludon.

  • Flash Cannon: Flash Cannon is for Fairy-types like Mimikyu and Primarina, which can ignore Draco Meteor. After Archaludon uses Focus Energy, it will always OHKO physically defensive Unaware Clefable.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt is more immediately threatening to Primarina than Flash Cannon, and it also prevents Archaludon from getting walled by Corviknight. While Flash Cannon is much more consistent against Clefable overall, Focus Energy + Thunderbolt can still get the job done on Mega Clefable because of its new typing.

  • Substitute: Substitute can block status moves like Yawn from Hippowdon and Umbreon, giving Archaludon an opportunity to set up Focus Energy safely.

  • Stamina versus Sturdy: The choice between abilities comes down primarily to what SP spread Archaludon is running. If Archaludon is using a bulky spread, it should have Stamina; if it's using a purely offensive spread, Sturdy is preferable.

Other Options

  • Foul Play and Dark Pulse: Even with a Modest nature and a Focus Energy boost, Archaludon cannot reliably 2HKO HP-invested King's Shield Aegislash with Thunderbolt. Foul Play allows Archaludon to always 2HKO physical attacker Aegislash in Shield forme, and it will also always 2HKO special attacker variants after a Focus Energy boost. Dark Pulse is another option that isn't as efficient against physical attacker Aegislash but makes it possible to threaten Gholdengo, which Foul Play can't do.

EV Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 SpA / 2 Spe with Modest: This is a simple bulky attacker spread that lets Archaludon work particularly well against slower cycle and stall teams; it also helps Archaludon respond better to threats that try to set up while using Focus Energy. For example, maximum HP Archaludon avoids the OHKO from Mega Gyarados's +1 Earthquake. Substitute sets appreciate the HP investment as well, since Umbreon's Foul Play will almost never break Substitute in one hit.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest or Timid: Focusing on Speed lets Archaludon outrun variants of Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott that have some Speed investment. A Modest nature gives an unboosted Draco Meteor the best shot of OHKOing specially defensive variants of Garchomp, but a Timid nature will allow Archaludon to outrun Adamant Mimikyu and Speed tie at worst with opposing Archaludon.
